Jeg så på mens en mann prøvde å sage en stor plate finer i to. Han snakket med noen andre menn mens han saget, og det virket som om han ikke var særlig opptatt av å få snittet rett. Jeg la merke til at han fortsatte å sage lenger og lenger bort fra linjen han hadde riper i fineren med en spiker. Etter at han var flere tommer unna, forsøkte en av vennene hans å gjøre ham oppmerksom på det, men han latet som han ikke hørte. Han prøvde å tilfeldig føre den gamle håndsagen tilbake mot linjen, samtidig som han fortsatte å snakke med mennene, uten å gjøre noe stort nummer av det. Til slutt, etter at han var mer enn en fot ute, stoppet han. Han visste nå at han hadde et problem, et problem han ikke kunne fikse.

Jeg måtte tenke: «Er dette hva vi gjør som kirke, Kristi brud?» Vi tar ikke avdrift veldig alvorlig; vi tillater at ting kommer inn i vår midte. Vi sier: «Det er ikke så farlig, la oss ikke være kritiske.» Men jo lenger vi venter, desto vanskeligere blir det å rette opp. Først sjokkerer det oss; senere blir det den nye normalen. Hvordan kan vi vite om vi har drevet av? Det burde være like enkelt som å vurdere hvor vi pleide å være, sammenligne det med hvor vi er nå, og så evaluere forandringen med hva Bibelen lærer.

Siden å kjempe mot avdrift ikke er populært, vil menn i kirken ikke gjøre det. Noen i våre kirker som driver mot verden, har perfeksjonert et «feel-good»-evangelium. De snakker i vei om hvor nære de kommer Jesus, og hvor velsignet de er, men deres retning er tydeligvis ikke i tråd med Skriftens lære. De er på vei mot verden.

Det finnes andre som ikke ønsker at kirken skal drive av, men som likevel har sine egne problemer—kjærlighet til penger, grådighet og lyst på fornøyelser. Ingen sier noe fordi det virker som om ingen vil høre. En populær respons er: «Ja, jeg vet det ikke er bra, men hva kan vi gjøre?» «Alle kirker har problemer.» Eller «Ja, jeg ville aldri tillatt det, men jeg føler ikke det er min plass å si noe.» «Det er ikke for min familie, men hvis andre vil gjøre det, er det greit.»

Vi lever i en «meg»-tid. Alt handler om meg. De konservative, anabaptistiske folkegruppene vikler seg inn i sosiale medier, selfies, tweeting, Facebook og hva enn det måtte være. Vi elsker oss selv så mye at vi snakker, handler og kler oss på måter som trekker oppmerksomhet mot oss—vi promoterer oss selv. Vi snakker om å se bra ut, føle oss bra og leve bra. Hva skjedde med å fremme Jesus? Husk at Jesus sa: For den som vil bevare sitt liv, skal miste det; men den som mister sitt liv for min skyld, skal finne det –Matteus 16:25.

Hvorfor virker det så vanskelig å se hvilken retning vi går i? Hvis alt handler om oss, så handler det ikke alt om Jesus. Hvis vi er opptatt av siste mote og de fineste bilene, lastebilene og husene, så handler det ikke alt om Jesus. Vi kan ikke tilfredsstille vårt kjød og samtidig si at vi er kristne.

Jeg ble nylig spurt hvorfor noen pastorer mister sine barn til verden. I de fleste tilfeller mener jeg det er samme grunn som mange anabaptister mister sine barn til mørkets rike—fedrene har mistet et gudfryktig syn for hjemmene sine. De lever et maktesløst liv og lar verden komme inn. Kanskje har de ikke TV, men hva med internett? Det tillater fortsatt verdens påvirkning å komme inn. Også bruker far mer tid på sin virksomhet og mer tid på å nyte livet enn han gjør på å søke Guds ansikt.

Mange amerikanere drar på korttidsmisjon. Mange ganger ser det ut som ungdommene som reiser, vil treffe stranden eller andre fornøyelser så snart de går av flyet. Hvorfor? Fordi det er det de enten blir lært eller får lov til hjemme—å søke nytelse. De har ikke blitt lært å fornekte kjødet; de har ikke sett foreldrene fornekte kjødet. Noen av oss kan være så langt av veien at vi må gjøre som snekkeren i begynnelsen av denne artikkelen—ydmyke oss og begynne på nytt.

Ektefedre drar sine uvillige koner inn i verden, koner dytter sine menn ut i verden, og barna drar sine foreldre med ut i verden. Og dessverre, siden den moderne kirken har kastet av seg alle former for disiplin og struktur, kan alle bli værende i kirken og forgifte den med sine verdslige ideer (i det minste så lenge du smiler og sier du elsker Jesus). Husk Skriften: Dersom dere elsker meg, holder dere mine bud –Johannes 14:15. Og: Den som sier: «Jeg kjenner ham,» men ikke holder hans bud, han er en løgner, og sannheten er ikke i ham –1 Johannes 2:4.

Her er noen områder der kirken driver av.

Broderlig kjærlighet

Derav skal alle kjenne at dere er mine disipler, om dere har kjærlighet til hverandre –Johannes 13:35.

Folk har besøkt vår kirke og spurt om vi praktiserer det hellige kyss. Jeg svarer at det gjør vi; men forståelsen av nødvendigheten av å elske hverandre kommer først. Mange kirker avskaffer det hellige kyss, som klart er befalt i Ordet. Og det virker passende fordi de har sluttet å elske hverandre. Jeg tror ikke vi forstår viktigheten av dette emnet—å ha kjærlighet en for den andre. Når vår kjærlighet får oss til å lide for hverandre, ser verden det. Ofte stopper et broderskap å elske hverandre fordi de ikke lenger kjemper «sammen». De har blitt uavhengige.

Noen av de største handlingene av kjærlighet for hverandre har skjedd på slagmarken. Menn har kastet seg over granater, og de har lagt seg foran kuler for å redde kameratene. Fordi de har kjempet sammen, ser de etter hverandre. Hva hvis en soldat som marsjerer ut i kamp, merker at en medsoldats magasin faller fra geværet? Hva ville han gjøre? Ville han forbli stille fordi kameraten kunne bli sint? Eller ville han forbli stille fordi han visste at han hadde sine egne problemer? Nei. Han ville hjelpe sin bror. Hvis ugudelige menn på slagmarken kan praktisere dette, hvorfor kan ikke Guds folk gjøre det i kirken? Før jeg ble omvendt, var jeg i militæret. Jeg valgte å lide for mitt land. Nå som jeg er kristen, velger jeg å lide for min Herre.

Kleskikk

Dette er det mest åpenbare, men også det mest oversette. Den verdslige kirken sier: «Det er hjertet som teller, så hvordan vi ser ut på utsiden spiller ingen rolle». Blir anabaptistene lurt av dette? Verden pleide å kle seg anstendig, men fjernsyn og Hollywood begynte å fremme en fokus på menneskekroppen. Sikkert ville ikke kirken følge Hollywood. Men hva er forskjellen—en kvinne i verden som åpenbart kler seg uanstendig, eller en kvinne i kirken kledd i en kappekjole som sitter tett og med en liten slapp hodebekledning hengende på baksiden av hodet? Det er liten forskjell, bortsett fra at den ene hevder å være kristen og den andre ikke gjør det. Kjære, verden ler av oss.

Så hvordan starter alt? Subtilt. Først fjerner man en fold her eller en rynke der, så begynner man å bruke litt mindre stoff, til slutt begynner man å kjøpe sterkere, skarpere farger. Menn stikker skjorten ut, bytter til jeans, så til skinny jeans, løsner noen knapper, lar håret vokse litt. Kjøp et par av de «kule» merkevarmeskoene, og en cowboyhatt. Djevelen er ingen tåpe. Hvis du slipper en frosk i kokende vann, vil den hoppe ut raskt. Hvis du koker vannet som inneholder frosken, vil den sakte koke ihjel. Er det for sent for oss å hoppe ut? Med Gud er alt mulig. Brødre og søstre, det er hjertet som teller; og hvis vi ønsker å se ut som verden, er vårt hjerte verdslig og trenger å renses—renses ved Jesu så mektige blod.

Fornøyelse

Dere har levd i lyst på jorden, og gjordt dere selv gemyttlige; dere har næret deres hjerter som i en slaktdag. Dere har fordømt og drept den rettferdige, og han gjør ikke motstand mot dere –Jakob 5:5-6.

Men det som falt blant torner, er de som har hørt; og når de har gått ut, kveles de av bekymringer og rikdom og livets lyst, og bærer ikke frukt til fullkommenhet –Lukas 8:14.

Viss også dette: I de siste dager skal det komme farlige tider. For menneskene skal være egenkjære, pengekjære, skrytende, hovmodige, spottere, ulydige mot foreldre, utakknemlige, ugudelige, uten naturlig hengivenhet, uten fordragelighet, ærekrenkere, ukontrollerte, grusomme, hatere av det gode, forrædere, hovmodige, oppblåste, mer tilhengere av nytelsen enn tilhengere av Gud, som har et skinn av gudsfrykt, men fornekter dens kraft. Deg vekk fra slike –2 Timoteus 3:1-5.

Når vi er overgitt til fornøyelser, skiller vi oss fra den lidelse vi er kalt til, og dermed fra den lønn som kommer av å lide.

Husk, når vi gir oss litt på en sak i vår generasjon, vil våre barn gå lenger med det. Når våre barn gleder seg over å gå på møte bare på grunn av volleyballkampen som er planlagt etterpå, er det ikke godt. Når de vil på misjonstur på grunn av fornøyelsene ved havet, er det ikke bra. Jeg sier ikke at disse tingene er onde, men når de blir hovedsaken, har vi et alvorlig problem. Gleder vi oss over å gjøre de ting Gud gleder seg over? Gleder vi oss over salmesang lenger? Gleder vi oss over å hjelpe de fattige? Hva med å besøke enker? Jeg tror at hvis fedrene har sine prioriteringer rette, og virkelig elsker å gjøre Guds ting selv om kjødet lider, så vil også våre barn (neste generasjon), som VI er ansvarlige for, gjøre det. Jeg sier ofte til folk at de ikke trenger å følge Jesus. De kan elske verden og livets lyst, men de kan ikke fortsette å sitte i vår kirke og late som om de er kristne. Folk vil kanskje si at det er for hardt, men jeg tror Jesus sa det samme: Jeg kjenner dine gjerninger, at du verken er kald eller varm. Hadde du vært enten kald eller varm! Men fordi du er lunken og verken varm eller kald, vil jeg spytte deg ut av min munn –Åpenbaringen 3:15-16.

Dette er ikke en komplett liste, for det finnes mange andre måter kirken driver mot verden på. Min bønn er at først kan vi se problemet, og for det andre, at vi kan ta tak i det. Husk at litt surdeig syrner hele deigen. (1 Korinterbrev 5)

Det pågår en kamp; mørkets rike presser på. Djevelen vet virkelig at han kun har kort tid. La oss ta et standpunkt, legge ned våre hvite flagg og ta opp våre sverd. La oss fjerne forrædere, verden og synden som har kommet inn i kirken. La oss rense kirken og kjempe den gode troskamp.

Hvordan stopper vi avdriften? Hvordan etterlater vi en trofast generasjon? Først må fedrene lære sine barn, og lederne i kirken må lære dem alle. De tidlige anabaptistene møttes så ofte de kunne, og det var vanligvis ute i været, i noen skoger et sted. Vår kirke her samles fem ganger i uken. Å kun møtes på søndager, tror jeg, viser hvor våre prioriteringer ligger.

Og han gav noen til å være apostler, noen profeter, noen evangelister, noen hyrder og lærere, For å utruste de hellige til tjenestegjerning, til oppbyggelse av Kristi kropp, inntil vi alle når fram til enheten i troen og i kunnskapen om Guds Sønn, til et fullt menneske, til målet for Kristi fullhet – Efeserne 4:11-13.

Det virker som om Gud ville gi oss lærere, pastorer, evangelister, profeter og apostler hvis vi ville bruke dem.

La oss gjøre dette personlig—det kan være områder av avdrift i mitt liv. Vi trenger å hjelpe hverandre før vi alle driver mot ødeleggelse. Kanskje kan vi holde oss, men vi må også bekymre oss for våre barn. Hvis vi kunne komme sammen og være ærlige med oss selv og med hverandre om hva Skriftene klart lærer, ville vi være mer forsiktige. Hvis vi kunne studere Guds Ord sammen, med åpne hjerter og sinn, tror jeg vi kunne styrke det som er igjen. Jeg tror at hvis vi falt på våre ansikter for Gud, ville han helbrede våre kirker. Må Gud velsigne oss alle med en dypere vandring med Ham.

I watched as a man attempted to cut a large sheet of plywood in half. He was talking with a few other men while he was cutting, and it seemed that he wasn’t too concerned about making the cut straight. I noticed that he continued to cut further and further from the line that he had scratched into the piece of plywood with a nail. After he was several inches off, one of his friends tried to point it out but he pretended to ignore him. He tried to casually guide the old handsaw back towards the line, while continuing to talk with the men, not making a big deal of it. Finally, after he was more than a foot off, he stopped. He knew now that he had a problem, a problem he could not fix.

I had to think, “Is this what we are doing as the church, the bride of Christ?” We are not too serious about drifting off the straight and narrow way; we allow things to come into our midst. We say, “It’s not a big deal, let’s not be critical.” But the longer we wait, the harder it will be to straighten out. At first it shocks us; later it becomes the new normal. How do we tell if we have drifted? It should be as easy as considering where we used to be, and comparing it that with where we are now, then evaluating the change with what the Bible teaches.

Since fighting against drift is not popular, men in the church don’t want to do it. Some people in our churches who are drifting towards the world have perfected a feel-good gospel. They go on and on about how close they are getting to Jesus, and how blessed they are, but their direction is clearly not in line with the teachings of Scripture. They’re headed towards the world.

There are others who don’t want the church to drift, yet they have their own problems—the love of money, covetousness, and a love of pleasure. No one says anything because it seems that nobody wants to hear. A popular response is, “Yes, I know it’s not good, but what can we do?” “All churches have problems.” Or “Yes, I would never allow that, but I don’t feel it’s in my place to speak up about it.” “It’s not for my family, but if others want to do that, its fine.”

We live in a “me” age. Everything is about me. The conservative, Anabaptist people are getting tangled up in social media, selfies, tweeting, Facebook, and you name it. We love ourselves to the extent that we talk, act, and dress in ways that draw attention to ourselves—we promote ourselves. We talk about looking good, feeling good, and living good. What happened to promoting Jesus? Remember, Jesus said: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25.

Why does it seem so hard to tell which direction we are going? If we are all about ourselves, then we are not all about Jesus. If we are into the latest fashions and the nicest cars, trucks, and houses, then we are not all about Jesus. We cannot indulge ourselves in pleasing the flesh, and still say we are Christians.

I was recently asked why some pastors lose their children to the world. In most cases, I believe it’s the same reason that many Anabaptists are losing their children to the kingdom of darkness—the fathers have lost a godly vision for their homes. They live a powerless life and allow the world to come in. Maybe they do not have television, but what about the internet? This still allows the influence of the world to come in. Also, Dad spends more time with his business and more time enjoying life than he does seeking the face of God.

Many Americans go on short-term missions. Many times, it seems that the youth who go want to hit the beach or some other pleasure and relaxation as soon as they get off the plane. Why? Because that’s what they are either taught or allowed to do back home—seek pleasure. They haven’t been taught to deny the flesh; they haven’t seen their parents deny the flesh. Some of us might be so far off the mark that we need to do like the carpenter at the beginning of this article—Humble ourselves and start over.

Husbands are pulling their unwilling wives into the world, wives are pushing their husbands into the world, and children are dragging their parents into the world. And unfortunately, since the modern church has thrown off all forms of discipline and structure, everyone can stay in the church and pollute it with their worldly ideas (at least as long as you smile and say you love Jesus.) Remember the Scriptures: If ye love me, keep my commandments –John 14:15. And, He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him –1 John 2:4.

Here are some areas of drift in the church.

Brotherly love

By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another –John 13:35.

People have visited our church and asked if we practice the holy kiss. I reply that we do; however, understanding the need to love one another comes first. Many churches are doing away with the holy kiss, which is clearly instructed in the Word. And it seems appropriate because they have stopped loving one another. I don’t believe we understand the importance of this topic—having love one for another. When our love causes us to suffer for one another, the world sees it. Often, the reason a brotherhood stops loving each other is because they are not in the fight “together” anymore. They have become independent.

Some of the greatest acts of showing love for one another have happened on the battlefield. Men have jumped on grenades, and they have jumped in front of bullets to save their comrades. Because they have fought together, they look out for each other. What if a soldier marching out to battle would notice a fellow soldier’s ammunition clip fall from his gun? What would he do? Would he remain quiet because his comrade might get mad? Or would he remain quiet because he knew that he had his own problems? No. He would help his brother. If ungodly men on the battlefield can practice this, why can’t God’s people do so in the church? Before I was converted, I was in the military. I chose to suffer for my country. Now that I’m a Christian, I now choose to suffer for my Lord.

Dress

This is the most obvious, but also the most overlooked. The worldly church says, “It’s the heart that counts, so how we appear on the outside doesn’t matter”. Are the Anabaptists falling for this? The world used to dress modestly, but television and Hollywood began to promote a focus on the human body. Surely the church wouldn’t follow Hollywood. But what is the difference—a woman of the world who is obviously dressed immodestly, or a woman of the church dressed with a cape dress that is form-fitting, and with a little covering hanging skimpily on the back of her head? There is little difference, except the one claims to be a Christian and the other one doesn’t. Dear ones, the world is laughing at us.

So how does it all start? Subtly. First remove a pleat here or a gather there, then start using a little less material, finally, start buying brighter bolder colors. The men untuck the shirt, switch to jeans, then skinny jeans, undo a few buttons, grow out the hair a little. Buy a pair of the “cool” name brand shoes, and a cowboy hat. The devil is no fool. If you drop a frog into boiling water, it will jump out quickly. If you boil the water that contains the frog, he will slowly cook to death. Is it too late for us to jump out? With God all things are possible. Brothers and sisters, it is the heart that counts; and if we desire to look like the world, our heart is worldly and needs to be cleaned—cleaned by the ever so powerful blood of Jesus.

Pleasure

Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter. Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you –James 5:5-6.

And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection –Luke 8:14.

This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

When we are given to pleasure, we separate ourselves from the sufferings we have been called to, therefore separating us from the reward received from suffering.

Remember, when we give in a little on any issue during our generation, our children will go farther with it. When our children enjoy going to church only because of the volleyball game that’s scheduled afterward, it’s not good. When they want to go on a mission trip because of the pleasures of the ocean, it’s not good. I’m not saying those things are bad, but when they become the focal point, we have a serious problem. Do we enjoy doing the things that God enjoys? Do we enjoy hymn sings anymore? Do we enjoy helping the poor? What about visiting the widows? I believe if the fathers have their priorities right, and they truly love doing the things of God even if the flesh suffers, then so will our children, (the next generation) for which WE are responsible. I often tell people that they don’t need to follow Jesus. They can love the world, and the pleasures of this life, but they cannot continue sitting in our church and pretend they are Christians. People might say that’s too harsh, but I believe Jesus said the same thing. I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:15-16.

This is not a complete list as there are many other ways that the church is drifting towards the world. My prayer is that, first, we could see the problem, and second, we could deal with it. Remember a little leaven leavens the lump. (1 Corinthians 5)

There is a battle that’s raging; the kingdom of darkness is pressing in. The devil truly knows he has but a short time. Let us make a stand, put down our white flags, and pick up our swords. Let us remove the traitors, the world, and the sin that has come into the church. Let us purify the church and fight the good fight of faith.

How do we stop the drift? How do we leave behind a faithful generation? First, the fathers need to teach their children, and the leaders in the church need to teach them all. The early Anabaptists met as many times as they could, and that was usually out in the weather, in some woods somewhere. Our church here meets five times a week. Meeting on Sundays only, I believe, shows where our priorities are.

And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ: – Ephesians 4:11-13.

It seems that God would give us teachers, pastors, evangelists, prophets, and apostles if we would use them.

Let’s make this personal—there could be areas of drift in my life. We need to help each other before we all drift into ruin. Maybe we can maintain, but we also need to be concerned about our children. If we could get together and be honest with ourselves and with one another about what the scriptures clearly teach, then we would be more careful. If we could study God’s Word together, with open hearts and minds, I believe we could strengthen that which remains. I believe if we would fall on our faces before God, He would heal our churches. May God bless us all in a deeper walk with Him.

Я наблюдал, как мужчина пытался распилить большой лист фанеры пополам. Он разговаривал с несколькими другими мужчинами во время пиления и, казалось, не слишком переживал о том, чтобы распил получился ровным. Я заметил, что он всё дальше и дальше уходил от линии, которую он поцарапал на фанере гвоздём. После того как он отступил на несколько дюймов, один из его друзей попытался указать ему на это, но он делал вид, что не замечает. Он пытался непринуждённо повернуть старую ручную пилу обратно к линии, продолжая разговаривать с мужчинами, не делая по этому поводу большого дела. Наконец, когда он ушёл более чем на фут, он остановился. Он теперь знал, что у него проблема, проблему, которую он не в силах исправить.

Мне пришлось подумать: «Не так ли мы поступаем как Церковь, невеста Христова?» Мы недостаточно серьёзно относимся к тому, чтобы не отбиваться от прямого и узкого пути; мы дозволяем вещам войти в нашу среду. Мы говорим: «Это не большая проблема, давайте не будем критиковать». Но чем дольше мы ждём, тем труднее будет выправить положение. Сначала это шокирует нас; позже это становится новой нормой. Как же нам понять, отбились ли мы? Это должно быть так же просто, как вспомнить, где мы были раньше, сравнить это с тем, где мы теперь, а затем оценить изменение с точки зрения учения Библии.

Поскольку борьба с отступлением непопулярна, люди в церкви не хотят этим заниматься. Некоторые в наших общинах, которые тянутся к миру, усовершенствовали благостную евангелию. Они неустанно говорят о том, как близко они становятся к Иисусу и как благословенны они, но их направление явно не соответствует учению Писания. Они направляются в мир.

Есть и другие, кто не хочет, чтобы церковь дрейфовала, но у них свои проблемы — любовь к деньгам, жадность и любовь к удовольствиям. Никто ничего не говорит, потому что кажется, что никому не хочется слушать. Популярный ответ: «Да, я знаю, что это плохо, но что мы можем поделать?» «У всех церквей есть проблемы». Или: «Да, я бы никогда этого не допустил, но не чувствую, что мне место высказываться об этом». «Это не про мою семью, но если другие хотят так делать, то пусть делают».

Мы живём в «я»-эпоху. Всё про меня. Консервативные анабаптистские люди путаются в социальных сетях, селфи, твитах, Facebook и во всём прочем. Мы любим себя настолько, что говорим, действуем и одеваемся так, чтобы привлекать к себе внимание — мы продвигаем самих себя. Мы говорим о том, как выглядеть хорошо, чувствовать себя хорошо и жить хорошо. Куда же делось продвижение Иисуса? Помните, Иисус сказал: Ибо всякий, кто хочет спасти свою жизнь, тот потеряет её; а кто потеряет жизнь мою ради, тот найдёт её –Matthew 16:25.

Почему так трудно понять, в каком направлении мы идём? Если всё про нас, то мы не про Иисуса. Если нам важна последняя мода и самые красивые машины, грузовики и дома, то мы не про Иисуса. Мы не можем потакать плоти и при этом утверждать, что мы христиане.

Недавно меня спросили, почему некоторые пасторы теряют своих детей для мира. В большинстве случаев я считаю, что причина та же, по которой многие анабаптисты теряют своих детей для царства тьмы — отцы потеряли богобоязненную картину для своих домов. Они ведут бесплодную жизнь и позволяют миру войти. Может, у них нет телевизора, но как насчёт интернета? Он по-прежнему приносит влияние мира. Также отец проводит больше времени с бизнесом и больше времени наслаждается жизнью, чем ищет лица Божьего.

Многие американцы ездят на краткосрочные миссии. Часто кажется, что молодёжь, отправляющаяся туда, хочет первым делом попасть на пляж или к какому-нибудь другому развлечению и отдыху, как только сойдёт с самолёта. Почему? Потому что им так либо учат, либо позволяют это дома — искать удовольствия. Им не учили отрекаться от плоти; они не видели, как их родители отказываются от плоти. Некоторые из нас могут быть так далеко от правды, что нам нужно сделать как плотник в начале этой статьи — смириться и начать заново.

Мужья тянут своих нежелающих жен в мир, жёны толкают своих мужей в мир, а дети волокут родителей в мир. И, к сожалению, поскольку современная церковь отбросила все формы дисциплины и структуры, каждый может оставаться в церкви и загрязнять её своими мирскими идеями (по крайней мере, пока ты улыбаешься и говоришь, что любишь Иисуса). Помните Писание: Если вы любите Меня, соблюдите Мои заповеди –John 14:15. И: Кто говорит: Я познал Его, и не соблюдает заповедей Его, тот лжец, и истины в нём нет –1 John 2:4.

Вот некоторые области дрейфа в церкви.

Братская любовь

По тому узнают все, что вы Мои ученики, если будете иметь любовь между собою –John 13:35.

Люди приходили в нашу церковь и спрашивали, практикуем ли мы святое поцелование. Я отвечаю, что да; однако сначала нужно понять необходимость любить друг друга. Многие церкви отказываются от святаго поцелования, что явно предписано в Слове. И это кажется уместным, потому что они перестали любить друг друга. Я не думаю, что мы понимаем важность этой темы — иметь любовь друг к другу. Когда наша любовь заставляет нас страдать друг за друга, мир это видит. Часто причина, по которой братство перестаёт любить друг друга, в том, что они больше не борются «вместе». Они стали независимыми.

Некоторые из величайших проявлений любви друг к другу происходили на поле боя. Люди прыгали на гранаты и вставали на пути пуль, чтобы спасти товарищей. Поскольку они сражались вместе, они заботились друг о друге. Что если солдат, отправляющийся в бой, заметит, что у товарища из ружья выпал магазин с патронами? Что он сделает? Останется ли он спокойным, потому что товарищ может рассердиться? Или промолчит, потому что у него самого свои проблемы? Нет. Он поможет брату. Если нечестивые люди на поле боя могут так поступать, почему не могут так поступать люди Божьи в церкви? До обращения я служил в армии. Я выбрал страдать за свою страну. Теперь, будучи христианином, я выбираю страдать за моего Господа.

Одежда

Это самый очевидный, но одновременно и наиболее игнорируемый вопрос. Мирская церковь говорит: «Сердце имеет значение, поэтому то, как мы выглядим снаружи, не имеет значения». Падают ли анабаптисты на это? Раньше мир одевался скромно, но телевидение и Голливуд начали продвигать акцент на человеческом теле. Конечно, церковь не последовала бы за Голливудом. Но в чём разница — женщина мира, явно одетая неподобающе, или женщина из церкви в платье с капюшоном, которое облегает фигуру, и с небольшой покрывалкой, небрежно повисшей на затылке? Разницы почти нет, кроме того, что одна именует себя христианкой, а другая нет. Дорогие, мир смеётся над нами.

И как же всё начинается? Тонко. Сначала убирают один складок или сборку здесь или там, затем начинают использовать немного меньше материала, в конце концов покупают яркие, более дерзкие цвета. Мужчины заправляют рубашку не внутрь, переходят на джинсы, потом на узкие джинсы, растёгивают пару пуговиц, отращивают волосы чуть длиннее. Покупают пару «крутых» брендовых ботинок и ковбойскую шляпу. Дьявол не дурак. Если бросить лягушку в кипящую воду, она быстро выпрыгнет. Если же воду нагревать постепенно, лягушка медленно сварится. Не поздно ли нам выпрыгнуть? С Богом всё возможно. Братья и сёстры, важно сердце; и если мы желаем выглядеть как мир, наше сердце мирское и нуждается в очищении — очищении мощнейшей кровью Иисуса.

Удовольствие

Вы жили в удовольствии на земле и предавались распутству; вы питали сердца ваши, словно в день убоя. Вы осуждали и убивали праведника, и он не противится вам –James 5:5-6.

А что упало среди терний, те, выслушавши, уходят и душатся в заботах, богатстве и похотях житейских и не приносят плода до совершенства –Luke 8:14.

Знай ещё, что в последние дни наступят времена тяжелые. Люди будут любителями самих себя, любителями денег, хвастунами, гордыми, богохульниками, непокорными родителям, неблагодарными, нечистыми, без естественной привязанности, вероломными, клеветниками, нестриманными, беспощадными, ненавидящими добро, предателями, безрассудными, надменными, любителями удовольствий более, нежели любителями Бога, имеющими вид благочестия, но силы его отрицающими; от таких отворачивайся –2 Timothy 3:1-5.

Когда мы предаёмся удовольствиям, мы отрываемся от тех страданий, к которым призваны, тем самым отрывая себя от награды, получаемой в страдании.

Помните: если мы немного уступаем в каком-либо вопросе в нашем поколении, наши дети пойдут дальше. Когда дети посещают церковь только ради волейбольной игры, запланированной после службы, это нехорошо. Когда они хотят поехать в миссию из‑за удовольствий океана, это нехорошо. Я не говорю, что эти вещи сами по себе плохи, но когда они становятся главным, у нас серьёзная проблема. Насколько мы любим дела, которые любит Бог? Насколько нам нравятся совместные пения гимнов? Насколько нам нравится помогать бедным? Что насчёт посещения вдов? Я верю, что если отцы имеют правильные приоритеты и действительно любят делать дела Божьи, даже если плоть страдает, то и наши дети (следующее поколение), за которых МЫ несём ответственность, будут так поступать. Я часто говорю людям, что им не обязательно следовать за Иисусом. Они могут любить мир и удовольствия этой жизни, но они не могут продолжать сидеть в нашей церкви и притворяться христианами. Люди могут сказать, что это слишком строго, но я верю, что Иисус сказал то же самое. Я знаю дела твои: ты ни холоден, ни горяч; о, коли бы ты был холоден или горяч. Итак, понеже ты тёпл, и ни холоден, ни горяч, извергну тебя из уст Моих –Revelation 3:15-16.

Это не исчерпывающий список, так как есть множество других способов, которыми церковь дрейфует к миру. Моя молитва, чтобы, во‑первых, мы увидели проблему, и, во‑вторых, чтобы мы с ней справились. Помните: малая закваска заквашивает всё тесто. (1 Corinthians 5)

Идёт битва; царство тьмы наступает. Дьявол действительно знает, что времени у него немного. Встанем, опустим наши белые флаги и возьмём мечи. Уберём предателей, мир и грех, которые вошли в церковь. Очистим церковь и будем вести добрую брань веры.

Как остановить дрейф? Как оставить верное поколение? Во‑первых, отцы должны научать своих детей, а лидеры в церкви должны учить всех. Ранние анабаптисты собирались как можно чаще, и это обычно было на открытом воздухе, в каких‑нибудь лесах. Наша церковь собирается здесь пять раз в неделю. Собираясь только по воскресеньям, я считаю, мы показываем, где наши приоритеты.

И Он поставил одних Апостолами, а одних пророками, а одних Евангелистами, а одних пастырями и учителями, для наставления святых на дело служения, для созидания Тела Христова, доколе мы все не придём в единство веры и в познание Сына Божия, в человека совершенного, в меру полного роста Христова: – Ephesians 4:11-13.

Кажется, Бог дал бы нам учителей, пастырей, евангелистов, пророков и апостолов, если бы мы их использовали.

Сделаем это личным — возможно, в моей жизни тоже есть области дрейфа. Нам нужно помогать друг другу, прежде чем мы все дрейфуем к гибели. Может, мы сможем удержаться, но нам также нужно заботиться о наших детях. Если бы мы могли собираться и быть честными с собой и друг с другом относительно того, чему ясно учат Писания, мы были бы более осмотрительны. Если бы мы могли вместе изучать Слово Божие с открытыми сердцами и умами, я верю, мы могли бы укрепить то, что осталось. Я верю, если бы мы пали ниц пред Богом, Он исцелил бы наши церкви. Да благословит нас всех Бог более глубокой жизнью с Ним.

That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling… –Ephesians 1:17-18.

We all have things we pursue in many aspects of our life. We all need to spend time fulfilling our responsibilities at work and at home. As Anabaptist people, we are known to possess a solid work ethic; but that is not all there is to living the Christian life. We may fellowship with likeminded believers from our church or community, but does our Christian life consist of anything more? Does practically living out our Christian life just mean being a member of our church and having personal devotions every day? Are we free to spend most of our day pursuing things that bring worldly gain? Perhaps we think that we need to spend some time as a volunteer or as a missionary in order to have more value in the Kingdom of Heaven.

What is purpose? Do you have purpose? Everyone has things they pursue, whether it is preparing themselves for a certain sport, pursuing a career, or devoting time to a certain hobby. An athlete spends many hours preparing himself for the goal he has set. An individual studying to become a doctor sacrifices many hours of his time with the goal of becoming a physician. What are the things you are pursuing, and do you have a specific goal in mind? More importantly, let’s examine whether the time we are investing in our pursuits now will bring an eternal return.

God has given each of us a responsibility

In Luke 19 is the parable of the nobleman giving his servants talents to invest. Consider the charge he gave his servants in verse 13. He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return. And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come –Luke 19:12-13.

This parable applies to each one of us. Each of us has different responsibilities, from filling our responsibilities at home, to administrative roles in a place of business. While we do not all own equal responsibilities, we have all been given “talents” to use. We all have a place to fill. We should be making the best of the resources we have been given to invest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

Back to my question, “Does living our Christian life just mean being a member of our church and having personal devotions once a day?” If the Lord has given each of us resources to invest, then we need to consider what we are doing with the time we are given every day. Often, we can budget plenty of time pursuing materialistic things such as hunting, sports, vehicles, etc. While all these things can be useful and healthy, do the things we are pursuing have eternal gain? We don’t seem to be afraid to devote hours of our time on our latest project, however it seems we have a hard time finding a place in our schedule for God’s work.

Personal responsibility

It is easy to have the mindset that, unless we are sacrificing our time in some voluntary capacity in a mission-oriented place, then there is not a lot more than can be done for the Kingdom of Heaven. Is that the reality though? Like the servants in the parable, we have each been given resources that we need to “occupy till the Lord returns”. The Lord has placed each of us in a unique place to serve in His kingdom, whether it is at home, on the job, or on the mission field. We have opportunities around us to exercise those gifts and show the love of Christ. The consideration should be whether I am actually seeing those opportunities or missing them because I am not looking for them. The more time we prioritize serving His Kingdom, the more we will see the needs around us. Remember, there are people around us every day that we can influence for God.

Recognizing our opportunities

Some time ago, I had a coworker come to my office and ask me a simple technical question. I was able to answer the question and work resumed as normal. But I had to wonder why he left the shop and came to me. He was within talking distance of multiple other individuals that would have been able to answer his question. Looking back, I realized that I had an opportunity to provide a listening ear and some caring words for this individual. He was facing some serious personal and relational challenges in life, and he needed someone who cared for him. I realized that there was probably a deeper reason he went out of his way to find an answer to his question. Was I the only one there that could have listened and shared with him? Certainly not. It was an opportunity for me. I could have chosen to be annoyed at him because he was taking up my time for something that someone else could have helped him with. But the question is—did I have the humility to recognize that it was an opportunity for me to reach out to him?

Where do I start?

We all have opportunities around us to exercise our talents. Jesus said: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men –Matthew 5:13. Salt always affects its environment no matter what it is used for. If we are compared to salt, then we should be affecting the environment around us all the time. Our Christian life then becomes more than simply going to church or spending some personal time praying and reading the Bible.

Start by asking God to help you see areas where you can serve others in everyday life. You have an opportunity to impact the lives of those around you. It might be your family, coworkers, customers, or people you meet while away from home. The point is, you have the opportunity around you to offer someone help, to encourage them, or to give them a hand. Are you making the best of those opportunities?

Another thing you should do is evaluate your personal life and the time you spend doing other activities. Are there things you are doing which take up your time and that have no benefit in the Kingdom of God? Maybe God has given you a gift that you are hiding instead of using to invest in His Kingdom. Do you spend time praying and seeking God’s will for your life? Do you spend time studying the Word of God? When our personal time with God becomes a higher priority for us, then our time spent pursuing God’s Kingdom will also become a higher priority. Is there sin hindering you from living out your Christian life? Confess it. Repent of it. Then… Go, and sin no more!

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:1-2.

In the beginning of the article, I asked what you are pursuing. Does your life show that fulfilling God’s will is your highest priority, or is there something else that takes that spot? Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost –Romans 15:13. There are people around us that do not have the hope of a better, future life to strive for that we do. It is up to us to share that with others. Ask God for His Spirit to guide you and show you your opportunities. You cannot sit back and wait for the opportunities to come to you; you need to go find them. Go light your world!

Dat die God van onse Here Jesus Christus, die Vader van die heerlikheid, julle die gees van wysheid en openbaring in die kennis van Hom mag gee: dat die oë van julle verstand verlig word; dat julle mag weet wat die hoop van sy roeping is… – Efesiërs 1:17-18.

Ons het almal sake waarna ons in verskeie aspekte van ons lewe nastreef. Ons moet almal tyd bestee om ons verantwoordelikhede by die werk en by die huis te vervul. As Anabapistiese mense staan ons bekend as iemand met ’n sterk werksetiek; maar dit is nie alles wat die Christelike lewe behels nie. Ons kan gemeente met ewegesinde gelowiges uit ons kerk of gemeenskap hê, maar bestaan ons Christelike lewe uit meer as dit? Beteken dit prakties om ons Christelike lewe uit te leef bloot om ’n lid van ons kerk te wees en persoonlike godsdienstigheid elke dag te beoefen? Is ons vry om die grootste deel van ons dag te spandeer aan sake wat wêreldlike wins bring? Dalk dink ons ons moet ’n rukkie as ’n vrywilliger of as ’n sendeling dien om meer waarde te hê in die Koninkryk van die hemel.

Wat is doel? Het jy doel? Almal het sake waarna hulle nastreef, hetsy om voor te berei vir ’n sport, om ’n loopbaan na te streef, of om tyd aan ’n stokperdjie te gee. ’n Sportman bestee baie ure wat hy voorberei vir die doel wat hy gestel het. Iemand wat studeer om dokter te word, offer baie ure van sy tyd op met die doel om ’n geneesheer te word. Wat is die dinge waarna jy nastreef, en het jy ’n spesifieke doel voor oë? Meer belangrik, laat ons ondersoek of die tyd wat ons nou in ons nastrewings belê, ’n ewige opbrengs sal bring.

God het aan elk van ons ’n verantwoordelikheid gegee

In Lukas 19 is die gelykenis van die edelman wat sy dienaars talente gee om te belê. Oorweeg die opdrag wat hy aan sy dienaars gegee het in vers 13. En Hy het gesê: ‘’n Bepaalde edelman het in ’n ver land gegaan om vir hom ’n koninkryk te ontvang en terug te keer. En hy het sy tien dienaars geroep en hulle tien pond gegee, en gesê: „Bestuur totdat Ek kom.”’ – Lukas 19:12-13.

Die gelykenis geld vir elk van ons. Almal van ons het verskillende verantwoordelikhede, van die vervulling van ons pligte by die huis tot administratiewe rolle in ’n besigheid. Al besit ons nie almal gelyke verantwoordelikhede nie, is ons almal gegee ‘‘talente’’ om te gebruik. Ons het almal ’n plek om te vervul. Ons behoort die beste te maak van die hulpbronne wat ons gegee is om in die Koninkryk van die hemel te belê.

Terug na my vraag: “Beteken dit om ons Christelike lewe te leef bloot dat ons ’n lid van ons kerk is en persoonlike stiltetyd een keer per dag het?” As die Here elk van ons hulpbronne gegee het om te belê, dan moet ons oorweeg wat ons met die tyd doen wat ons elke dag gegee word. Dikwels kan ons baie tyd begroot om materialistiese dinge na te jaag soos jag, sport, voertuie, ens. Al kan al daardie dinge nuttig en gezond wees, het die sake waarna ons nastreef ewige wins? Ons lyk nie bang om ure van ons tyd aan ons nuutste projek toe te wy nie, maar dit lyk asof ons moeilik ’n plek in ons skedule vir God se werk kan vind.

Persoonlike verantwoordelikheid

Dit is maklik om die ingesteldheid te hê dat, tensy ons ons tyd opoffer in ’n vrywillige hoedanigheid op ’n sendinggerigte plek, daar nie veel meer vir die Koninkryk van die hemel gedoen kan word nie. Is daardie egter die werklikheid? Soos die dienaars in die gelykenis, is ons elk gegee hulpbronne wat ons moet “bestuur totdat die Here terugkom”. Die Here het elk van ons in ’n unieke plek geplaas om in Sy koninkryk te dien, hetsy by die huis, by die werk, of op die sendingveld. Ons het geleenthede rondom ons om daardie gawes uit te oefen en die liefde van Christus te betoon. Die oorweging behoort te wees of ek werklik daardie geleenthede sien of dit mis omdat ek nie daarna soek nie. Hoe meer tyd ons prioriteit gee aan die diens van Sy Koninkryk, hoe meer sal ons die behoeftes rondom ons sien. Onthou, daar is mense rondom ons elke dag wat ons vir God kan beïnvloed.

Ons geleenthede herken

’n Geruime tyd gelede het ’n kollega my kantoor toe gekom en my ’n eenvoudige tegniese vraag gevra. Ek kon die vraag beantwoord en die werk het soos gewoonlik voortgegaan. Maar ek het my afgevra hoekom hy die Winkel verlaat en na my toe gekom het. Hy was binne geselsafstand van verskeie ander persone wat sy vraag sou kon beantwoord. As ek terugdink, het ek besef dat ek ’n geleentheid gehad het om ’n luisterende oor en ’n paar sorgsame woorde vir hierdie persoon te bied. Hy het ernstige persoonlike en relationele uitdagings in die lewe ervaar, en hy het iemand nodig gehad wat omgee vir hom. Ek het besef daar was waarskynlik ’n dieper rede waarom hy moeite gedoen het om ’n antwoord te kry. Was ek die enigste een daar wat na hom kon luister en met hom kon deel? Sekerlik nie. Dit was ’n geleentheid vir my. Ek kon gekies het om geïrriteerd te wees omdat hy my tyd geneem het vir iets wat iemand anders sou kon help. Maar die vraag is—het ek die nederigheid gehad om te herken dat dit ’n geleentheid vir my was om na hom uit te reik?

Waar begin ek?

Ons het almal geleenthede rondom ons om ons talente uit te oefen. Jesus het gesê: Julle is die sout van die aarde; maar as die sout sy geur verloor het, waarmee sal dit weer gesout word? Dit is sterker niks meer werd as om weggegooi te word en deur mense vertrap te word. – Matteus 5:13. Sout beïnvloed sy omgewing altyd, maak nie saak waarvoor dit gebruik word nie. As ons vergelyk word met sout, behoort ons die omgewing rondom ons altyd te beïnvloed. Ons Christelike lewe word dan meer as bloot kerk toe gaan of ’n bietjie persoonlike tyd spandeer om te bid en die Bybel te lees.

Begin deur God te vra om jou te help areas te sien waar jy ander in die alledaagse lewe kan dien. Jy het ’n geleentheid om die lewens van diegene rondom jou te beïnvloed. Dit kan jou familie wees, kollegas, kliënte, of mense wat jy teëkom wanneer jy van die huis af weg is. Die punt is, jy het die geleentheid rondom jou om iemand hulp te bied, hulle aan te moedig of ’n hand te reik. Maak jy die beste van daardie geleenthede?

’n Ander ding wat jy behoort te doen, is om jou persoonlike lewe en die tyd wat jy aan ander aktiwiteite bestee te evalueer. Is daar dinge wat jy doen wat jou tyd opneem en wat geen voordeel in God se Koninkryk bied nie? Miskien het God jou ’n gawe gegee wat jy wegsteek in plaas daarvan om dit te gebruik om in Sy Koninkryk te belê. Bestee jy tyd aan gebed en om God se wil vir jou lewe te soek? Bestee jy tyd aan die studie van God se Woord? Wanneer ons persoonlike tyd met God ’n hoër prioriteit vir ons word, sal ons ook meer prioriteit gee aan tyd wat ons spandeer om God se Koninkryk na te jaag. Is daar ’n sonde wat jou verhinder om jou Christelike lewe uit te leef? Bely dit. Bekeer jou daarvan. Dan… Gaan, en sondig nie meer nie!

En aangesien ons so ’n groot skare getuies rondom ons het, laat ons alle omweg en die sonde wat ons so maklik innig omvou, afwerp, en laat ons met volharding die wedloop hardloop wat voor ons lê, en al die tyd op Jesus aansien, die Beginner en Bevollinder van ons geloof; wat, ter wille van die vreugde wat voor Hom gestel was, die kruis verduur het en die smaad verag het, en is gaan sit aan die regterhand van die troon van God. – Hebreërs 12:1-2.

Aan die begin van die artikel het ek gevra waarna jy nastreef. Wys jou lewe dat om God se wil te vervul jou hoogste prioriteit is, of is daar iets anders wat daardie plek inneem? En die God van die hoop vul julle met alle vreugde en vrede in die geloof, sodat julle mag oorvloed in die hoop, deur die krag van die Heilige Gees. – Romeine 15:13. Daar is mense rondom ons wat nie die hoop op ’n beter, toekomstige lewe het om na te streef soos ons nie. Dit lê by ons om dit met ander te deel. Vra God vir Sy Gees om jou te lei en jou jou geleenthede te wys. Jy kan nie terugsit en wag dat die geleenthede na jou toe kom nie; jy moet uitgaan en hulle gaan soek. Gaan, lig jou wêreld!

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

Når vi ser utover gatene av hjem rundt oss, sørger vi når vi får øye på én kristen tragedie etter en annen. Nesten enhver kristen har nære slektninger som har opplevd skilsmisse, et opprørsk barn eller anstrengte ekteskapelige forhold. Kanskje roper vi til Gud og undrer oss over hvorfor det er slik, for dette er sannelig ikke Hans plan. Her ser vi apostelen Paulus ta fram et forbløffende prinsipp som er lite forstått og enda mindre brukt — et helliget hjem. Det er det enhver oppriktig troende ønsker og søker, men få greier å fatte. Kristen tro er ikke et stempel som automatisk kloner avkom i samme ånd. Likevel må Skriften være sann, og det må virkelig finnes en helliggjørende effekt som en sann troende bringer inn i et hjem. Dette er ingen garanti for at den vantro ektefellen eller barna i foreningen blir frelst, men når en troende mann eller kvinne handler i samsvar med Skriften og Guds Ånd, vil den innvirkningen de har på hjemmet tillate Guds kraft å være synlig, og en nådens vei blir utøst inn i livsbanen for alle som bor der.

Vår maktesløshet skyldes ikke mangel på Guds kraft, men fordi vår svake forståelse er infisert og infiltrert av påvirkningene fra denne verden. Tro på Gud alene er uvegerlig en mektig kraft, mens tro injisert av menneskelig resonnement og utålmodighet knapt vil vise seg mer effektiv enn Abrahams og Hagar sine forsøk på å frambringe et hellig og helliget barn.

Hva er det da som helliger hjemmet? Overfladisk iakttagelse vil merke at det ikke er nok bare å være en troende for å få det til. Å hellige er å gjøre rent og hellig. Det er en prosess av filtrering og en atskillelse fra det som er uren for å bringe større renhet til objektet som helliges. Fariseerne forstod prinsippet godt. De brukte mange strenge timer på å ta hensyn til utallige små detaljer for å gjøre sine kar hellige. Likevel mislyktes de dyptgående.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

Hvor tåpelig det ville være for en mann å vaske bare utsiden av en kopp, som skal sees, og å la innsiden være skitten, som skal brukes. Likevel finnes det dem som bare unngår de skandaløse synder — de som ville ødelegge ryktet deres blant mennesker — men som likevel tillater seg stolthet og moralsk forfall i sitt hjerte. Det er dette som gjør dem avskyelige for den rene og hellige Gud. Slik er det når en mann eller kvinne søker å rense sitt hjem ved overfladisk vask. Fariseiske forsøk på å rote frem og fjerne overfladiske detaljer og inkonsekvenser fra livene til deres ektefelle og barn, for å hellige dem, er som regel fruktløse.

Uansett hvor kvikkøyd de er i andre ting; Kristus kaller dem blinde. I Kristi vurdering er de som ikke kjenner ondskapen i sine egne hjerter — de som ikke ser, og ikke hater, den hemmelige synd som ligger der — fremmede for helliggjørelsen. Selv-uvitenhet er den mest skammelige og skadelige uvitenhet. Regelen er: «Rens først det som er innenfor, for å bli renset fra åndens urenhet.» Fordervede affekter og tilbøyeligheter, de skjulte lyster som ligger i sjelen, usett og uobserverbart, disse må først gjenkjennes, avdødes og undertrykkes. Hvis det tas behørig omsorg om det, vil utsiden i forlengelsen også bli ren. Ytre motiver og påskjønnelser kan holde utsiden ren, mens innsiden forblir skitten; men hvis fornyet helliggjørende nåde gjør innsiden ren, vil det ha en varig og dyp innflytelse på utsiden, for det styrende prinsipp er innenfor. Hvis hjertet blir godt bevart, er alt i orden, …for av det utgår livets kilder –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Her taler Peter om at en hustru kan vinne sin mann med den riktige velvillighet som nevnes i Korinter. Selv om hun ikke har en ubetinget garanti for å helliggjøre sin mann, vil hun uten den åpenbart ha liten framgang. Eunike var en jødisk kvinne som ved å ta imot troen på Kristus fant seg i et ulikt ok med en greker. Vi leser at oppriktig tro først ble virket i hennes mor Lois, og det påvirket Eunike. Dette igjen hadde en helliggjørende virkning på den unge Timoteus, som da ble gjort rede for Herrens tjeneste. Vi har ingen beretning om at hans far ble utadd til troen, men man kan bare forestille seg den indre uro i brystet til denne unge jødisk-kvinnelige moren mens hun ærbødig hedret sin husbond og ikke omskar sin sønn, men heller overga ham til bønn. Her kommer vi til den andre vitale dimensjonen av hjemmets helliggjørelse. Selv om hun ikke var styrket til å lære sin mann, hadde hun tilsynelatende vunnet hans respekt nok til å få lære sin sønn i hjemmet. Dette gjorde hun nitidig… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

Når hjertet til den troende blir tatt hånd om først, faller hjemmets synlige dimensjoner på plass etter hvert. Verdslige påvirkninger har liten appell for den gryende Guds barn. Guds Ord må få sin fulle plass når det deles med barna så vel som de voksne, for det er nyttig til helliggjørelse. En ektemann skal vaske sin kone og sine barn (så vel som seg selv) ved å forvalte Guds Ord slik at han kan helliggjøre og rense sitt hjem.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

Når Guds Ord får full autoritet i hjemmet, blir det det styrende prinsipp som hjemmet opererer rundt. Det må få lov til å filtrere ut massemedienes påvirkning og alle onde kommunikasjoners krefter, som vil ødelegge gode skikker.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individer i hjemmet vil kanskje ikke alltid sette pris på den veiledningen de får fra det, men de må underordne seg det, og som regel gjør de det innstendig. De fleste av oss har mottatt veiledning fra våre foreldre som vi ikke satte pris på da, men som vi år senere har kommet til å forstå velsignelsen ved deres lederskap. Lederskap som ikke leder, uttrykker ikke kjærlighet, og vil etterlate hjemmet uhelliget og dets medlemmer frakoblet. Selv om det er temmelig ukomfortabelt og upraktisk å be barn om å gjøre uten det andre deltar i, blir de ikke helliget ved å følge sine jevnaldrende, men heller ved sannheten. For oss som foreldre finnes det ingen større glede enn å vite at våre barn vandrer i sannheten. Likeså finnes det ingen større glede for dem enn å vandre i den. Daglige familiegudstjenester er en samlende kraft i hjemmet som er sentral og integrert for hjemmets helliggjørelse. Vi tør ikke unnskylde den autoritet vi gir Ordet, heller ikke slakke på bruken av det. Det er et feilaktig evangelium å tro at sjeler blir kvalt når de holdes til de befalingene som finnes i det.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Kristus, som hodet for sitt hjem, brukte ingen kompliserte midler for å helliggjøre sine barn. Hans liv viste en konstant bevaring av seg selv i Guds kjærlighet gjennom tro og bønn, og forvaltningen av Guds Ord for dem omkring Ham. Til tider snublet de i det, strevde innvendig, og misforsto Ham, men den bevarende kraft hvilte ikke på laurbær av overtalende ord, sta kraft, morsomme aktiviteter eller forstandig resonnement.

Selv om et hjem fra tid til annen må bruke disse midlene, bærer de i seg selv ikke den helliggjørende kraften. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.
