That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling… –Ephesians 1:17-18.

우리는 삶의 여러 측면에서 추구하는 것들이 있습니다. 직장과 가정에서의 책임을 다하는 데 시간을 할애해야 합니다. 아나뱁티스트 사람들로서 우리는 단단한 직업 윤리를 지닌 것으로 알려져 있지만, 그것이 기독교인의 삶의 전부는 아닙니다. 우리는 교회나 공동체에서 뜻을 같이하는 신자들과 교제할 수 있지만, 우리 그리스도인의 삶이 그것으로 전부일까요? 기독교인의 삶을 실제로 사는 것이 단지 우리 교회의 구성원이 되고 매일 개인 경건을 갖는 것만을 의미할까요? 세속적 이익을 가져다주는 일들을 하루의 대부분을 추구하는 데 자유로워도 될까요? 어쩌면 우리는 천국에서 더 큰 가치를 얻으려면 자원봉사자나 선교사로서 시간을 좀 더 써야 한다고 생각할지도 모릅니다.

목적이란 무엇입니까? 당신에게 목적이 있습니까? 누구나 특정 스포츠를 준비하거나, 직업을 추구하거나, 특정 취미에 시간을 바치는 등 추구하는 것이 있습니다. 운동선수는 자신이 세운 목표를 위해 많은 시간을 준비에 쏟습니다. 의사가 되기 위해 공부하는 사람은 의사가 되겠다는 목표를 가지고 많은 시간을 희생합니다. 당신은 어떤 것을 추구하고 있으며, 특정한 목표가 있습니까? 더 중요한 것은, 지금 우리가 추구하는 것들에 투자하고 있는 시간이 영원한 열매를 가져다줄 것인지 검토해 보자는 것입니다.

하나님은 우리 각자에게 책임을 주셨다

누가복음 19장에는 귀족이 종들에게 달란트를 맡겨 투자하게 한 비유가 있습니다. 그가 종들에게 준 명령을 13절에서 생각해 보십시오. 이에 가로되 한 사람 귀국할 새 자기 나라를 얻고자 먼 나라로 가니 내 일이 끝날 때까지 그들에게 맡겨 두라 하고 열 사람을 불러 열 달란트를 주고 가라 명하여 이르되 내게 올 때까지 장사하라 하니라 –누가복음 19:12-13.

이 비유는 우리 각자에게 적용됩니다. 우리 각자는 가정에서의 책임을 다하는 것부터 사업장의 관리적 역할에 이르기까지 서로 다른 책임을 가지고 있습니다. 우리 모두가 동일한 책임을 가진 것은 아니지만, 우리는 모두 사용해야 할 “달란트”를 받았습니다. 우리 각자 채워야 할 자리가 있습니다. 우리는 천국을 위해 투자하기 위해 주어진 자원을 최대한 잘 활용해야 합니다.

다시 질문으로 돌아가 보겠습니다. “기독교인의 삶이 단지 우리 교회의 구성원이 되고 하루에 한 번 개인 경건을 갖는 것만을 의미하는가?” 주께서 우리 각자에게 투자할 자원을 주셨다면, 우리는 매일 주어진 시간을 가지고 무엇을 하고 있는지 고려해야 합니다. 종종 우리는 사냥, 스포츠, 차량 등과 같은 물질적인 것들을 추구하는 데 많은 시간을 배분할 수 있습니다. 이런 모든 것들이 유익하고 건전할 수는 있지만, 우리가 추구하는 것들이 영원한 유익을 가져다주고 있습니까? 우리는 최신 프로젝트에 몇 시간씩 기꺼이 투자하는 데에는 주저하지 않는 듯하지만, 정작 하나님의 일에 쓸 시간을 스케줄에서 찾는 것은 어려워하는 것 같습니다.

개인적 책임

선교 지향적인 장소에서 어떤 자원봉사적 희생을 하지 않는 한 천국을 위해 더 이상 할 수 있는 일이 많지 않다는 사고방식을 갖기 쉽습니다. 그러나 그것이 현실일까요? 비유 속 종들처럼, 우리 각자는 주께서 돌아오실 때까지 “장사하라”는 자원을 받았습니다. 주님은 우리 각자를 가정에서든 직장에서든 선교 현장이든 그분의 나라에서 섬기도록 독특한 자리(위치)에 두셨습니다. 우리는 주신 은사를 행사하고 그리스도의 사랑을 보여줄 기회들을 주변에서 가집니다. 문제는 내가 실제로 그런 기회를 보고 있는가, 아니면 찾지 않기 때문에 놓치고 있는가 하는 점입니다. 우리가 그분의 나라를 섬기는 것을 더 우선순위에 둘수록, 우리는 주변의 필요를 더 많이 보게 될 것입니다. 기억하십시오, 매일 주변에 우리가 하나님을 위해 영향 줄 수 있는 사람들이 있습니다.

기회를 인식하기

얼마 전에 한 동료가 사무실로 와서 간단한 기술적 질문을 한 적이 있습니다. 나는 그 질문에 답할 수 있었고 일은 평소대로 재개되었습니다. 그러나 나는 왜 그가 작업장을 떠나 나에게 왔는지 의아해했습니다. 그는 근처에 있었고 그 질문에 답할 수 있는 다른 사람들이 여럿 있었습니다. 돌이켜보니 나는 그 사람에게 귀 기울여 주고 다정한 말을 건넬 기회를 가졌다는 것을 깨달았습니다. 그는 삶에서 심각한 개인적·관계적 문제에 직면해 있었고, 누군가의 관심이 필요했습니다. 내가 그가 일부러 내게로 와서 질문을 찾으러 온데에는 더 깊은 이유가 있었을 것이라고 깨달았습니다. 그를 들어주고 나눌 수 있는 사람은 나만이었을까요? 물론 아닙니다. 그것은 나에게 주어진 기회였습니다. 나는 누군가 다른 사람이 도와줄 수 있는 일을 내 시간을 빼앗는다고 짜증을 냈을 수도 있습니다. 그러나 문제는—그것이 내가 그에게 손을 내밀 기회였다는 것을 인식할 겸손이 있었느냐 하는 것입니다.

어디서 시작할 것인가?

우리 주변에는 우리가 가진 은사를 행사할 수 있는 기회들이 있습니다. 예수님은 말씀하셨습니다: 너희는 세상의 소금이니 소금이 만일 그 맛을 잃으면 무엇으로 짜게 하리요 후에는 아무 쓸데없어 다만 밖에 버려져 사람들에게 밟힐 뿐이니라 –마태복음 5:13. 소금은 그것이 어떤 용도로 사용되든 항상 그 환경에 영향을 미칩니다. 우리가 소금과 비유된다면 우리는 항상 우리 주변 환경에 영향을 미쳐야 합니다. 그러므로 우리의 그리스도인 생활은 단순히 교회에 가거나 개인적으로 기도하고 성경을 읽는 것 이상의 것이 됩니다.

먼저 하나님께 일상생활 속에서 다른 사람을 섬길 수 있는 영역을 보게 해 달라고 기도하십시오. 당신은 주변 사람들의 삶에 영향을 줄 기회를 가지고 있습니다. 그것은 당신의 가족일 수도 있고, 직장 동료나 고객일 수도 있으며, 집을 떠나 만난 사람들일 수도 있습니다. 요점은 당신 주변에 누군가에게 도움을 제공하거나 격려하거나 손을 내밀 수 있는 기회가 있다는 것입니다. 당신은 그 기회를 잘 활용하고 있습니까?

또 하나 해야 할 일은 자신의 개인 생활과 다른 활동에 소비하는 시간을 평가하는 것입니다. 당신의 시간을 차지하고 있으나 하나님의 나라에 이익이 되지 않는 일들이 있습니까? 어쩌면 하나님이 주신 은사를 감추고 있어 그것을 가지고 그분의 나라에 투자하지 않을지도 모릅니다. 당신은 자신의 삶을 위해 하나님의 뜻을 구하며 기도하는 시간을 갖고 있습니까? 하나님의 말씀을 공부하는 시간을 갖고 있습니까? 우리의 개인적 하나님과의 시간이 더 높은 우선순위가 될 때, 하나님 나라를 추구하는 데 드리는 시간도 더 높은 우선순위가 될 것입니다. 당신의 그리스도인 생활을 방해하는 죄가 있습니까? 고백하십시오. 회개하십시오. 그리고… 가서 다시는 죄를 짓지 마십시오!

이러므로 우리도 이처럼 많은 증인들이 둘러싼 것을 보았으니 모든 무거운 것과 얽매이기 쉬운 죄를 벗어 버리고 인내로서 우리 앞에 놓인 경주를 하자자 바라보자 우리의 믿음의 주되 온전케 하시는 이인 예수를 바라며 그가 앞에 두신 즐거움을 위하여 십자가를 참으사 부끄러움을 게이치 아니하시고 하나님의 보좌 우편에 앉으시니라 –히브리서 12:1-2.

글 머리에서 당신에게 무엇을 추구하는지 물었습니다. 당신의 삶은 하나님의 뜻을 이루는 것이 가장 높은 우선순위임을 보여 줍니까, 아니면 그 자리를 차지한 다른 것이 있습니까? 소망의 하나님이 너희를 모든 기쁨과 평강으로 믿음 안에서 충만케 하사 성령의 능력으로 소망이 넘치게 하시기를 원하노라 –로마서 15:13. 우리 주변에는 우리처럼 더 나은 미래의 삶에 대한 소망이 없어 애쓰지 못하는 사람들이 있습니다. 그것을 다른 사람들과 나누는 일은 우리에게 달려 있습니다. 하나님께 그분의 영으로 너희를 인도하여 기회를 보이시도록 구하십시오. 기회가 저절로 여러분에게 오기를 가만히 앉아 기다릴 수는 없습니다; 여러분이 나가서 그것들을 찾아야 합니다. 나가서 너희의 세상에 빛을 비치십시오!

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Hilsener i kristen kjærlighet til alle. I dette nummeret av bladet (sommer 2023)… artikkelen om kirkens historie fokuserer på bibelsk profeti knyttet til endetiden og noen ulike måter som bestemte elementer i kirken over årene kom på avveie fra den bibelske undervisningen slik den gjaldt deres dagligliv. I sin artikkel forsøker Donny Brechbill, som sammen med sin kone underviser flere ekteskapsseminarer hvert år, å spisse inn på et utfordrende tema—noen av de grunnleggende problemene de ser hos kvinner som sliter i kirken. Lee Rufener tar en ukomplisert tilnærming i sitt forsøk på å dele noe ekspositorisk undervisning om praktiske måter å ha et helliget hjem på. Vi har en ny forfatter for søstrene denne gangen som deler en byrde på sitt hjerte—å innpode Guds Ord i neste generasjons hjerter.

Pluss flere interessante emner. Nyt lesningen.

Hvis du blir oppbygd eller oppmuntret av innholdet fra noen av forfatterne, ville det være en velsignelse for oss om du svarer oss per post eller e-post. Vi sender dette videre til våre skribenter til deres gagn.

Nylig grublet jeg over temaet forandring. Som jeg tidligere har skrevet, har vi gått gjennom en god del forandringer som familie. I løpet av de siste 1 til 2 årene flyttet vi til et annet bosted, jeg fikk en ny jobb, og endelig, takk og lov, har jeg for det meste blitt frisk fra de fleste langtidsvirkningene av covid. En spesiell takk til hver av dere som har bedt for helsen min.

Mens jeg satt stille og mimret, ble jeg overrasket over alle tingene som har endret seg i de over 40 årene jeg kan huske. (Selv om jeg er over 50 husker jeg egentlig ikke mye fra de tidligste årene av livet mitt.)

Som gutt kjørte jeg rundt i kjøretøy som ikke hadde sikkerhetsbelter og definitivt ingen kollisjonsputer. Da begge disse «livrednings»-innretningene først ble introdusert, husker jeg godt de mange diskusjonene om hvorvidt de virkelig reddet liv eller om det motsatte var sant. Alle kjøretøy var tidligere bakhjulsdrift eller firehjulsdrift. Hvor underlig det virket da de første forhjulsdrevne bilene begynte å dukke opp. Nå har vi hybridbiler med et press mot helt elektriske biler.

For over førti år siden hadde de fleste bønder bensindrevne traktorer med forgasser eller dieseltraktorer med manuelt drevne innsprøytningspumper. I dag er de fleste traktorer utstyrt med en datamaskin og tilsynelatende mil med ledninger og elektronikk. Den gang kunne de fleste bønder vedlikeholde eller reparere sitt eget utstyr; nå er det behov for diagnostiske maskiner og spesialverktøy som koster mye penger og tar mange timer å lære å bruke. Dette gjør at de fleste bønder er avhengige av ekspertisen til spesialiserte reparatører, som også koster mye penger.

Så var det covid. Det var en stressende tid. Har du lagt merke til hva som har forandret seg under, etter eller som et resultat av covid? Når jeg omgås andre, sier rutinemessig noen at dette eller hint er annerledes siden covid. Er det bare jeg, eller er almenheten siden covid mindre vennlig og mer privat i sine interaksjoner? La oss granske våre egne samhandlinger for å sikre at vi fortsatt er Guds «lys» og «salt» for denne mørke verden, og at vi ikke mister vår «saltighet». Dessuten er det hjelp-ønskes-skilt overalt. Hvorfor? Det virker for meg som om covid har svekket den lille arbeidsetikken som ennå var i samfunnet vårt, og fått den til å avta enda mer.

Så er det saken med mobiltelefoner og el-sykler. Hva har disse to tilsynelatende urelaterte produktene til felles? Fra mitt ståsted, ved observasjon av amishene i Holmes County, har disse to tingene endret et folk og en kultur på en mer betydelig måte enn nesten noe annet i nyere tid.

Hvor etterlater dette oss? Hebreerbrevets forfatter sier at For presteembedets endring må også loven nødvendigvis endres – Hebreerne 7:12. Så vi ser at Gud forandret ting etter hva Han så som riktig; dermed, hvis vi trenger å forandre oss for å bli mer bibelske, bør vi gjøre det. Men apostelen Paulus sier at vi ikke lenger skal være barn, kastet hit og dit og ført omkring av enhver lærevind… – Efeserne 4:14.

Og fordi lovløsheten skal gjøre seg verre, skal kjærligheten hos de fleste bli kald. Men den som står ut til enden, han skal bli frelst – Matteus 24:12-13. Så la oss være årvåkne i disse endetider når forandring skjer mer og mer rundt oss. Måtte vi være blant dem som står ut til enden.

We spend all our days chasing the dollar.
The devil smiles as he tightens our collar.

We need time for God, and our families too.
Maybe less time at work could surely do.

Do we have time for that still small voice?
Or does our money talk, and give us no choice?

We all know the Bible—no work, no eat.
But money will bind us until death we meet.

The more we have, the more we need;
The love of money starts with a seed.

Lying to yourself is a foolish thing—
“Freedom, or bondage?” is the question I bring.

آزادی، یا غلامی — کون سا ہوگا؟
یا کیا وہ ایک ہی ہیں؛ کیا کوئی دیکھ سکتا ہے؟

لوگ وہ چیزیں پسند کرتے ہیں جو پیسوں سے خریدی جا سکیں،
اپنی زندگیاں بیچ دیتے ہیں، اور کوئی وجہ نہیں بتاتے۔

آرام و آس کے لیے بل ڈھیر ہوتے جاتے ہیں؛
“ہماری بیویوں کا کیا، یا بچوں کو خوش کرنے کا کیا مطلب؟”

ہم سارا دن ڈالر کے پیچھے بھاگتے گزارتے ہیں۔
شیطان مسکراتا ہے جب وہ ہماری گردن کا کالر سخت کرتا ہے۔

ہمیں خدا کے لیے وقت چاہیے، اور اپنے خاندان کے لیے بھی۔
شاید کام میں کم وقت دینے سے یہ ہو ہی جائے۔

کیا ہمارے پاس اُس نرم سی آواز کے لیے وقت ہے؟
یا کیا ہمارا پیسہ بولتا ہے، اور ہمیں کوئی انتخاب نہیں دیتا؟

ہم سب بائبل جانتے ہیں — نہ کام، نہ کھانا۔
مگر پیسہ ہمیں موت تک باندھ دے گا۔

جتنا زیادہ ہمارے پاس ہوتا ہے، اتنا ہی زیادہ ہمیں چاہیے؛
محبتِِِ پیسہ ایک بیج سے شروع ہوتی ہے۔

خود سے جھوٹ بولنا ایک نادان کام ہے —
“آزادی، یا غلامی؟” یہی سوال میں اٹھاتا ہوں۔

“My, it’s warm!” exclaimed Mom. “A nice, good rain is what we need to cool things off a bit.”

It was Saturday, near the end of June, and the weather had been particularly hot and humid that day. Ellie’s mother had been cleaning the house and preparing some food for the company that was invited to come for lunch on Sunday after church.

As the afternoon moved into early evening, it felt like it became even hotter, and no breezes were to be found. Ellie’s father was resting in a hammock out on the lawn while the rest of the family tried to find the most comfortable place to seek relief from the heat.

As evening approached, so did the clouds. They arrived suddenly, along with gusts of wind that began to stir up the dust. Lightning started to flash across the sky and the thunder rumbled in the distance.

“Quickly, children!” called Mom. “Put away your toys; it’s about to storm!”

Ellie looked around in alarm. It was getting dark very quickly and the sky looked strange—almost angry. She quickly gathered up her playthings and hurried into the house. Dad was no longer sleeping on the hammock. The wind had almost toppled it over and him along with it! He, too, hurried into the house; the wind causing the door to slam violently behind him. The family gathered on the sunporch to watch the approaching storm. There were windows to the west and south, so they had a good vantage point from which to watch the coming rain. The wind was blowing with a force that Ellie had never experienced in all her seven years. She noted the concern and alarm on her parents’ faces as they watched and waited.

Then it began to rain. Great sheets of rain were being driven against the windows and Ellie wondered if it was possible that it was raining hard enough to break the glass.

“What was that?” exclaimed Mom as suddenly, a sheet of tin whizzed past the sunporch windows and disappeared beyond the garden.

“I think it’s part of the garage roof,” said Dad in disbelief while peering cautiously through the windows.

Upon hearing this, Mom directed the children to stand by the cellar door. If things got worse, down they would go! Ellie felt so scared. What was going to happen to them? Would their house blow away? Would any of them get hurt?

As abruptly as the storm began, it calmed. The wind stopped, the rain slowed, and very soon the sun was shining again. The family cautiously ventured outdoors to see what all had happened during the storm.

“Look!” said Dad. “The garage roof is gone and so is the south wall!”

“Why does Gerald’s house look so strange?” Mom pointed toward their next-door neighbors. “Why, look! The entire roof is gone from their house!” Indeed, the roof had been cleanly stripped away and the gable ends stoically stood there, holding up nothing.

The wail of sirens could be heard in the distance and as they looked around the neighborhood, they could see smoke just beyond some trees.

“That’s got to be Melvin’s barn burning!” exclaimed Dad. “I’m going to go see what I can do to help.” He raced for his truck and was soon hurrying out the driveway.

The winds had been so strong that some electric poles were blown over causing the electricity to be disconnected so there were no lights or fans. After the storm had passed the humidity and heat had returned making the night hot and muggy. Yet the grown-ups from the area worked long into the night, helping each other to clean up what they could of the storm damage.

Of special interest was our neighbor Melvin. His barn had collapsed on top of dozens of cattle and then a fire had broken out. The neighbor men tried desperately to rescue what cattle they could, but in the end, many of the steers could not be saved.

Sunday came, but no one went to church. The morning was spent over at Melvin’s, hauling away dead cattle, clearing away burnt hay, and simply just being there for one another. It was hard, grim work. Ellie clearly remembers how awful the smell was. And she could barely bring herself to watch the loading up of the dead steers. When lunch time came, their company arrived, but no one was very hungry. Ellie’s younger brother sobbed, “All I can think about is those poor steers!”

Ellie was surprised how powerful a storm could be. And scary! Would they experience another twister? Might more buildings collapse, and another barn or house burn down? A seed of fear began to grow in Ellie’s heart. Throughout that summer and for many summers after, every time the rumble of thunder was heard or she heard the words “tornado warning”, her heart would beat faster, and a knot would settle in her stomach. How she dreaded each storm! She wished they would all just pass by their home. Why did God allow storms, anyway?

“You need to trust God, Ellie,” her mother would say. “He’s the One who made the weather, and He is in control of everything that happens. He might not always keep us from experiencing frightening times, but He is always there to take care of us.”

As she grew older, Ellie learned to take this advice to heart. Her fear of storms faded, and, in its place, she developed a fascination with how storms develop and form. Knowing that God is the Master of the wind is still a comfort and an assurance to her. Most of all, as she has learned to trust God in every area of her life, she has found Him to always be faithful. Learning to replace fear with trust always brings peace to the heart.

“আরে, কেমন গরম!” মাকে বললেন। “মনে হচ্ছে একটু ভালো, ভিজিয়ে দেওয়ার মতো বৃষ্টি লাগবে তাপটা কমাতে।”

এটি ছিল শনিবার, জুন মাসের শেষের দিকে, এবং ওই দিন আবহাওয়া বিশেষ করে গরম ও আর্দ্র ছিল। এলির মাকে বাড়ি পরিষ্কার করছিলেন এবং রবিবার চার্চের পরে দুপুরের খাবারের জন্য আমন্ত্রিত অতিথিদের জন্য কিছু খাবার প্রস্তুত করছিলেন।

এমন সময় বিকেল থেকে সন্ধ্যায় যাওয়ার সঙ্গে সঙ্গে আরও গরম লাগতে লাগল, এবং কোন হাওয়ার আবছা ছোঁয়াও দেখা যাচ্ছিল না। এলির বাবা লনে হ্যামকেতে বিশ্রাম নিচ্ছিলেন, আর পরিবারের বাকিরা তাপ থেকে আরাম পেতে সবচেয়ে আরামদায়ক জায়গা খুঁজছিলেন।

সন্ধ্যা নেমে আসার সাথে সাথেই মেঘও এলো। তারা হঠাৎ এসে হাজির হল, ঝাঁপটা দিয়ে বায়ুর ঝটকা যা ধুলোতে উত্থাপন করতে লাগল। আকাশে বজ্রপাত ঝলসে উঠল এবং দূরে দূরে বজ্রগর্জন শোনা গেল।

“দ্রুত, ছেলে-মেয়ে!” মা ডাকলেন। “তোমাদের খেলনা-কুদুস রাখো; ঝড় আসতে চলেছে!”

এলি চমকে চারদিকে তাকালো। খুব দ্রুত অন্ধকার নেমে আসছে এবং আকাশ অদ্ভুত—প্রায় রোষায়িত—লেগে ছিল। সে দ্রুত তার খেলনা তুলে নিয়ে বাড়ির মধ্যবিত্তে দৌড়ে ঢুকল। বাবা আর হ্যামকেতে ঘুমাচ্ছেন না। হাওয়া প্রায় হ্যামকেটিকে উল্টে দিচ্ছিল এবং বাবাকেও ছিটকে ফেলছিল! তিনি ও দ্রুত বাড়ির ভিতরে এলেন; হাওয়ার তীব্রতায় দরজাটি জোরে ধাক্কা খেয়ে বন্ধ হয়ে গেল। পরিবারটি এসে সানপোরচে জমায়েত হলো ঝড়টার দিকে দেখার জন্য। পশ্চিম ও দক্ষিণ দিকে জানালা ছিল, তাই তারা আসন্ন বৃষ্টিকে ভালভাবে দেখতে পাচ্ছিল। হাওয়া এমন তীব্র বেগে বইছিল যা এলি তার সাত বছরের জীবনে কখনও অনুভব করেনি। তারা দেখছিলেন এবং অপেক্ষা করছিলেন—তার মা-বাবার চোখে উদ্বেগ ও আতঙ্ক দেখা যাচ্ছিল।

তারপর বৃষ্টি শুরু হল। জানালার ওপর দিয়ে বিশাল ঝরনার মতো বৃষ্টি ধাক্কা খেতে লাগল এবং এলি ভেবে উঠল—এত জোরে বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে যে শয়তানের কাচও ভেঙে যেতে পারে কি না।

“কী ছিল সেটা?” মা বিস্ময়ে বললেন হঠাৎ, একটি টিনের পাতা সানপোরচের জানালার পাশ দিয়ে ঝট করে কেটে গিয়ে বাগানের ওপরে অদৃশ্য হয়ে গেল।

“মনে হয় গ্যারেজের ছাদ থেকে কিছু ছিঁড়ে এসেছে,” বাবা অবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে বললেন, সতর্কতাসহ জানালার বাইরে চুপচাপ তাকিয়ে।

এটা শুনে মা শিশুদের সেলে দরজার পাশে দাঁড়াতে বললেন। যদি অবস্থা খারাপ হয়, তারা নীচে যাবে! এলি খুব ভয় পেয়েছিল। তাদের কী হবে? তাদের বাড়ি উড়ে যাবে কি? তাদের মধ্যে কারও আহত হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা আছে কি?

যেভাবে ঝড়টি শুরু হয়েছিল, তেমনি হঠাৎ শান্তও হয়ে গেল। হাওয়া থেমে গেল, বৃষ্টি ধীর হয়ে এলো, এবং খুব শিগগিরই সূর্য আবার ঝলমল করতে লাগল। পরিবারটি সাবধানে বাইরে গেলো দেখতে যে ঝড়ে কী কী ঘটেছে।

“দেখো!” বাবা বললেন। “গ্যারেজের ছাদ নেই এবং দক্ষিণ দেয়ালটাও নেই!”

“জেরাল্ডের বাড়িটা কেন এত অদ্ভুত দেখাচ্ছে?” মা পাশের প্রতিবেশীর দিকে ইঙ্গিত করে বললেন। “দেখো! তাদের বাড়ির পুরো ছাদই উধাও!” সত্যিই, ছাদটি পরিষ্কারভাবে ছেঁড়ে গেছে এবং গ্যাবল শেষগুলো নীরবে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে, কিছুই ধরে রাখছে না।

দূরে সাইরেনের কেও কেও শব্দ শোনা যাচ্ছিল এবং তারা আশেপাশা এলাকায় তাকালে কিছু গাছের ওপরে ধোঁয়া দেখা গেল।

“অবশ্যই সেটাই মেলভিনের খামারের আগুন!” বাবা বললেন। “আমি যাচ্ছি দেখে কী করে সাহায্য করতে পারি।” তিনি ট্রাকে ছুটে চললেন এবং শীঘ্রই ড্রাইভওয়েতে বেরিয়ে পড়লেন।

হাওয়াগুলো এত শক্তিশালী ছিল যে কয়েকটি বিদ্যুতের খুঁটি ভেঙে পড়ে ফলে বিদ্যুৎ বিচ্ছিন্ন হয়ে গিয়েছিল; তাই লাইট বা ফ্যান কাজ করছিল না। ঝড় কেটে যাওয়ার পর আর্দ্রতা ও শীতলতা ফিরে এসেছিল, রাতটি পুনরায় গরম ও আর্দ্র হয়ে উঠল। তবুও এলাকাজুড়ে বড়রা রাতভর কাজ করল, একে অপরকে সাহায্য করে ঝড়ের ক্ষতিগুলো পরিষ্কার করতে।

বিশেষভাবে যে ঘটনাটি মনোরম ছিল তা হলো আমাদের প্রতিবেশী মেলভিন। তার খামার ধসে পড়ে ডজনখানেক গরুর ওপর এবং পরে সেখানে আগুন ধরল। প্রতিবেশী পুরুষেরা চেষ্টা করল যত গরু বাঁচানো যায় উদ্ধার করতে, কিন্তু শেষে অনেক ষাঁড়কে বাঁচানো যায়নি।

রবিবার এলো, কিন্তু কেউই চার্চে যায়নি। সকালের বেলা মেলভিনের বাড়িতে কেটেছে—মৃত গরুগুলো তুলতে, পোড়া খড় সরাতে এবং একে অপরের পাশে দাঁড়াতে। কাজটি কঠিন, কঠোর ছিল। এলি স্পষ্টভাবে মনে রেখেছে কত নিকৃষ্ট গন্ধ ছিল। এবং সে দুর্বলভাবে মৃত ষাঁড়গুলো লোড হতে দেখার সাহস পাচ্ছিল না। দুপুরের সময় তাদের অতিথিরা এসেছিল, কিন্তু কারো বেশি ক্ষুধা ছিল না। এলির ছোট ভাই কাতর কানে বলল, “আমি শুধু সেই দয়নীয় ষাঁড়গুলোর কথা ভাবতেই পারছি!”

এলি বিস্মিত হয়েছিল ঝড় কতটা শক্তিশালী হতে পারে। এবং ভয়ঙ্করও! তারা কি আরেকটি ঘূর্ণিঝড়ের সম্মুখীন হবে? আরও কোনো ভবন ভেঙে পড়বে, আরেকটি ঝড় বা বাড়ি জ্বলবে? ভয়ের একটি বীজ এলির হৃদয়ে বাড়তে শুরু করল। সেই গ্রীষ্ম এবং তার পর অনেক গ্রীষ্ম ধরে, প্রতিবার বজ্রগর্জন শোনা গেলে বা “টর্নেডো সতর্কতা” শব্দটি তার কানে এলে, তার হৃদস্পন্দন দ্রুততরে হয়ে উঠত, এবং পেটের মধ্যে একটি গিঁট জমে যেত। সে প্রতিটি ঝড়কে ভয় করত! সে চাইত সব ঝড় যেন তাদের বাড়ির পাশ দিয়ে কেটে যায়। ঈশ্বর কেন ঝড়কে অনুমতি দেন—এই প্রশ্নটি তার মনেই ঘুরপাক খাত?

“তোমাকে ঈশ্বরের ওপর বিশ্বাস করতে হবে, এলি,” তার মা বলতেন। “তিনি হলেন যে মানুষ আবহাওয়াকে সৃষ্টি করেছেন, এবং তিনি সব ঘটনার নিয়ন্ত্রণে আছেন। তিনি হয়তো সব ভয়ানক সময় থেকে আমাদের রক্ষা করবেন না, কিন্তু তিনি সবসময় আমাদের যত্ন নেবেন। ”

বলার সাথে সাথে বড় হওয়ার সঙ্গে এলি এই পরামর্শটিকে হৃদয়ে গ্রহণ করতে শিখল। তার ঝড়ের ভয় ফিকে হয়ে গেল, এবং তার জায়গায় তিনি ঝড় কীভাবে গড়ে ওঠে ও বিকাশ পায় তা নিয়ে একরকম আগ্রহ তৈরি করলেন। জানতে পেরে যে ঈশ্বরই বাতাসের স্বामी—এটি এখনও তার কাছে সান্ত্বনা ও নিশ্চয়তা হয়ে আছে। সবচেয়ে বেশি, তিনি যখন জীবনের প্রতিটি ক্ষেত্রে ঈশ্বরের ওপর বিশ্বাস করতে শিখেছেন, তিনি দেখেছেন তিনি সবসময় বিশ্বস্ত। ভয়কে বিশ্বাসে বদলে ফেলা সবসময় হৃদয়ে শান্তি নিয়ে আসে।

This story starts in Switzerland, in the 1500s. A group of Christian believers, desiring to obey Jesus and return to the teachings of the Apostles and the early Church, separated from both the Catholic and Protestant state-run Churches in several Cantons of Switzerland. They were referred to as the Swiss Brethren and were deemed as enemies of the state, by the Catholics and Protestants alike. Their enemies called them “Anabaptists” because they rejected infant baptism. They also refused military service, obeying Christ’s commands to “bless them that persecute you” and “love your enemies”. Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith. In the early 1600s, when the authorities could not stop the movement in this manner, they began confiscating the believer’s homes, farms, and belongings, then exiled them from Switzerland.

Europe had just gone through the devastations of the Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648). In some places, like the Palatinate (Pfaltzland) in Germany, as many as 70% of the inhabitants had died of either war or disease. Many of the Hoffs (house/barn fort enclosures) were burned out and the fields were left uncultivated for years. In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms because of their reputation as excellent husbandmen and tillers of the soil.

There were three official Churches recognized by the Germans: Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed. Although the Swiss Brethren were needed economically, and their faith was tolerated, their churches were not recognized. There were limits on how many of them could meet together at one time, and many times they were not allowed to purchase the farms that they were improving because they were considered foreigners.

The Swiss-operated farms did indeed prosper in time, partly due to their use of a superior crop rotation system, which helped them feed more dairy cattle, and, in turn, allowed them to produce milk through the winters. Another major improvement was the introduction of the legume, clover. This came from seed which the Dutch Mennonites gifted to them. After about 50 years, the difference the Swiss had made in agriculture was noticeable enough that some frustrated German neighbors accused them of “Ferhexing” (the Pennsylvania Dutch term for witchcraft) the ground (which of course was not true). So, life in the Pfaltzland wasn’t getting better for the Swiss Brethren.

In the year 1708, they experienced a bitterly cold, long winter. So cold that some of their stored root crops froze in the cold cellars. Sometime after this, William Penn and the Quakers heard of the plight of these Swiss Anabaptists. In 1682, William Penn had been granted the colony of Pennsylvania and wanted to conduct what he called the “Holy Experiment”. He envisioned a land where all races and religions could dwell together in peace. He had special interest in those groups persecuted by the European State Churches. As a Quaker, he too had suffered persecution by the state church of England. He welcomed Quakers from England, Huguenots from France, Mennonites from Holland, German Baptist, Schwenkfelders and Pietists from Germany, as well as Swiss Brethren and Jews from wherever they were sojourning and/or suffering.

That is the background for our account of Hans Graeff (Groff) who lived from c.1661-1746. Hans had been converted to the faith of the Swiss Brethren, but his wife, Anna (Bare) Graeff had stayed with the Protestant State Church. When the door opened to pioneer in Pennsylvania, Hans was interested in going, but Anna was not. Possibly they planned to have him get settled in over there and then come back for her. Hans first came to Pennsylvania in 1696. Later, Hans ended up leading a small group of the Swiss Brethren (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & the Funks to name a few) to Germantown, about seven miles north of Philadelphia in that day, which was the first permanent settlement of the Anabaptists in the New World. Many of those first settlers were from Holland and Sweden and were part of the Mennonite Church of the Netherlands. The Swiss immigrants spent the winter of 1709 in Germantown—the women doing spinning for the many weavers of Germantown and the men traveling to a new Anabaptist settlement at Skippack, where they were learning many of the skills needed to go to the frontier. It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.

In 1710, the group moved up to the Conestoga Valley where Hans Groff had previously identified some very rich and well-watered lands, 60 miles west of Germantown and civilization. Life would indeed be difficult. Wolves, bears, panthers, bobcats and other predators abounded. There were also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer in abundance (which were glad to eat whatever the settlers planted). Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples, white pines, and oaks, some six feet in diameter and over 100 feet tall, covered much of their new lands (except for some open meadows, left by the native Americans and wetlands). These huge trees would need to be cut down by hand with axes and two-man saws. The closest doctor, apothecary, hardware, or general store was 60 miles away. It would be challenging and dangerous work, but they were free! Free to obey their conscience. Free to practice their religion. Free to own land in this beautiful wilderness. Free to love and witness to their neighbors—the Conestoga tribe and French traders. They received a land patent for 10,000 acres for their families and others that might come later.

Partly due to severe persecution, in 1710, a group of Swiss Brethren moved to the Mannheim area of Germany. Seven years later, in 1717, they made the trip across the Atlantic. There were more than 60 families that came to the Conestoga Valley in the fall of that year, including my ancestors, Hans and Magdalena Hess and their three children (they were eventually blessed with a total of 11). You could say that from then on, the floodgates opened, and masses of Anabaptists fled Europe to “Penn’s Promised Land”. From 1730 and later, as this wilderness became tamed, there were also many Lutheran, Reformed, and Catholic people who came over from Germany to find better financial opportunities, filling this part of Pennsylvania with many German-dialect speakers.

I greatly enjoyed speaking with the noted Lancaster County Anabaptist historian, Amos Hoover, while writing this article. He gave many insights and details, but we both agreed, it is challenging to put together all the facts and details from so long ago. Gleaning from a couple authors’ accounts, the story goes something like this:

Misunderstanding

Sometime, after being in Penn’s woods for a number of years, Hans Groff received word that his wife, Anna (Bare) Groff, back in Europe, had passed away. He was very grieved and mourned, as he didn’t know it and wasn’t there to bury her. In a few years, he married Susanna Kendig. They lived first in the Strasburg area, then built a substantial homestead in the area now called Groffdale. This union was blessed with nine children.

Years later, a woman showed up in the community and introduced herself as Mrs. Hans Groff. She had become an Anabaptist in Europe and had made the perilous trip across the Atlantic to find her husband. According to her, a person with the same name as herself had died, and the word given to Hans was not true about his first wife’s death. Hans was mortified, although he was innocent regarding his second marriage. He had no desire to be a polygamist or to commit adultery. The frontier church leaders held counsel and gave a recommendation—that the younger, pioneer wife with so many young children needed the husband to provide for them. It is said that Hans didn’t feel clear to stay with either of them but did support both of his wives and their children financially. He was noted as a tireless traveler, riding to Philadelphia with furs then back out into the vast frontier with blankets, brass kettles and other trade good for the Native Americans. If you have heard or read this account with different details, so have I. Only eternity will reveal all these details exactly.

Medicine

Hans’s first wife chose to live as a single sister in that church community. Instead of becoming bitter with her husband, her God, and her circumstances, she chose a life of service to her neighbors. She lived in a little house, with a small barn (possibly built by Hans for her) on top of a steep hill overlooking Farmersville, called “Cat’s Back Hill”. The ruins of this early 1700s house and barn were still evident less than 50 years ago. Apparently, she was a midwife, before coming to this country and continued in this profession once she was here. She had a lot of experience with growing herbs and making herbal remedies. She was possibly the closest one to being a doctor for many miles around. From what I can find out, she spent her time being a blessing to the local community with her medical knowledge and wisdom, her homemade herbal medicines, and her midwifery. Many of our Lancaster County forefathers may not have survived the rigorous pioneer life if it had not been for this dear Sister’s servanthood and medical knowledge. Interestingly, years later, one of Hans’s sons from the second wife, David Groff, went away to study medicine. Once his studies were completed, he came back as a doctor and helped his father’s first wife minister to the many settlers in fast growing Lancaster County.

This story provides a glimpse into some of the interesting details surrounding the life of conservative Anabaptists just before and during the establishing of Colonial America. There were difficulties involving freedom of religion and worship in their homelands of Europe, but their travels to, and eventual day-to-day living in, a new, free country was acquainted with challenges as well. One encouragement that we can see in this story was the willingness of these individuals to allow God’s principles to guide them each step of the way.

Questa storia inizia in Svizzera, nel 1500. Un gruppo di credenti cristiani, desiderosi di obbedire a Gesù e tornare agli insegnamenti degli Apostoli e della Chiesa primitiva, si separò sia dalla Chiesa cattolica sia dalle Chiese protestanti statali in diversi Cantoni svizzeri. Venivano chiamati Fratelli svizzeri e furono considerati nemici dello stato, sia dai cattolici sia dai protestanti. I loro nemici li chiamarono “anabattisti” perché rifiutavano il battesimo infantile. Rifiutavano anche il servizio militare, obbedendo ai comandi di Cristo di “benedire quelli che vi perseguitano” e di “amare i vostri nemici”. Molti furono arrestati, imprigionati, torturati senza pietà e infine molti furono martirizzati per non aver rinnegato la loro fede. Nei primi anni del 1600, quando le autorità non potevano fermare il movimento in questo modo, cominciarono a confiscare le case, le fattorie e i beni dei credenti, quindi li esiliarono dalla Svizzera.

L'Europa aveva appena attraversato le devastazioni della Guerra dei Trent'Anni (1618-1648). In alcuni luoghi, come il Palatinato (Pfaltzland) in Germania, fino al 70% degli abitanti era morto a causa della guerra o delle malattie. Molti degli Hoffs (recinti domestici/fienili fortificati) erano bruciati e i campi rimasero incolti per anni. Nella metà del 1600, il Principe locale, l'Elettore Ludwig, invitò i Fratelli svizzeri esiliati nel Palatinato per aiutare a ricostruire le fattorie, a causa della loro reputazione come eccellenti agricoltori e coltivatori della terra.

C'erano tre Chiese ufficiali riconosciute dai tedeschi: cattolica, luterana e riformata. Sebbene i Fratelli svizzeri fossero necessari economicamente e la loro fede fosse tollerata, le loro chiese non erano riconosciute. C'erano limiti su quante persone potevano riunirsi insieme in una volta, e molte volte non era permesso loro acquistare le fattorie che stavano migliorando perché erano considerati stranieri.

Le fattorie operate dagli svizzeri prosperarono col tempo, in parte grazie all'uso di un superiore sistema di rotazione delle colture, che li aiutò a nutrire più bovini da latte e, a sua volta, permise loro di produrre latte durante l'inverno. Un altro importante miglioramento fu l'introduzione delle leguminose, il trifoglio. Questo venne da semi che i mennoniti olandesi regalarono loro. Dopo circa 50 anni, la differenza che gli svizzeri avevano fatto nell'agricoltura era abbastanza evidente che alcuni vicini tedeschi frustrati li accusarono di “Ferhexing” (il termine dei Pennsylvania Dutch per stregoneria) del terreno (cosa che ovviamente non era vera). Così, la vita nel Pfaltzland non migliorava per i Fratelli svizzeri.

Nell'anno 1708, vissero un inverno gelidamente freddo e lungo. Tanto freddo che alcune delle loro radici conservate si gelarono nelle cantine fredde. Poco dopo, William Penn e i Quaccheri vennero a conoscenza della sorte di questi anabattisti svizzeri. Nel 1682, a William Penn era stata concessa la colonia della Pennsylvania e voleva condurre quello che chiamava il “Santo Esperimento”. Immaginava una terra dove tutte le razze e religioni potessero convivere in pace. Aveva un interesse speciale per quei gruppi perseguitati dalle Chiese statali europee. In quanto Quacchero, anche lui aveva subito persecuzioni da parte della Chiesa statale d'Inghilterra. Accolse Quaccheri dall'Inghilterra, ugonotti dalla Francia, mennoniti dall'Olanda, battisti tedeschi, schwenkfelder e pietisti dalla Germania, così come Fratelli svizzeri e ebrei da ovunque stessero soggiornando e/o soffrendo.

Questo è lo sfondo del nostro racconto su Hans Graeff (Groff) che visse circa dal 1661 al 1746. Hans si era convertito alla fede dei Fratelli svizzeri, ma sua moglie, Anna (Bare) Graeff era rimasta con la Chiesa protestante statale. Quando si aprì la porta per pionierare in Pennsylvania, Hans era interessato ad andare, ma Anna no. Forse avevano pensato che lui si sarebbe sistemato laggiù e poi sarebbe tornato a prenderla. Hans venne per la prima volta in Pennsylvania nel 1696. Più tardi, Hans finì per guidare un piccolo gruppo dei Fratelli svizzeri (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & i Funk, per citarne alcuni) a Germantown, circa sette miglia a nord di Philadelphia a quei tempi, che fu il primo insediamento permanente degli anabattisti nel Nuovo Mondo. Molti di quei primi coloni provenivano dall'Olanda e dalla Svezia e facevano parte della Chiesa mennonita dei Paesi Bassi. Gli immigrati svizzeri passarono l'inverno del 1709 a Germantown—le donne filando per i numerosi tessitori di Germantown e gli uomini viaggiando verso un nuovo insediamento anabattista a Skippack, dove imparavano molte delle abilità necessarie per andare verso la frontiera. Sembra che qui i Fratelli svizzeri vennero per la prima volta noti come Mennisti o Mennoniti.

Nel 1710, il gruppo si trasferì nella Conestoga Valley dove Hans Groff aveva precedentemente individuato alcune terre molto ricche e ben irrigate, a 60 miglia a ovest di Germantown e della civiltà. La vita sarebbe stata davvero difficile. Lupi, orsi, pantere, linci e altri predatori abbondavano. C'erano anche alci, bisonti boschivi e cervi dalla coda bianca in abbondanza (che erano lieti di mangiare qualunque cosa i coloni piantassero). Enormi noci americane, noce, castagni, aceri, pini bianchi e querce, alcune di sei piedi di diametro e oltre 100 piedi di altezza, coprivano gran parte delle loro nuove terre (eccetto alcune praterie aperte, lasciate dai nativi americani e aree umide). Questi enormi alberi dovevano essere abbattuti a mano con asce e seghe a due uomini. Il medico, l'apotecario, il negozio di ferramenta o il negozio generale più vicino erano a 60 miglia di distanza. Sarebbe stato un lavoro impegnativo e pericoloso, ma erano liberi! Liberi di obbedire alla propria coscienza. Liberi di praticare la propria religione. Liberi di possedere terre in questa bellissima natura selvaggia. Liberi di amare e testimoniare ai loro vicini—la tribù Conestoga e i commercianti francesi. Ricevettero una patente di 10.000 acri per le loro famiglie e per altri che avrebbero potuto venire più tardi.

In parte a causa delle severe persecuzioni, nel 1710 un gruppo di Fratelli svizzeri si trasferì nella zona di Mannheim in Germania. Sette anni dopo, nel 1717, intrapresero il viaggio attraverso l'Atlantico. Più di 60 famiglie vennero nella Conestoga Valley nell'autunno di quell'anno, inclusi i miei antenati, Hans e Magdalena Hess e i loro tre figli (furono infine benedetti con un totale di 11). Si potrebbe dire che da allora le porte si spalancarono e masse di anabattisti fuggirono dall'Europa verso la “Terra promessa di Penn”. Dal 1730 in poi, mentre questa natura selvaggia veniva addomesticata, arrivarono anche molte persone luterane, riformate e cattoliche provenienti dalla Germania in cerca di migliori opportunità finanziarie, riempiendo questa parte della Pennsylvania con molti parlanti dialetti tedeschi.

Ho molto apprezzato parlare con il noto storico anabattista della contea di Lancaster, Amos Hoover, mentre scrivevo questo articolo. Mi ha dato molti approfondimenti e dettagli, ma entrambi siamo d'accordo che è difficile mettere insieme tutti i fatti e i dettagli di così tanto tempo fa. Raccogliendo da alcuni resoconti di autori, la storia va più o meno così:

Malinteso

Qualche tempo dopo essere stato nei boschi di Penn per alcuni anni, Hans Groff ricevette la notizia che sua moglie, Anna (Bare) Groff, in Europa, era morta. Ne fu molto addolorato e pianse, poiché non lo sapeva e non era lì per seppellirla. Dopo alcuni anni, sposò Susanna Kendig. Vissero prima nell'area di Strasburg, poi costruirono una consistente fattoria nell'area ora chiamata Groffdale. Questa unione fu benedetta con nove figli.

Anni dopo, una donna si presentò nella comunità e si presentò come la signora Hans Groff. Si era convertita all'anabattismo in Europa e aveva compiuto il pericoloso viaggio attraverso l'Atlantico per cercare suo marito. Secondo lei, una persona con lo stesso nome di lei era morta, e l'informazione data a Hans sulla morte della sua prima moglie non era vera. Hans fu mortificato, anche se era innocente riguardo al suo secondo matrimonio. Non aveva nessun desiderio di essere un poligamo o di commettere adulterio. I leader della chiesa di frontiera tennero consiglio e diedero una raccomandazione—che la moglie più giovane, pioniera, con tanti figli piccoli avesse bisogno del marito per provvedere a loro. Si dice che Hans non si sentisse chiaro nel restare con nessuna delle due, ma sostenne entrambe le sue mogli e i loro figli finanziariamente. Era noto come un instancabile viaggiatore, a cavallo fino a Filadelfia con pellicce e poi di nuovo nella vasta frontiera con coperte, caldaie di ottone e altri beni da scambiare con i nativi americani. Se avete sentito o letto questo racconto con dettagli diversi, anch'io. Solo l'eternità rivelerà tutti questi particolari esattamente.

Medicina

La prima moglie di Hans scelse di vivere come sorella single nella comunità ecclesiale. Invece di amareggiarsi con suo marito, con Dio e con le sue circostanze, scelse una vita di servizio verso i suoi vicini. Visse in una casetta, con un piccolo fienile (possibilmente costruito da Hans per lei) sulla sommità di una ripida collina che domina Farmersville, chiamata “Cat's Back Hill”. Le rovine di questa casa e di questo fienile dei primi anni del 1700 erano ancora evidenti meno di 50 anni fa. Apparentemente era una ostetrica, prima di venire in questo paese e continuò questa professione una volta arrivata. Aveva molta esperienza nella coltivazione di erbe e nella preparazione di rimedi a base di erbe. Era forse la persona più vicina a fare il ruolo di medico per molte miglia intorno. Da quanto riesco a scoprire, trascorse il suo tempo essendo una benedizione per la comunità locale con la sua conoscenza medica e saggezza, i suoi rimedi casalinghi a base di erbe e la sua ostetricia. Molti dei nostri progenitori della contea di Lancaster potrebbero non aver sopravvissuto alla rigida vita di pionieri se non fosse stato per il servizio e la conoscenza medica di questa cara Sorella. Curiosamente, anni dopo, uno dei figli di Hans dalla seconda moglie, David Groff, andò via per studiare medicina. Una volta completati gli studi, tornò come medico e aiutò la prima moglie di suo padre a servire i molti coloni nella contea di Lancaster in rapida crescita.

Questa storia offre uno sguardo su alcuni dei dettagli interessanti che circondano la vita degli anabattisti conservatori poco prima e durante l'istituzione dell'America coloniale. Ci furono difficoltà riguardanti la libertà di religione e di culto nelle loro patrie europee, ma i loro viaggi verso, e la successiva vita quotidiana in, un nuovo paese libero ebbero anch'essi le loro sfide. Un incoraggiamento che possiamo vedere in questa storia è la disponibilità di questi individui a lasciare che i principi di Dio li guidassero a ogni passo del cammino.

This story starts in Switzerland, in the 1500s. A group of Christian believers, desiring to obey Jesus and return to the teachings of the Apostles and the early Church, separated from both the Catholic and Protestant state-run Churches in several Cantons of Switzerland. They were referred to as the Swiss Brethren and were deemed as enemies of the state, by the Catholics and Protestants alike. Their enemies called them “Anabaptists” because they rejected infant baptism. They also refused military service, obeying Christ’s commands to “bless them that persecute you” and “love your enemies”. Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith. In the early 1600s, when the authorities could not stop the movement in this manner, they began confiscating the believer’s homes, farms, and belongings, then exiled them from Switzerland.

Europe had just gone through the devastations of the Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648). In some places, like the Palatinate (Pfaltzland) in Germany, as many as 70% of the inhabitants had died of either war or disease. Many of the Hoffs (house/barn fort enclosures) were burned out and the fields were left uncultivated for years. In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms because of their reputation as excellent husbandmen and tillers of the soil.

There were three official Churches recognized by the Germans: Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed. Although the Swiss Brethren were needed economically, and their faith was tolerated, their churches were not recognized. There were limits on how many of them could meet together at one time, and many times they were not allowed to purchase the farms that they were improving because they were considered foreigners.

The Swiss-operated farms did indeed prosper in time, partly due to their use of a superior crop rotation system, which helped them feed more dairy cattle, and, in turn, allowed them to produce milk through the winters. Another major improvement was the introduction of the legume, clover. This came from seed which the Dutch Mennonites gifted to them. After about 50 years, the difference the Swiss had made in agriculture was noticeable enough that some frustrated German neighbors accused them of “Ferhexing” (the Pennsylvania Dutch term for witchcraft) the ground (which of course was not true). So, life in the Pfaltzland wasn’t getting better for the Swiss Brethren.

In the year 1708, they experienced a bitterly cold, long winter. So cold that some of their stored root crops froze in the cold cellars. Sometime after this, William Penn and the Quakers heard of the plight of these Swiss Anabaptists. In 1682, William Penn had been granted the colony of Pennsylvania and wanted to conduct what he called the “Holy Experiment”. He envisioned a land where all races and religions could dwell together in peace. He had special interest in those groups persecuted by the European State Churches. As a Quaker, he too had suffered persecution by the state church of England. He welcomed Quakers from England, Huguenots from France, Mennonites from Holland, German Baptist, Schwenkfelders and Pietists from Germany, as well as Swiss Brethren and Jews from wherever they were sojourning and/or suffering.

That is the background for our account of Hans Graeff (Groff) who lived from c.1661-1746. Hans had been converted to the faith of the Swiss Brethren, but his wife, Anna (Bare) Graeff had stayed with the Protestant State Church. When the door opened to pioneer in Pennsylvania, Hans was interested in going, but Anna was not. Possibly they planned to have him get settled in over there and then come back for her. Hans first came to Pennsylvania in 1696. Later, Hans ended up leading a small group of the Swiss Brethren (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & the Funks to name a few) to Germantown, about seven miles north of Philadelphia in that day, which was the first permanent settlement of the Anabaptists in the New World. Many of those first settlers were from Holland and Sweden and were part of the Mennonite Church of the Netherlands. The Swiss immigrants spent the winter of 1709 in Germantown—the women doing spinning for the many weavers of Germantown and the men traveling to a new Anabaptist settlement at Skippack, where they were learning many of the skills needed to go to the frontier. It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.

In 1710, the group moved up to the Conestoga Valley where Hans Groff had previously identified some very rich and well-watered lands, 60 miles west of Germantown and civilization. Life would indeed be difficult. Wolves, bears, panthers, bobcats and other predators abounded. There were also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer in abundance (which were glad to eat whatever the settlers planted). Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples, white pines, and oaks, some six feet in diameter and over 100 feet tall, covered much of their new lands (except for some open meadows, left by the native Americans and wetlands). These huge trees would need to be cut down by hand with axes and two-man saws. The closest doctor, apothecary, hardware, or general store was 60 miles away. It would be challenging and dangerous work, but they were free! Free to obey their conscience. Free to practice their religion. Free to own land in this beautiful wilderness. Free to love and witness to their neighbors—the Conestoga tribe and French traders. They received a land patent for 10,000 acres for their families and others that might come later.

Partly due to severe persecution, in 1710, a group of Swiss Brethren moved to the Mannheim area of Germany. Seven years later, in 1717, they made the trip across the Atlantic. There were more than 60 families that came to the Conestoga Valley in the fall of that year, including my ancestors, Hans and Magdalena Hess and their three children (they were eventually blessed with a total of 11). You could say that from then on, the floodgates opened, and masses of Anabaptists fled Europe to “Penn’s Promised Land”. From 1730 and later, as this wilderness became tamed, there were also many Lutheran, Reformed, and Catholic people who came over from Germany to find better financial opportunities, filling this part of Pennsylvania with many German-dialect speakers.

I greatly enjoyed speaking with the noted Lancaster County Anabaptist historian, Amos Hoover, while writing this article. He gave many insights and details, but we both agreed, it is challenging to put together all the facts and details from so long ago. Gleaning from a couple authors’ accounts, the story goes something like this:

Misunderstanding

Sometime, after being in Penn’s woods for a number of years, Hans Groff received word that his wife, Anna (Bare) Groff, back in Europe, had passed away. He was very grieved and mourned, as he didn’t know it and wasn’t there to bury her. In a few years, he married Susanna Kendig. They lived first in the Strasburg area, then built a substantial homestead in the area now called Groffdale. This union was blessed with nine children.

Years later, a woman showed up in the community and introduced herself as Mrs. Hans Groff. She had become an Anabaptist in Europe and had made the perilous trip across the Atlantic to find her husband. According to her, a person with the same name as herself had died, and the word given to Hans was not true about his first wife’s death. Hans was mortified, although he was innocent regarding his second marriage. He had no desire to be a polygamist or to commit adultery. The frontier church leaders held counsel and gave a recommendation—that the younger, pioneer wife with so many young children needed the husband to provide for them. It is said that Hans didn’t feel clear to stay with either of them but did support both of his wives and their children financially. He was noted as a tireless traveler, riding to Philadelphia with furs then back out into the vast frontier with blankets, brass kettles and other trade good for the Native Americans. If you have heard or read this account with different details, so have I. Only eternity will reveal all these details exactly.

Medicine

Hans’s first wife chose to live as a single sister in that church community. Instead of becoming bitter with her husband, her God, and her circumstances, she chose a life of service to her neighbors. She lived in a little house, with a small barn (possibly built by Hans for her) on top of a steep hill overlooking Farmersville, called “Cat’s Back Hill”. The ruins of this early 1700s house and barn were still evident less than 50 years ago. Apparently, she was a midwife, before coming to this country and continued in this profession once she was here. She had a lot of experience with growing herbs and making herbal remedies. She was possibly the closest one to being a doctor for many miles around. From what I can find out, she spent her time being a blessing to the local community with her medical knowledge and wisdom, her homemade herbal medicines, and her midwifery. Many of our Lancaster County forefathers may not have survived the rigorous pioneer life if it had not been for this dear Sister’s servanthood and medical knowledge. Interestingly, years later, one of Hans’s sons from the second wife, David Groff, went away to study medicine. Once his studies were completed, he came back as a doctor and helped his father’s first wife minister to the many settlers in fast growing Lancaster County.

This story provides a glimpse into some of the interesting details surrounding the life of conservative Anabaptists just before and during the establishing of Colonial America. There were difficulties involving freedom of religion and worship in their homelands of Europe, but their travels to, and eventual day-to-day living in, a new, free country was acquainted with challenges as well. One encouragement that we can see in this story was the willingness of these individuals to allow God’s principles to guide them each step of the way.

הסיפור הזה מתחיל בשוויץ, במאה ה-16. קבוצת מאמינים נוצרים, שחפצה לציית לישו ולחזור לתורות השליחים ולכנסייה הקדומה, נפרדה גם מהכנסייה הקתולית וגם מהכנסייה הפרוטסטנטית הנשלטת על ידי המדינה בכמה קנטונים בשוויץ. קראו להם האלפים השוויצרים והם נחשבו אויבי המדינה, הן בעיני הקתולים והן בעיני הפרוטסטנטים. אויביהם כינו אותם "האנבפטיסטים" משום שסירבו לטבילת תינוקות. הם גם סירבו לשירות צבאי, בצייתם לפקודותיו של המשיח "ברכו את רודפיכם" ו"אהבו את אויביכם". רבים נעצרו, נכלאו, עונו ללא רחמים ולבסוף רבים מהם נרצחו על אמונתם מכיוון שלא חזרו מהם. בתחילת המאה ה-17, כאשר הרשויות לא יכלו לעצור את התנועה בשיטה זו, הן החלו בהחרמת בתי המאמינים, חוותיהם ורכושם, ואז גירשו אותם מתוך שוויץ.

אירופה הרסה זה עתה את עצמה במלחמת השלושים שנה (1618–1648). במקומות מסוימים, כמו בפלטצלאנד (Pfaltzland) בגרמניה, כ-70% מהתושבים מתו כתוצאה ממלחמה או ממחלה. רבות מהחוות המבוצרות (Hoffs — בתי/מחסני חווה) נשרפו והשדות נותרו בלתי מעובדים למשך שנים. באמצע המאה ה-17, הנסיך המקומי, הבוחר לודוויג, הזמין את האנבפטיסטים המגורשים לפלטצלאנד כדי לעזור לשקם את החוות בגלל המוניטין שלהם כחקלאים מצוינים ומעבדי אדמה.

בגרמניה היו שלוש כנסיות רשמיות מוכרות: קתולית, לותרנית ורפורמית. אף על פי שהאנבפטיסטים השוויצרים נדרשו מבחינה כלכלית ואמונתם הובלה, כנסיותיהם לא הוכרו. היו מגבלות על כמה מהם יכלו להתכנס יחד בכל פעם, ולעתים רבות לא הותר להם לרכוש את החוות שהם שיפרו משום שהחשיבו אותם לזרים.

החוות ששויפו על ידי השוויצרים אכן שגשגו עם הזמן, חלקית בזכות שיטת סבב היבול המתקדמת שלהם, שסייעה להאכיל יותר בקר חלב ולהפיק חלב גם בחורפים. שיפור משמעותי נוסף היה הכנסת הקלובר, קוטנית שמשפחת הקטניות — התוסף הגיע מזרעים שנתרמו להם על ידי המנוניטים ההולנדים. לאחר כ-50 שנה, השינוי שחלו האיכרים השוויצרים בחקלאות היה בולט עד ששכנים גרמנים מתוסכלים האשימו אותם ב"Ferhexing" (מונח פנסילבני-דויטש לכישוף) של האדמה (כמובן שלא היה בכך אמת). לכן, החיים בפלטצלאנד לא נהיו טובים יותר עבור האנבפטיסטים השוויצרים.

בשנת 1708 חוו חורף ארוך וקשה באופן מכאיב. היה כל כך קר עד שחלק מהשורשים המאוחסנים שלהם קפאו במרתפים הקרים. לאחר זמן מה שמעו ויליאם פן והקוייקרים על מצוקתם של האנבפטיסטים השוויצרים האלה. בשנת 1682 ניתנה לויליאם פן קולוניה בפנסילבניה והוא רצה לקיים מה שקרא לו "הניסוי הקדוש". הוא דמיין ארץ שבה כל הגזעים והדתות יוכלו לחיות יחד בשלום. היו לו עניין מיוחד בקבוצות שנרדפו על ידי כנסיות המדינה האירופיות. כקוייקר, גם הוא סבל מרדיפות בידי הכנסייה הממלכתית באנגליה. הוא קיבל בברכה קוייקרים מאנגליה, הוגנוטים מצרפת, מנוניטים מהולנד, באפטיסטים גרמנים, שוונקפלדרים ופייטיסטים מגרמניה, כמו גם אנבפטיסטים שוויצרים ויהודים מכל מקום שבו שהו או סבלו.

זהו הרקע לסיפורו של הנס גראף (גרוף) שחי בערך בין 1661–1746. הנס הוסב לאמונת האנבפטיסטים השוויצרים, אך אשתו אנה (בר) גראף נשארה בכנסייה הפרוטסטנטית הממלכתית. כשנפתחה ההזדמנות להקים מושבה בפנסילבניה, הנס רצה לנסוע, אבל אנה לא רצתה. ייתכן שתכננו שהוא ייסע קודם, יתבסס שם ואז יחזור להשיג אותה. הנס הגיע לראשונה לפנסילבניה בשנת 1696. מאוחר יותר הוביל הנס קבוצה קטנה של האנבפטיסטים השוויצרים (הנס וקריסטיאן הר, מרטין מיילין, יעקב מולר, מרטין קֶנדיג, מרטין אוברהולצר, ונדל בומן והפונקס למיניהם) לג'רמנטאון, בערך שבעה מייל צפונית לפילדלפיה באותה תקופה, שהייתה ההתיישבות הקבועה הראשונה של האנבפטיסטים בעולם החדש. רבים מהמתיישבים הראשונים היו מהולנד ומשוודיה והיו חלק מכנסיית המנוניטים של הולנד. המהגרים השוויצרים בילו את חורף 1709 בג'רמנטאון — הנשים טוווֹת עבור הרבים מהאריגים של ג'רמנטאון והגברים נסעו להתיישבות אנבפטיסטית חדשה בסקיפאק, שם למדו הרבה מהכישורים הנדרשים לחיי הגבול. נראה כי כאן הפכו האנבפטיסטים השוויצרים לראשונה לנודעים כ'מניסטים' או מנוניטים.

בשנת 1710 עברה הקבוצה לעמק קונסטוגה, שם הנס גרוף זיהה קודם לכן אדמות עשירות ומלולאות מים, 60 מיילים מערבית לג'רמנטאון ולציוויליזציה. החיים אכן היו קשים. זאבים, דובים, פנתרים, בובקאט וטורפים אחרים שפעו. היו גם איילים, ביזונים יעריים וצבי לבנים בשפע (שהם שמחו לאכול את מה שהמתיישבים שתלו). עצי אגוז ענקיים, היקורי, ערמונים, מייפלים, אורני וני pין לבנים, חלקם בקוטר של כשתיים מטרים ובעלי גובה מעל 30 מטרים, כיסו חלק גדול מאדמתם החדשה (למעט כמה מרבצים פתוחים שהשאירו האמריקאים הילידים ובתי גידול ביצתיים). עצים עצומים אלה היה צריך לכרות ביד עם גרזנים ומקסים דו-אישיים. הרופא הקרוב ביותר, בית המרקחת, כלי הבניין או החנות הכללית היו 60 מיילים משם. זה היה עבודה מאתגרת ומסוכנת, אך הם היו חופשיים! חופשיים לציית למצפונם. חופשיים לעסוק בדתם. חופשיים להחזיק אדמה ביער הפראי היפה הזה. חופשיים לאהוב ולעדות לשכניהם — שבט הקונסטוגה וסוחרים צרפתים. הם קיבלו פטנט אדמה על 10,000 דונם עבור משפחותיהם ואחרים שעשויים לבוא מאוחר יותר.

חלקית בגלל רדיפות קשות, בשנת 1710 עברה קבוצה של אנבפטיסטים שוויצרים לאזור מאנהיים שבגרמניה. שבע שנים לאחר מכן, בשנת 1717, הם חצו את האוקיינוס האטלנטי. יותר מ-60 משפחות הגיעו לעמק קונסטוגה בסתיו אותה שנה, כולל אבותיי, הנס ומגדלנה הס וגילם שלושת ילדיהם (לבסוף ברכו אותם בסך הכל ב-11 ילדים). אפשר לומר שמעתה הדרך נפתחה, והמונים של אנבפטיסטים נמלטו מאירופה אל "ארץ ההבטחה של פן". משנת 1730 ואילך, כשהיער הזה נתהדר והפך למתורבת, גם הרבה אנשים לותרנים, רפורמיים וקתולים הגיעו מגרמניה לחפש הזדמנויות כלכליות טובות יותר, ומילאו חלק זה של פנסילבניה ברבים דוברי הניב הגרמני.

נהניתי מאוד משיחה עם ההיסטוריון הבולט של מחוז לנקסטר בנושא האנבפטיסטים, אמוס הובר, בזמן שכתבתי את המאמר הזה. הוא נתן הרבה תובנות ופרטים, אך הסכמנו שלשני הצדדים קשה להרכיב את כל העובדות והפרטים מהעבר הרחוק. מתוך דלות מקורות של כמה סופרים, הסיפור הולך בערך כך:

אי-הבנה

כשנח על פניו כמה שנים ביערות פן, הנס גרוף קיבל עדכון שאשתו, אנה (בר) גרוף, שבאירופה, נפטרה. הוא התאבל מאוד, שכן לא ידע על כך ולא היה שם לקבור אותה. לאחר כמה שנים נשא לאישה את סוזנה קֶנדיג. הם גרו תחילה באזור סטראסבורג ואז בנו חווה מרשימה באזור שכיום נקרא גרופאדל. מאותו איחוד נולדו תשעה ילדים.

שנים לאחר מכן הופיעה אישה בקהילה והציגה את עצמה כגברת הנס גרוף. היא הוסבה לאנבפטיסטית באירופה ועשתה את המסע המסוכן מעבר לאוקיינוס כדי למצוא את בעלה. לפי דבריה, אישה בעלת אותו השם מתה, וההודעה שנמסרה להנס על מות אשתו הראשונה לא הייתה נכונה. הנס נבוך ומבולבל, אף על פי שהיה חף מפשע לגבי נישואיו השניים. לא היה לו רצון להיות פוליגמי או לקיים ניאוף. מנהיגי הכנסייה בגבול קיימו עיצבון ונתנו המלצה — שהאישה הצעירה, החלוצה, עם כל כך הרבה ילדים קטנים זקוקה לבעלה לפרנסותיהם. אומרים שהנס לא הרגיש ברור להישאר עם אף אחת מהן אך תמך בשתי נשותיו ובילדיהן מבחינה כלכלית. ציינו אותו כנוסע עקשן, רוכב לפילדלפיה עם פרוות ואז חזרה אל הגבול הרחב עם שמיכות, קומקומי פליז וסחורות מסחר אחרות לאמריקאים הילידים. אם שמעתם או קראתם גרסה אחרת של סיפור זה עם פרטים שונים, גם אני שמעתי. רק הנצח יגלה את כל הפרטים בדיוק.

רפואה

אשתו הראשונה של הנס בחרה לחיות כאחות רווקה בקהילת הכנסייה ההיא. במקום להיות מרירה כלפי בעלה, אלוהיה והנסיבות, בחרה בחיי שירות לשכניה. היא חיה בבית קטן, עם אסם קטן (אולי נבנה עבורה על ידי הנס) על גבעה תלולה המשקיפה על פארמסוויל, שנקראה "גבעת גב החתול". חורבות בית ואסם מאמצע המאה ה-18 היו עדיין נראות לפני פחות מ-50 שנה. נראה כי הייתה מכשירה/מיילדת עוד לפני שיגרה לארץ זו והמשיכה במקצוע זה לאחר שהייתה כאן. הייתה לה המון ניסיון בגידול עשבים ובהכנת תרופות צמחיות. ייתכן שהייתה הקרובה ביותר לדמות של רופא למרחקים של מיילים רבים סביב. לפי מה ששמעתי, הקדישה את זמנה להיות ברכה לקהילה המקומית עם ידיעתה וחכמתה הרפואית, תרופות ביתיות מעשביה ומקצועה כמיילדת. רבים מאבותינו במחוז לנקסטר לא היו שורדים את חיי המגֵן הקשים אלמלא הייתה רוח השירות וידיעת הרפואה של אחותנו היקרה הזו. מעניין שלהמשך השנים אחד מבניו של הנס מאשתו השנייה, דיוויד גרוף, נסע ללמוד רפואה. בסיום לימודיו חזר כרופא ועזר לאשתו הראשונה של אביו לשרת את המתיישבים הרבים במחוז לנקסטר שהלך וגדל במהירות.

סיפור זה מציע הצצה לכמה מהפרטים המרתקים סביב חייהם של אנבפטיסטים שמרניים ממש לפני ובמהלך הקמת אמריקה הקולוניאלית. היו קשיים בנוגע לחופש הדת והפולחן בארצות מולדתם באירופה, אבל מסעם אל מול היומיום החדש והרפתקני בארץ חופשית הציג גם אתגרים. עידוד אחד שאנו יכולים לראות בסיפור זה היה נכונותם של אנשים אלה לאפשר לעקרונותיו של אלוהים להנחות אותם בכל צעד ושעל.

That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling… –Ephesians 1:17-18.

We all have things we pursue in many aspects of our life. We all need to spend time fulfilling our responsibilities at work and at home. As Anabaptist people, we are known to possess a solid work ethic; but that is not all there is to living the Christian life. We may fellowship with likeminded believers from our church or community, but does our Christian life consist of anything more? Does practically living out our Christian life just mean being a member of our church and having personal devotions every day? Are we free to spend most of our day pursuing things that bring worldly gain? Perhaps we think that we need to spend some time as a volunteer or as a missionary in order to have more value in the Kingdom of Heaven.

What is purpose? Do you have purpose? Everyone has things they pursue, whether it is preparing themselves for a certain sport, pursuing a career, or devoting time to a certain hobby. An athlete spends many hours preparing himself for the goal he has set. An individual studying to become a doctor sacrifices many hours of his time with the goal of becoming a physician. What are the things you are pursuing, and do you have a specific goal in mind? More importantly, let’s examine whether the time we are investing in our pursuits now will bring an eternal return.

God has given each of us a responsibility

In Luke 19 is the parable of the nobleman giving his servants talents to invest. Consider the charge he gave his servants in verse 13. He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return. And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come –Luke 19:12-13.

This parable applies to each one of us. Each of us has different responsibilities, from filling our responsibilities at home, to administrative roles in a place of business. While we do not all own equal responsibilities, we have all been given “talents” to use. We all have a place to fill. We should be making the best of the resources we have been given to invest in the Kingdom of Heaven.

Back to my question, “Does living our Christian life just mean being a member of our church and having personal devotions once a day?” If the Lord has given each of us resources to invest, then we need to consider what we are doing with the time we are given every day. Often, we can budget plenty of time pursuing materialistic things such as hunting, sports, vehicles, etc. While all these things can be useful and healthy, do the things we are pursuing have eternal gain? We don’t seem to be afraid to devote hours of our time on our latest project, however it seems we have a hard time finding a place in our schedule for God’s work.

Personal responsibility

It is easy to have the mindset that, unless we are sacrificing our time in some voluntary capacity in a mission-oriented place, then there is not a lot more than can be done for the Kingdom of Heaven. Is that the reality though? Like the servants in the parable, we have each been given resources that we need to “occupy till the Lord returns”. The Lord has placed each of us in a unique place to serve in His kingdom, whether it is at home, on the job, or on the mission field. We have opportunities around us to exercise those gifts and show the love of Christ. The consideration should be whether I am actually seeing those opportunities or missing them because I am not looking for them. The more time we prioritize serving His Kingdom, the more we will see the needs around us. Remember, there are people around us every day that we can influence for God.

Recognizing our opportunities

Some time ago, I had a coworker come to my office and ask me a simple technical question. I was able to answer the question and work resumed as normal. But I had to wonder why he left the shop and came to me. He was within talking distance of multiple other individuals that would have been able to answer his question. Looking back, I realized that I had an opportunity to provide a listening ear and some caring words for this individual. He was facing some serious personal and relational challenges in life, and he needed someone who cared for him. I realized that there was probably a deeper reason he went out of his way to find an answer to his question. Was I the only one there that could have listened and shared with him? Certainly not. It was an opportunity for me. I could have chosen to be annoyed at him because he was taking up my time for something that someone else could have helped him with. But the question is—did I have the humility to recognize that it was an opportunity for me to reach out to him?

Where do I start?

We all have opportunities around us to exercise our talents. Jesus said: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men –Matthew 5:13. Salt always affects its environment no matter what it is used for. If we are compared to salt, then we should be affecting the environment around us all the time. Our Christian life then becomes more than simply going to church or spending some personal time praying and reading the Bible.

Start by asking God to help you see areas where you can serve others in everyday life. You have an opportunity to impact the lives of those around you. It might be your family, coworkers, customers, or people you meet while away from home. The point is, you have the opportunity around you to offer someone help, to encourage them, or to give them a hand. Are you making the best of those opportunities?

Another thing you should do is evaluate your personal life and the time you spend doing other activities. Are there things you are doing which take up your time and that have no benefit in the Kingdom of God? Maybe God has given you a gift that you are hiding instead of using to invest in His Kingdom. Do you spend time praying and seeking God’s will for your life? Do you spend time studying the Word of God? When our personal time with God becomes a higher priority for us, then our time spent pursuing God’s Kingdom will also become a higher priority. Is there sin hindering you from living out your Christian life? Confess it. Repent of it. Then… Go, and sin no more!

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God –Hebrews 12:1-2.

In the beginning of the article, I asked what you are pursuing. Does your life show that fulfilling God’s will is your highest priority, or is there something else that takes that spot? Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost –Romans 15:13. There are people around us that do not have the hope of a better, future life to strive for that we do. It is up to us to share that with others. Ask God for His Spirit to guide you and show you your opportunities. You cannot sit back and wait for the opportunities to come to you; you need to go find them. Go light your world!

Att vår Herre Jesu Kristi Gud, härlighetens Fader, må ge er ande av vishet och uppenbarelse i kunskapen om honom: att upplysa era hjärtas ögon; att ni må veta vad som är hoppet av hans kallelse… –Efesierbrevet 1:17-18.

Vi har alla saker vi eftersträvar i många aspekter av våra liv. Vi behöver alla ägna tid åt att fullgöra våra ansvar på arbetet och i hemmet. Som anabaptistiska människor är vi kända för att ha en stark arbetsmoral; men det är inte allt i det kristna livet. Vi kan ha gemenskap med likasinnade troende från vår kyrka eller vårt samhälle, men består vårt kristna liv av något mer? Betyder det praktiska leverandet av vårt kristna liv bara att vara medlem i vår kyrka och ha personliga andakter varje dag? Är vi fria att tillbringa större delen av vår dag med att eftersträva saker som ger världslig vinning? Kanske tänker vi att vi behöver ägna tid som volontär eller som missionär för att ha mer värde i himmelriket.

Vad är syfte? Har du ett syfte? Alla har saker de strävar efter, vare sig det är att förbereda sig för en viss sport, sikta på en karriär eller ägna tid åt en viss hobby. En idrottsman spenderar många timmar för att förbereda sig för det mål han satt upp. En person som studerar till läkare offrar många timmar av sin tid med målet att bli läkare. Vilka är de saker du eftersträvar, och har du ett specifikt mål i sikte? Viktigare är att vi undersöker om den tid vi nu investerar i våra strävanden kommer att ge en evig avkastning.

Gud har gett oss var och en ett ansvar

I Lukasevangeliet 19 finns liknelsen om fursten som gav sina tjänare talenter att förvalta. Tänk på det uppdrag han gav sina tjänare i vers 13. Han sade därför: En viss furste for bort till främmande land för att taga till sig ett rike och sedan återkomma. Och när han kallade sina tio tjänare gav han dem tio penningar och sade till dem: Förvärva intill dess jag kommer –Lukas 19:12-13.

Denna liknelse gäller var och en av oss. Vi har alla olika ansvarsområden, från att fylla våra ansvar i hemmet till administrativa roller i ett företag. Fast vi inte alla har lika stora ansvar, har vi alla fått “talanger” att bruka. Vi har alla en plats att fylla. Vi bör göra det bästa av de resurser vi fått för att investera i himmelriket.

Tillbaka till min fråga: ”Betyder det kristna livet bara att vara medlem i vår kyrka och ha personliga andakter en gång om dagen?” Om Herren har gett var och en av oss resurser att investera, måste vi överväga vad vi gör med den tid vi får varje dag. Ofta kan vi avsätta gott om tid åt materiella ting såsom jakt, sporter, fordon med mera. Medan alla dessa ting kan vara nyttiga och hälsosamma, har det vi eftersträvar evig vinning? Vi verkar inte vara rädda för att ägna timmar åt vårt senaste projekt, men det verkar som om vi har svårt att hitta en plats i vårt schema för Guds verk.

Personligt ansvar

Det är lätt att ha inställningen att om vi inte offrar vår tid i någon frivillig kapacitet på en missionsinriktad plats, så finns det inte mycket mer att göra för himmelriket. Är det verkligen verkligheten? Liksom tjänarna i liknelsen har var och en av oss fått resurser som vi måste “tjäna med intill dess Herren kommer”. Herren har placerat var och en av oss i en unik plats att tjäna i sitt rike, vare sig det är hemma, på jobbet eller på missionsfältet. Vi har möjligheter omkring oss att använda de gåvorna och visa Kristi kärlek. Frågan bör vara om jag faktiskt ser dessa möjligheter eller missar dem för att jag inte letar efter dem. Ju mer tid vi prioriterar att tjäna hans rike, desto mer kommer vi att se behoven omkring oss. Kom ihåg att det finns människor omkring oss varje dag som vi kan påverka för Gud.

Att känna igen våra möjligheter

För en tid sedan kom en kollega in på mitt kontor och ställde en enkel teknisk fråga. Jag kunde svara på frågan och arbetet fortsatte som vanligt. Men jag undrade varför han lämnade verkstaden och kom till mig. Han stod inom samtalsavstånd från flera andra personer som hade kunnat svara på hans fråga. När jag i efterhand tänkte på det insåg jag att jag hade en möjlighet att erbjuda ett lyssnande öra och några omtänksamma ord till denne person. Han stod inför allvarliga personliga och relationsmässiga utmaningar i livet, och han behövde någon som brydde sig om honom. Jag insåg att det förmodligen fanns en djupare anledning till att han gick ut ur sin väg för att få svar på sin fråga. Var jag den enda där som kunde ha lyssnat och delat med honom? Sannerligen inte. Det var en möjlighet för mig. Jag kunde ha valt att bli irriterad på honom eftersom han tog av min tid för något som någon annan kunde ha hjälpt honom med. Men frågan är – hade jag ödmjukheten att se att det var en möjlighet för mig att ta kontakt med honom?

Var börjar jag?

Vi har alla möjligheter omkring oss att använda våra talanger. Jesus sade: Ni är jordens salt. Men om saltet mister sin sälta, hur skall man åter göra det salt? Det duger därefter varken till jord eller till gödsel, utan man kastar ut det – Matteus 5:13. Salt påverkar alltid sin omgivning oavsett vad det används till. Om vi jämförs med salt, då bör vi påverka vår omgivning hela tiden. Vårt kristna liv blir då mer än att bara gå i kyrkan eller ägna lite personlig tid åt bön och Bibelläsning.

Börja med att be Gud hjälpa dig att se områden där du kan tjäna andra i vardagen. Du har en möjlighet att påverka livet för dem omkring dig. Det kan vara din familj, kollegor, kunder eller människor du möter när du är bortrest. Poängen är att du har möjligheter omkring dig att erbjuda någon hjälp, uppmuntra dem eller ge dem en hand. Utnyttjar du dessa möjligheter på bästa sätt?

En annan sak du bör göra är att utvärdera ditt personliga liv och den tid du ägnar åt andra aktiviteter. Finns det saker du gör som tar upp din tid och som inte har någon nytta i Guds rike? Kanske har Gud gett dig en gåva som du gömmer istället för att använda för att investera i hans rike. Tillbringar du tid i bön och söker Guds vilja för ditt liv? Tillbringar du tid med att studera Guds Ord? När vår personliga tid med Gud blir en högre prioritet för oss, kommer också vår tid att ägna oss åt att söka Guds rike att bli en högre prioritet. Finns det synd som hindrar dig från att leva ut ditt kristna liv? Bekänn den. Omvänd dig från den. Sedan… Gå bort och synda inte mer!

Vi se då omkring oss på en så stor skara vittnen, låt oss lägga bort allt som tynger och synden som så lätt slår an, och låt oss springa uthålligt i kampen som ligger framför oss, med blicken fäst vid Jesus, trons upphovsman och fullkomnare, som för den glädje som låg framför honom uthärdade korset, och satte skam åt det, och tog plats på Guds trons högra sida –Hebreerbrevet 12:1-2.

I början av artikeln frågade jag vad du eftersträvar. Visar ditt liv att att uppfylla Guds vilja är din högsta prioritet, eller finns det något annat som tar den platsen? Men må hoppets Gud fylla er med all glädje och frid i tron, så att ni överflödar i hopp genom den helige Andes kraft –Romarbrevet 15:13. Det finns människor omkring oss som inte har det hopp om ett bättre framtida liv att sträva efter som vi har. Det är upp till oss att dela det med andra. Be Gud om hans Ande att leda dig och visa dig dina möjligheter. Du kan inte bara sitta tillbaka och vänta på att möjligheterna kommer till dig; du måste gå och hitta dem. Gå och tänd ditt ljus i världen!
