As we discussed in the first part of this two-part series, cancer is not a single entity. Various cancers have general similarities in that they develop from normal cells which mutate to make them grow in an uncontrolled, unnatural fashion, yet each type of cancer behaves in its specific, unique way.

Some cancers are aggressive, and some are much slower growing. Some tend to be localized and are quite slow to spread to other parts of the body, whereas others are likely to show up in locations far from where they began.

It is not possible to make blanket statements about cancers, but in this section, I will discuss some general things about prevention and treatment, then I’ll finish with some thoughts about us as Christians relating to someone who is dealing with cancer.

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

Many of the things that increase the risk of cancer are things that (hopefully) we, as Christian people, are already avoiding.

Tobacco is one such thing. Tobacco, when smoked, increases the risk of lung cancer. It also increases the risk of head cancer, neck cancers, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, and cancers of the liver and bladder.

Alcohol is another substance that raises the risk of cancer. Liver, voice box, and esophagus cancers are all related to alcohol consumption. Some people claim to drink alcohol for “health benefits,” but there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. Even people who drink moderately have an increased risk of death related to their alcohol usage.i

Another thing that should be limited is exposure to ultraviolet radiation. We know that UV radiation increases the risk of skin cancers, so wearing clothing that protects, such as hats and long-sleeved garments, and using sunblock can reduce this risk.

On the positive side of things, healthy eating habits, such as consuming lots of fruits and vegetables and avoiding highly processed foods, will reduce the risk of colon cancer.ii Fiber seems to be a key here and higher levels of dietary fiber are helpful. Additionally, fruits and vegetables are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals and are supportive of a healthy immune system. It is recommended to eat at least two servings of fruit and five servings of vegetables per day.

It is interesting that while people who eat healthy diets have a decreased risk of cancer, there is little evidence that there are specific vitamins that will prevent cancer. That is, there is little benefit if you eat a very unhealthy diet and then take vitamins in an effort to compensate for your unwise choices.

Prior to doing a controlled test it is always hard to know whether or not a certain supplement will help. Vitamin E is an antioxidant and so it was thought to be helpful in the prevention of cancer. However, it turns out that studies have not shown this to be true. Actually, in high doses, it seems to increase the risk of certain cancers and heart disease.iii

Rather than trying to find the right supplements, it is more important to make certain that we are eating healthy diets.

Chemotherapy

Now, let us move to a brief discussion about different types of treatment for cancer. Chemotherapy is probably what most people think of first. It was first used in the 1940s when doctors used a derivative of nitrogen mustard to treat lymphoma.

Since that time, hundreds of different medications have been developed as chemotherapy, designed to attack the cancer cells. It is hard to generalize about chemotherapy because there are so many different medications designed to treat different cancers and because they have different side effects.

Due to the fact that they attack cells that are rapidly multiplying, many of these drugs tend to make a person’s hair fall out since hair cells are of the rapidly multiplying type. Nausea, vomiting, and blood count alterations (low white cell counts) are other common side effects.

If a cancer has spread from its initial location, chances are good that it will require more than just one type of medication in order to achieve remission.

Even if a cancer hasn’t spread, surgeons will often recommend doing some chemotherapy ahead of surgery to shrink the tumor and to make surgical removal easier.

While chemotherapy sounds scary, it actually works quite well for certain types of cancers, such as blood cancers (like leukemias), lymphoma, and breast cancer.

These days, cancer doctors test the biopsied cancer cells for genetic markers. As a family doctor, I see these reports but, since I am not a specialist in this field, I find them somewhat confusing. The important thing to remember is that these markers help to predict what the best drugs are to use on a specific type of cancer.

Surgery

For many years, surgery was the cornerstone of cancer treatment. Cancers that have not spread can be removed entirely, allowing a person to move forward without any further treatment.

Often, by the time that a person’s cancer is discovered, it is too late to completely remove it. Surgery can still be helpful. For one thing, it gives a sample of the cancer for testing to help identify the best treatment. More than that, even if a cancer has spread, there are times that a tumor needs to be removed, simply because of the organs that it is putting pressure on.

I have heard some people claim that it is dangerous for a cancer to be exposed to oxygen. They believe that cancer cells spread faster after the tissues are opened up and exposed to the air during surgery. There is no documented evidence to support this idea. Many people do seem to get sicker after having an exploratory surgery when their cancer is being diagnosed. But the issue isn’t really the air getting into the cancer cells, rather the cancer was most certainly at the point of beginning to exhibit serious symptoms, and the surgery simply brought things to a head. Also, any surgery will be stressful for any person’s body, which will only increase the wearing down of a person’s already taxed strength and vitality—their ability to stay on top of a debilitating illness.

Typically, when a tumor is removed, nearby lymph glands will be sampled to see if they contain cancer cells. This presence, or absence, of cells helps with the “staging” of the cancer (such as “stage 3” or “stage 4”) and will provide insight for further treatment to prevent a chance of recurrence.

Immunotherapy

One of the newest treatments of cancer is called immunotherapy. These are medications that rev up a patient’s immune system to clear their body of cancer cells.

This sounds great and you would think the side effects should be minimal. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always work according to plan. Some cancers don’t respond to these sorts of treatments. And as far as side effects go, these medications can result in autoimmune diseases. When a medication is prescribed that makes the immune system extra active (or over-active), sometimes it begins to attack the patient’s own organs. While some of these side effects get better with the cessation of treatment, not all of them go away.

As an example, I had a patient who took immunotherapy for melanoma that had spread to his lymph glands. He was cured of the cancer, but the immunotherapy damaged his saliva glands enough that he has ongoing issues with a dry mouth. At this point, it seems unlikely that he will regain that moisture in his mouth.

Future Treatments

There will probably be more treatments in the future, targeting specific types of cancers. Something that is currently under investigation are vaccines that would target specific types of cancers. Currently none of these are available except in clinical trials.

Choosing Wisely

Oncologists (cancer specialists) do not know the future. They talk in terms of percentages. One protocol has an 86 percent chance of achieving a two-year remission from cancer, another only 56 percent. The same thing is true for side effects. While a doctor can tell you that 26 percent of patients get nauseated with a treatment, that doesn’t tell you if you will be one of that 26 percent and whether that nausea will be controllable with anti-nausea medication.

In deciding what course of treatment to choose, you will find no Bible passage to indicate one direction or another. Having a good oncologist who will explain things carefully—both the chance of success and risk of side effects—is key. There are times that you may need to change to a different cancer doctor, simply because the one you have does not take the time that you need to feel comfortable with your treatment.

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. We need wisdom in many areas of our lives, but certainly choosing how to navigate medical decisions is one of those areas. It is a wonderful thing that God has promised to give us the wisdom that we need—if we just ask.

Prayer—both personal prayer and by your church community—is very important. Prayers can be for healing. It can also be for caring, Christian, medical caregivers, and for wisdom in choosing the best treatments.

Sometimes God cures through doctors and medications. Sometimes, He heals in spite of them. Sometimes He decides it is time for us to go home to be with Him, thereby providing us with a new body that is not sick and broken.

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. With all of the medical technology available to us, it is easy to forget that healing comes from God. All the chemotherapy in the world will not avail if God does not work an act of healing. At the same time, there are many times that God works in miraculous ways to heal despite the dire predictions made by the medical professionals or other well-meaning individuals.

Often the best that a patient can do is to choose (according to their best judgment) the best treatment course (based on success rate and side effects) and then see how things go. If the side effects are too severe or the treatment doesn’t seem to be working, there is always the option to change.

Ultimately, when healing comes, regardless of how it comes, it is God that provides that healing. Let us never forget that.

Cancer Takes Energy

Relating to someone with cancer is not much different from relating to a person with any other chronic illness. There are differences though.

Both having cancer and receiving treatment for the cancer takes a lot of energy out of a person. While it is important not to ignore someone who has cancer, it is just as important to remember that they do not have endless energy supplies. A ten- or fifteen-minute visit may be all that they can handle. It is best to let them decide the length of visits that they have energy for.

Hesitate to Give Advice

Your “cousin” may have had cancer and may have gotten better after taking a particular supplement or visiting a particular clinic. Sharing that information with a person who is dealing with cancer is just one more piece of information for them to process out of a “thousand” others they may have received. It seems as though someone with cancer is often bombarded with advice and recommendations from well-meaning friends and family.

It is hard to figure out what the best thing is to do when a person is already low on energy. Sometimes, cancer patients simply have prayed that God would bless their choices and then have left the outcome in His hands.

If the cancer patient asks for your input, you can give it, but if not, it is probably best to hold off on the temptation to give unsought advice.

Listen

There is never a situation where listening isn’t beneficial. It is through listening that we allow others to unburden themselves from fears and frustrations. Listening can help the person to put their thoughts into words. More than that, we may hear ways in which we can help.

Maybe it is someone telling you the (too long) story of how their doctor missed their cancer. Or perhaps, it is them telling you about their fears regarding either their cancer or their treatments.

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. This verse comes in the midst of James talking about anointing with oil, confession of sins, and physical healing.

We can certainly pray for, and with, someone who is dealing with cancer. Listening helps us to know how best we can pray for them. It lets us know what their particular struggle is on a given day and how we can best lift them up to the throne.

The passage in James makes it clear that healing does not come from the oil that is poured over someone, but rather from God’s work in their life. The prayer, the faith, and the obedient action is more important than the anointing oil, although all demonstrate a dependence on a God who is always faithful.

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

If it is not enough to pray for someone who is dealing with a serious illness, it is certainly not enough to tell them, “God bless you.”

Figuring out what things someone with cancer needs help with may not be easy, but often even little tasks are difficult for them. It could be that they need transportation to a chemotherapy appointment. Maybe they need help with making a meal, with childcare, or with cleaning their house. Helping in whatever ways we can makes a huge difference for those who are dealing with the fatigue and stress of cancer.

More than that, the important thing is that we make the effort to demonstrate our love to those in our church body who are suffering. Paul told the Corinthians that when …one member suffer[s], all the members suffer with it… –1 Corinthians 12:26. Whenever there is a need, the rest of the local church body has an obligation and should have a deep desire to help in whatever way they can.

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

Chemotherapy can cause a cancer patient to have an extremely weak immune system. A normal white cell count is between 4,000 and 10,000. but during cancer treatments I have seen patient’s white cell count drop down to 200. In this scenario, if they catch any type of infection, they will be unable to fight off that infection and will end up in the hospital.

It is important to understand that someone in this condition who chooses to keep their distance is not necessarily trying to avoid fellowship. Rather, they are trying to avoid an unneeded hospital stay for what cancer doctors call a “neutropenic fever” (a febrile illness with a really low white cell count).

In these sorts of situations, phone calls or even text messages go a long way toward helping a brother or sister feel that they are not alone, even when they cannot physically be around other people.

Conclusion

I wish I could give a complete run down of every type of cancer out there and the best treatment for each one. That would be beyond my capability and further, it would be outdated within six months’ time.

What I can say is that prayer is key. Prayer for the Holy Spirit’s leading (see John 16:13), for energy for each day, for healing, and for God’s will to be done. Most of all, we need to pray that God would be glorified in and through us. (See 1 Peter 4:11) There have been so many people who were able to speak to their nurses and doctors about their Lord, even as they dealt with side effects and cancer symptoms.

It is easy to read all the instructions about giving up worrying that is found in Scripture and think that it should be easy to cast our cares on Him (see 1 Peter 5:7). However, it is much harder to put into practice. We may feel one day as though we have conquered fear and wake up the next morning with every bit as much anxiety as we ever had.

It is in this that we desperately need a church community. We are not alone, but we will feel alone unless we have brothers and sisters around us who help us as they are able and who pray for us in our valleys and rejoice with us in our times of victory.

It is only then, that we can come to the place that the Apostle Paul did when he said, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. Of course, he was talking about a possible execution, but his resignation to God’s will was total. I pray that we too might reach that place, even as we deal with something as difficult as cancer.

Как мы обсуждали в первой части этой двухсерийной публикации, рак не является единым заболеванием. Различные виды рака имеют общие сходства в том, что они развиваются из нормальных клеток, которые мутируют и начинают расти неконтролируемо, ненормальным образом, тем не менее каждый тип рака ведёт себя по‑своему, специфически и уникально.

Некоторые раки агрессивны, а некоторые растут гораздо медленнее. Некоторые, как правило, локализованы и довольно медленно распространяются в другие части тела, тогда как другие с большой вероятностью появляются в местах, отдалённых от места их возникновения.

Нельзя делать общие утверждения обо всех раках, но в этом разделе я обсужу некоторые общие вещи о профилактике и лечении, а в завершение поделюсь мыслями о том, как нам, христианам, относиться к человеку, борющемуся с раком.

Изменения образа жизни для предотвращения рака

Многие факторы, которые повышают риск рака, — это то, от чего (надеюсь) мы, как христиане, уже воздерживаемся.

Табак — один из таких факторов. Курение табака увеличивает риск рака лёгких. Оно также повышает риск онкологических заболеваний головы, шеи, пищевода, желудка, а также печени и мочевого пузыря.

Алкоголь — ещё одно вещество, повышающее риск развития рака. Рак печени, гортани и пищевода связан с потреблением алкоголя. Некоторые люди утверждают, что пьют алкоголь «ради пользы для здоровья», но не существует безопасного уровня употребления алкоголя. Даже люди, употребляющие алкоголь в умеренных количествах, имеют повышенный риск смерти, связанной с его употреблением.i

Ещё один фактор, который следует ограничить, — это воздействие ультрафиолетового излучения. Мы знаем, что УФ‑излучение повышает риск рака кожи, поэтому ношение защитной одежды, такой как шляпы и одежда с длинными рукавами, а также использование солнцезащитных средств может снизить этот риск.

С положительной стороны, здоровые пищевые привычки, такие как употребление большого количества фруктов и овощей и избегание сильно переработанных продуктов, снизят риск рака толстой кишки.ii Ключевую роль, по-видимому, играет клетчатка, и более высокое потребление пищевых волокон полезно. Кроме того фрукты и овощи богаты антиоксидантами, витаминами и минералами и поддерживают здоровую иммунную систему. Рекомендуется съедать по крайней мере два порции фруктов и пять порций овощей в день.

Интересно, что в то время как у людей, питающихся здорово, риск рака снижен, есть мало доказательств того, что какие‑то конкретные витамины предотвращают рак. То есть мало пользы, если вы едите очень нездоровую пищу, а затем принимаете витамины в попытке компенсировать свои неблагоразумные выборы.

До проведения контролируемого теста всегда трудно знать, поможет ли тот или иной препарат. Витамин Е — антиоксидант, и считалось, что он полезен для предотвращения рака. Однако исследования не подтвердили этого. На самом деле в больших дозах он, похоже, увеличивает риск некоторых видов рака и сердечных заболеваний.iii

Вместо попыток подобрать «правильные» добавки важно прежде всего питаться здоровой пищей.

Химиотерапия

Перейдём к краткому обсуждению различных видов лечения рака. Химиотерапия — это то, о чём большинство людей думает в первую очередь. Впервые её стали применять в 1940‑х годах, когда врачи использовали производное азотной горчицы для лечения лимфомы.

С тех пор были разработаны сотни различных препаратов в качестве химиотерапии, предназначенных для атаки раковых клеток. Трудно обобщать про химиотерапию, потому что существует так много различных препаратов для лечения разных видов рака и у них разные побочные эффекты.

Поскольку они атакуют быстро размножающиеся клетки, многие из этих препаратов вызывают выпадение волос, так как клетки волос также быстро делятся. Тошнота, рвота и изменения в показателях крови (низкий уровень белых кровяных телец) — другие распространённые побочные эффекты.

Если рак распространился из места своего возникновения, вероятно, потребуется более одного вида препарата, чтобы добиться ремиссии.

Даже если рак не распространился, хирурги нередко рекомендуют проведение химиотерапии до операции, чтобы уменьшить опухоль и облегчить её хирургическое удаление.

Хотя химиотерапия звучит устрашающе, на самом деле она хорошо помогает при некоторых видах рака, таких как заболевания крови (например, лейкемии), лимфома и рак молочной железы.

В наши дни онкологи тестируют биопсийные образцы раковых клеток на генетические маркеры. Как семейный врач, я вижу эти отчёты, но, поскольку я не специалист в этой области, они иногда кажутся мне запутанными. Важно помнить, что эти маркёры помогают предсказать, какие препараты будут наилучшими для лечения конкретного типа рака.

Хирургия

В течение многих лет хирургия была краеугольным камнем лечения рака. Рак, который не распространился, можно полностью удалить, позволив человеку двигаться дальше без дополнительного лечения.

Часто к моменту обнаружения рака его уже невозможно полностью удалить. Операция всё равно может быть полезной. Во‑первых, она даёт образец опухоли для тестирования, чтобы определить наилучшее лечение. Более того, даже если рак распространился, иногда опухоль необходимо удалить просто потому, что она давит на жизненно важные органы.

Я слышал от некоторых людей утверждение, что опасно подвергать опухоль контакту с кислородом. Они полагают, что раковые клетки распространяются быстрее после того, как ткани вскрыты и контактируют с воздухом во время операции. Нет документальных доказательств в поддержку этой идеи. Многие действительно чувствуют себя хуже после диагностической операции, когда у них выявляют рак. Но дело не в том, что воздух «попал» в раковые клетки, а в том, что рак, по всей видимости, уже начал давать серьёзные симптомы, и операция просто ускорила проявление этих симптомов. Кроме того, любая операция стрессирует организм, что дополнительно истощает силы человека и его способность справляться с изнурительным заболеванием.

Обычно при удалении опухоли берут на анализ близлежащие лимфатические узлы, чтобы проверить наличие раковых клеток. Это присутствие или отсутствие клеток помогает в «стадировании» рака (например, «стадия 3» или «стадия 4») и даёт представление о дальнейших шагах лечения для предотвращения рецидива.

Иммунотерапия

Один из новейших методов лечения рака называется иммунотерапией. Это препараты, которые «заводят» иммунную систему пациента, чтобы она очищала организм от раковых клеток.

Звучит прекрасно, и можно было бы ожидать минимальных побочных эффектов. К сожалению, всё не всегда идёт по плану. Некоторые виды рака не реагируют на такие методы. Что касается побочных эффектов, эти препараты могут вызывать аутоиммунные заболевания. Когда препарат делает иммунную систему чрезмерно активной, она иногда начинает атаковать собственные органы пациента. Некоторые побочные эффекты ослабевают после прекращения лечения, но не все исчезают полностью.

Например, у меня был пациент, который получал иммунотерапию при меланоме, распространившейся на лимфатические узлы. Он был излечен от рака, но иммунотерапия повредила его слюнные железы настолько, что у него постоянно сухость во рту. По нынешним данным маловероятно, что влажность в его рту восстановится.

Будущие методы лечения

Вероятно, в будущем появится больше методов лечения, нацеленных на конкретные типы рака. В настоящее время исследуются вакцины, которые могли бы нацеливаться на определённые виды рака. В настоящее время ни одна из них не доступна, кроме как в клинических испытаниях.

Обдуманный выбор

Онкологи (специалисты по раку) не знают будущего. Они говорят языком процентов. Одна схема лечения даёт 86‑процентную вероятность достижения двухлетней ремиссии, другая — только 56‑процентную. То же самое относится и к побочным эффектам. Врач может сказать, что 26 процентов пациентов испытывают тошноту при лечении, но это не скажет вам, будете ли вы одним из этих 26 процентов и будет ли эта тошнота контролироваться противорвотными средствами.

При принятии решения о курсе лечения в Библии вы не найдёте указания в ту или иную сторону. Важно иметь хорошего онколога, который тщательно объяснит и шансы на успех, и риски побочных эффектов. Иногда нужно сменить врача, просто потому что ваш врач не уделяет времени, необходимого вам, чтобы вы почувствовали себя уверенно в выбранном лечении.

Если же у кого из вас недостает мудрости, да просит у Бога, дающего всем просто и без упрёка, и дастся ему — Иакова 1:5. Нам нужна мудрость во многих областях жизни, и, безусловно, выбор пути в медицинских вопросах — одна из таких областей. Прекрасно, что Бог обещал дать нам нужную мудрость, если мы просто попросим.

Молитва — как личная, так и от лица церковного сообщества — очень важна. Молиться можно о исцелении, о заботливых христианских медицинских работниках и о мудрости при выборе наилучших методов лечения.

Иногда Бог исцеляет через врачей и лекарства. Иногда Он исцеляет вопреки ним. Иногда Он решает, что пришло время идти домой к Нему, даруя нам новое тело, не болеющее и не сломанное.

Благослови, душа моя, Господа, и не забывай всех благодеяний Его: Он прощает все беззакония твои; Он исцеляет все болезни твои — Псалом 103:2-3. При всём наличии современной медицинской техники легко забыть, что исцеление исходит от Бога. Вся химиотерапия мира не поможет, если Бог не совершит акт исцеления. В то же время нередко Бог действует чудесным образом, исцеляя вопреки мрачным прогнозам врачей или других доброжелательных людей.

Часто лучшее, что пациент может сделать, — это выбрать (по своей лучшей оценке) наилучший курс лечения (основываясь на вероятности успеха и побочных эффектах) и посмотреть, как пойдут дела. Если побочные эффекты слишком тяжёлы или лечение не даёт эффекта, всегда есть возможность сменить курс.

В конечном счёте, когда приходит исцеление, независимо от того, каким путём оно пришло, это Бог даёт это исцеление. Не будем об этом забывать.

Рак отнимает силы

Отношения с человеком, у которого рак, во многом не отличаются от отношений с человеком, больным другим хроническим заболеванием. Тем не менее есть различия.

И само наличие рака, и его лечение отнимают у человека много сил. Хотя важно не игнорировать человека с раком, также важно помнить, что его ресурсы энергии ограничены. Десяти- или пятнадцатиминутного визита может быть всё, что он сможет выдержать. Лучше позволить ему самому решать, какой длительности визиты он может выдержать.

Не спешите давать советы

Ваш «двоюродный брат» мог болеть раком и, возможно, поправился после приёма определённой добавки или посещения того или иного клиники. Поделиться этой информацией с человеком, который борется с раком, — это ещё один фрагмент информации среди «тысячи» других, которые он, возможно, уже получил. Людей с раком часто заваливают советами и рекомендациями от доброжелательных друзей и родственников.

Трудно решить, что лучше делать, когда у человека и так мало сил. Иногда пациенты просто молятся, прося Бога благословить их выборы, и оставляют исход в Его руках.

Если пациент просит вашего совета, вы можете его дать, но если не просит, лучше удержаться от соблазна навязывать непрошеные рекомендации.

Слушайте

Всегда полезно выслушать. Через слушание мы позволяем другим освободиться от страхов и разочарований. Слушание помогает человеку выразить свои мысли словами. Более того, мы можем услышать, чем можем помочь.

Возможно, это будет слишком длинный рассказ о том, как врач пропустил у них рак. А может быть, они расскажут о своих страхах, связанных с раком или лечением.

Молитесь

Молитва праведника, имеющая силу, много может — Иакова 5:16. Этот стих стоит в тексте Иакова, где речь идёт об елеосвящении, исповеди и телесном исцелении.

Мы, безусловно, можем молиться за человека, борющегося с раком, и молиться вместе с ним. Слушание помогает нам понять, о чём конкретно молиться в тот или иной день и как лучше вознести их к Престолу.

Отрывок у Иакова показывает, что исцеление не исходит от самого елея, которым помазывают человека, а от Божьего действия в его жизни. Молитва, вера и послушное действие важнее самого помазания елеем, хотя и помазание демонстрирует зависимость от Бога, который верен всегда.

Помогайте с мелкими делами

Если брат или сестра нагие и лишены ежедневной пищи, и кто‑нибудь из вас скажет им: идите с миром, грейтесь и насыщайтесь; но не даст им необходимых для тела вещей — что пользы? — Иакова 2:15-16.

Если молитвы за человека, страдающего серьёзной болезнью, недостаточны, то недостаточно и просто сказать: «Бог благослови тебя.»

Иногда трудно понять, в чём именно нуждается больной раком, но часто даже небольшие дела даются ему с трудом. Это может быть подвоз на приём по поводу химиотерапии. Может понадобиться помощь с приготовлением еды, присмотром за детьми или уборкой дома. Помощь в любых посильных делах существенно облегчает жизнь тех, кто сталкивается с усталостью и стрессом вследствие рака.

Ещё важнее — проявить любовь к страдающим в нашем церковном собрании. Павел сказал коринфянам: Если один член страдает, все члены вместе с ним страдают… — 1 Коринфянам 12:26. Когда возникает нужда, остальная церковная община обязана и должна с желанием помогать, как только сможет.

Будьте готовы держаться на расстоянии

Химиотерапия может сделать иммунную систему пациента крайне ослабленной. Нормальный уровень лейкоцитов — между 4 000 и 10 000, но во время лечения я видел, как у пациентов уровень белых клеток падал до 200. В такой ситуации при любой инфекции они не смогут её побороть и окажутся в больнице.

Важно понимать, что человек в таком состоянии, который предпочитает держаться на расстоянии, не обязательно избегает общения. Он пытается избежать ненужной госпитализации из‑за того, что онкологи называют «нейтропенической лихорадкой» (лихорадочное состояние при очень низком уровне лейкоцитов).

В таких условиях телефонный звонок или даже текстовое сообщение очень помогают брату или сестре чувствовать, что они не одиноки, даже когда не могут физически находиться среди людей.

Заключение

Мне бы очень хотелось дать полный обзор каждого типа рака и лучшего лечения для каждого из них. Это было бы сверх моих возможностей и, кроме того, устарело бы в течение шести месяцев.

Что я могу сказать — молитва имеет ключевое значение. Молитесь о водительстве Святого Духа (ср. Иоанна 16:13), о силе на каждый день, о исцелении и о том, да будет воля Божья. Прежде всего молитесь, чтобы Бог прославился в нас и через нас (ср. 1 Петра 4:11). Было много людей, которые, даже сталкиваясь с побочными эффектами и симптомами рака, успевали говорить своим медсёстрам и врачам о своём Господе.

Легко прочитать наставления Писания о том, чтобы не заботиться (ср. 1 Петра 5:7), и подумать, что легко положить наши заботы на Него. На практике это гораздо труднее. В один день мы можем почувствовать, что победили страх, а проснуться на следующее утро с тем же беспокойством, что и раньше.

В этом нам крайне нужна церковная община. Мы не одиноки, но будем чувствовать себя одинокими, если рядом не будет братьев и сестер, которые помогают, чем могут, молятся за нас в наших долинах и радуются с нами в наших победах.

Только тогда мы можем прийти к тому месту, где был апостол Павел, когда сказал: Ибо для меня жизнь — Христос, а смерть — приобретение — Филиппийцам 1:21. Конечно, он говорил о возможной казни, но его преданность Божьей воле была полной. Молюсь, чтобы и мы достигли такой готовности, даже сталкиваясь с чем‑то таким трудным, как рак.

As we discussed in the first part of this two-part series, cancer is not a single entity. Various cancers have general similarities in that they develop from normal cells which mutate to make them grow in an uncontrolled, unnatural fashion, yet each type of cancer behaves in its specific, unique way.

Some cancers are aggressive, and some are much slower growing. Some tend to be localized and are quite slow to spread to other parts of the body, whereas others are likely to show up in locations far from where they began.

It is not possible to make blanket statements about cancers, but in this section, I will discuss some general things about prevention and treatment, then I’ll finish with some thoughts about us as Christians relating to someone who is dealing with cancer.

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

Many of the things that increase the risk of cancer are things that (hopefully) we, as Christian people, are already avoiding.

Tobacco is one such thing. Tobacco, when smoked, increases the risk of lung cancer. It also increases the risk of head cancer, neck cancers, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, and cancers of the liver and bladder.

Alcohol is another substance that raises the risk of cancer. Liver, voice box, and esophagus cancers are all related to alcohol consumption. Some people claim to drink alcohol for “health benefits,” but there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. Even people who drink moderately have an increased risk of death related to their alcohol usage.i

Another thing that should be limited is exposure to ultraviolet radiation. We know that UV radiation increases the risk of skin cancers, so wearing clothing that protects, such as hats and long-sleeved garments, and using sunblock can reduce this risk.

On the positive side of things, healthy eating habits, such as consuming lots of fruits and vegetables and avoiding highly processed foods, will reduce the risk of colon cancer.ii Fiber seems to be a key here and higher levels of dietary fiber are helpful. Additionally, fruits and vegetables are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals and are supportive of a healthy immune system. It is recommended to eat at least two servings of fruit and five servings of vegetables per day.

It is interesting that while people who eat healthy diets have a decreased risk of cancer, there is little evidence that there are specific vitamins that will prevent cancer. That is, there is little benefit if you eat a very unhealthy diet and then take vitamins in an effort to compensate for your unwise choices.

Prior to doing a controlled test it is always hard to know whether or not a certain supplement will help. Vitamin E is an antioxidant and so it was thought to be helpful in the prevention of cancer. However, it turns out that studies have not shown this to be true. Actually, in high doses, it seems to increase the risk of certain cancers and heart disease.iii

Rather than trying to find the right supplements, it is more important to make certain that we are eating healthy diets.

Chemotherapy

Now, let us move to a brief discussion about different types of treatment for cancer. Chemotherapy is probably what most people think of first. It was first used in the 1940s when doctors used a derivative of nitrogen mustard to treat lymphoma.

Since that time, hundreds of different medications have been developed as chemotherapy, designed to attack the cancer cells. It is hard to generalize about chemotherapy because there are so many different medications designed to treat different cancers and because they have different side effects.

Due to the fact that they attack cells that are rapidly multiplying, many of these drugs tend to make a person’s hair fall out since hair cells are of the rapidly multiplying type. Nausea, vomiting, and blood count alterations (low white cell counts) are other common side effects.

If a cancer has spread from its initial location, chances are good that it will require more than just one type of medication in order to achieve remission.

Even if a cancer hasn’t spread, surgeons will often recommend doing some chemotherapy ahead of surgery to shrink the tumor and to make surgical removal easier.

While chemotherapy sounds scary, it actually works quite well for certain types of cancers, such as blood cancers (like leukemias), lymphoma, and breast cancer.

These days, cancer doctors test the biopsied cancer cells for genetic markers. As a family doctor, I see these reports but, since I am not a specialist in this field, I find them somewhat confusing. The important thing to remember is that these markers help to predict what the best drugs are to use on a specific type of cancer.

Surgery

For many years, surgery was the cornerstone of cancer treatment. Cancers that have not spread can be removed entirely, allowing a person to move forward without any further treatment.

Often, by the time that a person’s cancer is discovered, it is too late to completely remove it. Surgery can still be helpful. For one thing, it gives a sample of the cancer for testing to help identify the best treatment. More than that, even if a cancer has spread, there are times that a tumor needs to be removed, simply because of the organs that it is putting pressure on.

I have heard some people claim that it is dangerous for a cancer to be exposed to oxygen. They believe that cancer cells spread faster after the tissues are opened up and exposed to the air during surgery. There is no documented evidence to support this idea. Many people do seem to get sicker after having an exploratory surgery when their cancer is being diagnosed. But the issue isn’t really the air getting into the cancer cells, rather the cancer was most certainly at the point of beginning to exhibit serious symptoms, and the surgery simply brought things to a head. Also, any surgery will be stressful for any person’s body, which will only increase the wearing down of a person’s already taxed strength and vitality—their ability to stay on top of a debilitating illness.

Typically, when a tumor is removed, nearby lymph glands will be sampled to see if they contain cancer cells. This presence, or absence, of cells helps with the “staging” of the cancer (such as “stage 3” or “stage 4”) and will provide insight for further treatment to prevent a chance of recurrence.

Immunotherapy

One of the newest treatments of cancer is called immunotherapy. These are medications that rev up a patient’s immune system to clear their body of cancer cells.

This sounds great and you would think the side effects should be minimal. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always work according to plan. Some cancers don’t respond to these sorts of treatments. And as far as side effects go, these medications can result in autoimmune diseases. When a medication is prescribed that makes the immune system extra active (or over-active), sometimes it begins to attack the patient’s own organs. While some of these side effects get better with the cessation of treatment, not all of them go away.

As an example, I had a patient who took immunotherapy for melanoma that had spread to his lymph glands. He was cured of the cancer, but the immunotherapy damaged his saliva glands enough that he has ongoing issues with a dry mouth. At this point, it seems unlikely that he will regain that moisture in his mouth.

Future Treatments

There will probably be more treatments in the future, targeting specific types of cancers. Something that is currently under investigation are vaccines that would target specific types of cancers. Currently none of these are available except in clinical trials.

Choosing Wisely

Oncologists (cancer specialists) do not know the future. They talk in terms of percentages. One protocol has an 86 percent chance of achieving a two-year remission from cancer, another only 56 percent. The same thing is true for side effects. While a doctor can tell you that 26 percent of patients get nauseated with a treatment, that doesn’t tell you if you will be one of that 26 percent and whether that nausea will be controllable with anti-nausea medication.

In deciding what course of treatment to choose, you will find no Bible passage to indicate one direction or another. Having a good oncologist who will explain things carefully—both the chance of success and risk of side effects—is key. There are times that you may need to change to a different cancer doctor, simply because the one you have does not take the time that you need to feel comfortable with your treatment.

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. We need wisdom in many areas of our lives, but certainly choosing how to navigate medical decisions is one of those areas. It is a wonderful thing that God has promised to give us the wisdom that we need—if we just ask.

Prayer—both personal prayer and by your church community—is very important. Prayers can be for healing. It can also be for caring, Christian, medical caregivers, and for wisdom in choosing the best treatments.

Sometimes God cures through doctors and medications. Sometimes, He heals in spite of them. Sometimes He decides it is time for us to go home to be with Him, thereby providing us with a new body that is not sick and broken.

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. With all of the medical technology available to us, it is easy to forget that healing comes from God. All the chemotherapy in the world will not avail if God does not work an act of healing. At the same time, there are many times that God works in miraculous ways to heal despite the dire predictions made by the medical professionals or other well-meaning individuals.

Often the best that a patient can do is to choose (according to their best judgment) the best treatment course (based on success rate and side effects) and then see how things go. If the side effects are too severe or the treatment doesn’t seem to be working, there is always the option to change.

Ultimately, when healing comes, regardless of how it comes, it is God that provides that healing. Let us never forget that.

Cancer Takes Energy

Relating to someone with cancer is not much different from relating to a person with any other chronic illness. There are differences though.

Both having cancer and receiving treatment for the cancer takes a lot of energy out of a person. While it is important not to ignore someone who has cancer, it is just as important to remember that they do not have endless energy supplies. A ten- or fifteen-minute visit may be all that they can handle. It is best to let them decide the length of visits that they have energy for.

Hesitate to Give Advice

Your “cousin” may have had cancer and may have gotten better after taking a particular supplement or visiting a particular clinic. Sharing that information with a person who is dealing with cancer is just one more piece of information for them to process out of a “thousand” others they may have received. It seems as though someone with cancer is often bombarded with advice and recommendations from well-meaning friends and family.

It is hard to figure out what the best thing is to do when a person is already low on energy. Sometimes, cancer patients simply have prayed that God would bless their choices and then have left the outcome in His hands.

If the cancer patient asks for your input, you can give it, but if not, it is probably best to hold off on the temptation to give unsought advice.

Listen

There is never a situation where listening isn’t beneficial. It is through listening that we allow others to unburden themselves from fears and frustrations. Listening can help the person to put their thoughts into words. More than that, we may hear ways in which we can help.

Maybe it is someone telling you the (too long) story of how their doctor missed their cancer. Or perhaps, it is them telling you about their fears regarding either their cancer or their treatments.

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. This verse comes in the midst of James talking about anointing with oil, confession of sins, and physical healing.

We can certainly pray for, and with, someone who is dealing with cancer. Listening helps us to know how best we can pray for them. It lets us know what their particular struggle is on a given day and how we can best lift them up to the throne.

The passage in James makes it clear that healing does not come from the oil that is poured over someone, but rather from God’s work in their life. The prayer, the faith, and the obedient action is more important than the anointing oil, although all demonstrate a dependence on a God who is always faithful.

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

If it is not enough to pray for someone who is dealing with a serious illness, it is certainly not enough to tell them, “God bless you.”

Figuring out what things someone with cancer needs help with may not be easy, but often even little tasks are difficult for them. It could be that they need transportation to a chemotherapy appointment. Maybe they need help with making a meal, with childcare, or with cleaning their house. Helping in whatever ways we can makes a huge difference for those who are dealing with the fatigue and stress of cancer.

More than that, the important thing is that we make the effort to demonstrate our love to those in our church body who are suffering. Paul told the Corinthians that when …one member suffer[s], all the members suffer with it… –1 Corinthians 12:26. Whenever there is a need, the rest of the local church body has an obligation and should have a deep desire to help in whatever way they can.

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

Chemotherapy can cause a cancer patient to have an extremely weak immune system. A normal white cell count is between 4,000 and 10,000. but during cancer treatments I have seen patient’s white cell count drop down to 200. In this scenario, if they catch any type of infection, they will be unable to fight off that infection and will end up in the hospital.

It is important to understand that someone in this condition who chooses to keep their distance is not necessarily trying to avoid fellowship. Rather, they are trying to avoid an unneeded hospital stay for what cancer doctors call a “neutropenic fever” (a febrile illness with a really low white cell count).

In these sorts of situations, phone calls or even text messages go a long way toward helping a brother or sister feel that they are not alone, even when they cannot physically be around other people.

Conclusion

I wish I could give a complete run down of every type of cancer out there and the best treatment for each one. That would be beyond my capability and further, it would be outdated within six months’ time.

What I can say is that prayer is key. Prayer for the Holy Spirit’s leading (see John 16:13), for energy for each day, for healing, and for God’s will to be done. Most of all, we need to pray that God would be glorified in and through us. (See 1 Peter 4:11) There have been so many people who were able to speak to their nurses and doctors about their Lord, even as they dealt with side effects and cancer symptoms.

It is easy to read all the instructions about giving up worrying that is found in Scripture and think that it should be easy to cast our cares on Him (see 1 Peter 5:7). However, it is much harder to put into practice. We may feel one day as though we have conquered fear and wake up the next morning with every bit as much anxiety as we ever had.

It is in this that we desperately need a church community. We are not alone, but we will feel alone unless we have brothers and sisters around us who help us as they are able and who pray for us in our valleys and rejoice with us in our times of victory.

It is only then, that we can come to the place that the Apostle Paul did when he said, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. Of course, he was talking about a possible execution, but his resignation to God’s will was total. I pray that we too might reach that place, even as we deal with something as difficult as cancer.

正如我们在本系列两部分的第一部分中讨论的，癌症并不是一种单一的实体。各种癌症有共同的相似性，即它们由正常细胞突变而来，导致细胞以不受控制、不自然的方式生长，但每种癌症又以其特定的、独特的方式表现。

有些癌症具有侵袭性，而有些则生长得慢得多。有些倾向于局限于原发部位，并且蔓延到身体其他部位的速度相当缓慢，而另一些则可能出现在远离起始部位的位置。

无法对癌症作一概而论的陈述，但在本节中，我将讨论一些关于预防和治疗的一般事项，然后我将以作为基督徒与正在与癌症抗争的人相处的一些思考来结束。

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

许多会增加癌症风险的事情，是我们作为基督徒（希望如此）已经在避免的事物。

烟草就是其中之一。吸烟会增加患肺癌的风险。它还会增加头部肿瘤、颈部肿瘤、食道癌、胃癌以及肝脏和膀胱癌的风险。

酒精是另一种会提高癌症风险的物质。肝癌、喉癌和食道癌都与酒精消费有关。有些人声称饮酒有“健康益处”，但没有安全的饮酒水平。即使是适量饮酒的人，其与酒精使用相关的死亡风险也有所增加。i

还应当限制的是紫外线辐射的暴露。我们知道紫外线会增加皮肤癌的风险，因此佩戴能遮护的服装，例如帽子和长袖衣物，并使用防晒霜可以降低这种风险。

从积极方面看，健康的饮食习惯，例如多吃水果和蔬菜并避免高度加工食品，会降低结肠癌的风险。ii 纤维在此处似乎是关键，较高水平的膳食纤维是有益的。此外，水果和蔬菜富含抗氧化剂、维生素和矿物质，有助于维持健康的免疫系统。建议每天至少食用两份水果和五份蔬菜。

有趣的是，尽管饮食健康的人患癌风险较低，但几乎没有证据表明特定的维生素可以预防癌症。也就是说，如果你饮食非常不健康，然后服用维生素以弥补不明智的选择，几乎没有益处。

在进行对照试验之前，总是很难知道某种补充剂是否有帮助。维生素E是一种抗氧化剂，因此曾被认为有助于预防癌症。然而，事实证明研究并未显示这一点。实际上，在高剂量下，它似乎会增加某些癌症和心脏病的风险。iii

与其尝试去找正确的补充剂，更重要的是确保我们食用健康的饮食。

Chemotherapy

现在，让我们简要讨论不同类型的癌症治疗。化疗可能是大多数人首先想到的。它最早在20世纪40年代被使用，当时医生使用一种氮芥衍生物来治疗淋巴瘤。

自那时起，已有数百种不同的药物被开发为化疗药物，旨在攻击癌细胞。由于有许多不同的药物用于治疗不同的癌症，而且它们有不同的副作用，因此很难对化疗进行概括。

由于这些药物攻击的是快速分裂的细胞，许多药物往往会导致患者脱发，因为毛发细胞属于快速分裂的类型。恶心、呕吐和血细胞计数改变（白细胞计数低）是其他常见的副作用。

如果癌症已经从初发部位扩散，很可能需要不止一种药物才能实现缓解。

即使癌症尚未扩散，外科医生也常建议在手术前进行一些化疗以缩小肿瘤，使手术切除更容易。

尽管化疗听起来可怕，但它实际上对某些类型的癌症效果相当好，例如血液系统癌症（如白血病）、淋巴瘤和乳腺癌。

如今，癌症医生会对活检的癌细胞进行基因标志物测试。作为一名家庭医生，我会看到这些报告，但由于我不是该领域的专家，我觉得这些报告有些令人困惑。重要的是要记住，这些标志物有助于预测针对特定类型癌症最佳药物的选择。

Surgery

多年来，手术一直是癌症治疗的基石。尚未扩散的癌症可以被完全切除，使病人能够在无需进一步治疗的情况下继续前行。

通常，在发现病人的癌症时，已很难完全切除。手术仍然可以起到帮助作用。一方面，它提供了癌症样本以供检测，从而有助于确定最佳治疗方案。更重要的是，即使癌症已经扩散，有时肿瘤仍需被切除，仅仅因为它对周围器官产生了压力。

我听过一些人声称暴露在氧气中对癌症有危险。他们认为在手术期间组织被打开并暴露在空气中后，癌细胞会更快地扩散。没有文件证据支持这个观点。许多人在进行诊断性的探索性手术后确实似乎变得更虚弱。但问题并不是真正的空气进入了癌细胞，而是癌症很可能已达到开始出现严重症状的阶段，手术只是把事情推到了前台。另外，任何手术都会给人的身体带来压力，这只会加剧病人已被消耗的体力和精力——他们应对衰弱性疾病的能力。

通常，当肿瘤被切除时，附近的淋巴结会被取样，以查看是否含有癌细胞。这种有无癌细胞的存在有助于癌症的“分期”（例如“第3期”或“第4期”），并为进一步的治疗以预防复发提供见解。

Immunotherapy

一种较新的癌症治疗方法称为免疫治疗。这些药物能激活患者的免疫系统以清除体内的癌细胞。

这听起来很棒，你会认为副作用应该很少。不幸的是，它并不总是按计划工作。有些癌症对这类治疗无反应。至于副作用，这些药物可能导致自身免疫性疾病。当处方的药物使免疫系统额外活跃（或过度活跃）时，有时它会开始攻击患者自身的器官。虽然有些副作用在停止治疗后会好转，但并非所有副作用都会消失。

举例来说，我有一位患者接受了用于已扩散至淋巴结的黑色素瘤的免疫治疗。他被治愈了，但免疫治疗损伤了他的唾液腺，导致他持续出现口干问题。目前看来，他很可能无法恢复口腔的湿润。

Future Treatments

未来可能会有更多针对特定类型癌症的治疗方法。目前正在研究的一项内容是针对特定类型癌症的疫苗。目前这些都还不可用，除非在临床试验中。

Choosing Wisely

肿瘤科医生（癌症专科医生）并不知道未来。他们以百分比来表述。一种方案有86%的几率实现两年缓解，而另一种只有56%。副作用也是如此。虽然医生可以告诉你26%的患者在某种治疗中会感到恶心，但那并不能告诉你你是否会成为那26%中的一员，以及这种恶心是否可以用抗恶心药物控制。

在决定选择何种治疗方案时，你不会在圣经中找到指向某一方向或另一方向的经文。拥有一位会认真解释事宜的优秀肿瘤科医生——既说明成功的机会，也说明副作用的风险——至关重要。有时你可能需要换另一位癌症医生，仅仅因为你现在的医生没有给予你足够的时间，让你对治疗感到放心。

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. 我们在生活的许多方面都需要智慧，但在如何处理医疗决策方面，这无疑是其中之一。神应许如果我们恳求就会赐给我们所需的智慧——这是极其美好的事。

祷告——无论是个人祷告还是你教会群体的代祷——都非常重要。祷告可以为医治，也可以为体贴的基督徒医护人员祷告，并为选择最佳治疗的智慧祷告。

有时神通过医生和药物来医治。有时祂不顾这些而行医治。有时祂决定我们回到祂那里，给我们一个不再疾病和破碎的新身体。

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. 拥有所有这些可用的医疗技术，我们很容易忘记医治来自神。如果神不在其中行医治，世上的化疗也无济于事。与此同时，许多时候神以奇妙的方式医治，尽管医疗专业人员或其他善意的人做出了险峻的预测，神仍照常行奇事。

病人通常能做的最好的选择就是根据他们的最好判断选择最合适的治疗方案（基于成功率和副作用），然后观察进展。如果副作用太严重或治疗似乎无效，总有更换方案的选项。

归根结底，当医治来临时，无论通过何种方式，都是神赐予的医治。让我们永远不要忘记这一点。

Cancer Takes Energy

与癌症患者相处与与任何其他慢性病患者相处并无太大不同，但仍有差异。

无论是患上癌症还是接受癌症治疗，都会消耗一个人大量精力。虽然重要的是不要忽视癌症患者，但同样重要的是要记住他们并非拥有无限的精力供应。十到十五分钟的探访可能就是他们所能承受的全部。最好让他们决定他们有精力接待多长时间的来访。

Hesitate to Give Advice

你的“表亲”可能曾得过癌症，并在服用某种补充剂或去某个诊所治疗后痊愈。与正在与癌症斗争的人分享这些信息，只是他们需要从成千上万条建议中再处理的一条信息。似乎癌症患者常常受到来自善意的朋友和家人的建议和推荐的轰炸。

当一个人已然精力匮乏时，很难弄清什么是最好的做法。有时，癌症患者只是祈求神祝福他们的选择，然后将结果交在祂手中。

如果癌症患者请求你的意见，你可以给予，但如果没有，最好还是克制住给出未经请求建议的冲动。

Listen

没有任何情形是倾听无益的。正是通过倾听，我们让他人把恐惧和挫折倾诉出来。倾听可以帮助病人把他们的想法用言语表达出来。更重要的是，我们也可能听到我们能够帮助的方式。

也许有人会告诉你他们的医生是如何长期漏诊他们的癌症。或者，也许是他们向你倾诉他们对癌症或治疗的恐惧。

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. 这节经文出现在雅各谈论用油抹膏、认罪以及身体医治的段落之中。

我们当然可以并且应当为正在与癌症斗争的人祷告并与他们一同祷告。倾听帮助我们知道如何更好地为他们祷告。它让我们知道他们当日特别的挣扎是什么，以及我们如何最好地将他们举到宝座前。

雅各书的段落明确表明，医治不是来自于倒在某人身上的油，而是来自神在他们生命中的作为。祷告、信心和顺服的行动比抹油更为重要，尽管所有这些都表明对那位始终信实的神的依靠。

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

如果仅仅为正在面对严重疾病的人祷告还不够，那么仅仅跟他们说一句“愿神祝福你”肯定更不够。

弄清楚一个癌症患者需要什么帮助可能并不容易，但通常即使是微小的任务对他们来说也很困难。可能他们需要去化疗医院的交通安排。也许他们需要帮助做饭、照看孩子或打扫房子。在我们能够帮助的任何方面伸出援手，对那些正在承受癌症疲惫和压力的人都会产生巨大的差别。

更重要的是，我们要努力向在教会肢体中受苦的人展示我们的爱。保罗告诉哥林多人，当…一个肢体受苦，所有肢体就一同受苦… –1 Corinthians 12:26. 每当有需要时，当地教会的其余肢体有责任且应有强烈的愿望尽其所能提供帮助。

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

化疗可能导致癌症患者的免疫系统极度虚弱。正常的白细胞计数在4000到10000之间，但在癌症治疗期间我见过患者的白细胞计数降到200。在这种情况下，如果他们感染任何类型的病原体，将无法抵抗感染，最终会住院。

重要的是要理解，处于这种状况而选择保持距离的人并不一定是在回避团契。相反，他们是在尽力避免因所谓的“中性粒细胞减少性发热”（一种伴随极低白细胞计数的发热性疾病）而不得不住院。

在这种情况下，电话或短信在帮助弟兄或姊妹感到并非孤单方面具有很大作用，即便他们无法亲自与他人接触。

Conclusion

我希望能给出每种癌症及其最佳治疗方法的完整概述。但那超出我的能力，而且六个月内也可能变得过时。

我能说的是，祷告是关键。为圣灵的引导祷告（参见约翰福音16:13），为每日的精力祷告，为医治祷告，并为神的旨意成就在祷告中祈求。最重要的是，我们需要为神在我们当中并借着我们得荣耀而祷告。（参见彼得前书4:11）有许多人即便在面对副作用和癌症症状时，仍能与他们的护士和医生谈论他们的主。

我们很容易阅读圣经中关于不要忧虑的劝诫，并认为把忧虑卸给祂（参见彼得前书5:7）应该很容易。然而，将其付诸实践要困难得多。我们可能某日觉得自己已战胜恐惧，次日醒来却仍和以往一样充满焦虑。

在这方面我们极其需要教会群体。我们并非孤单，但若没有周围弟兄姊妹在能力所及之处帮助并在我们在谷中时为我们祷告、在我们得胜时与我们同乐，我们就会感到孤单。

只有这样，我们才能达到使徒保罗所达到的境地，他说，For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. 当然，他当时谈论的是可能的处决，但他对神旨意的顺服是完全的。我祈求我们也能达到那样的境地，即便我们正在面对像癌症这样艰难的事。

“My, it’s warm!” exclaimed Mom. “A nice, good rain is what we need to cool things off a bit.”

It was Saturday, near the end of June, and the weather had been particularly hot and humid that day. Ellie’s mother had been cleaning the house and preparing some food for the company that was invited to come for lunch on Sunday after church.

As the afternoon moved into early evening, it felt like it became even hotter, and no breezes were to be found. Ellie’s father was resting in a hammock out on the lawn while the rest of the family tried to find the most comfortable place to seek relief from the heat.

As evening approached, so did the clouds. They arrived suddenly, along with gusts of wind that began to stir up the dust. Lightning started to flash across the sky and the thunder rumbled in the distance.

“Quickly, children!” called Mom. “Put away your toys; it’s about to storm!”

Ellie looked around in alarm. It was getting dark very quickly and the sky looked strange—almost angry. She quickly gathered up her playthings and hurried into the house. Dad was no longer sleeping on the hammock. The wind had almost toppled it over and him along with it! He, too, hurried into the house; the wind causing the door to slam violently behind him. The family gathered on the sunporch to watch the approaching storm. There were windows to the west and south, so they had a good vantage point from which to watch the coming rain. The wind was blowing with a force that Ellie had never experienced in all her seven years. She noted the concern and alarm on her parents’ faces as they watched and waited.

Then it began to rain. Great sheets of rain were being driven against the windows and Ellie wondered if it was possible that it was raining hard enough to break the glass.

“What was that?” exclaimed Mom as suddenly, a sheet of tin whizzed past the sunporch windows and disappeared beyond the garden.

“I think it’s part of the garage roof,” said Dad in disbelief while peering cautiously through the windows.

Upon hearing this, Mom directed the children to stand by the cellar door. If things got worse, down they would go! Ellie felt so scared. What was going to happen to them? Would their house blow away? Would any of them get hurt?

As abruptly as the storm began, it calmed. The wind stopped, the rain slowed, and very soon the sun was shining again. The family cautiously ventured outdoors to see what all had happened during the storm.

“Look!” said Dad. “The garage roof is gone and so is the south wall!”

“Why does Gerald’s house look so strange?” Mom pointed toward their next-door neighbors. “Why, look! The entire roof is gone from their house!” Indeed, the roof had been cleanly stripped away and the gable ends stoically stood there, holding up nothing.

The wail of sirens could be heard in the distance and as they looked around the neighborhood, they could see smoke just beyond some trees.

“That’s got to be Melvin’s barn burning!” exclaimed Dad. “I’m going to go see what I can do to help.” He raced for his truck and was soon hurrying out the driveway.

The winds had been so strong that some electric poles were blown over causing the electricity to be disconnected so there were no lights or fans. After the storm had passed the humidity and heat had returned making the night hot and muggy. Yet the grown-ups from the area worked long into the night, helping each other to clean up what they could of the storm damage.

Of special interest was our neighbor Melvin. His barn had collapsed on top of dozens of cattle and then a fire had broken out. The neighbor men tried desperately to rescue what cattle they could, but in the end, many of the steers could not be saved.

Sunday came, but no one went to church. The morning was spent over at Melvin’s, hauling away dead cattle, clearing away burnt hay, and simply just being there for one another. It was hard, grim work. Ellie clearly remembers how awful the smell was. And she could barely bring herself to watch the loading up of the dead steers. When lunch time came, their company arrived, but no one was very hungry. Ellie’s younger brother sobbed, “All I can think about is those poor steers!”

Ellie was surprised how powerful a storm could be. And scary! Would they experience another twister? Might more buildings collapse, and another barn or house burn down? A seed of fear began to grow in Ellie’s heart. Throughout that summer and for many summers after, every time the rumble of thunder was heard or she heard the words “tornado warning”, her heart would beat faster, and a knot would settle in her stomach. How she dreaded each storm! She wished they would all just pass by their home. Why did God allow storms, anyway?

“You need to trust God, Ellie,” her mother would say. “He’s the One who made the weather, and He is in control of everything that happens. He might not always keep us from experiencing frightening times, but He is always there to take care of us.”

As she grew older, Ellie learned to take this advice to heart. Her fear of storms faded, and, in its place, she developed a fascination with how storms develop and form. Knowing that God is the Master of the wind is still a comfort and an assurance to her. Most of all, as she has learned to trust God in every area of her life, she has found Him to always be faithful. Learning to replace fear with trust always brings peace to the heart.

“Oj, vad det är varmt!” utropade mamma. “Ett gott, rejält regn är precis vad vi behöver för att svalka av lite.”

Det var lördag, i slutet av juni, och vädret hade varit ovanligt varmt och kvavt den dagen. Ellies mamma hade städat huset och förberett lite mat för de gäster som var inbjudna att komma på lunch på söndagen efter kyrkan.

När eftermiddagen övergick i tidig kväll kändes det som om det blev ännu varmare, och inte en vindpust fanns att känna. Ellies pappa vilade i en hängmatta ute på gräsmattan medan resten av familjen försökte hitta den mest bekväma platsen för att få lindring från värmen.

När kvällen närmade sig gjorde molnen detsamma. De kom plötsligt, tillsammans med vindbyar som började virvla upp dammet. Blixtar började flämta över himlen och åskan mullrade i fjärran.

“Skynda er, barn!” ropade mamma. “Plocka undan era leksaker; det är på väg att storma!”

Ellie såg sig omkring i förskräckelse. Det blev mörkt väldigt snabbt och himlen såg konstig—nästan arg—ut. Hon samlade snabbt ihop sina leksaker och skyndade in i huset. Pappa sov inte längre i hängmattan. Vinden hade nästan vält den och honom med den! Han skyndade också in i huset; vinden fick dörren att slå igen med ett våldsamt dån bakom honom. Familjen samlades på verandan för att se på den annalkande stormen. Det fanns fönster mot väster och söder, så de hade en god utkikspunkt för att bevittna det kommande regnet. Vinden blåste med en kraft som Ellie aldrig upplevt under sina sju år. Hon noterade oro och ängslan i sina föräldrars ansikten medan de tittade och väntade.

Sedan började det regna. Stora regnstrimmor slog mot fönstren och Ellie undrade om det var möjligt att det regnade så hårt att glaset kunde gå sönder.

“Vad var det där?” utropade mamma när plötsligt en plåtbit susade förbi verandafönstren och försvann bortom trädgården.

“Jag tror det är en del av garagetaket,” sade pappa i misstro medan han försiktigt kikade genom fönstren.

När mamma hörde detta beordrade hon barnen att stå vid källardörren. Om det blev värre skulle de gå ner dit! Ellie kände sig så rädd. Vad skulle hända med dem? Skulle deras hus blåsa bort? Skulle någon av dem skadas?

Lika plötsligt som stormen började, ebbade den ut. Vinden avtog, regnet mattades, och mycket snart sken solen igen. Familjen vågade sig försiktigt ut för att se vad som hade hänt under stormen.

“Titta!” sade pappa. “Garagetaket är borta och det södra väggen också!”

“Varför ser Geralds hus så konstigt ut?” pekade mamma mot grannarna bredvid. “Titta! Taket är helt borta från deras hus!” Visserligen hade taket rivits bort och gaveländarna stod istället där, stoiskt, utan att bära något.

Sirenernas klagande ljud hördes i fjärran och när de såg sig omkring i området kunde de se rök strax bortom några träd.

“Det måste vara Melvins lada som brinner!” utropade pappa. “Jag ska se vad jag kan göra för att hjälpa.” Han sprang till sin lastbil och skyndade snart ut på uppfarten.

Vinden hade varit så stark att några elstolpar blåsts omkull och fått elen att brytas, så det fanns inga lampor eller fläktar. Efter att stormen dragit förbi återkom fukten och hettan vilket gjorde natten varm och kvav. Ändå arbetade de vuxna i området långt in på natten och hjälpte varandra att städa upp vad de kunde av stormskadorna.

Särskilt iögonfallande var vår granne Melvin. Hans lada hade kollapsat över dussintals nötkreatur och sedan hade en eld brutit ut. Grannens män försökte förtvivlat rädda vad de kunde av nötkreaturen, men till slut kunde många av tjurarna inte räddas.

Söndagen kom, men ingen gick till kyrkan. Morgonen tillbringades hos Melvin med att forsla bort döda djur, rensa bort bränt hö och helt enkelt finnas där för varandra. Det var hårt, dyster arbete. Ellie minns tydligt hur fruktansvärd lukten var. Och hon klarade knappt av att se på när de lastade upp de döda tjurarna. När lunchdags kom anlände deras gäster, men ingen var särskilt hungrig. Ellies lillebror snyftade: “Allt jag kan tänka på är de stackars tjurarna!”

Ellie var förvånad över hur kraftfull en storm kunde vara. Och hur skrämmande! Skulle de uppleva en ny tornado? Skulle fler byggnader kollapsa, och kanske en annan lada eller ett annat hus eldhärjas? Ett frö av rädsla började växa i Ellies hjärta. Under hela den sommaren och i många somrar efteråt, varje gång åskan hördes eller hon hörde orden “tornadovarning”, slog hennes hjärta snabbare och en knut satte sig i magen. Hur hon fruktade varje storm! Hon önskade att de alla bara skulle gå förbi deras hem. Varför tillät Gud stormar, egentligen?

“Du måste lita på Gud, Ellie,” brukade hennes mamma säga. “Han är den som skapade vädret, och Han har kontroll över allt som händer. Han kanske inte alltid håller oss från att möta skrämmande tider, men Han finns alltid där för att ta hand om oss.”

När hon blev äldre lärde sig Ellie att ta detta råd till hjärtat. Hennes rädsla för stormar avtog, och i dess ställe utvecklade hon en fascination för hur stormar bildas och utvecklas. Att veta att Gud är vindens Herre är fortfarande en tröst och en försäkran för henne. Framför allt, när hon har lärt sig att förtrösta på Gud i varje område av sitt liv, har hon funnit att Han alltid är trofast. Att lära sig ersätta rädsla med förtröstan ger alltid frid i hjärtat.

In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

خُداوندِ مسیح کی محبت کے سلام حاضرینِ محترم۔ اِس رسالے کے اِس شمارے (Summer 2023)… چرچ ہسٹری کا مضمون قیامت کے اوقات سے متعلق بائبل کی نبوت پر مرکوز ہے اور ساتھ ساتھ اُن مختلف طریقوں پر بھی روشنی ڈالتا ہے جن کے ذریعے برسوں کے دوران چرچ کے بعض عناصر روزمرہ زندگی کے سلسلے میں بائبلی تعلیم سے منحرف ہو گئے۔ اپنے مضمون میں ڈونی بریچبل، جو اپنی زوجہ کے ساتھ ہر سال کئی شادیاتی سیمینار منعقد کرتے ہیں، ایک نازک موضوع پر روشنی ڈالنے کی کوشش کرتے ہیں—کلیسیا میں جدوجہد کرتی ہوئی عورتوں کے ساتھ جو بنیادی مسائل وہ دیکھتے ہیں اُن میں سے چند۔ لی روفینر ایک بے باک انداز اختیار کرتے ہیں جب وہ پاکیزہ گھر رکھنے کے عملی طریقوں پر بعض بیانیہ تعلیمات شیئر کرنے کی کوشش کرتے ہیں۔ اس بار بہنوں کے لیے ہمارے پاس ایک نئی لکھاری ہے جو اپنے دل میں ایک بوجھ بانٹتی ہے—اگلی نسل کے دلوں میں خدا کا کلام راسخ کرنے کا کام۔

مزید دلچسپ موضوعات بھی شامل ہیں۔ لطف اٹھائیے۔

اگر آپ لکھاریوں کے کسی بھی مواد سے تعمیری یا حوصلہ افزا محسوس کرتے ہیں تو ہمارے پاس ڈاک یا ای میل کے ذریعے جواب بھیجنا آپ کے لیے برکت کا باعث ہوگا۔ ہم یہ آراء اپنے لکھاریوں کو اُن کے فائدے کے لیے پہنچا دیتے ہیں۔

حال ہی میں، میں تبدیلی کے موضوع پر غور و فکر کر رہا تھا۔ جیسا کہ میں نے پہلے لکھا بھی ہے، ہم نے بطورِ خاندان کافی تبدیلیاں گزاری ہیں۔ گزشتہ ایک سے دو سال کے دوران ہم نے رہائش تبدیل کی، مجھے نوکری بدلنی پڑی، اور آخرکار، خدا کا شکر ہے، میں کووِڈ کے طویل المدتی اثرات سے کافی حد تک بحال ہو چکا ہوں۔ میری صحت کے لیے دعا کرنے والے ہر فرد کا خاص شکریہ۔

جب میں خاموش یادوں میں ٹھہرا تو مجھے اُن تمام چیزوں پر حیرت ہوئی جو چالیس سالوں سے زائد عرصے میں بدل گئی ہیں جو میری یاداشت میں ہیں۔ (اگرچہ میری عمر پچاس سے اوپر ہے، مگر بچپن کے ابتدائی سالوں کی بہت سی باتیں مجھے یاد نہیں ہیں۔)

بچپن میں میں ایسی گاڑیوں میں سفر کرتا تھا جن میں سیٹ بیلٹ نہیں ہوتے تھے اور یقیناً ایئر بیگز بھی نہیں ہوتے تھے۔ جب یہ دونوں "زندگی بچانے" والے آلات پہلی بار متعارف کرائے گئے تو مجھے اچھی طرح یاد ہے کہ اس بارے میں بہت سی بحثیں ہوئیں کہ آیا وہ واقعی زندگیاں بچاتے ہیں یا ان کا اثر الٹا ہے۔ تمام گاڑیاں پہلے پچھلے پہیوں سے چلتی تھیں یا چار پہیوں سے چلتی تھیں۔ جب پہلی بار اگلے پہیے سے چلنے والی گاڑیاں سامنے آئیں تو یہ عجیب لگا۔ اب ہمارے پاس ہائبرِڈ گاڑیاں ہیں اور مکمل برقی گاڑیوں کی طرف پیش قدمی ہو رہی ہے۔

چالیس سال پہلے زیادہ تر کسانوں کے پاس کاربوریٹر والی پیٹرول ٹریکٹر یا دستی انجیکٹر پمپ والا ڈیزل ٹریکٹر ہوتا تھا۔ آج کل زیادہ تر ٹریکٹر کمپیوٹر سے لیس ہیں اور بظاہر میلوں کی وائرنگ اور برقی آلات ہیں۔ اُس وقت زیادہ تر کسان اپنے سازو سامان کی دیکھ بھال یا مرمت خود کر لیتے تھے؛ اب تشخیصی مشینوں اور مہنگے خاص اوزار کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے جنہیں چلانا سیکھنے میں بہت گھنٹے لگتے ہیں۔ اس کے نتیجے میں زیادہ تر کسان مہارت رکھنے والے مرمت کرنے والوں پر انحصار کرتے ہیں جن کی خدمات بھی بہت قیمت طلب کرتی ہیں۔

پھر کووِڈ آیا۔ وہ ایک کشیدہ وقت تھا۔ کیا آپ نے محسوس کیا کہ کووِڈ کے دوران، بعد میں، یا کووِڈ کے نتیجے میں کیا تبدیلیاں آئیں؟ جب میں دوسروں کے ساتھ بات کرتا ہوں تو عام طور پر کوئی نہ کوئی کہتا ہے کہ کووِڈ کے بعد یہ یا وہ چیز مختلف ہو گئی ہے۔ کیا صرف مجھے ایسا محسوس ہوتا ہے، یا کووِڈ کے بعد عام لوگ اپنے تعاملات میں کم دوستانہ اور زیادہ نجی ہو گئے ہیں؟ آئیں ہم اپنی باہمی روابط کا جائزہ لیں تاکہ یقینی بنائیں کہ ہم ابھی بھی اس تاریک دنیا میں خدا کی "روشنی" اور "نمک" بنے ہوئے ہیں، اور اپنی "نمکینی" نہ کھو رہے ہوں۔ نیز ہر طرف "ہیلپ وانٹڈ" یعنی ملازمت درکار کے اعلانات نظر آتے ہیں۔ کیوں؟ میرے خیال میں کووِڈ نے اُس تھوڑی سی محنتی اخلاقیات کو بھی کمزور کرنے کی حوصلہ افزائی کی جو ہماری سوسائٹی میں ابھی باقی تھی۔

پھر سیل فونز اور الیکٹرک بائیکس کا معاملہ ہے۔ یہ دونوں بظاہر غیر مربوط چیزیں کیا مشترک رکھتی ہیں؟ میری نگاہ سے، ہولمز کاؤنٹی کے ایمش لوگوں کا مشاہدہ کرتے ہوئے یہ دونوں اشیاء ایک قوم اور ثقافت کو تبدیل کرنے میں تقریباً ہر دوسری چیز سے زیادہ بڑے پیمانے پر اثرانداز ہوئی ہیں۔

یہ سب ہمیں کہاں چھوڑتا ہے؟ عبرانیوں کے لکھنے والے نے کہا کہ قربانیوں کے منصب کے بدل جانے کے سبب لازم ہے کہ شریعت میں بھی تبدیلی ہو—Hebrews 7:12۔ لہٰذا، ہم دیکھتے ہیں کہ خدا نے جب مناسب سمجھا تو چیزیں بدل دیں، پس اگر ہمیں زیادہ بائبلی بننے کے لیے بدلنا پڑے تو ہمیں بدل جانا چاہیے۔ لیکن رسول پال نے کہا کہ اب ہم بچے نہ رہیں جو ہر سیکھ کی ہوا سے بہہ لئے جاتے اور ہر تبلیغ کی لہر کے ساتھ لے جایا جاتے ہیں…—Ephesians 4:14۔

اور کیونکہ بدی میں اضافہ ہوگا، بہتوں کی محبت ٹھنڈی پڑ جائے گی۔ مگر جو آخر تک ثابت رہے گا وہ نجات پائے گا—Matthew 24:12-13۔ پس، آیئے ہم ان آخری ایام میں چوکنا رہیں جب ہمارے اردگرد تبدیلیاں تیزی سے ہو رہی ہیں۔ دعا ہے کہ ہم اُن میں سے ہوں جو آخر تک ثابت رہیں گے۔
