Como discutimos en la primera parte de esta serie de dos entregas, el cáncer no es una entidad única. Varios tipos de cáncer tienen similitudes generales en que se desarrollan a partir de células normales que mutan para crecer de forma incontrolada y antinatural, sin embargo, cada tipo de cáncer se comporta de manera específica y única.

Algunos cánceres son agresivos y otros crecen mucho más lentamente. Algunos tienden a permanecer localizados y son bastante lentos en diseminarse a otras partes del cuerpo, mientras que otros es más probable que aparezcan en lugares lejanos a donde comenzaron.

No es posible hacer afirmaciones generales sobre todos los cánceres, pero en esta sección discutiré algunas cuestiones generales sobre prevención y tratamiento, y terminaré con algunas reflexiones sobre nosotros como cristianos relacionándonos con alguien que está afrontando un cáncer.

Cambios en el estilo de vida para prevenir cánceres

Muchas de las cosas que aumentan el riesgo de cáncer son cosas que (con suerte) nosotros, como cristianos, ya evitamos.

El tabaco es una de ellas. El tabaco, cuando se fuma, aumenta el riesgo de cáncer de pulmón. También aumenta el riesgo de cánceres de cabeza, cánceres de cuello, cáncer de esófago, cáncer de estómago y cánceres de hígado y vejiga.

El alcohol es otra sustancia que eleva el riesgo de cáncer. Los cánceres de hígado, laringe y esófago están relacionados con el consumo de alcohol. Algunas personas afirman beber alcohol por “beneficios para la salud”, pero no existe un nivel seguro de consumo de alcohol. Incluso las personas que beben con moderación tienen un mayor riesgo de muerte relacionado con su consumo de alcohol.i

Otra cosa que debería limitarse es la exposición a la radiación ultravioleta. Sabemos que la radiación UV aumenta el riesgo de cánceres de piel, por lo que usar ropa que proteja, como sombreros y prendas de mangas largas, y usar protector solar puede reducir este riesgo.

En el lado positivo, los hábitos alimentarios saludables, como consumir muchas frutas y verduras y evitar alimentos altamente procesados, reducirán el riesgo de cáncer de colon.ii La fibra parece ser clave aquí y niveles más altos de fibra dietética son útiles. Además, las frutas y verduras son ricas en antioxidantes, vitaminas y minerales y favorecen un sistema inmunitario sano. Se recomienda comer al menos dos porciones de fruta y cinco porciones de verduras al día.

Es interesante que, mientras las personas que siguen dietas saludables tienen un riesgo disminuido de cáncer, hay poca evidencia de que existan vitaminas específicas que prevengan el cáncer. Es decir, hay poco beneficio si consumes una dieta muy poco saludable y luego tomas vitaminas en un esfuerzo por compensar tus elecciones poco sabias.

Antes de realizar una prueba controlada siempre es difícil saber si cierto suplemento ayudará o no. La vitamina E es un antioxidante y por ello se pensó que podría ayudar en la prevención del cáncer. Sin embargo, resulta que los estudios no han mostrado que esto sea cierto. De hecho, en dosis altas parece aumentar el riesgo de ciertos cánceres y de enfermedad cardíaca.iii

Más que intentar encontrar los suplementos adecuados, es más importante asegurarnos de que estamos llevando dietas saludables.

Quimioterapia

Ahora, pasemos a una breve discusión sobre los diferentes tipos de tratamiento para el cáncer. La quimioterapia es probablemente lo primero en lo que piensa la mayoría de la gente. Se utilizó por primera vez en la década de 1940 cuando los médicos emplearon un derivado de la mostaza nitrogenada para tratar linfomas.

Desde entonces, se han desarrollado cientos de medicamentos distintos como quimioterapia, diseñados para atacar las células cancerosas. Es difícil generalizar sobre la quimioterapia porque hay tantos medicamentos diferentes diseñados para tratar distintos cánceres y porque tienen efectos secundarios distintos.

Debido a que atacan células que se multiplican rápidamente, muchos de estos fármacos tienden a provocar la caída del cabello de una persona, ya que las células del cabello son de ese tipo de rápida multiplicación. Náuseas, vómitos y alteraciones en los recuentos sanguíneos (recuentos bajos de glóbulos blancos) son otros efectos secundarios comunes.

Si un cáncer se ha diseminado desde su ubicación inicial, lo más probable es que requiera más de un tipo de medicamento para lograr la remisión.

Incluso si un cáncer no se ha diseminado, los cirujanos a menudo recomendarán administrar algo de quimioterapia antes de la cirugía para reducir el tumor y facilitar su extirpación quirúrgica.

Aunque la quimioterapia suene aterradora, en realidad funciona bastante bien para ciertos tipos de cáncer, como los cánceres de la sangre (como las leucemias), el linfoma y el cáncer de mama.

Hoy en día, los oncólogos analizan las células cancerosas biopsiadas en busca de marcadores genéticos. Como médico de familia, veo estos informes pero, dado que no soy especialista en este campo, me resultan algo confusos. Lo importante a recordar es que estos marcadores ayudan a predecir cuáles son los mejores fármacos para usar en un tipo específico de cáncer.

Cirugía

Durante muchos años, la cirugía fue la piedra angular del tratamiento del cáncer. Los cánceres que no se han diseminado pueden extirparse por completo, permitiendo que una persona siga adelante sin más tratamiento.

A menudo, cuando se descubre el cáncer de una persona, ya es demasiado tarde para eliminarlo por completo. La cirugía todavía puede ser útil. Por un lado, proporciona una muestra del cáncer para su análisis y así ayudar a identificar el mejor tratamiento. Además, incluso si un cáncer se ha diseminado, hay ocasiones en que es necesario extirpar un tumor simplemente por los órganos sobre los que está ejerciendo presión.

He escuchado a algunas personas afirmar que es peligroso que un cáncer esté expuesto al oxígeno. Creen que las células cancerosas se diseminan más rápido después de que los tejidos se abren y se exponen al aire durante la cirugía. No hay evidencia documentada que respalde esta idea. A muchas personas sí parece que se les agrava la enfermedad tras una cirugía exploratoria cuando se está diagnosticando su cáncer. Pero la cuestión no es realmente que el aire entre en las células cancerosas, sino que el cáncer casi con seguridad ya estaba en un punto en que comenzaba a mostrar síntomas graves, y la cirugía simplemente precipitó las cosas. Además, cualquier cirugía supone un estrés para el cuerpo de la persona, lo que sólo incrementará el desgaste de la fuerza y vitalidad ya mermadas de la persona, es decir, su capacidad para mantenerse por encima de una enfermedad debilitante.

Típicamente, cuando se extirpa un tumor, se muestrean los ganglios linfáticos cercanos para ver si contienen células cancerosas. Esta presencia o ausencia de células ayuda con el “estadío” del cáncer (como “estadio 3” o “estadio 4”) y proporcionará información para el tratamiento ulterior con el fin de prevenir la posibilidad de recurrencia.

Inmunoterapia

Uno de los tratamientos más nuevos contra el cáncer se llama inmunoterapia. Son medicamentos que activan el sistema inmunitario del paciente para que elimine las células cancerosas de su cuerpo.

Esto suena muy bien y uno pensaría que los efectos secundarios deberían ser mínimos. Desafortunadamente, no siempre funciona según lo planeado. Algunos cánceres no responden a este tipo de tratamientos. Y en cuanto a los efectos secundarios, estos medicamentos pueden provocar enfermedades autoinmunes. Cuando se prescribe un fármaco que hace que el sistema inmunitario esté más activo (o hiperactivo), a veces comienza a atacar los propios órganos del paciente. Si bien algunos de estos efectos secundarios mejoran con la suspensión del tratamiento, no todos desaparecen.

Como ejemplo, tuve un paciente que recibió inmunoterapia por un melanoma que se había diseminado a sus ganglios linfáticos. Se curó del cáncer, pero la inmunoterapia dañó sus glándulas salivales lo suficiente como para que tuviera problemas continuos con la sequedad bucal. En este punto, parece improbable que recupere esa humedad en la boca.

Tratamientos futuros

Probablemente habrá más tratamientos en el futuro dirigidos a tipos específicos de cáncer. Algo que actualmente se investiga son las vacunas que atacarían tipos específicos de cáncer. Actualmente ninguna de estas está disponible fuera de ensayos clínicos.

Elegir sabiamente

Los oncólogos (especialistas en cáncer) no conocen el futuro. Hablan en términos de porcentajes. Un protocolo tiene un 86 por ciento de probabilidad de lograr una remisión de dos años del cáncer, otro sólo el 56 por ciento. Lo mismo ocurre con los efectos secundarios. Aunque un médico puede decirle que el 26 por ciento de los pacientes experimentan náuseas con un tratamiento, eso no le dice si usted será uno de ese 26 por ciento ni si esas náuseas serán controlables con medicación antiemética.

Al decidir qué curso de tratamiento elegir, no encontrará un pasaje bíblico que indique una dirección u otra. Tener un buen oncólogo que explique las cosas con cuidado, tanto la probabilidad de éxito como el riesgo de efectos secundarios, es clave. Hay ocasiones en que puede ser necesario cambiar a otro médico oncólogo, simplemente porque el que tiene no dedica el tiempo que usted necesita para sentirse cómodo con su tratamiento.

Si alguno de ustedes carece de sabiduría, pídala a Dios, quien da a todos abundantemente y sin reproche, y le será dada – Santiago 1:5. Necesitamos sabiduría en muchas áreas de nuestras vidas, pero sin duda elegir cómo navegar las decisiones médicas es una de esas áreas. Es algo maravilloso que Dios haya prometido darnos la sabiduría que necesitamos, si tan solo la pedimos.

La oración—tanto la oración personal como la de su comunidad de iglesia—es muy importante. Se puede orar por sanidad. También se puede orar por cuidadores médicos cristianos y compasivos, y por sabiduría al elegir los mejores tratamientos.

A veces Dios cura por medio de médicos y medicamentos. A veces, Él sana a pesar de ellos. A veces decide que es momento de que vayamos a casa para estar con Él, proporcionándonos así un cuerpo nuevo que no esté enfermo ni quebrantado.

Bendice, alma mía, al SEÑOR, y no olvides ninguno de sus beneficios: Él es quien perdona todas tus iniquidades; el que sana todas tus dolencias – Salmo 103:2-3. Con toda la tecnología médica disponible, es fácil olvidar que la sanidad viene de Dios. Toda la quimioterapia del mundo no servirá si Dios no obra un acto de sanidad. Al mismo tiempo, hay muchas ocasiones en que Dios obra de maneras milagrosas para sanar a pesar de las predicciones desesperadas realizadas por los profesionales médicos u otras personas bienintencionadas.

A menudo lo mejor que un paciente puede hacer es elegir (según su mejor juicio) el mejor curso de tratamiento (basado en la tasa de éxito y los efectos secundarios) y luego ver cómo van las cosas. Si los efectos secundarios son demasiado severos o el tratamiento no parece estar funcionando, siempre existe la opción de cambiar.

En última instancia, cuando llega la sanidad, independientemente de cómo llegue, es Dios quien provee esa sanidad. Nunca lo olvidemos.

El cáncer consume energía

Relacionarse con alguien que tiene cáncer no es muy diferente de relacionarse con una persona con cualquier otra enfermedad crónica. Sin embargo, hay diferencias.

Tanto tener cáncer como recibir tratamiento para el cáncer quitan mucha energía a una persona. Si bien es importante no ignorar a alguien que tiene cáncer, es igual de importante recordar que no tienen suministros de energía infinitos. Una visita de diez o quince minutos puede ser todo lo que puedan soportar. Es mejor dejar que ellos decidan la duración de las visitas para las que tienen energía.

Dudar antes de dar consejos

Su “primo” puede haber tenido cáncer y puede haberse recuperado tras tomar un suplemento en particular o visitar una clínica determinada. Compartir esa información con una persona que está afrontando un cáncer es solo una pieza más de información que tendrá que procesar entre los “miles” de otras que puede haber recibido. Parece que a alguien con cáncer con frecuencia se le bombardea con consejos y recomendaciones de amigos y familiares bienintencionados.

Es difícil averiguar cuál es la mejor cosa a hacer cuando una persona ya está con poca energía. A veces, los pacientes con cáncer simplemente han orado para que Dios bendiga sus decisiones y luego han dejado el resultado en Sus manos.

Si el paciente con cáncer pide su opinión, puede dársela, pero si no lo hace, probablemente sea mejor resistir la tentación de dar consejos no solicitados.

Escuchar

No hay ninguna situación en la que escuchar no sea beneficioso. Es mediante la escucha que permitimos a otros desahogarse de miedos y frustraciones. Escuchar puede ayudar a la persona a poner sus pensamientos en palabras. Además, podemos escuchar maneras en que podemos ayudar.

Tal vez sea alguien contándole la historia (demasiado larga) de cómo su médico pasó por alto su cáncer. O tal vez es que nos cuente sus temores respecto a su cáncer o a sus tratamientos.

Orar

…La oración eficaz del justo puede mucho – Santiago 5:16. Este versículo aparece en medio de Santiago hablando sobre la unción con aceite, la confesión de pecados y la sanidad física.

Ciertamente podemos orar por, y con, alguien que está lidiando con un cáncer. Escuchar nos ayuda a saber cómo orar mejor por ellos. Nos permite conocer cuál es su lucha particular en un día dado y cómo podemos presentarlos mejor ante el trono.

El pasaje en Santiago deja claro que la sanidad no proviene del aceite que se vierte sobre alguien, sino del trabajo de Dios en su vida. La oración, la fe y la acción obediente son más importantes que el aceite de la unción, aunque todos demuestran dependencia de un Dios que siempre es fiel.

Hacer pequeñas tareas

Si un hermano o una hermana están desnudos y carecen del alimento diario, y alguno de ustedes les dice: Id en paz, calentaos y saciaos; y no les dais las cosas necesarias para el cuerpo, ¿de qué aprovecha? – Santiago 2:15-16.

Si no basta con orar por alguien que enfrenta una enfermedad grave, ciertamente no basta con decirles “Dios te bendiga”.

Descubrir qué cosas necesita alguien con cáncer puede no ser fácil, pero a menudo incluso tareas pequeñas les resultan difíciles. Podría ser que necesiten transporte para una cita de quimioterapia. Tal vez necesiten ayuda para preparar una comida, con el cuidado de los niños o con la limpieza de la casa. Ayudar en todo lo que podamos marca una gran diferencia para quienes enfrentan la fatiga y el estrés del cáncer.

Además, lo importante es que hagamos el esfuerzo por demostrar nuestro amor a quienes en nuestra congregación están sufriendo. Pablo dijo a los corintios que cuando …un miembro padece, todos los miembros padecen con él… – 1 Corintios 12:26. Siempre que hay una necesidad, el resto del cuerpo local de la iglesia tiene una obligación y debería tener un profundo deseo de ayudar en todo lo que pueda.

Esté dispuesto a mantener la distancia

La quimioterapia puede provocar que un paciente con cáncer tenga el sistema inmunitario extremadamente débil. Un recuento normal de glóbulos blancos está entre 4,000 y 10,000, pero durante los tratamientos contra el cáncer he visto recuentos de glóbulos blancos bajar hasta 200. En este escenario, si contraen cualquier tipo de infección, no podrán combatirla y acabarán en el hospital.

Es importante comprender que alguien en esta condición que decide mantener su distancia no está necesariamente tratando de evitar la comunión. Más bien, intenta evitar una estancia hospitalaria innecesaria por lo que los oncólogos llaman una “fiebre neutropénica” (una enfermedad febril con un recuento de glóbulos blancos muy bajo).

En situaciones de este tipo, las llamadas telefónicas o incluso los mensajes de texto son de gran ayuda para que un hermano o hermana sienta que no está solo, incluso cuando no pueden estar físicamente cerca de otras personas.

Conclusión

Desearía poder ofrecer un resumen completo de todos los tipos de cáncer que existen y el mejor tratamiento para cada uno. Eso estaría más allá de mi capacidad y, además, quedaría desactualizado en el plazo de seis meses.

Lo que sí puedo decir es que la oración es clave. Oración por la dirección del Espíritu Santo (ver Juan 16:13), por energía para cada día, por sanidad y por que se haga la voluntad de Dios. Sobre todo, debemos orar para que Dios sea glorificado en y a través de nosotros. (Ver 1 Pedro 4:11) Ha habido tantas personas que pudieron hablar con sus enfermeras y médicos acerca de su Señor, incluso mientras lidiaban con efectos secundarios y síntomas del cáncer.

Es fácil leer todas las instrucciones sobre dejar de afanarnos que se encuentran en las Escrituras y pensar que debería ser fácil echar sobre Él nuestras preocupaciones (ver 1 Pedro 5:7). Sin embargo, es mucho más difícil ponerlo en práctica. Podemos sentir un día que hemos vencido el temor y despertar a la mañana siguiente con tanto o más ansiedad que antes.

Es en esto que necesitamos desesperadamente una comunidad de iglesia. No estamos solos, pero nos sentiremos solos a menos que tengamos hermanos y hermanas a nuestro alrededor que nos ayuden dentro de sus posibilidades y que oren por nosotros en nuestros valles y se regocijen con nosotros en nuestros tiempos de victoria.

Es sólo entonces cuando podemos llegar al lugar al que llegó el apóstol Pablo cuando dijo, Porque para mí el vivir es Cristo, y el morir es ganancia – Filipenses 1:21. Por supuesto, él hablaba de una posible ejecución, pero su resignación a la voluntad de Dios fue total. Oro para que nosotros también podamos alcanzar ese lugar, incluso mientras afrontamos algo tan difícil como el cáncer.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.

یہ نظم عام طور پر اس خیال کے ساتھ سمجھی جاتی ہے کہ یہ کسی عورت کی طرف سے تخلیق کی گئی سب سے عظیم تر نظموں میں سے ایک ہے۔ آج شائع ہونے والے تقریباً ہر ہمنال یا نغمات کی کتاب میں یہ مل سکتی ہے۔ اس نظم نگارہ نے بڑھتی ہوئی خواہشات اور زندگی سے لطف اندوزی میں کمال حاصل کیا؛ وہ توانائی سے بھرپور، زندہ دل، خوبصورت، ہونہار اور ایک ایسی شخصیت تھی جس کی "بلند حیثیت نے ہمیشہ ان تمام لوگوں پر گہرا اثر چھوڑا جو اسے جانتے تھے"۔ اگرچہ اس کی زندگی بھرپور اور مفید تھی، وہ مختصر تھی اور اس کی نازک اور کمزور طبیعت نے اسے مختصر کر دیا۔ اس نظم کی کہانی نے مصیبت اور سختیوں، حتیٰ کہ موت کے وقت بھی، بہت سے لوگوں کی زندگیوں کو چھوا ہے۔ خدا نے اسے لوگوں کے دلوں کو موجودہ آلام سے آسمان کی طرف، اس زندگی کے مافوق الفطرت حقائق کی طرف کھینچنے کے لئے استعمال کیا ہے۔

سارہ فلاور ایڈم 22 فروری 1805 کو ہارلو، انگلینڈ میں بنجامن اور ایلیزا فلاور کے ہاں پیدا ہوئیں۔ جب وہ پانچ سال کی تھیں تو ان کی والدہ تپ دق، جسے آج ٹیوبَرکولوسِس کہا جاتا ہے، سے فوت ہو گئیں۔ سارہ اور ان کی بڑی بہن ایلیزا بھی اسی جسمانی کمزوری کے وارث تھیں۔ نظم نگار کے بارے میں میں 101 Hymn Stories سے نقل کرتا ہوں: "وہ اپنی متعدد ادبی کامیابیوں کے لیے بھی وسیع پیمانے پر جانی جاتی تھیں، حالانکہ ان کی نازک صحت ہمیشہ ان کی کئی امنگوں کے لیے رکاوٹ رہی۔"

سن 1834 میں، جب سارہ 29 سال کی تھیں، انہوں نے ایک معروف موجد اور سول انجینئر جان بریجس سے شادی کی۔ یہ نمایاں جوڑا اپنے ازدواجی دورِ حیات کے دوران لندن، انگلینڈ میں رہا، جب تک کہ نظم نگار کی موت چودہ سال بعد 1848 میں، کم عمری 43 سال پر واقع نہیں ہوئی۔

As we discussed in the first part of this two-part series, cancer is not a single entity. Various cancers have general similarities in that they develop from normal cells which mutate to make them grow in an uncontrolled, unnatural fashion, yet each type of cancer behaves in its specific, unique way.

Some cancers are aggressive, and some are much slower growing. Some tend to be localized and are quite slow to spread to other parts of the body, whereas others are likely to show up in locations far from where they began.

It is not possible to make blanket statements about cancers, but in this section, I will discuss some general things about prevention and treatment, then I’ll finish with some thoughts about us as Christians relating to someone who is dealing with cancer.

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

Many of the things that increase the risk of cancer are things that (hopefully) we, as Christian people, are already avoiding.

Tobacco is one such thing. Tobacco, when smoked, increases the risk of lung cancer. It also increases the risk of head cancer, neck cancers, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, and cancers of the liver and bladder.

Alcohol is another substance that raises the risk of cancer. Liver, voice box, and esophagus cancers are all related to alcohol consumption. Some people claim to drink alcohol for “health benefits,” but there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. Even people who drink moderately have an increased risk of death related to their alcohol usage.i

Another thing that should be limited is exposure to ultraviolet radiation. We know that UV radiation increases the risk of skin cancers, so wearing clothing that protects, such as hats and long-sleeved garments, and using sunblock can reduce this risk.

On the positive side of things, healthy eating habits, such as consuming lots of fruits and vegetables and avoiding highly processed foods, will reduce the risk of colon cancer.ii Fiber seems to be a key here and higher levels of dietary fiber are helpful. Additionally, fruits and vegetables are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals and are supportive of a healthy immune system. It is recommended to eat at least two servings of fruit and five servings of vegetables per day.

It is interesting that while people who eat healthy diets have a decreased risk of cancer, there is little evidence that there are specific vitamins that will prevent cancer. That is, there is little benefit if you eat a very unhealthy diet and then take vitamins in an effort to compensate for your unwise choices.

Prior to doing a controlled test it is always hard to know whether or not a certain supplement will help. Vitamin E is an antioxidant and so it was thought to be helpful in the prevention of cancer. However, it turns out that studies have not shown this to be true. Actually, in high doses, it seems to increase the risk of certain cancers and heart disease.iii

Rather than trying to find the right supplements, it is more important to make certain that we are eating healthy diets.

Chemotherapy

Now, let us move to a brief discussion about different types of treatment for cancer. Chemotherapy is probably what most people think of first. It was first used in the 1940s when doctors used a derivative of nitrogen mustard to treat lymphoma.

Since that time, hundreds of different medications have been developed as chemotherapy, designed to attack the cancer cells. It is hard to generalize about chemotherapy because there are so many different medications designed to treat different cancers and because they have different side effects.

Due to the fact that they attack cells that are rapidly multiplying, many of these drugs tend to make a person’s hair fall out since hair cells are of the rapidly multiplying type. Nausea, vomiting, and blood count alterations (low white cell counts) are other common side effects.

If a cancer has spread from its initial location, chances are good that it will require more than just one type of medication in order to achieve remission.

Even if a cancer hasn’t spread, surgeons will often recommend doing some chemotherapy ahead of surgery to shrink the tumor and to make surgical removal easier.

While chemotherapy sounds scary, it actually works quite well for certain types of cancers, such as blood cancers (like leukemias), lymphoma, and breast cancer.

These days, cancer doctors test the biopsied cancer cells for genetic markers. As a family doctor, I see these reports but, since I am not a specialist in this field, I find them somewhat confusing. The important thing to remember is that these markers help to predict what the best drugs are to use on a specific type of cancer.

Surgery

For many years, surgery was the cornerstone of cancer treatment. Cancers that have not spread can be removed entirely, allowing a person to move forward without any further treatment.

Often, by the time that a person’s cancer is discovered, it is too late to completely remove it. Surgery can still be helpful. For one thing, it gives a sample of the cancer for testing to help identify the best treatment. More than that, even if a cancer has spread, there are times that a tumor needs to be removed, simply because of the organs that it is putting pressure on.

I have heard some people claim that it is dangerous for a cancer to be exposed to oxygen. They believe that cancer cells spread faster after the tissues are opened up and exposed to the air during surgery. There is no documented evidence to support this idea. Many people do seem to get sicker after having an exploratory surgery when their cancer is being diagnosed. But the issue isn’t really the air getting into the cancer cells, rather the cancer was most certainly at the point of beginning to exhibit serious symptoms, and the surgery simply brought things to a head. Also, any surgery will be stressful for any person’s body, which will only increase the wearing down of a person’s already taxed strength and vitality—their ability to stay on top of a debilitating illness.

Typically, when a tumor is removed, nearby lymph glands will be sampled to see if they contain cancer cells. This presence, or absence, of cells helps with the “staging” of the cancer (such as “stage 3” or “stage 4”) and will provide insight for further treatment to prevent a chance of recurrence.

Immunotherapy

One of the newest treatments of cancer is called immunotherapy. These are medications that rev up a patient’s immune system to clear their body of cancer cells.

This sounds great and you would think the side effects should be minimal. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always work according to plan. Some cancers don’t respond to these sorts of treatments. And as far as side effects go, these medications can result in autoimmune diseases. When a medication is prescribed that makes the immune system extra active (or over-active), sometimes it begins to attack the patient’s own organs. While some of these side effects get better with the cessation of treatment, not all of them go away.

As an example, I had a patient who took immunotherapy for melanoma that had spread to his lymph glands. He was cured of the cancer, but the immunotherapy damaged his saliva glands enough that he has ongoing issues with a dry mouth. At this point, it seems unlikely that he will regain that moisture in his mouth.

Future Treatments

There will probably be more treatments in the future, targeting specific types of cancers. Something that is currently under investigation are vaccines that would target specific types of cancers. Currently none of these are available except in clinical trials.

Choosing Wisely

Oncologists (cancer specialists) do not know the future. They talk in terms of percentages. One protocol has an 86 percent chance of achieving a two-year remission from cancer, another only 56 percent. The same thing is true for side effects. While a doctor can tell you that 26 percent of patients get nauseated with a treatment, that doesn’t tell you if you will be one of that 26 percent and whether that nausea will be controllable with anti-nausea medication.

In deciding what course of treatment to choose, you will find no Bible passage to indicate one direction or another. Having a good oncologist who will explain things carefully—both the chance of success and risk of side effects—is key. There are times that you may need to change to a different cancer doctor, simply because the one you have does not take the time that you need to feel comfortable with your treatment.

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. We need wisdom in many areas of our lives, but certainly choosing how to navigate medical decisions is one of those areas. It is a wonderful thing that God has promised to give us the wisdom that we need—if we just ask.

Prayer—both personal prayer and by your church community—is very important. Prayers can be for healing. It can also be for caring, Christian, medical caregivers, and for wisdom in choosing the best treatments.

Sometimes God cures through doctors and medications. Sometimes, He heals in spite of them. Sometimes He decides it is time for us to go home to be with Him, thereby providing us with a new body that is not sick and broken.

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. With all of the medical technology available to us, it is easy to forget that healing comes from God. All the chemotherapy in the world will not avail if God does not work an act of healing. At the same time, there are many times that God works in miraculous ways to heal despite the dire predictions made by the medical professionals or other well-meaning individuals.

Often the best that a patient can do is to choose (according to their best judgment) the best treatment course (based on success rate and side effects) and then see how things go. If the side effects are too severe or the treatment doesn’t seem to be working, there is always the option to change.

Ultimately, when healing comes, regardless of how it comes, it is God that provides that healing. Let us never forget that.

Cancer Takes Energy

Relating to someone with cancer is not much different from relating to a person with any other chronic illness. There are differences though.

Both having cancer and receiving treatment for the cancer takes a lot of energy out of a person. While it is important not to ignore someone who has cancer, it is just as important to remember that they do not have endless energy supplies. A ten- or fifteen-minute visit may be all that they can handle. It is best to let them decide the length of visits that they have energy for.

Hesitate to Give Advice

Your “cousin” may have had cancer and may have gotten better after taking a particular supplement or visiting a particular clinic. Sharing that information with a person who is dealing with cancer is just one more piece of information for them to process out of a “thousand” others they may have received. It seems as though someone with cancer is often bombarded with advice and recommendations from well-meaning friends and family.

It is hard to figure out what the best thing is to do when a person is already low on energy. Sometimes, cancer patients simply have prayed that God would bless their choices and then have left the outcome in His hands.

If the cancer patient asks for your input, you can give it, but if not, it is probably best to hold off on the temptation to give unsought advice.

Listen

There is never a situation where listening isn’t beneficial. It is through listening that we allow others to unburden themselves from fears and frustrations. Listening can help the person to put their thoughts into words. More than that, we may hear ways in which we can help.

Maybe it is someone telling you the (too long) story of how their doctor missed their cancer. Or perhaps, it is them telling you about their fears regarding either their cancer or their treatments.

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. This verse comes in the midst of James talking about anointing with oil, confession of sins, and physical healing.

We can certainly pray for, and with, someone who is dealing with cancer. Listening helps us to know how best we can pray for them. It lets us know what their particular struggle is on a given day and how we can best lift them up to the throne.

The passage in James makes it clear that healing does not come from the oil that is poured over someone, but rather from God’s work in their life. The prayer, the faith, and the obedient action is more important than the anointing oil, although all demonstrate a dependence on a God who is always faithful.

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

If it is not enough to pray for someone who is dealing with a serious illness, it is certainly not enough to tell them, “God bless you.”

Figuring out what things someone with cancer needs help with may not be easy, but often even little tasks are difficult for them. It could be that they need transportation to a chemotherapy appointment. Maybe they need help with making a meal, with childcare, or with cleaning their house. Helping in whatever ways we can makes a huge difference for those who are dealing with the fatigue and stress of cancer.

More than that, the important thing is that we make the effort to demonstrate our love to those in our church body who are suffering. Paul told the Corinthians that when …one member suffer[s], all the members suffer with it… –1 Corinthians 12:26. Whenever there is a need, the rest of the local church body has an obligation and should have a deep desire to help in whatever way they can.

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

Chemotherapy can cause a cancer patient to have an extremely weak immune system. A normal white cell count is between 4,000 and 10,000. but during cancer treatments I have seen patient’s white cell count drop down to 200. In this scenario, if they catch any type of infection, they will be unable to fight off that infection and will end up in the hospital.

It is important to understand that someone in this condition who chooses to keep their distance is not necessarily trying to avoid fellowship. Rather, they are trying to avoid an unneeded hospital stay for what cancer doctors call a “neutropenic fever” (a febrile illness with a really low white cell count).

In these sorts of situations, phone calls or even text messages go a long way toward helping a brother or sister feel that they are not alone, even when they cannot physically be around other people.

Conclusion

I wish I could give a complete run down of every type of cancer out there and the best treatment for each one. That would be beyond my capability and further, it would be outdated within six months’ time.

What I can say is that prayer is key. Prayer for the Holy Spirit’s leading (see John 16:13), for energy for each day, for healing, and for God’s will to be done. Most of all, we need to pray that God would be glorified in and through us. (See 1 Peter 4:11) There have been so many people who were able to speak to their nurses and doctors about their Lord, even as they dealt with side effects and cancer symptoms.

It is easy to read all the instructions about giving up worrying that is found in Scripture and think that it should be easy to cast our cares on Him (see 1 Peter 5:7). However, it is much harder to put into practice. We may feel one day as though we have conquered fear and wake up the next morning with every bit as much anxiety as we ever had.

It is in this that we desperately need a church community. We are not alone, but we will feel alone unless we have brothers and sisters around us who help us as they are able and who pray for us in our valleys and rejoice with us in our times of victory.

It is only then, that we can come to the place that the Apostle Paul did when he said, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. Of course, he was talking about a possible execution, but his resignation to God’s will was total. I pray that we too might reach that place, even as we deal with something as difficult as cancer.

Soos ons in die eerste deel van hierdie tweeledige reeks bespreek het, is kanker nie 'n enkele entiteit nie. Verskeie kankers het algemene ooreenkomste in dat hulle ontwikkel uit normale selle wat muteer wat veroorsaak dat hulle op 'n onbeheerde, onnatuurlike wyse groei, maar elke soort kanker tree tog op sy eie spesifieke, unieke manier op.

Sommige kankers is aggressief, en ander groei baie stadiger. Sommige het 'n neiging om plaaslik te bly en is baie stadig om na ander dele van die liggaam te versprei, terwyl ander geneig is om op plekke ver van waar hulle begin het te verskyn.

Dit is nie moontlik om algemene stellings oor kankers te maak nie, maar in hierdie afdeling sal ek sommige algemene dinge oor voorkoming en behandeling bespreek, en dan sal ek afsluit met 'n paar gedagtes oor ons as Christene in verhouding tot iemand wat met kanker te doen het.

Lewenstylveranderinge om Kankers te Voorkom

Baie van die dinge wat die risiko van kanker verhoog, is dinge wat ons, as Christelike mense, hopelik reeds vermy.

Tobak is een so 'n ding. Tobak, wanneer dit gerook word, verhoog die risiko van longkanker. Dit verhoog ook die risiko van kopkanker, nekkankers, slukdermkanker, maagkanker, en kankers van die lewer en blaas.

Alkohol is 'n ander stof wat die risiko van kanker verhoog. Lewerkanker, strottenhoofkanker, en slukdermkanker is almal verwant aan alkoholgebruik. Sommige mense beweer dat hulle alkohol drink vir “gesondheidsvoordele,” maar daar is geen veilige vlak van alkoholgebruik nie. Selfs mense wat matig drink, het 'n verhoogde risiko van doodverwante gevolge van hul alkoholgebruik.i

'n Ander ding wat beperk moet word, is blootstelling aan ultravioletstraling. Ons weet dat UV-straling die risiko van velkankers verhoog, so om klere te dra wat beskerming bied, soos hoede en langmouklere, en om sonskerm te gebruik kan hierdie risiko verminder.

Aan die positiewe kant sal gesonde eetgewoontes, soos die verbruik van baie vrugte en groente en die vermyding van sterk verwerkte voedsel, die risiko van dikderm‑/rektumkanker verminder.ii Vesel blyk hier 'n sleutel te wees en hoër vlakke van dieetvesel is nuttig. Verder is vrugte en groente ryk aan antioksidante, vitamiene en minerale en ondersteunend tot 'n gesonde immuunstelsel. Dit word aanbeveel om ten minste twee porsies vrugte en vyf porsies groente per dag te eet.

Dit is interessant dat terwyl mense wat gesonde dieetgewoontes het 'n verlaagde risiko van kanker het, daar min bewyse is dat daar spesifieke vitamiene is wat kanker sal voorkom. Dit wil sê, daar is min voordeel as jy 'n baie ongesonde dieet eet en dan vitamiene inneem in 'n poging om jou onwyse keuses te kompenseer.

Voor 'n beheerde toets is dit altyd moeilik om te weet of 'n sekere aanvulling sal help of nie. Vitamien E is 'n antioksidant en daarom is gedink dit sal nuttig wees in die voorkoming van kanker. Dit blyk egter dat studies dit nie as waar getoon het nie. In hoë dosisse blyk dit trouens die risiko van sekere kankers en hartsiektes te verhoog.iii

In plaas daarvan om te probeer om die regte aanvullings te vind, is dit meer belangrik om seker te maak dat ons gesonde dieetgewoontes volg.

Chemoterapie

Kom ons gaan nou na 'n kort bespreking oor verskillende soorte behandeling vir kanker. Chemoterapie is waarskynlik wat die meeste mense eerste daaraan dink. Dit is die eerste keer in die 1940's gebruik toe dokters 'n afgeleide van stikstofmosterd gebruik het om limfoom te behandel.

Sedert daardie tyd is honderde verskillende medikasies as chemoterapie ontwikkel, ontwerp om die kankerselle aan te val. Dit is moeilik om te veralgemeen oor chemoterapie omdat daar soveel verskillende medikasies is wat vir verskillende kankers ontwerp is en omdat hulle verskillende newe‑effekte het.

As gevolg van die feit dat hulle selle aanval wat vinnig deel, het baie van hierdie dwelms 'n neiging om 'n persoon se hare te laat uitval aangesien hairselle van die vinnig deelende tipe is. Naarheid, braking en veranderings in bloedtelling (laag witbloedseltelling) is ander algemene newe‑effekte.

As 'n kanker van sy oorspronklike lokasie versprei het, is die kanse goed dat dit meer as net een soort medikasie sal verg om remissie te bereik.

Selfs as 'n kanker nie versprei het nie, sal chirurge dikwels aanbeveel om 'n bietjie chemoterapie voor chirurgie te gee om die gewas te verklein en sodoende bedryfsverwydering makliker te maak.

Hoewel chemoterapie eng klink, werk dit eintlik baie goed vir sekere tipes kankers, soos bloedkankers (soos leukemieë), limfoom, en borskanker.

Deesdae toets kankerdokters die biopsieerde kankerselle vir genetiese merkers. As huisdokter sien ek hierdie verslae, maar aangesien ek nie 'n spesialis op hierdie gebied is nie, vind ek dit ietwat verwarrend. Die belangrike ding om te onthou is dat hierdie merkers help om te voorspel watter die beste dwelms is om op 'n spesifieke tipe kanker te gebruik.

Chirurgie

Vir baie jare was chirurgie die hoeksteen van kankerbehandeling. Kankers wat nie versprei het nie, kan heeltemal verwyder word, wat 'n persoon toelaat om vorentoe te beweeg sonder verdere behandeling.

Oftentlik is dit teen die tyd dat 'n persoon se kanker ontdek word te laat om dit heeltemal te verwyder. Chirurgie kan steeds nuttig wees. Vir een ding gee dit 'n monster van die kanker vir toetsing om te help om die beste behandeling te identifiseer. Meer as dit, selfs as 'n kanker versprei het, is daar tye dat 'n gewas verwyder moet word, eenvoudig as gevolg van die organe waarop dit druk uitoefen.

Ek het gehoor dat sommige mense beweer dat dit gevaarlik is vir 'n kanker om aan suurstof blootgestel te word. Hulle glo dat kankerselle vinniger versprei nadat die weefsels oopgemaak en aan die lug blootgestel word tydens chirurgie. Daar is geen gedokumenteerde bewyse om hierdie idee te ondersteun nie. Baie mense lyk wel sieker nadat hulle 'n verkennende operasie ondergaan het wanneer hul kanker gediagnoseer word. Maar die saak is nie werklik die lug wat in die kankerselle inkom nie; eerder was die kanker heel seker al by die punt om ernstige simptome te begin toon, en die chirurgie het eenvoudig dinge aan die lig gebring. Ook sal enige operasie stresvol wees vir 'n persoon se liggaam, wat net sal bydra tot die uitputting van 'n persoon se reeds belasde krag en vitaliteit—hul vermoë om bo 'n uitputtende siekte te bly.

Tipies, wanneer 'n gewas verwyder word, sal nabygeleë limfkliere bemonster word om te sien of hulle kankerselle bevat. Die teenwoordigheid of afwesigheid van selle help met die “stadiering” van die kanker (soos “stadium 3” of “stadium 4”) en sal insig gee vir verdere behandeling om 'n kans vir terugkeer te voorkom.

Immunoterapie

Een van die nuutste behandelings van kanker word immunoterapie genoem. Dit is medikasies wat 'n pasiënt se immuunstelsel aanskakel om hul liggaam van kankerselle te suiwer.

Dit klink wonderlik en jy sou dink die newe‑effekte sou minimaal wees. Ongelukkig werk dit nie altyd volgens plan nie. Sommige kankers reageer nie op hierdie soort behandelings nie. En wat newe‑effekte betref, kan hierdie medikasies outo‑immuun siektes veroorsaak. Wanneer 'n medikasie voorgeskryf word wat die immuunstelsel ekstra aktief (of ooraktief) maak, begin dit soms die pasiënt se eie organe aanval. Terwyl sommige van hierdie newe‑effekte verbeter met die staak van behandeling, verdwyn nie almal nie.

Byvoorbeeld, ek het 'n pasiënt gehad wat immunoterapie geneem het vir melanoom wat na sy limfkliere versprei het. Hy is genees van die kanker, maar die immunoterapie het sy speekselkliere genoeg beskadig dat hy aanhoudende probleme met 'n droë mond het. Op hierdie stadium lyk dit onwaarskynlik dat hy daardie vog in sy mond sal herwin.

Toekomstige Behandelings

Daar sal waarskynlik meer behandelings in die toekoms wees wat op spesifieke tipes kankers teiken. Iets wat tans ondersoek word, is entstowwe wat spesifieke tipes kankers sou teiken. Tans is geen van hierdie beskikbaar behalwe in kliniese proewe nie.

Wyse Keuses

Onkoloë (kankerspesialiste) ken nie die toekoms nie. Hulle praat in terme van persentasies. Een protokol het 'n 86 persent kans om 'n tweejaarlikse remissie van kanker te bereik, 'n ander slegs 56 persent. Dieselfde geld vir newe‑effekte. Terwyl 'n dokter jou kan vertel dat 26 persent van pasiënte naarheid ervaar met 'n behandeling, sê dit jou nie of jy een van daardie 26 persent sal wees en of daardie naarheid beheersbaar sal wees met anti‑nausa medikasie nie.

In die besluitneming oor watter behandelingskursus om te kies, sal jy geen Bybelvers vind wat een rigting bo die ander aandui nie. Om 'n goeie onkoloog te hê wat dinge noukeurig sal verduidelik—beide die kans op sukses en die risiko van newe‑effekte—is sleutel. Daar is tye dat jy dalk na 'n ander kankerdokter moet verander, eenvoudig omdat die een wat jy het nie die tyd neem wat jy nodig het om gemaklik te voel met jou behandeling nie.

As iemand van julle wysheid ontbreek, laat hom vir God vra, wat aan alle mense vrygewig gee en nie oproepe nie; en dit sal aan hom gegee word – Jakobus 1:5. Ons het wysheid in baie areas van ons lewens nodig, maar sekerlik is die keuse hoe om mediese besluite te navigeer een van daardie areas. Dit is 'n wonderlike ding dat God belowe het om ons die wysheid te gee wat ons nodig het—as ons net vra.

Gebed—sowel persoonlike gebed as deur jou kerkgemeenskap—is baie belangrik. Gebede kan wees vir genesing. Dit kan ook wees vir sorgsame, Christelike, mediese versorgers, en vir wysheid in die keuse van die beste behandelings.

Soms genees God deur dokters en medikasie. Soms genees Hy ondanks hulle. Soms besluit Hy dat dit tyd is dat ons huis toe gaan om by Hom te wees, en gee ons daardeur 'n nuwe liggaam wat nie siek en gebreek is nie.

Loof die HERE, my siel, en vergeet nie al sy weldade nie: Hy vergeef al jou ongeregtighede; Hy genees al jou siektes – Psalm 103:2-3. Met al die mediese tegnologie wat vir ons beskikbaar is, is dit maklik om te vergeet dat genesing van God kom. Al die chemoterapie in die wêreld sal nie help as God nie 'n daad van genesing werk nie. Tegelykertyd is daar baie kere dat God op wonderlike maniere werk om te genees ondanks die kommerwekkende voorspellings wat deur mediese professionele persone of ander welbedoelende individue gemaak is.

Dikwels is die beste wat 'n pasiënt kan doen om (volgens hul beste oordeel) die beste behandelingskursus te kies (gegrond op sukseskoers en newe‑effekte) en dan te kyk hoe dinge verloop. As die newe‑effekte te ernstig is of die behandeling lyk nie asof dit werk nie, is daar altyd die opsie om te verander.

Uiteindelik, wanneer genesing kom, ongeag hoe dit kom, is dit God wat daardie genesing voorsien. Laat ons dit nooit vergeet nie.

Kanker Neem Energie

In verhouding tot iemand met kanker is nie veel anders as in verhouding tot 'n persoon met enige ander chroniese siekte nie. Daar is egter verskille.

Om kanker te hê en om behandeling vir die kanker te ontvang neem baie energie uit 'n persoon. Terwyl dit belangrik is om nie iemand met kanker te ignoreer nie, is dit net so belangrik om te onthou dat hulle nie oneindige energiebronne het nie. 'n Tien‑ of vyftienminuut besoek mag al wees wat hulle kan hanteer. Dit is die beste om hulle te laat besluit oor die duur van besoeke waarvoor hulle energie het.

Hesiteer om Raad te Gee

Jou “neef” het dalk kanker gehad en het dalk beter geraak nadat hy 'n bepaalde aanvulling geneem het of 'n bepaalde kliniek besoek het. Om daardie inligting te deel met 'n persoon wat met kanker te doen het, is net nog 'n stukkie inligting wat hulle uit 'n “duisend” ander wat hulle ontvang het moet prosesseer. Dit lyk asof iemand met kanker dikwels bestorm word met advies en aanbevelings van welbedoelende vriende en familie.

Dit is moeilik om uit te vind wat die beste ding is om te doen wanneer 'n persoon reeds laag aan energie is. Soms het kankerpasiënte eenvoudig vir God gebid dat Hy hul keuses sal seën en het dan die uitkoms in Sy hande gelaat.

As die kankerpasiënt vir jou om insette vra, kan jy dit gee, maar indien nie, is dit waarskynlik die beste om die versoeking te weerstaan om ongevraagd advies te gee.

Luister

Daar is nooit 'n situasie waar luister nie voordelig is nie. Dit is deur luister dat ons ander toelaat om hulself te verlig van vrese en frustrasies. Luister kan help dat die persoon hul gedagtes in woorde sit. Meer as dit, kan ons maniere hoor waarop ons kan help.

Miskien is dit iemand wat jou die (te lang) verhaal vertel van hoe hul dokter hul kanker gemis het. Of dalk vertel hulle jou van hul vrese wat betrekking het op óf hul kanker óf hul behandelings.

Bid

…Die kragtige gebed van 'n regverdige mens werk baie – Jakobus 5:16. Hierdie vers kom te midde van Jakobus se praat oor die salwing met olie, belydenis van sondes, en fisiese genesing.

Ons kan sekerlik bid vir en met iemand wat met kanker te doen het. Luister help ons om te weet hoe ons die beste vir hulle kan bid. Dit laat ons weet wat hul spesifieke stryd op 'n bepaalde dag is en hoe ons hulle die beste na die troon kan ophef.

Die gedeelte in Jakobus maak duidelik dat genesing nie van die olie kom wat oor iemand uitgegooi word nie, maar eerder van God se werk in hul lewe. Die gebed, die geloof, en die gehoorsame aksie is belangriker as die salwingolie, alhoewel almal 'n afhanklikheid van 'n God wat altyd getrou is demonstreer.

Doen Klein Take

As 'n broeder of suster kaal is en geen daaglikse voedsel het nie, en een van julle tot hulle sê: Gaan in vrede, wees verwarm en verzadig; en tog gee julle nie aan hulle wat die liggaam benodig nie; wat help dit? – Jakobus 2:15-16.

As dit nie genoeg is om vir iemand wat met 'n ernstige siekte te doen het te bid nie, is dit beslis nie genoeg om vir hulle te sê, “God seën jou.”

Om uit te vind wat dinge iemand met kanker hulp nodig het mag nie maklik wees nie, maar dikwels is selfs klein take moeilik vir hulle. Dit kan wees dat hulle vervoer na 'n chemoterapietyd nodig het. Miskien het hulle hulp nodig om 'n ete te maak, met kinderoppas, of met die skoonmaak van hul huis. Om te help op wat manier ons kan maak 'n reuseverskil vir diegene wat met die moegheid en stres van kanker te doen het.

Meer as dit, die belangrike ding is dat ons die moeite doen om ons liefde aan diegene in ons kerkliggaam wat ly, te toon. Paulus het vir die Korintiërs gesê dat wanneer …een lid ly, almal die lede saam met hom ly… – 1 Korintiërs 12:26. Wanneer daar 'n behoefte is, het die res van die plaaslike kerkliggaam 'n verpligting en moet 'n diep begeerte hê om te help op watter manier hulle kan.

Wees Bereid om Jou Afstand te Hou

Chemoterapie kan veroorsaak dat 'n kankerpasiënt 'n uiters swak immuunstelsel het. 'n Normale witbloedseltelling is tussen 4,000 en 10,000, maar tydens kankerbehandelings het ek pasiënte se witbloedseltelling sien daal tot 200. In hierdie scenario, as hulle enige tipe infeksie kry, sal hulle nie daardie infeksie kan beveg nie en sal hulle in die hospitaal beland.

Dit is belangrik om te verstaan dat iemand in hierdie toestand wat kies om afstand te hou nie noodwendig probeer om gemeenskap te vermy nie. Eerder probeer hulle 'n onnodige hospitaalopname vermy vir wat kankerdokters noem 'n “neutropeniese koors” (ʼn koorsende siekte met 'n regtig lae witbloedseltelling).

In hierdie soort situasies gaan telefoongesprekke of selfs teksboodskappe 'n lang pad om 'n broeder of suster te laat voel dat hulle nie alleen is nie, selfs wanneer hulle fisies nie by ander mense kan wees nie.

Gevolgtrekking

Ek wens ek kon 'n volledige uiteensetting gee van elke tipe kanker daaruit en die beste behandeling vir elk. Dit sou buite my vermoë wees en verder sou dit binne ses maande verouderd wees.

Wat ek kan sê, is dat gebed sleutel is. Gebed vir die Heilige Gees se leiding (sien Johannes 16:13), vir energie vir elke dag, vir genesing, en dat God se wil geskied. Bo alles moet ons bid dat God verheerlik sal word in en deur ons. (Sien 1 Petrus 4:11) Daar is soveel mense wat in staat was om met hul verpleegkundiges en dokters oor hul Here te praat, selfs terwyl hulle met newe‑effekte en kankersimptome te doen gehad het.

Dit is maklik om al die instruksies oor omgee wat in die Skrif gevind word te lees en te dink dit behoort maklik te wees om ons kommer op Hom te gooi (sien 1 Petrus 5:7). Dit is egter baie moeiliker om dit in praktyk te bring. Ons mag eendag voel asof ons vrees oorkom het en die volgende oggend opstaan met net soveel angs as wat ons nog ooit gehad het.

Dit is hierin dat ons dringend 'n kerkgemeenskap nodig het. Ons is nie alleen nie, maar ons sal ons alleen voel tensy ons broeders en susters om ons het wat help soos hulle kan en wat vir ons bid in ons dale en met ons juig in ons tye van oorwinning.

Dit is eers dan dat ons by die plek kan kom waar die Apostel Paulus was toe hy gesê het, Want my lewe is Christus en my sterwe is wins – Filippense 1:21. Natuurlik praat hy oor 'n moontlike onthoofding, maar sy oorgawe aan God se wil was totaal. Ek bid dat ons ook daardie plek mag bereik, selfs terwyl ons met iets so moeilik soos kanker te doen het.

Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:4-7.

“Oh God, give us mothers like Eunice and grandmothers like Lois. Give us women who are women of faith. Give us women who know how to stand for truth against the tide of human rationalization that is destroying the lives of so many well-meaning people. Give us women who are unwavering in their loyalty to Jesus Christ, to their husbands, and to their calling to represent the spirit of Jesus in all of life. Amen”.

History has proven that women are as influential as men in forming the fabric of society and of the Christian community. An argument could be made that they exert an even greater influence if you consider the fact that they have a huge role in shaping the values of little children and, whether or not they dress and conduct themselves according to godly modesty, they can influence the morality of the masses of men around them.

Hence the call for women to be women of faith. Not only does a woman’s faith influence those around her, but every woman has her own personal journey. Her journey is a search for identity, security, and purpose for her life.

Today’s women are inundated with voices that claim to offer the fulfillment that their heart desires. As with their mother Eve, many of these voices appeal to her feminine spirit, but as their mother Eve discovered, unless it is the voice of God, it leads to death and destruction.

The Bible abounds with accounts of women who lived by faith. Consider the harlot Rahab. Bible scholars cannot agree that she was worthy of that title, but it has come down to us as such. She heard the stories of the God of Israel. When she encountered the spies and heard their ominous prediction for her city she chose to believe.

She was a native of Jericho. Jericho was her home. Jericho had high stone walls and brave defenders. She would have had many reasons to place her faith in that which was familiar to her, and which had sustained her in the past.

She chose to place her faith in the God of Israel. The men of Israel told her that if she would hang a scarlet thread from her window on the wall, her house and her life would be spared. A scarlet thread. Not much by way of identity or security, but Rahab hung her faith on a scarlet thread. That scarlet thread represented the power of the God of Israel and, as we know today, it is a beautiful type of the blood of Jesus.

The call to be a woman of faith is a call to turn away from the ideology of the world and to embrace what in the eyes of the world is a futile remedy—a scarlet thread. Rahab’s faith was rooted in her knowledge of the God of Israel and His plan to judge her people. The scarlet thread was her hope of deliverance.

I would like for us to consider how faith in God impacts the primary desires of the feminine heart. Every woman longs for identity, security, and purpose. Jesus has come to meet that heart longing.

Identity –“Who am I?”

This is a question that everyone is compelled to ask at some point in their life—often in adolescence. Young men tend to carve out their identity based in whom they admire and their vocational inclinations. Young women, especially in our Anabaptist communities, are largely at the mercy of the prominent men in their lives to define their identity.

This is not purely cultural. When God said to Eve, …thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee –Genesis 3:16, He was declaring that she and her female descendants would look to the man to define an essential part of their nature.

Fathers play a key role in the early development of a little girl’s identity. Abusive fathers, absent fathers, and indifferent fathers leave in their wake little girls who are uncertain of who they are, or of their value as a person. A father who affirms his daughter’s godly femininity gives her a priceless gift. By that, I mean praising her for qualities of feminine virtue, blessing her for efforts to be chaste and modest, and yes, telling her that she is beautiful.

A woman’s heart will ultimately turn toward a husband. God said, “Thy desire shall be to thy husband”, not to thy father. Most women marry thinking that they have at last found their “savior” and rightly so. Did Paul not say in Ephesians chapter five that the husband is “the savior of the body”? Should a wife not expect to receive from her husband love, affirmation, protection, and provision? This is due to her by divine decree. A godly husband will do everything in his power to provide for her in this way.

“Thy desire shall be to thy husband” is given in the context of the fall. It was one of the consequences of the fall. It is a statement without the promise of fulfillment. This leaves us to believe that, although driven by desire, that desire may go unfulfilled.

What is a woman to do if her husband is unwilling or unable to satisfy her heart’s desire? What if a woman does not have a husband? She must become a woman of faith. Until a woman has found her identity in Jesus, no man will be able to satisfy the deepest longings of her heart.

Many marriages suffer because the wife expects her husband to meet the deep longings of her heart that only Jesus can fulfill. Many men are made to feel inadequate and withdraw when they are expected to be, and to do, for their wives what only Jesus can do.

Calling all women to be women of faith

Women of faith are women who know who they are in Christ Jesus. They have found the deepest longings of their feminine heart met in Him. Because their heart longings are satisfied, they have become a well spring of life to their husband, to their children, and to others.

Security –“Who will protect me?”

Being a woman has always been risky. Women are very vulnerable. In addition to the fact that they are physically more delicate, women are more susceptible to emotional vacillations, and I believe that based on what the Bible has to say about Eve’s deception, that women tend to be more vulnerable to spiritual deception (see 1 Timothy 2:14).

This does not make them inferior to men. Their emotional sensitivity makes them more attune to the many realities of relational problems than many men are. In this, their insight can be a positive thing, helping to balance us men in some of our natural weaknesses. Whatever comparisons we choose to make, I think we can all agree that women need the protection that men offer.

What if the man that is supposed to be protecting you is a coward? We have an example of just such a situation in the Bible. The man’s name is Abraham—yes… the father of faith. Even strong men sometimes make cowardly decisions.

Abraham and Sarah were traveling into Egypt. As they neared Egypt, Abraham became afraid for his life. His wife Sarah was a beautiful woman and Abraham was aware that Egypt was a heathen nation with very loose morals. He was afraid that the Egyptians would kill him so they could have his wife. Abraham said to Sarah, Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee –Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was indeed Abraham’s half-sister. They had the same father, but not the same mother. Abraham’s contingency plan leaves Sarah in a very difficult position. We read nothing of Sarah’s reaction to Abraham’s plan. All we know is that …Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:6.

It would appear that Sarah was not afraid. Her faith was not dependent on Abraham’s protection. She was relying on a higher power. Sarah’s faith gave her a place in the hall of faith in Hebrews chapter 11 and made her Peter’s example of how wives are to relate to their husbands.

The substance of this story is in the outcome. Because of Sarah’s faith, she was delivered from the hand of Pharaoh, the most powerful world ruler of the day. It was Sarah’s faith, not Abraham’s, which protected her.

Women look to men for security, and it is right that they should. Men protect their women as best they can. I believe that when men and women are living within their God-given roles, there is a lot of protection and security available; however, we do live in a fallen world. We do not always honorably fulfill our roles and sometimes God allows evil to befall even the most pious.

Calling all women to be women of faith even as Sarah

Do you have faith to believe that God is bigger than your husband or your father? Are you willing to trust God to overrule where your husband may be weak or even rebellious against God or the church?

A woman of faith is a woman who chooses to trust God in the absence of a reasonable path forward. A woman of faith continues to do what is right, even though it may not be a path of guaranteed security because …The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me –Hebrews 13:6.

Purpose – “Why am I here?”

This is a question that everyone asks at some point in life. We want our lives to have meaning and purpose. The futility of a meaningless living drives men and women into depression and despair. Living purposefully blesses us and others and brings honor to our Creator.

When men think of living purposefully, they envision… a battle to fight, a mountain to conquer, a noble goal to strive for. We men tend to be vision-oriented and goal-focused.

What does it mean for a woman to live purposefully?

Luke gives us some insight into this in the account of Jesus’ visit to the home of Mary and Martha. (See Luke 10:38-42) Jesus would frequently stop by this home when He was passing through Bethany. Here He knew He would find great hospitality and engaging conversation. Today was no exception.

As He relaxed in their sitting room, Mary sat at His feet asking questions and listening intently as He revealed to her the purpose of His life and His future destiny. Mary came to understand things about Jesus that even His disciples had failed to grasp.

Matthew records that when Jesus was dining in the house of Simon a woman, thought to be Mary of Bethany, entered, and knelt and anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive ointment. When the disciples complained about “this waste” Jesus said to them: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial –Matthew 26:12.

Where did Mary get this understanding? Was it not when she was “sitting at Jesus feet?”

Martha on the other hand was “cumbered about much serving”. Now Jesus had to eat. Someone needed to prepare food and I am certain that Jesus enjoyed Martha’s delicious provisions. But Jesus chided her with “Martha, Martha”. Notice the familial tone of his voice.

He was not judging her nor condemning her. He was challenging her to take time for the important things in life. He commended Mary for she …hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her –Luke 10:42.

I would like to suggest that most of our anxiety is of our own making. We set goals for our life that Jesus never required. We place expectations upon ourselves that have no eternal merit. Like Martha, we stress over frivolity, and damage relationships over trivial matters. Yes, supper must be served, and Mary should help, but not to neglect the “better part”.

Calling all women to be women of faith as Mary who loved to linger at Jesus feet

Life for a wife and mother is full of pressing demands. Defuse your life of stress and anxiety by spending time listening for the voice of Jesus—that “still small voice” that Elijah finally heard.

Stress and anxiety will melt away in the presence of Jesus. God speaks to us by His Holy Spirit through His Word. If it is a challenge for you to find time to sit down with your Bible, then you can quiet your spirit with your hands in the dishwater, or while folding the laundry, or as you once again prepare a meal for your family. At times like this you can commune with God. You can pray to your Father in heaven. You can say things like “I love you Lord Jesus, speak to me through Your Word, bring peace to my soul; quiet the wrestlings of my mind; help me to enter into Your rest; give me Your peace.” Then you can listen as His Spirit prompts your spirit with nuggets of truth from the Scriptures that are hidden away in your heart.

Summary –Calling all women to be women of faith

For your own personal wellbeing:

Women today are bombarded by self-help resources in the form of books, podcasts, social media, and seminars. Much of it is good and can be helpful, but nothing will replace a personal relationship and a daily walk with Jesus.

For the wellbeing of your children:

Today, more than ever we need mothers to be women of faith who can project onto their children that walking with God is real and satisfying. Young Timothy was influenced by the unfeigned faith of his mother and of his grandmother. Never underestimate the effect of the influence of your life on the lives of those who follow you.

For the strength of your husband:

Men today need the support of faithful women, especially their wife. A man’s daily walk can be fortified or diminished by the woman in his life. It has been said “Behind every successful man is woman”. A man is tremendously influenced for good or ill by the women in his life.

For the good of the Church:

Woman of faith, the church needs you. Women bring a grace to the church that is desperately needed. Your prayers are needed. Your testimony gives encouragement. Your song moves our hearts. Your smile gives hope. Your peaceful, joyful countenance of a soul that’s at rest in Jesus is an influence that is rivaled by little else in this world.
