ברצון רב לראותך, נזכר בדמעותייך, למען אמלא שמחה; כשאני נזכר באמונתך הבלתי מזויפת אשר שורה בך, אשר ראשונה שורה בסבתך לואיס ובאמך אונייס; ואני משוכנע שהיא גם בך. על-כן אני זוכרך לעורר את מתנת האלהים השורה בך על-ידי הנחת ידי. כי האלהים לא נתן לנו רוח פחד, כי אם רוח כוח ואהבה ושפיטה נכונה – 2 Timothy 1:4-7.

"אוי אלהים, תן לנו אמהות כמוה אוניּס ותוּבות סבתות כזאת לואיס. תן לנו נשים שהן נשים של אמונה. תן לנו נשים שיודעות לעמוד בעד האמת כנגד גל ההתאזרחות האנושית ההמחקקה אשר הורס חיי כל-כך הרבה אנשים בעלי כוונה טובה. תן לנו נשים הנאמנות לישוע המשיח, לנישואיהן ולקריאתן לייצג את רוח ישוע בכל תחומי החיים. אמן".

היסטוריה הראתה שנשים משפיעות לא פחות מן הגברים בעיצוב מרקם החברה ובקהילה הנוצרית. ניתן לטעון שאפילו השפעתן גדולה יותר אם לוקחים בחשבון שהן ממלאות תפקיד עצום בעיצוב ערכי הילדים הקטנים, ואם הן עוטות או לא מתנהגות לפי צניעות אלוהית—הן יכולות להשפיע על המוסר של המונים של גברים סביבן.

מכאן הקריאה לנשים להיות נשים של אמונה. לא רק שאמונתה של אישה משפיעה על הסובבים אותה, אלא שלכל אישה יש מסע אישי משלה. מסעה הוא חיפוש זהות, ביטחון ותכלית לחייה.

נשים של היום מוצפות קולות המבטיחים להן הגשמה של רצון ליבה. בדומה לאימוּתן חוה, קולות רבים אלה נוגעים לרוח נשיותה, אך כפי שאמוּתן חוה למדה, אלא אם כן קול אלהים—הוא מוביל למוות ולהרס.

התנ"ך שופע סיפורים של נשים שחיו באמונה. שקלו את הזונה רחב. מלומדי המקרא אין הסכמה מוחלטת אם הייתה ראויה לתואר זה, אך כך ירד לדורותינו. היא שמעה את סיפורי אלהי ישראל. כשנפגשה עם הרגלים ושמעה את תחזיתם המאיימת על עירה בחרה להאמין.

היא הייתה ילידת יריחו. יריחו היה ביתה. ליריחו היו חומות אבן גבוהות ומגינים אמיצים. היו לה סיבות רבות להניח את אמונתה במה שהיה לה מוכר וששימש אותה בעבר.

היא בחרה לשים את אמונתה באלהי ישראל. אנשי ישראל אמרו לה שאם תתלה חוט ארגמן מן החלון שבחומה, ביתה וחייה יינצלו. חוט ארגמן. לא הרבה בזה מבחינת זהות או ביטחון, אך רחב תלי את אמונתה על חוט ארגמן. חוט הארגמן הזה ייצג את כוחו של אלהי ישראל וכפי שאנו יודעים היום, הוא סוגה יפה מדם ישוע.

הקריאה להיות אישה של אמונה היא קריאה להפנות עורף לאידיאולוגיה של העולם ולאמץ מה שבעיני העולם הוא תרופה פחות תוחלתית—חוט ארגמן. אמונתה של רחב הייתה מושרשת בידיעתה את אלהי ישראל ואת תוכניתו לשפוט את עמו. חוט הארגמן היה תקוותה לישועה.

ברצוני שנשקול כיצד אמונה באלהים משפיעה על תשוקות ליבו של נשי. כל אישה משתוקקת לזהות, לביטחון ולמטרה. ישוע בא כדי לפגוש את כמיהה של הלב הזה.

זהות – "מי אני?"

זו שאלה שכל אחד נאלץ לשאול בנקודה כלשהי בחייו—לעתים קרובות בבגרות הנעורים. נערים נוטים לעצב את זהותם על-פי מי שהם מעריצים והנטיות המקצועיות שלהם. נערות, במיוחד בקהילות האונאבאפטיסטיות שלנו, למדי נתונות לחסד של הגברים הבולטים בחייהן שיסמכו להן את הזהות.

זה אינו רק עניין תרבותי. כשאלהים אמר לאשה חוה, …ונשואתך תהיה לבעלך והוא ישלוט בך – Genesis 3:16, הוא הכריז שהיא וצאצאיה הנקבות יפנו אל הגבר כדי להגדיר חלק מהותי מטבען.

אבות משחקים תפקיד מפתח בהתפתחות המוקדמת של זהותה של ילדה קטנה. אבות מתעללים, אבות נעדרים ואבות אדישים מותירים אחריהם בנות קטנות שאינן בטוחות מי הן או ערכן כאדם. אב המאשר את נשיותה האלוהית של בתו נותן לה מתנה שאין לה מחיר. בכוונתי בכך לשבח אותה על תכונות של מעלה נשית, לברך את מאמציה להיות טהורה וצנועה, וכן, לומר לה שהיא יפה.

לב של אישה יתחדש לבסוף אל עבר בעל. אלהים אמר, "נשואתך תהיה אל בעלך", לא אל אביך. רוב הנשים נישאות תוך מחשבה שמצאו סוף-סוף את "המושיע" שלהן וזה מוצדק. האם פאולוס לא אמר באפסיים פרק חמש שהבעל הוא "המושיע של הגוף"? האם לא מצפה שאשה תקבל מבעלה אהבה, אישור, הגנה וכלכלה? זו חובה לוּנת על-פי צו אלוהי. בעל חסיד יעשה הכול בעזרת כוחו כדי לספק לה בכך.

"נשואתך תהיה אל בעלך" ניתן בהקשר הנפילה. זו הייתה אחת מתוצאות הנפילה. זו אמירה בלי הבטחת הגשמה. זאת מותירה אותנו להאמין שלמרות שהרצון מונע על-ידי משיכה, ייתכן שרצון זה יישאר ללא מענה.

מה תעשה אישה אם בעלה אינו מוכן או אינו יכול לספק את כמיהת ליבה? ומה אם לאישה אין בעל? עליה להיות אישה של אמונה. עד שאשה לא תמצא את זהותה במשיח ישוע, אף גבר לא יוכל לספק את הכמיהות העמוקות של ליבה.

נישואין רבים סובלים מכיוון שהאשה מצפה שבעלה יענה על הכמיות העמוקות של ליבה שרק ישוע יכול למלא. גברים רבים מרגישים חסרי-כוח ונאחזים אחורה כשהם מצופים להיות ולעשות עבור נשותיהם את מה שרק ישוע יכול לעשות.

קריאה לכל הנשים להיות נשים של אמונה

נשים של אמונה הן נשים שיודעות מי הן במשיח ישוע. הן מצאו את הכמיהות העמוקות של לבן הנשי מסופקות בו. מפני שכמיות לבן מסופקות, הן נהיו מעיין של חיים עבור בעליהן, ילדיהן ואחרים.

ביטחון – "מי יגן עלי?"

להיות אישה תמיד היה מסוכן. נשים פגיעות מאוד. בנוסף לעובדה שהן פיזית עדינות יותר, נשים נוטות יותר לתמורות רגשיות, ואני מאמין שלפי מה שהתנ"ך אומר על שימתה של חוה, נשים נוטות אף להיות פגיעות יותר להתעה רוחנית (ראה 1 Timothy 2:14).

זה לא הופך אותן לפחותות מן הגברים. הרגישות הרגשית שלהן הופכת אותן ערניות יותר למציאויות רבות של בעיות יחסים מאשר רבים מהגברים. בכך, התובנה שלהן יכולה להיות דבר חיובי, המסייע לאזן אותנו הגברים בחלק מחולשותינו הטבעיות. לא משנה אילו השוואות נבחר לערוך, אני חושב שכולנו יכולים להסכים שנשים צריכות את ההגנה שהגברים מציעים.

מה אם האיש שאמור להגן עלייך הוא פחדן? יש לנו דוגמה למצב כזה בתנ"ך. שמו של האיש הוא אברהם—כן… אבי האמונה. גם אנשים חזקים לפעמים עושים החלטות פחדניות.

אברהם ושָרה נסעו למצרים. כשהתקרבו למצרים, אברהם פחד על חייו. אשתו שרה הייתה אישה יפה ואברהם ידע שמצרים היא אומה עובדת אלילים עם מוסר רופף. הוא חשש שהמצרים יהרגו אותו כדי שיקחו את אשתו. אברהם אמר לשרה, נא אמרי אנכי אחותי: למען ייטב לי בעבורך ונחיתה בחיי בגללך – Genesis 12:13.

אכן שרה הייתה חצי אחותו של אברהם. להם היה אותו אב אך לא אותה אם. תוכנית הגיבוי של אברהם השאירה את שרה במצב קשה מאוד. אין אצלנו כל קריאה לתגובה של שרה לתוכנית אברהם. כל מה שאנו יודעים הוא ש…שרה צייתה לאברהם וקראה לו אדון: שעל-כן אתןכן בנותיהן, כל עוד תעשי טוב וזה לא תיבהלי מכל תימה – 1 Peter 3:6.

נראה ששרה לא פחדה. אמונתה לא הייתה תלויה בהגנתו של אברהם. היא הסתמכה על כוח גבוה יותר. אמונתה של שרה נתנה לה מקום בהיכל האמונה שבאיגרת אל העברים פרק 11 והפכה אותה לדוגמה של פטרוס כיצד נשותיהן צריכות להתייחס לבעליהן.

עיקרון הסיפור הוא בתוצאה. בגלל אמונתה של שרה היא נמשׂלה מידי פרעה, השליט החזק ביותר של הימים ההם. זו הייתה אמונת שרה, לא אימונו של אברהם, שהגנה עליה.

נשים מסתכלות על גברים לצורך ביטחון, וזה נכון שיהיה כך. גברים מגנים על נשותיהם כמיטב יכולתם. אני מאמין שכאשר גברים ונשים חיים במסגרת התפקידים שנתן להם אלהים, יש הרבה הגנה וביטחון; עם זאת, אנו חיים בעולם נפל. אנו לא תמיד ממלאים את תפקידינו בכבוד ולעיתים אלהים מרשה שרעות תפלוש אפילו אל החסידים ביותר.

קריאה לכל הנשים להיות נשים של אמונה כשרה

האם יש בך אמונה להאמין שהאלהים גדול יותר מבעלך או מאביך? האם את מוכנה לבטוח באלהים שיתעל מעלה כאשר בעלך חלש או אפילו מרדני נגד האלהים או נגד הכנסייה?

אישה של אמונה היא אישה שבוחרת לבטוח באלהים בהיעדר דרך סבירה קדימה. אישה של אמונה ממשיכה לעשות את הישר, אף על פי שזה עשוי לא להיות דרך של ביטחון מובטח כי …ה׳ הוא עזרי, לא אירא מה יעשה לי אדם – Hebrews 13:6.

מטרה – "מדוע אני כאן?"

זו שאלה שכל אחד שואל בנקודה מסוימת בחיים. אנו רוצים לחיות חיים בעלי משמעות ותכלית. השוואיות של חיים חסרי משמעות דוחפת גברים ונשים לדיכאון ולייאוש. לחיות באופן מכוון מברכת אותנו ואת אחרים ומביאה כבוד לברואנו.

כשגברים חושבים על חיים בעלי מטרה הם מדמיינים… קרב לנצח, הר לכבוש, מטרה אצילית לשאוף אליה. אנחנו, הגברים, נוטים להיות מכווני חזון וממוקדי מטרה.

מה משמעות לחיות באורח ממוקד למען אישה?

לוקס נותן לנו תובנה לזה בסיפור ביקור ישוע בבית מרים ומרתא. (ראה Luke 10:38-42) ישוע היה פעמים רבות עובר בבית הזה כאשר עבר בבית עניה. כאן ידע למצוא הכנסת אורחים גדולה ושיחה מרתקת. היום לא היה יוצא מן הכלל.

בהשבתו בסלונם, מרים ישבה לרגליו ושאלה שאלות והקשיבה בתשומת לב כשהוא גילה לה את ייעוד חייו וגורלו העתידי. מרים החלה להבין דברים על ישוע שאפילו תלמידיו לא הצליחו לתפוס.

מתיאו רושם שכאשר ישוע אכל בבית שמעון אישה, הנחשבת למרים מבית עניה, נכנסה, כרעה וברחה ושחמה את רגלי ישוע בשמן יקר. כשהתלוננו התלמידים על "בזבוז זה" אמר להם ישוע: כי באותה שפכה היא על גופי את השמן הזה למאורע קברי – Matthew 26:12.

מאין באה למרים הבנה זו? האם לא היה זה כאשר ישבה "לרגלי ישוע"?

מרתא לעומת זאת הייתה "שרויה המשרתת בהרבה". כעת ישוע היה צריך לאכול. מישהי הייתה צריכה להכין את האוכל ואני בטוח שישוע נהנה ממאכליה הטעימים של מרתא. אך ישוע נזף בה ב"מרתא, מרתא". שימו לב לטון המשפחתי בקולו.

הוא לא שפט אותה ולא גינה אותה. הוא אתגר אותה לקחת זמן לדברים החשובים בחיים. הוא שיבח את מרים שלפיו …בחרה בחלק הטוב אשר לא ילקח ממנה – Luke 10:42.

ברצוני להציע שרוב חרדתנו היא תוצרתנו אנחנו עצמנו. אנו מציבים מטרות לחיינו שישוע מעולם לא דרש. אנו מטילים על עצמנו ציפיות שאין להן ערך נצחי. בדומה למרתא, אנו מתוחים על שטויות ומזיקים ליחסים על עניינים שולי ערך. כן, ארוחת הערב צריכה להיות מוגשת, ומרים צריכה לעזור, אך לא להזניח את ה"החלק הטוב".

קריאה לכל הנשים להיות נשים של אמונה כמרים שאהבו להתרפק לרגלי ישוע

חיי אשה נשואה ואם מלאים בדרישות לוחצות. פזרי מתח וחרדה בחייך על-ידי בילוי זמן בהאזנה לקול ישוע—אותו "קול דמום הדק" שאליהו בסוף שמע.

מתחים וחרדות יימסו בנוכחות ישוע. אלהים מדבר אלינו ברוחו הקדושה דרך דברו. אם זהו אתגר עבורך למצוא זמן לשבת עם ספר התנ"ך, תוכלי להשקיט את רוחך עם ידייך במדיח הכלים, או בעת קיפול הכביסה, או כאשר את שוב מכינה ארוחה למשפחתך. בזמנים אלה תוכלי להיות בקשר עם האלהים. תוכלי להתפלל לאביך שבשמים. תוכלי לומר דברים כמו "אני אוהבת אותך אדוני ישוע, דבר אלי דרך הדבר שלך, הביא שלום לנפשי; השקט את מאבקי מחשבתי; עזור לי לחדור למנוחתך; תן לי את שלוםך." ואז תוכלי להקשיב כשהרוח שלו מנחה את רוחך בגרגירי אמת מתוך הכתובים שמוסתרים בלבך.

סיכום – קריאה לכל הנשים להיות נשים של אמונה

לרווחתך האישית:

נשים של היום מוצפות במשאבי עזרה עצמית כמו ספרים, פודקאסטים, רשתות חברתיות וסמינרים. חלק גדול מזה טוב ויכול להיות מועיל, אך אף דבר לא יחליף מערכת יחסים אישית והליכה יומית עם ישוע.

לרווחת ילדיך:

היום, יותר מתמיד אנחנו זקוקים לאמהות שהן נשים של אמונה שיוכלו לשדר לילדיהן שההליכה עם האלהים היא אמיתית ומספקת. טימותיוס הצעיר הושפע מאמונתה הבלתי מזויפת של אמו וסבתו. אל תמעיטי בערכה של השפעת חייך על חיי הבאים אחריך.

לעוצמת בעלך:

גברים של היום זקוקים לתמיכת נשים נאמנות, ובמיוחד של רעייתם. הליכתו היומית של גבר יכולה להתחזק או להיחלש על-ידי האישה בחייו. נאמר "מאחורי כל גבר מצליח עומדת אישה". גבר מושפע מאוד לטוב או לרע על-ידי הנשים בחייו.

לטובת הכנסייה:

אישה של אמונה, הכנסייה זקוקה לך. נשים מביאות לכנסייה חסד שנואש ממנו. תפילותייך נחוצות. עדותך נותנת עידוד. שירתך נוגעת בלבנו. חיוכך מעניק תקווה. פנייתך השלווה ושמחת נשמה השוכנת במנוחת ישוע היא השפעה שמעומדת במעט מאוד בעולם הזה.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.

Cet hymne est universellement considéré comme l’un des plus grands hymnes jamais composés par une femme. On le trouve dans presque tous les recueilshymniques ou livres d’hymnes publiés aujourd’hui. Cette auteure d’hymnes était une femme d’une grande ambition et d’un grand goût de la vie ; une personne pleine de vie, vive, belle, talentueuse, et dont « le caractère élevé faisait toujours une profonde impression sur tous ceux qui la connaissaient ». Bien qu’elle ait eu une vie pleine et productive, elle fut courte, hâtée par sa constitution délicate et frêle. L’histoire de cet hymne a touché de nombreuses vies en des temps de détresse et d’épreuve, y compris la mort. Il a été utilisé par Dieu pour attirer les cœurs des hommes hors de leurs détresses présentes, vers le ciel, vers les réalités immortelles au-delà de cette vie.

Sarah Flower Adam est née à Harlow, en Angleterre, le 22 février 1805, de Benjamin et Eliza Flower. Quand elle avait cinq ans, sa mère mourut de consomption, connue aujourd’hui sous le nom de tuberculose. Sarah et sa sœur aînée Eliza héritèrent aussi de la même faiblesse physique. À propos de l’auteure de l’hymne, je cite 101 Hymn Stories : « Elle était également largement connue pour ses nombreuses réalisations littéraires, bien que sa santé délicate ait toujours été un handicap pour ses nombreuses ambitions. »

En 1834, à l’âge de 29 ans, Sarah épousa un inventeur et ingénieur civil éminent, John Brydges. Ce couple distingué fit leur foyer à Londres, en Angleterre, pendant toute la durée de leur mariage, jusqu’à la mort de l’auteure de l’hymne quatorze ans plus tard, en 1848, à l’âge précoce de 43 ans.

Sarah et sa sœur aînée Eliza formaient une équipe remarquable dans le domaine de la musique—écrivant et composant de nouveaux chants. L’aînée était une musicienne accomplie, et la cadette la parolière d’hymnes. Un jour, leur pasteur, le Rév. William Johnson Fox, demanda à ces deux sœurs remarquables si elles accepteraient de l’aider à compiler un nouveau recueil d’hymnes pour sa congrégation. Elles s’engagèrent dans le projet, et bientôt furent occupées à l’aider à compléter le livre de chants. « Ensemble, elles contribuèrent treize textes et soixante-deux nouveaux airs. »

Un jour, alors que les deux sœurs se penchaient sur la tâche, le pasteur remarqua qu’il aurait aimé avoir un hymne pour conclure un sermon qu’il préparait sur le récit de Jacob et Ésaü. Eliza interrompit avec enthousiasme : « Sarah, voilà une excellente idée pour un nouvel hymne pour notre recueil. Pourquoi n’écrirais-tu pas ton propre hymne sur le rêve de Jacob ? »

« Splendide ! » répondit le pasteur. Plus tard ce jour-là, après avoir passé beaucoup de temps à étudier le récit de la Genèse, à en absorber l’atmosphère et à ressentir le mouvement dramatique de ce récit de l’Ancien Testament, Sarah se mit à écrire. Bientôt elle eut versifié l’intégralité de l’histoire biblique en ces cinq strophes de l’hymne immortel encore en usage aujourd’hui.

Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !
Même si c’est une croix
Qui m’élève ;
Pourtant tout mon chant serait,
Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !

Comme le vagabond,
Le soleil couché,
Les ténèbres sur moi,
Mon repos une pierre ;
Pourtant dans mes rêves je serais
Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !

Que là se montre le chemin,
Des marches vers le ciel :
Tout ce que tu m’envoies
Donné par miséricorde ;
Des anges pour m’appeler
Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !

Puis, dans mes pensées éveillées
Éclatantes de ta louange,
Hors de mes douleurs de pierre
Bethel j’élèverai ;
Ainsi par mes maux être
Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !

Ou si sur une aile joyeuse
Fendant le ciel,
Soleil, lune et étoiles oubliés,
Vers le haut je m’envole,
Toujours tout mon chant sera,
Plus près de toi, mon Dieu,
Plus près de toi !

Ce grand hymne fut écrit en 1840 et publié l’année suivante dans le recueil d’hymnes Hymns and Anthems préparé par le Rév. Fox, le pasteur de l’auteure de l’hymne. L’air original de l’hymne était une composition d’Eliza, la sœur aînée de Sarah. En 1844, le Rév. James Freeman Clarke introduisit l’hymne en Amérique, mais il ne devint pas bien connu avant douze ans. À ce moment-là l’hymne fut uni à la mélodie actuelle « Bethany » composée spécialement pour le texte par Lowell Mason, que l’on appelle parfois le père de la musique d’église et scolaire américaine. Parmi les autres hymnes de Mason figurent « From Greenland’s Icy Mountains », « When I Survey the Wondrous Cross », « A Charge to Keep I Have », « Joy to the World », « My Faith Looks Up to Thee », et « O Day of Rest and Gladness ».

De nombreux récits très intéressants ont été consignés en rapport avec l’utilisation de cet hymne, et son effet sur ceux qui le chantaient ou l’entendaient chanter. Lors du Boston Peace Jubilee de 1872, qui commémorait la fin de la guerre civile, cet hymne, « Nearer, My God to Thee », fut chanté par 50 000 voix. En 1871, trois théologiens réputés, les professeurs Hitchcock, Smith et Park, voyageaient en Palestine, lorsqu’ils entendirent arriver à leurs oreilles les faibles accords de « Bethany ». À propos de cet incident, je cite A Treasury of Hymn Stories : « En s’approchant, à leur grande étonnement, ils virent cinquante étudiants syriens debout sous des arbres en cercle, et chantant en arabe ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee’. Le professeur Hitchcock, parlant ensuite de l’événement, déclara que le chant de cet hymne chrétien par ces jeunes Syriens le fit pleurer, et l’affecta plus que tout chant qu’il eût jamais entendu auparavant. »

Lors du déluge de la ville de Johnstown du 31 mai 1889 (une tragédie qui tua plus de 2 000 personnes), un malheureux train de chemin de fer fut emporté par les eaux tourbillonnantes. Une jeune femme, destinée à être missionnaire, et en route pour l’Extrême-Orient, devint l’une de celles prises au piège dans un wagon de chemin de fer qui se retrouva retourné. Sans espoir de secours, elle parla calmement à la foule stupéfaite qui regardait, impuissante, la tragédie se dérouler tandis que le wagon coulait sous les eaux boueuses. Elle termina par une prière et en chantant « Nearer, my God, to Thee », rejoint par la foule en deuil et compatissante. Alors qu’elle chantait, elle mourut, venant en vérité plus près de son Dieu qu’elle aimait et qu’elle désirait servir.

Enfin, mais non des moindres, aux petites heures du 15 avril 1912, l’histoire du naufrage du fier et malheureux navire, le Titanic, ramène encore cette chanson à notre mémoire. De nombreux survivants ayant été témoins de cette grande tragédie ont attesté que l’hymne « Nearer, my God to Thee » fut la dernière chanson jouée avant que les vagues glaciales de l’océan Atlantique ne le fassent taire à jamais—alors que l’orchestre jouait, le grand navire sombra, plongeant dans les profondeurs, envoyant plus de 1 500 âmes dans l’éternité.

En conclusion, il est incroyable à quel point la musique et le chant nous affectent. Comme nous l’avons vu à travers certains de ces récits, de la louange au péril, de l’action de grâce à la tragédie, de l’adoration aux pires catastrophes que l’homme puisse éprouver, Dieu nous a donné ce don inestimable dans la possession intemporelle des vieux hymnes d’autrefois. Puissent-ils ne jamais perdre de leur éclat dans nos vies ni dans celles de notre postérité, jusqu’à ce jour final où le temps cessera d’exister.

This story starts in Switzerland, in the 1500s. A group of Christian believers, desiring to obey Jesus and return to the teachings of the Apostles and the early Church, separated from both the Catholic and Protestant state-run Churches in several Cantons of Switzerland. They were referred to as the Swiss Brethren and were deemed as enemies of the state, by the Catholics and Protestants alike. Their enemies called them “Anabaptists” because they rejected infant baptism. They also refused military service, obeying Christ’s commands to “bless them that persecute you” and “love your enemies”. Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith. In the early 1600s, when the authorities could not stop the movement in this manner, they began confiscating the believer’s homes, farms, and belongings, then exiled them from Switzerland.

Europe had just gone through the devastations of the Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648). In some places, like the Palatinate (Pfaltzland) in Germany, as many as 70% of the inhabitants had died of either war or disease. Many of the Hoffs (house/barn fort enclosures) were burned out and the fields were left uncultivated for years. In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms because of their reputation as excellent husbandmen and tillers of the soil.

There were three official Churches recognized by the Germans: Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed. Although the Swiss Brethren were needed economically, and their faith was tolerated, their churches were not recognized. There were limits on how many of them could meet together at one time, and many times they were not allowed to purchase the farms that they were improving because they were considered foreigners.

The Swiss-operated farms did indeed prosper in time, partly due to their use of a superior crop rotation system, which helped them feed more dairy cattle, and, in turn, allowed them to produce milk through the winters. Another major improvement was the introduction of the legume, clover. This came from seed which the Dutch Mennonites gifted to them. After about 50 years, the difference the Swiss had made in agriculture was noticeable enough that some frustrated German neighbors accused them of “Ferhexing” (the Pennsylvania Dutch term for witchcraft) the ground (which of course was not true). So, life in the Pfaltzland wasn’t getting better for the Swiss Brethren.

In the year 1708, they experienced a bitterly cold, long winter. So cold that some of their stored root crops froze in the cold cellars. Sometime after this, William Penn and the Quakers heard of the plight of these Swiss Anabaptists. In 1682, William Penn had been granted the colony of Pennsylvania and wanted to conduct what he called the “Holy Experiment”. He envisioned a land where all races and religions could dwell together in peace. He had special interest in those groups persecuted by the European State Churches. As a Quaker, he too had suffered persecution by the state church of England. He welcomed Quakers from England, Huguenots from France, Mennonites from Holland, German Baptist, Schwenkfelders and Pietists from Germany, as well as Swiss Brethren and Jews from wherever they were sojourning and/or suffering.

That is the background for our account of Hans Graeff (Groff) who lived from c.1661-1746. Hans had been converted to the faith of the Swiss Brethren, but his wife, Anna (Bare) Graeff had stayed with the Protestant State Church. When the door opened to pioneer in Pennsylvania, Hans was interested in going, but Anna was not. Possibly they planned to have him get settled in over there and then come back for her. Hans first came to Pennsylvania in 1696. Later, Hans ended up leading a small group of the Swiss Brethren (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & the Funks to name a few) to Germantown, about seven miles north of Philadelphia in that day, which was the first permanent settlement of the Anabaptists in the New World. Many of those first settlers were from Holland and Sweden and were part of the Mennonite Church of the Netherlands. The Swiss immigrants spent the winter of 1709 in Germantown—the women doing spinning for the many weavers of Germantown and the men traveling to a new Anabaptist settlement at Skippack, where they were learning many of the skills needed to go to the frontier. It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.

In 1710, the group moved up to the Conestoga Valley where Hans Groff had previously identified some very rich and well-watered lands, 60 miles west of Germantown and civilization. Life would indeed be difficult. Wolves, bears, panthers, bobcats and other predators abounded. There were also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer in abundance (which were glad to eat whatever the settlers planted). Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples, white pines, and oaks, some six feet in diameter and over 100 feet tall, covered much of their new lands (except for some open meadows, left by the native Americans and wetlands). These huge trees would need to be cut down by hand with axes and two-man saws. The closest doctor, apothecary, hardware, or general store was 60 miles away. It would be challenging and dangerous work, but they were free! Free to obey their conscience. Free to practice their religion. Free to own land in this beautiful wilderness. Free to love and witness to their neighbors—the Conestoga tribe and French traders. They received a land patent for 10,000 acres for their families and others that might come later.

Partly due to severe persecution, in 1710, a group of Swiss Brethren moved to the Mannheim area of Germany. Seven years later, in 1717, they made the trip across the Atlantic. There were more than 60 families that came to the Conestoga Valley in the fall of that year, including my ancestors, Hans and Magdalena Hess and their three children (they were eventually blessed with a total of 11). You could say that from then on, the floodgates opened, and masses of Anabaptists fled Europe to “Penn’s Promised Land”. From 1730 and later, as this wilderness became tamed, there were also many Lutheran, Reformed, and Catholic people who came over from Germany to find better financial opportunities, filling this part of Pennsylvania with many German-dialect speakers.

I greatly enjoyed speaking with the noted Lancaster County Anabaptist historian, Amos Hoover, while writing this article. He gave many insights and details, but we both agreed, it is challenging to put together all the facts and details from so long ago. Gleaning from a couple authors’ accounts, the story goes something like this:

Misunderstanding

Sometime, after being in Penn’s woods for a number of years, Hans Groff received word that his wife, Anna (Bare) Groff, back in Europe, had passed away. He was very grieved and mourned, as he didn’t know it and wasn’t there to bury her. In a few years, he married Susanna Kendig. They lived first in the Strasburg area, then built a substantial homestead in the area now called Groffdale. This union was blessed with nine children.

Years later, a woman showed up in the community and introduced herself as Mrs. Hans Groff. She had become an Anabaptist in Europe and had made the perilous trip across the Atlantic to find her husband. According to her, a person with the same name as herself had died, and the word given to Hans was not true about his first wife’s death. Hans was mortified, although he was innocent regarding his second marriage. He had no desire to be a polygamist or to commit adultery. The frontier church leaders held counsel and gave a recommendation—that the younger, pioneer wife with so many young children needed the husband to provide for them. It is said that Hans didn’t feel clear to stay with either of them but did support both of his wives and their children financially. He was noted as a tireless traveler, riding to Philadelphia with furs then back out into the vast frontier with blankets, brass kettles and other trade good for the Native Americans. If you have heard or read this account with different details, so have I. Only eternity will reveal all these details exactly.

Medicine

Hans’s first wife chose to live as a single sister in that church community. Instead of becoming bitter with her husband, her God, and her circumstances, she chose a life of service to her neighbors. She lived in a little house, with a small barn (possibly built by Hans for her) on top of a steep hill overlooking Farmersville, called “Cat’s Back Hill”. The ruins of this early 1700s house and barn were still evident less than 50 years ago. Apparently, she was a midwife, before coming to this country and continued in this profession once she was here. She had a lot of experience with growing herbs and making herbal remedies. She was possibly the closest one to being a doctor for many miles around. From what I can find out, she spent her time being a blessing to the local community with her medical knowledge and wisdom, her homemade herbal medicines, and her midwifery. Many of our Lancaster County forefathers may not have survived the rigorous pioneer life if it had not been for this dear Sister’s servanthood and medical knowledge. Interestingly, years later, one of Hans’s sons from the second wife, David Groff, went away to study medicine. Once his studies were completed, he came back as a doctor and helped his father’s first wife minister to the many settlers in fast growing Lancaster County.

This story provides a glimpse into some of the interesting details surrounding the life of conservative Anabaptists just before and during the establishing of Colonial America. There were difficulties involving freedom of religion and worship in their homelands of Europe, but their travels to, and eventual day-to-day living in, a new, free country was acquainted with challenges as well. One encouragement that we can see in this story was the willingness of these individuals to allow God’s principles to guide them each step of the way.

이 이야기는 1500년대 스위스에서 시작됩니다. 예수님을 순종하고 사도들과 초대 교회의 가르침으로 돌아가기를 원하는 기독교 신자들 무리가 스위스의 여러 칸톤에서 가톨릭과 국가 운영의 개신교 교회들로부터 분리되었습니다. 그들은 스위스 형제(Swiss Brethren)라 불렸고, 가톨릭과 개신교 양측 모두에게 국가의 적으로 간주되었습니다. 그들의 적들은 유아 세례를 거부했기 때문에 그들을 ‘재세례파(Anabaptists)’라 불렀습니다. 또한 그들은 “너희를 박해하는 자들을 복 주라”와 “너의 원수를 사랑하라”는 그리스도의 명령을 따라 군 복무도 거부했습니다. 많은 이들이 체포되고 투옥되었으며 무자비하게 고문당했고, 신앙을 철회하지 않았기 때문에 결국 많은 이들이 순교당했습니다. 1600년대 초에 당국이 이런 방식으로 운동을 막지 못하자 신자들의 집과 농장, 소유물을 몰수하고 스위스에서 추방하는 조치를 취했습니다.

유럽은 막 30년 전쟁(1618–1648)의 참화를 겪은 상태였습니다. 독일의 팔츠(Pfaltzland)와 같은 일부 지역에서는 주민의 최대 70%가 전쟁이나 질병으로 사망했을 정도였습니다. 많은 호프(Hoff: 가옥/외양간 포함한 요새화한 구획)들이 불타 버렸고 들판은 여러 해 동안 경작되지 못했습니다. 1600년대 중반, 현지의 귀족 선거후보인 루트비히(Ludwig)는 스위스에서 추방된 스위스 형제들을 농장을 재건하도록 초대했는데, 그들이 훌륭한 농부이자 토지를 잘 일구는 명성을 가지고 있었기 때문입니다.

당시 독일에는 공식적으로 인정되는 세 교회가 있었습니다: 가톨릭, 루터교, 그리고 개혁교회. 스위스 형제들은 경제적으로 필요했고 그들의 신앙은 관용되었지만, 그들의 교회는 인정받지 못했습니다. 한 번에 모일 수 있는 인원 수에 제한이 있었고, 그들이 개량한 농장을 외국인으로 여겨 매입을 허용하지 않는 경우도 많았습니다.

스위스인이 운영한 농장들은 시간이 흐르며 번영했습니다. 부분적으로는 우수한 윤작(輪作) 시스템을 사용해 더 많은 젖소를 먹일 수 있었고, 그 결과 겨울에도 우유를 생산할 수 있게 되었기 때문입니다. 또 다른 주요 개선은 콩과 식물인 클로버 도입이었습니다. 이 씨앗은 네덜란드의 메노나이트들이 선물로 준 것이었습니다. 약 50년 후, 스위스인들이 농업에 끼친 차이는 눈에 띄게 되어 일부 좌절한 독일인 이웃들은 그들이 땅을 ‘Ferhexing’(펜실베이니아 독일어로 ‘마법’이라는 뜻)했다고 비난하기도 했습니다(물론 사실이 아니었습니다). 그래서 팔츠랜드(Pfaltzland)에서의 스위스 형제들의 삶은 그다지 나아지지 않았습니다.

1708년, 그들은 몹시 춥고 긴 겨울을 겪었습니다. 너무 추워 저장해 둔 뿌리 작물들이 차가운 지하실에서 얼기도 했습니다. 이 일 이후 얼마 지나지 않아 윌리엄 펜(William Penn)과 퀘이커(Quakers)들은 이 스위스 재세례파들의 곤경을 알게 되었습니다. 1682년에 윌리엄 펜은 펜실베이니아 식민지를 부여받아 그가 ‘거룩한 실험(Holy Experiment)’이라 부른 것을 시행하려 했습니다. 그는 모든 인종과 종교가 함께 평화롭게 공존할 수 있는 땅을 구상했습니다. 그는 유럽의 국가 교회들에 의해 박해받는 집단들에 특별한 관심을 가졌습니다. 퀘이커였던 그는 자신도 잉글랜드의 국가 교회로부터 박해를 당한 바 있었습니다. 그는 잉글랜드의 퀘이커들, 프랑스의 위그노(Huguenots), 네덜란드의 메노나이트, 독일의 침례교인들, 슈베네크펠더(Schwenkfelders)와 경건주의자들, 그리고 스위스 형제들과 유대인들까지 그들이 유랑하거나 고통받고 있는 곳에서 환영했습니다.

이것이 대략 1661년경부터 1746년경까지 살았던 한스 그로프(Hans Graeff/Groff)의 이야기에 대한 배경입니다. 한스는 스위스 형제들의 신앙으로 개종했으나 그의 아내 안나(Anna Bare) 그로프는 개신교 국가 교회에 남아 있었습니다. 펜실베이니아에서 개척할 기회가 열렸을 때 한스는 가고자 했지만 안나는 그렇지 않았습니다. 아마 그들은 그가 먼저 정착해 그녀를 데리러 오려는 계획을 세웠을지도 모릅니다. 한스는 1696년에 처음 펜실베이니아에 왔습니다. 이후 한스는 소수의 스위스 형제들을 이끌고(한스와 크리스티안 헤르(Herr), 마틴 메일린(Martin Meylin), 야곱 뮐러(Jacob Muller), 마틴 켄디그(Martin Kendig), 마틴 오버홀처(Martin Oberholtzer), 웬델 보우먼(Wendell Bowman)과 펑크(Funk) 가문 등) 당시 필라델피아 북쪽 약 7마일에 있던 저먼타운(Germantown)으로 가서 신대륙에서 재세례파가 정착한 최초의 영구 거주지가 되었습니다. 그 초창기 정착민들 중 많은 이들은 네덜란드와 스웨덴 출신으로 네덜란드의 메노나이트 교회에 소속되어 있었습니다. 스위스 이민자들은 1709년 겨울을 저먼타운에서 보냈는데—여성들은 많은 저먼타운의 직조공들을 위해 방적을 했고, 남성들은 신대륙 전초지에서 필요한 기술들을 배우기 위해 새 재세례파 정착지인 스키팩(Skippack)으로 여행을 갔습니다. 이곳에서 스위스 형제들이 처음으로 ‘메니스츠(Mennists)’ 또는 메노나이트(Mennonites)로 알려지게 된 것으로 보입니다.

1710년에 그들은 한스 그로프가 이전에 매우 비옥하고 물이 풍부한 토지를 확인해 두었던 코네스토가(Conestoga) 계곡으로 옮겨갔습니다. 그곳은 저먼타운과 문명지로부터 서쪽으로 60마일 떨어진 곳이었습니다. 생활은 확실히 힘들었습니다. 늑대, 곰, 표범, 보브캣과 다른 포식동물들이 많았습니다. 들소와 흰꼬리사슴도 풍부했고(정착민들이 심은 것을 얼마든지 먹어 치웠습니다), 엄청난 크기의 호두나무, 히코리, 밤나무, 단풍나무, 백송(White pine)과 참나무들이 곳곳을 덮고 있었습니다. 어떤 나무는 지름이 6피트(약 1.8미터)에 높이가 100피트(약 30미터)가 넘기도 했습니다(일부 초원과 습지는 원주민들이 남겨 두었습니다). 이 거대한 나무들은 도끼와 두 사람이 사용하는 톱으로 베어야 했습니다. 가장 가까운 의사나 약국, 철물점, 잡화점은 60마일이나 떨어져 있었습니다. 도전적이고 위험한 일이었지만 그들은 자유로웠습니다! 양심에 따라 행동할 자유. 신앙을 실천할 자유. 이 아름다운 광야에서 토지를 소유할 자유. 이웃들—코네스토가 부족과 프랑스 상인들에게 사랑을 전하고 증언할 자유. 그들은 가족들과 향후 올지도 모를 이들을 위해 10,000에이커의 토지 특허를 받았습니다.

심한 박해 때문에 부분적으로 1710년에 한 무리의 스위스 형제들이 독일 만하임(Mannheim) 지역으로 이주했습니다. 7년 후인 1717년, 그들은 대서양을 건넜습니다. 그해 가을 코네스토가 계곡으로 온 가족이 60가족이 넘었는데, 여기에는 제 조상인 한스와 막달레나 헤스(Hans and Magdalena Hess)와 그들의 세 자녀도 포함되어 있었습니다(그들은 결국 총 11명의 자녀를 축복받았습니다). 그때부터 물꼬가 트여 많은 재세례파들이 유럽을 떠나 ‘펜의 약속의 땅(Penn’s Promised Land)’으로 도망쳤다고 말할 수 있습니다. 1730년 이후로 이 광야가 길들여지면서 재정적 기회를 찾아 독일에서 온 많은 루터교, 개혁교회, 가톨릭 신자들도 이 지역으로 건너와 많은 독일 방언 화자들로 펜실베이니아 일부를 채우게 되었습니다.

이 글을 쓰는 동안 저는 유명한 랭커스터 카운티의 재세례파 역사학자 에이모스 후버(Amos Hoover)와 대화를 나누는 것을 매우 즐겼습니다. 그는 많은 통찰과 세부사항을 주었지만, 우리 둘은 너무 오래전의 사실과 세부를 모두 모으는 일이 어렵다는 데 동의했습니다. 여러 저자의 기록을 수집해보면 이야기는 대략 다음과 같습니다:

오해

펜의 숲에서 몇 년을 보낸 뒤, 한스 그로프는 유럽에 남아 있던 그의 아내 안나(Anna Bare) 그로프가 세상을 떠났다는 소식을 들었습니다. 그는 매우 괴로워했고 애도했습니다. 그는 그 사실을 알지 못했고 장례식에 참석하지 못했기 때문입니다. 몇 년 후 그는 수잔나 켄디그(Susanna Kendig)와 결혼했습니다. 그들은 처음 스트라스버그(Strasburg) 지역에 살다가 이후 오늘날 그로프데일(Groffdale)이라 불리는 지역에 상당한 농가를 세웠습니다. 이 결합은 9명의 자녀로 복을 받았습니다.

수년 후 한 여성(자칭 Mrs. Hans Groff)이 공동체에 나타나 자신을 한스 그로프의 아내라고 소개했습니다. 그녀는 유럽에서 재세례파가 되었고 남편을 찾아 대서양을 건너오는 위험한 여행을 감행했다고 했습니다. 그녀의 주장에 따르면, 그녀와 같은 이름을 가진 사람이 죽었고, 한스에게 전해진 그 첫 아내의 죽음에 대한 소식은 사실이 아니었다고 했습니다. 한스는 충격을 받았지만, 그는 둘째 결혼에 대해 무고했습니다. 그는 일부다처가 되거나 간음하기를 원하지 않았습니다. 국경 교회 지도자들은 상의하고 권고를 내렸습니다—젊고 어린 자녀들이 많은 선구자 부인은 남편의 부양이 필요하다는 것이었습니다. 전해지는 말에 따르면 한스는 어느 쪽과 함께 있어야 할지 분명치 않았지만 두 아내와 그 자녀들을 재정적으로 지원했다고 합니다. 그는 모피를 가지고 필라델피아로 가고 다시 광대한 전초지로 담요, 놋 주전자와 원주민들과의 교환품을 가지고 돌아오는 피곤할 줄 모르는 여행자로 알려져 있었습니다. 만약 여러분이 이 이야기를 다른 세부로 들었거나 읽었다면, 저도 마찬가지입니다. 이러한 모든 세부는 영원만이 정확하게 드러낼 것입니다.

의술

한스의 첫 아내는 그 교회 공동체에서 독신 자매로 살기로 선택했습니다. 그녀는 남편과 하나님, 그리고 처지에 대해 원망하기보다 이웃을 섬기는 삶을 택했습니다. 그녀는 작은 집과 작은 외양간(아마도 한스가 지어주었을 것)을 가지고 경사가 급한 언덕 꼭대기에서 파머스빌(Farmersville)을 내려다보는 ‘캣스백 힐(Cat’s Back Hill)’에 살았습니다. 1700년대 초의 이 집과 외양간의 폐허는 50년도 채 되지 않아도 여전히 분명히 남아 있었습니다. 그녀는 이 나라에 오기 전에도 산파였고, 이곳에 와서도 이 직업을 계속한 것으로 보입니다. 그녀는 약초 재배와 약초 치료법을 만드는 데 많은 경험이 있었습니다. 아마도 수십 마일 반경에서 가장 의사에 가까운 존재였을 것입니다. 제가 알 수 있는 바에 따르면, 그녀는 의학 지식과 지혜, 자가 제작한 약초 약품, 산파술로 지역 공동체에 축복을 베푸는 데 시간을 보냈습니다. 랭커스터 카운티의 많은 선조들이 이 사랑하는 자매의 섬김과 의학 지식이 아니었다면 개척자의 고된 삶을 견디지 못했을 수도 있습니다. 흥미롭게도, 수년 후 한스의 둘째 아내에게서 난 아들 중 한 명인 데이비드 그로프(David Groff)는 의학 공부를 위해 떠났습니다. 그의 학업이 끝나자 그는 의사가 되어 돌아와 아버지의 첫 아내가 급속히 성장하던 랭커스터 카운티의 많은 정착민들을 돌보는 사역을 돕게 되었습니다.

이 이야기는 식민지 미국 건설 직전과 그 과정에서 보수적 재세례파들의 삶을 둘러싼 흥미로운 세부를 엿보게 해 줍니다. 그들의 유럽 본국에서는 종교와 예배의 자유와 관련된 어려움이 있었지만, 새로운 자유의 땅으로의 여행과 그곳에서의 일상 생활도 여러 도전을 동반했습니다. 이 이야기에서 우리가 볼 수 있는 한 가지 격려는 이 개인들이 매 걸음마다 하나님의 원리들이 그들을 인도하도록 기꺼이 허용했다는 점입니다.

Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:4-7.

“Oh God, give us mothers like Eunice and grandmothers like Lois. Give us women who are women of faith. Give us women who know how to stand for truth against the tide of human rationalization that is destroying the lives of so many well-meaning people. Give us women who are unwavering in their loyalty to Jesus Christ, to their husbands, and to their calling to represent the spirit of Jesus in all of life. Amen”.

History has proven that women are as influential as men in forming the fabric of society and of the Christian community. An argument could be made that they exert an even greater influence if you consider the fact that they have a huge role in shaping the values of little children and, whether or not they dress and conduct themselves according to godly modesty, they can influence the morality of the masses of men around them.

Hence the call for women to be women of faith. Not only does a woman’s faith influence those around her, but every woman has her own personal journey. Her journey is a search for identity, security, and purpose for her life.

Today’s women are inundated with voices that claim to offer the fulfillment that their heart desires. As with their mother Eve, many of these voices appeal to her feminine spirit, but as their mother Eve discovered, unless it is the voice of God, it leads to death and destruction.

The Bible abounds with accounts of women who lived by faith. Consider the harlot Rahab. Bible scholars cannot agree that she was worthy of that title, but it has come down to us as such. She heard the stories of the God of Israel. When she encountered the spies and heard their ominous prediction for her city she chose to believe.

She was a native of Jericho. Jericho was her home. Jericho had high stone walls and brave defenders. She would have had many reasons to place her faith in that which was familiar to her, and which had sustained her in the past.

She chose to place her faith in the God of Israel. The men of Israel told her that if she would hang a scarlet thread from her window on the wall, her house and her life would be spared. A scarlet thread. Not much by way of identity or security, but Rahab hung her faith on a scarlet thread. That scarlet thread represented the power of the God of Israel and, as we know today, it is a beautiful type of the blood of Jesus.

The call to be a woman of faith is a call to turn away from the ideology of the world and to embrace what in the eyes of the world is a futile remedy—a scarlet thread. Rahab’s faith was rooted in her knowledge of the God of Israel and His plan to judge her people. The scarlet thread was her hope of deliverance.

I would like for us to consider how faith in God impacts the primary desires of the feminine heart. Every woman longs for identity, security, and purpose. Jesus has come to meet that heart longing.

Identity –“Who am I?”

This is a question that everyone is compelled to ask at some point in their life—often in adolescence. Young men tend to carve out their identity based in whom they admire and their vocational inclinations. Young women, especially in our Anabaptist communities, are largely at the mercy of the prominent men in their lives to define their identity.

This is not purely cultural. When God said to Eve, …thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee –Genesis 3:16, He was declaring that she and her female descendants would look to the man to define an essential part of their nature.

Fathers play a key role in the early development of a little girl’s identity. Abusive fathers, absent fathers, and indifferent fathers leave in their wake little girls who are uncertain of who they are, or of their value as a person. A father who affirms his daughter’s godly femininity gives her a priceless gift. By that, I mean praising her for qualities of feminine virtue, blessing her for efforts to be chaste and modest, and yes, telling her that she is beautiful.

A woman’s heart will ultimately turn toward a husband. God said, “Thy desire shall be to thy husband”, not to thy father. Most women marry thinking that they have at last found their “savior” and rightly so. Did Paul not say in Ephesians chapter five that the husband is “the savior of the body”? Should a wife not expect to receive from her husband love, affirmation, protection, and provision? This is due to her by divine decree. A godly husband will do everything in his power to provide for her in this way.

“Thy desire shall be to thy husband” is given in the context of the fall. It was one of the consequences of the fall. It is a statement without the promise of fulfillment. This leaves us to believe that, although driven by desire, that desire may go unfulfilled.

What is a woman to do if her husband is unwilling or unable to satisfy her heart’s desire? What if a woman does not have a husband? She must become a woman of faith. Until a woman has found her identity in Jesus, no man will be able to satisfy the deepest longings of her heart.

Many marriages suffer because the wife expects her husband to meet the deep longings of her heart that only Jesus can fulfill. Many men are made to feel inadequate and withdraw when they are expected to be, and to do, for their wives what only Jesus can do.

Calling all women to be women of faith

Women of faith are women who know who they are in Christ Jesus. They have found the deepest longings of their feminine heart met in Him. Because their heart longings are satisfied, they have become a well spring of life to their husband, to their children, and to others.

Security –“Who will protect me?”

Being a woman has always been risky. Women are very vulnerable. In addition to the fact that they are physically more delicate, women are more susceptible to emotional vacillations, and I believe that based on what the Bible has to say about Eve’s deception, that women tend to be more vulnerable to spiritual deception (see 1 Timothy 2:14).

This does not make them inferior to men. Their emotional sensitivity makes them more attune to the many realities of relational problems than many men are. In this, their insight can be a positive thing, helping to balance us men in some of our natural weaknesses. Whatever comparisons we choose to make, I think we can all agree that women need the protection that men offer.

What if the man that is supposed to be protecting you is a coward? We have an example of just such a situation in the Bible. The man’s name is Abraham—yes… the father of faith. Even strong men sometimes make cowardly decisions.

Abraham and Sarah were traveling into Egypt. As they neared Egypt, Abraham became afraid for his life. His wife Sarah was a beautiful woman and Abraham was aware that Egypt was a heathen nation with very loose morals. He was afraid that the Egyptians would kill him so they could have his wife. Abraham said to Sarah, Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee –Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was indeed Abraham’s half-sister. They had the same father, but not the same mother. Abraham’s contingency plan leaves Sarah in a very difficult position. We read nothing of Sarah’s reaction to Abraham’s plan. All we know is that …Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:6.

It would appear that Sarah was not afraid. Her faith was not dependent on Abraham’s protection. She was relying on a higher power. Sarah’s faith gave her a place in the hall of faith in Hebrews chapter 11 and made her Peter’s example of how wives are to relate to their husbands.

The substance of this story is in the outcome. Because of Sarah’s faith, she was delivered from the hand of Pharaoh, the most powerful world ruler of the day. It was Sarah’s faith, not Abraham’s, which protected her.

Women look to men for security, and it is right that they should. Men protect their women as best they can. I believe that when men and women are living within their God-given roles, there is a lot of protection and security available; however, we do live in a fallen world. We do not always honorably fulfill our roles and sometimes God allows evil to befall even the most pious.

Calling all women to be women of faith even as Sarah

Do you have faith to believe that God is bigger than your husband or your father? Are you willing to trust God to overrule where your husband may be weak or even rebellious against God or the church?

A woman of faith is a woman who chooses to trust God in the absence of a reasonable path forward. A woman of faith continues to do what is right, even though it may not be a path of guaranteed security because …The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me –Hebrews 13:6.

Purpose – “Why am I here?”

This is a question that everyone asks at some point in life. We want our lives to have meaning and purpose. The futility of a meaningless living drives men and women into depression and despair. Living purposefully blesses us and others and brings honor to our Creator.

When men think of living purposefully, they envision… a battle to fight, a mountain to conquer, a noble goal to strive for. We men tend to be vision-oriented and goal-focused.

What does it mean for a woman to live purposefully?

Luke gives us some insight into this in the account of Jesus’ visit to the home of Mary and Martha. (See Luke 10:38-42) Jesus would frequently stop by this home when He was passing through Bethany. Here He knew He would find great hospitality and engaging conversation. Today was no exception.

As He relaxed in their sitting room, Mary sat at His feet asking questions and listening intently as He revealed to her the purpose of His life and His future destiny. Mary came to understand things about Jesus that even His disciples had failed to grasp.

Matthew records that when Jesus was dining in the house of Simon a woman, thought to be Mary of Bethany, entered, and knelt and anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive ointment. When the disciples complained about “this waste” Jesus said to them: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial –Matthew 26:12.

Where did Mary get this understanding? Was it not when she was “sitting at Jesus feet?”

Martha on the other hand was “cumbered about much serving”. Now Jesus had to eat. Someone needed to prepare food and I am certain that Jesus enjoyed Martha’s delicious provisions. But Jesus chided her with “Martha, Martha”. Notice the familial tone of his voice.

He was not judging her nor condemning her. He was challenging her to take time for the important things in life. He commended Mary for she …hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her –Luke 10:42.

I would like to suggest that most of our anxiety is of our own making. We set goals for our life that Jesus never required. We place expectations upon ourselves that have no eternal merit. Like Martha, we stress over frivolity, and damage relationships over trivial matters. Yes, supper must be served, and Mary should help, but not to neglect the “better part”.

Calling all women to be women of faith as Mary who loved to linger at Jesus feet

Life for a wife and mother is full of pressing demands. Defuse your life of stress and anxiety by spending time listening for the voice of Jesus—that “still small voice” that Elijah finally heard.

Stress and anxiety will melt away in the presence of Jesus. God speaks to us by His Holy Spirit through His Word. If it is a challenge for you to find time to sit down with your Bible, then you can quiet your spirit with your hands in the dishwater, or while folding the laundry, or as you once again prepare a meal for your family. At times like this you can commune with God. You can pray to your Father in heaven. You can say things like “I love you Lord Jesus, speak to me through Your Word, bring peace to my soul; quiet the wrestlings of my mind; help me to enter into Your rest; give me Your peace.” Then you can listen as His Spirit prompts your spirit with nuggets of truth from the Scriptures that are hidden away in your heart.

Summary –Calling all women to be women of faith

For your own personal wellbeing:

Women today are bombarded by self-help resources in the form of books, podcasts, social media, and seminars. Much of it is good and can be helpful, but nothing will replace a personal relationship and a daily walk with Jesus.

For the wellbeing of your children:

Today, more than ever we need mothers to be women of faith who can project onto their children that walking with God is real and satisfying. Young Timothy was influenced by the unfeigned faith of his mother and of his grandmother. Never underestimate the effect of the influence of your life on the lives of those who follow you.

For the strength of your husband:

Men today need the support of faithful women, especially their wife. A man’s daily walk can be fortified or diminished by the woman in his life. It has been said “Behind every successful man is woman”. A man is tremendously influenced for good or ill by the women in his life.

For the good of the Church:

Woman of faith, the church needs you. Women bring a grace to the church that is desperately needed. Your prayers are needed. Your testimony gives encouragement. Your song moves our hearts. Your smile gives hope. Your peaceful, joyful countenance of a soul that’s at rest in Jesus is an influence that is rivaled by little else in this world.

Nina tamaa kubwa ya kukukutana nawe, nikikumbuka machozi yako, ili niweze kujazwa kwa furaha; Ninapokumbuka imani isiyo ya uongo iliyokuwepo ndani yako, ambayo kwanza ilikaa katika babu yako Loisi, na katika mama yako Eunisi; na ninaamini kwamba pia iko ndani yako. Kwa hiyo nakukumbusha utunze kipawa cha Mungu kilichomo ndani yako kwa kumsimamisha mikono yangu juu yako. Kwa maana Mungu hatutolei roho ya woga; bali ya nguvu, na ya upendo, na ya akili timamu – 2 Timotheo 1:4-7.

“Ee Mungu, utupatie mama kama Eunisi na babu kama Loisi. Utupatie wanawake wa imani. Utupatie wanawake wanaojua kusimama kwa ajili ya ukweli dhidi ya mawimbi ya utafiti wa kibinadamu yanayoharibu maisha ya watu wengi wenye nia njema. Utupatie wanawake wasiyoegemea katika uaminifu wao kwa Yesu Kristo, kwa wake zao, na kwa wito wao wa kuwakilisha roho ya Yesu katika maisha yote. Amina”.

Historia imethibitisha kwamba wanawake wanachangia kwa nguvu sawa na wanaume katika kuunda muundo wa jamii na wa jamii ya Wakristo. Inaweza semekana kuwa wanatoa ushawishi mkubwa zaidi ukizingatia kuwa wana jukumu kubwa katika kuunda maadili ya watoto wachanga na, iwe wanavaa na kujitendea kwa unyenyekevu wa kiungu au la, wanaweza kuathiri maadili ya umati wa wanaume waliowazunguka.

Hivyo basi wito kwa wanawake kuwa wanawake wa imani. Imani ya mwanamke haikuathiri tu watu waliomzunguka, bali kila mwanamke ana safari yake ya kibinafsi. Safari yake ni kutafuta utambulisho, usalama, na kusudi la maisha yake.

Wanawake wa leo wanazidiwa kwa sauti nyingi zinazodai kutoa utimizaji unaotakiwa na moyo wao. Kama kwa mama yao Hawa, sauti nyingi hizi zinavuta roho yao ya kike, lakini kama mama yao Hawa alivyogundua, isipokuwa ni sauti ya Mungu, inasababisha mauti na uharibifu.

Biblia imejaa rekodi za wanawake waliouishi kwa imani. Fikiria juu ya mke haramu Rahabu. Watafiti wa Biblia hawawezi kukubaliana kabisa kwamba alistahili hadhi hiyo, lakini jina hilo limepitishwa kwetu hivyo. Alisikia hadithi za Mungu wa Israeli. Alipokutana na waangalizi na kusikia utabiri wao wa kuogofya kuhusu mji wake alichagua kuamini.

Alikuwa mzaliwa wa Yerikho. Yerikho ilikuwa nyumbani kwake. Yerikho ilikuwa na kuta za jiwe kubwa na walinzi jasiri. Angekuwa na sababu nyingi za kuweka imani yake kwa yale aliyoyafahamu na yaliomfikisha katika wakati uliopita.

Alichagua kuweka imani yake kwa Mungu wa Israeli. Wanaume wa Israeli walimwambia kwamba kama angeweka uzi mwekundu dirishani kwake juu ya ukuta, nyumba yake na maisha yake yangebaki salama. Uzi mwekundu. Si kitu kikubwa kwa ajili ya utambulisho au usalama, lakini Rahabu aliweka imani yake kwenye uzi mwekundu. Uzi huo mwekundu ulieleza nguvu ya Mungu wa Israeli na, kama tunavyojua leo, ni mfano mzuri wa damu ya Yesu.

Wito wa kuwa mwanamke wa imani ni wito wa kugeukia mbali itikadi ya dunia na kukumbatia kile ambacho kwa macho ya dunia ni tiba isiyo na maana—uzi mwekundu. Imani ya Rahabu ilitokana na ujuzi wake wa Mungu wa Israeli na mpango Wake wa kuhukumu watu wake. Uzi mwekundu ulikuwa tumaini lake la ukombozi.

Ningependa tufikirie jinsi imani kwa Mungu inavyoathiri tamaa kuu za moyo wa kike. Kila mwanamke anamtamania utambulisho, usalama, na kusudi. Yesu amekuja kukutana na tamaa hiyo ya moyo.

Utambulisho – “Mimi ni nani?”

Hili ni swali ambalo kila mtu anakuzwa kujiuliza kwa wakati fulani wa maisha—mara nyingi ujana. Vijana wa kiume hujenga utambulisho wao kwa msingi wa wanayowaheshimu na mwelekeo wao wa kazi. Vijana wa kike, hasa katika jamii zetu za Anabaptisti, kwa kiasi kikubwa wako mwembamba mbele ya wanaume maarufu katika maisha yao kuufafanua utambulisho wao.

Hii sio tu kitamaduni. Wakati Mungu alisema kwa Hawa, …tamaa yako itakuwa kwa mumeo, naye atakutawaliwa – Mwanzo 3:16, Alikuwa anatangaza kwamba yeye na uzao wake wa kike wangemwangalia mwanamume kumfafanulia sehemu muhimu ya asili yao.

Babá wana sehemu muhimu katika maendeleo ya mapema ya utambulisho wa msichana mdogo. Baba wakatili, baba wasioko, na baba wasiojali huacha msichana mdogo asiye na uhakika wa yeye ni nani, au thamani yake kama mtu. Baba anayeidhinisha uanamitindo wa mkewe anayemcha Mungu anamfunulia zawadi isiyoweza kupimika. Kwa hiyo, ninamaanisha kumpongeza kwa sifa za utu wa kike, kumbariki kwa jitihada za kuwa mchi na mwenye unyenyekevu, na ndiyo, kumwambia kwamba yeye ni mrembo.

Moyo wa mwanamke hatimaye utakgeuka kuelekea kwa mume. Mungu alisema, “Tamaa yako itakuwa kwa mumeo”, si kwa baba yako. Wanawake wengi wanaoa wakidhani kwamba hatimaye wamepata “mkombozi” wao na kwa msingi huo wako sahihi. Je, Paolo hakusema katika Waefeso sura tano kwamba mume ni “mkombozi wa mwili”? Je, mke asitarajia kupokea kutoka kwa mume wake upendo, uthibitisho, ulinzi, na malezi? Hayo ni haki yake kwa amri ya kimungu. Mume mtakatifu atafanya kila awezalo kutoa hayo kwa njia hiyo.

“Tamaa yako itakuwa kwa mumeo” imetolewa katika muktadha wa kuanguka. Ilikuwa mojawapo ya matokeo ya kuanguka. Ni kauli isiyo na ahadi ya kutimizwa. Hii inatuacha tukiamini kuwa, ingawa inachochewa na tamaa, tamaa hiyo inaweza kukosa kutimizwa.

Nini mwanamke afanye ikiwa mumewake hataki au hawezi kuridhisha tamaa ya moyo wake? Je, mwanamke hana mume? Lazima awe mwanamke wa imani. Hadi mwanamke apate utambulisho wake katika Yesu, hakuna mwanaume atakayemudu kuridhisha tamaa za ndani kabisa za moyo wake.

Ndoa nyingi zinateseka kwa sababu mke anatarajia mume wake akidhi tamaa za ndani kabisa za moyo wake ambazo ni Yesu pekee anayezitudisha. Wanaume wengi wanahisi kutokuwa na uwezo na kujibakisha wanapoatarajiwa kufanya, na kutenda, kwa wake zao kile ambacho ni Yesu pekee anayezikamilisha.

Wito kwa wanawake wote kuwa wanawake wa imani

Wanawake wa imani ni wanawake wanaojua ni nani wao katika Kristo Yesu. Wamepata tamaa za ndani kabisa za moyo wao zimekutana ndani Yake. Kwa sababu tamaa zao za moyo zimekamilika, wamegeuka kuwa chemchemi ya uzima kwa mume wao, kwa watoto wao, na kwa wengine.

Usalama – “Nani ataniulinda?”

Kuwa mwanamke imekuwa hatari kila wakati. Wanawake ni dhaifu sana. Mbali na ukweli kwamba kwa kimwili ni nyepesi zaidi, wanawake wanaweza kurahisika kubadilika kihisia, na naamini kutokana na kile Biblia inachosema kuhusu udanganyifu wa Hawa, kwamba wanawake huwa rahisi zaidi kwa udanganyifu wa kiroho (ona 1 Timotheo 2:14).

Hii haisi kuwaoza wa wanaume. Unyeti wao wa kihisia huwafanya wawe wa kuzingatia zaidi ukweli wa matatizo ya mahusiano kuliko wanaume wengi. Katika hili, maarifa yao yanaweza kuwa jambo jema, kusaidia kutulishana sisi wanaume katika baadhi ya udhaifu wetu wa asili. Iwe tunafanya kulinganisha gani, nadhani tunaweza kukubali kwamba wanawake wanahitaji ulinzi ambao wanaume hutoa.

Kama mwanaume anayepaswa kukulinda ni mwoga, je? Tuna mfano wa hali kama hiyo katika Biblia. Jina la mwanaume ni Abrahamu—ndiyo… baba wa imani. Hata wanaume wenye nguvu hupata kufanya maamuzi ya kukosa ujasiri.

Abrahamu na Sara walikuwa wakisafiri kwenda Misri. Walipokaribia Misri, Abrahamu alihofia maisha yake. Mke wake Sara alikuwa mwanamke mrembo na Abrahamu alijua kwamba Misri ilikuwa taifa la waabudu wa sanamu lenye maadili iliyokuwa laini sana. Alihofia kwamba Waegipita wangemuua ili wapate mkewe. Abrahamu alisema kwa Sara, Tamwani, sema, wewe ni dada yangu: ili niwe na heri kwa ajili yako; na nafsi yangu itaishi kwa ajili yako – Mwanzo 12:13.

Sara kwa kweli alikuwa nusu-dada wa Abrahamu. Walikuwa na baba mmoja, lakini si mama mmoja. Mpango wa dharura wa Abrahamu umaacha Sara katika nafasi ngumu sana. Hatutasoma chochote kuhusu jinsi Sara alivyoreact kwa mpango wa Abrahamu. Jambo pekee tunalojua ni kwamba …Sara alimtii Abrahamu, akimwita bwana: ambao ndio miongoni mwa nyinyi, kama mpendezavyo, msiogopi kwa hofu yoyote – 1 Petro 3:6.

Inaonekana kwamba Sara hakuwa na hofu. Imani yake haitegemei ulinzi wa Abrahamu. Alikuwa anategemea nguvu ya juu zaidi. Imani ya Sara ilimpa nafasi katika chumba cha waamini katika Waebrania sura 11 na kumfanya awe mfano wa Petro wa jinsi wake wanavyopaswa kuhusiana na waume zao.

Muhimu wa hadithi hii uko katika matokeo. Kwa sababu ya imani ya Sara, alitulizwa kutoka kwa mkono wa Farao, mfalme mwenye mamlaka mkubwa wa wakati wake. Ilikuwa imani ya Sara, si ya Abrahamu, ilimlinda.

Wanawake hawaitazami wanaume kwa ajili ya usalama, na ni sawa kuwa hivyo. Wanaume hulinda wake zao kwa kadri ya uwezo wao. Ninaamini kwamba wakati wanaume na wanawake wanaishi ndani ya nafasi walizotengwa na Mungu, kuna ulinzi mwingi na usalama unaopatikana; hata hivyo, tunaishi katika ulimwengu ulioporomoka. Hatutumii nyanja zetu kwa heshima kila wakati na wakati mwingine Mungu huruhusu uovu kutokea hata kwa mtaabika zaidi.

Wito kwa wanawake wote kuwa wanawake wa imani kama Sara

Je, una imani ya kuamini kwamba Mungu ni mkubwa zaidi kuliko mumeo au baba yako? Je, uko tayari kumtumainisha Mungu ashinde mahali ambapo mumeo anaweza kuwa dhaifu au hata makafiri dhidi ya Mungu au kanisa?

Mwanamke wa imani ni mwanamke anayechagua kumtumaini Mungu kwa kutokuwepo kwa njia ya busara mbele. Mwanamke wa imani anaendelea kufanya haki, ingawa inaweza isiwe njia ya usalama iliyohakikishwa kwa sababu …Bwana ni msaidizi wangu, sitokuwa na hofu ya mtu atakayenifanyia nini – Waebrania 13:6.

Kusudi – “Kwa nini niko hapa?”

Hili ni swali ambalo kila mtu huliuliza kwa wakati fulani wa maisha. Tunataka maisha yetu yawe na maana na kusudi. Upotevu wa kuishi bila maana unasukuma wanaume na wanawake katika msongo wa mawazo na kukata tamaa. Kuishi kwa kusudi kunatutunza na wengine na kuleta utukufu kwa Muumba wetu.

Wanaume wanapofikiri kuishi kwa kusudi, wanaiona… vita ya kupigana, mlima wa kushinda, lengo la heshima la kutamani kufikiwa. Sisi wanaume kwa kawaida tunazingatia maono na malengo.

Je, inamaanisha nini kwa mwanamke kuishi kwa kusudi?

Luka anatupatia mwanga kuhusu hili katika hadithi ya ziara ya Yesu katika nyumba ya Mariamu na Martha. (Ona Luka 10:38-42) Yesu mara nyingi alitembelea nyumba hii alipopita Bethania. Hapa alijua angepata ukarimu mkubwa na mazungumzo ya kuvutia. Leo haikuwa tukio la kipekee.

Anaporidhika katika chumba chao cha kukaa, Mariamu aliketi miguuni mwake auliza maswali na kusikiliza kwa makini alipomfunulia kusudi la maisha yake na hatima yake ya baadaye. Mariamu alifika kuelewa mambo kuhusu Yesu ambayo hata wanafunzi wake hawakuweza kuyafahamu.

Matiayo anarekodi kwamba Yesu alipokuwa akila katika nyumba ya Simone mwanamume, mwanamke, aliyedhaniwa kuwa Mariamu wa Bethania, aliingia, akainama na kumwagia miguu ya Yesu mafuta ya thamani. Wanafunzi walipokosoa kuhusu “hasa hii ya upotevu” Yesu akawaambia: Kwa maana alipotaka kumwacha huyo, alinifanya tayari kwa maziko yangu – Mathayo 26:12.

Je, Mariamu alipata uelewa huo wapi? Je, si alipokuwa “akiketi miguuni mwa Yesu?”

Martha kwa upande mwingine alikuwa “amechokea mno kuhudumia”. Sasa Yesu alihitaji kula. Mtu alihitaji kuandaa chakula na nina hakika kwamba Yesu alifurahia maandalizi ya ladha ya Martha. Lakini Yesu alimkosoa kwa “Martha, Martha”. Tazama toni ya kifamilia ya sauti yake.

Hakumhukumu wala kumhukumu kwa adhabu. Alimshinikiza achukue muda kwa mambo muhimu ya maisha. Alimpongeza Mariamu kwa kuwa …amechagua sehemu ile nzuri, ambayo haitatwaliwa kutoka kwake – Luka 10:42.

Ningependa kupendekeza kwamba wengi wa wasiwasi wetu ni matokeo ya tunayojiwekea sisi wenyewe. Tunapanga malengo kwa maisha yetu ambayo Yesu hakuwahi kuyaamuru. Tunaweka matarajio juu yetu ambayo hayana thamani ya milele. Kama Martha, tunasumbuka kwa vitu visivyo na maana, na kuharibu mahusiano kwa mambo madogo. Ndiyo, chakula cha jioni kinapaswa kutolewa, na Mariamu anapaswa kusaidia, lakini si kusahau “sehemu bora”.

Wito kwa wanawake wote kuwa wanawake wa imani kama Mariamu aliyependa kukaa miguuni mwa Yesu

Maisha kwa mke na mama yamejaa mahitaji yanayolazimisha. Punguza msongo wa maisha yako na wasiwasi kwa kutumia muda kusikiliza sauti ya Yesu—“sauti ile ndogo tulivu” aliyomsikia Eliya hatimaye.

Msongo na wasiwasi vitameng'enyuka mbele ya Yesu. Mungu anazungumza nasi kwa Roho Wake Mtakatifu kupitia Neno Lake. Ikiwa ni changamoto kwako kupata muda wa kukaa na Biblia yako, basi unaweza kutuliza roho yako ukiwa na mikono yako kwenye maji ya kuoshea vyombo, au unapofungua nguo, au unapoirudia tena kuandaa chakula kwa familia yako. Katika nyakati kama hizi unaweza kuwasiliana na Mungu. Unaweza kumuomba Baba yako aliyeko mbinguni. Unaweza kusema vitu kama “Nakupenda Ee Bwana Yesu, niene Neno Lako, lete amani kwa nafsi yangu; tuliza migogoro ya mawazo yangu; nisaidie nifikie mapumziko Yako; nizungushe kwa amani Yako.” Kisha unaweza kusikiliza Roho Yake akimuonya roho yako kwa vipande vya ukweli kutoka Maandiko yaliyofichwa ndani ya moyo wako.

Muhtasari – Wito kwa wanawake wote kuwa wanawake wa imani

Kwa ustawi wako binafsi:

Wanawake wa leo wanazidiwa na rasilimali za kujisaidia kwa njia ya vitabu, podikasti, mitandao ya kijamii, na semina. Mengi yake ni mazuri na yanaweza kusaidia, lakini hakuna kitakachemaliza uhusiano wa kibinafsi na matembezi ya kila siku na Yesu.

Kwa ustawi wa watoto wako:

Leo, zaidi kuliko hapo awali tunahitaji mama wawe wanawake wa imani ambao wanaweza kuwapeleka watoto wao kwamba kutembea na Mungu ni halisi na kuridhisha. Timotheo mchanga aliathiriwa na imani isiyo ya bandia ya mama yake na ya babu yake. Usikosema athari ya ushawishi wa maisha yako kwa maisha ya wale wanaokuja baada yako.

Kwa nguvu za mumeo:

Wanaume wa leo wanahitaji msaada wa wanawake waaminifu, hasa wake zao. Matembezi ya mtu wa kiume kila siku yanaweza kuimarishwa au kupunguzwa na mwanamke katika maisha yake. Imesema “Nyuma ya kila mwanaume aliyefanikiwa kuna mwanamke”. Mwanaume anaathiriwa sana kwa mema au mabaya na wanawake waliomo katika maisha yake.

Kwa ajili ya Kanisa:

Mwanamke wa imani, kanisa linakuhitaji. Wanawake huleta neema kwa kanisa ambayo inahitajika kwa dharura. Maombi yako yanahitajika. Ushuhuda wako hutoa faraja. Wimbo wako unaguswa mioyo yetu. Tabasamu lako linalotoa matumaini. Uso wako wenye amani na furaha wa roho iliyopumzika ndani ya Yesu ni ushawishi ambao hauwezi kulinganishwa kwa kitu kinginechoshi katika dunia hii.

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Hälsningar i kristen kärlek till er alla. I detta nummer av tidningen (sommar 2023)… Artikeln i kyrkohistoriedelen fokuserar på bibelprofetia som rör de yttersta tiderna och på olika sätt som delar av kyrkan genom åren kom avvägar från den bibliska undervisningen i sina vardagsliv. I sin artikel försöker Donny Brechbill, som tillsammans med sin fru håller flera äktenskapsseminarier varje år, att zooma in på ett utmanande ämne—några av de grundläggande problem som han ser hos kvinnor som kämpar i församlingen. Lee Rufener tar ett oförbehållsamt grepp i sin ansträngning att dela expositorisk undervisning om praktiska sätt att ha ett helgat hem. Vi har denna gång en ny skribent för systrarna som delar en börda i sitt hjärta—att ingjuta Guds Ord i nästa generations hjärtan.

Plus fler intressanta ämnen. Njut.

Om du blir uppbyggd eller uppmuntrad av någon av författarnas innehåll vore det en välsignelse om du svarade oss per post eller e‑post. Vi vidarebefordrar detta till våra skribenter till gagn för dem.

Nyligen funderade jag över ämnet förändring. Som jag tidigare skrivit har vi gått igenom en hel del förändringar som familj. Under de senaste 1–2 åren flyttade vi till en annan bostad, jag fick ett nytt jobb och slutligen, tack vare Herren, har jag till största delen återhämtat mig från de långvariga effekterna av covid. Ett särskilt tack till var och en som bett för min hälsa.

När jag stannade upp i stilla eftertanke blev jag överraskad över alla de saker som förändrats under de mer än 40 år som jag kan minnas. (Även om jag är över 50 minns jag inte mycket från de allra tidigaste åren i mitt liv.)

Som pojke åkte jag omkring i fordon utan säkerhetsbälte och definitivt inga krockkuddar. När båda dessa ”livräddande” anordningar först började introduceras minns jag väl de många diskussionerna om de verkligen var livräddande i sin effekt eller om det tvärtom rörde sig om något annat. Alla fordon brukade vara bakhjulsdrivna eller fyrhjulsdrivna. Hur märkligt det verkade när de första framhjulsdrivna bilarna började dyka upp. Nu har vi hybridfordon med en drivkraft mot rena elfordon.

För mer än fyrtio år sedan hade de flesta bönder bensindrivna traktorer med förgasare eller dieseltraktorer med en manuellt driven insprutningspump. Idag är de flesta traktorer utrustade med en dator och till synes mil av kablar och elektroniska prylar. Förr kunde de flesta bönder underhålla eller reparera sin egen utrustning; nu behövs diagnostiska maskiner och specialverktyg som kostar mycket pengar och tar många timmar att lära sig använda. Detta gör att de flesta bönder förlitar sig på specialiserade reparatörer, vilket också kostar mycket pengar.

Sedan kom covid. Det var en stressig tid. Har du märkt vad som förändrats under, efter eller till följd av covid? När jag umgås med andra säger någon rutinmässigt att si eller så är annorlunda sedan covid. Är det bara jag, eller är allmänheten sedan covid mindre vänlig och mer privat i sina interaktioner? Låt oss granska våra egna möten för att försäkra oss om att vi fortfarande är Guds ”ljus” och ”salt” i denna mörka värld, och att vi inte förlorar vår ”saltighet”. Dessutom finns det överallt skyltar om arbetskraft sökes. Varför? Det verkar som att covid har försvagat den lilla arbetsmoral som fortfarande fanns i vårt samhälle.

Sedan finns frågan om mobiltelefoner och el‑cyklar. Vad har dessa två orelaterade produkter gemensamt? Ur mitt perspektiv när jag iakttar amishfolket i Holmes County har dessa två föremål förändrat ett folk och en kultur mer i grunden än nästan något annat på senare tid.

Var lämnar detta oss? Hebreerbrevet säger att För prästadömet blir det nödvändigtvis också en förändring i lagen – Hebreerbrevet 7:12. Så vi ser att Gud ändrade saker när Han fann det lämpligt; således, om vi behöver förändras för att bli mer bibliska, då bör vi göra det. Men aposteln Paulus säger Att vi härefter icke längre skola vara barn, kastade hit och dit och förda omkring av vart och ett vinddrag av lära… – Efesierbrevet 4:14.

Och eftersom laglösheten skall tillta, skall kärleken hos de flesta svalna. Men den som står ut intill slutet, han skall bli frälst – Matteusevangeliet 24:12–13. Så låt oss vara vaksamma i dessa yttersta tider när förvandling sker alltmer omkring oss. Må vi vara bland dem som uthärdar intill änden.
