Jesus, upon His ascension back into His heavenly home, gave a final directive to His disciples, both to those physically present as He disappeared into the clouds, and to the myriad of believers who would come to know Him down through the ages. The story of His life and His gospel were to be preached unto all the world by those who called Him Lord. This global spreading of the Word, would, in the later vision of John, be proclaimed as one of the prerequisites of Jesus’ triumphant return at the end of time. John himself would be seen as a harbinger of these end times, based on Jesus’ words as recorded by John … If I will that he [John] tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. John 21:22.

The early Christians, understandably, felt that the return of Christ was imminent, even within the first century. The rapid expansion of Christianity, the complete moral depravity of the Roman culture, and the increasing intensity of persecution against them seemed to point to a swift and triumphant return of their Lord.

Now, two thousand years since Christ gave that promise, His soon return seems just as imminent as it did to the first century believers. Speculation on the time of His return, the manner of it, and the contributing factors are always current and controversial subjects. In the light of this continued earnest expectation of the end times, what have we to learn about our interpretations of prophecy from those who have attempted to decipher the prophetic portions of Scripture in earlier ages?

Jesus' first coming was surrounded and enveloped by perhaps the most recognizable misinterpretation of prophecy in the Bible. Roughly four hundred years of relative silence from God precluded His entry into the world in a physical, human body. His birth would be unnoticed in a society that was not only in desperate need of, but also expecting, a Savior to arrive. Daniel, writing the words God gave him, had told of a Messiah to come, and had even given a time that He would appear. Now, the Jews seethed under Roman rule, hanging their hopes on what they thought would be a sudden and triumphant extermination of the Roman troops and influence from their lands. To us, it is glaringly obvious that their interpretation of prophecy was not only incorrect, but for many, would lead them astray so that they did not even recognize or acknowledge the true Redeemer that was sent to them.

But what was it that caused this misinterpreted view? To us, it seems completely in order that Jesus would focus on the poor and destitute rather than opposing an occupying army. Jewish historians give an intriguing, but scarcely surprising, answer to the failure of the majority of their people to recognize Christ for who He was.

The religious atmosphere of first century Israel was one defined by corruption, bribery, lust for power, and all the unsavory aspects of a completely politically motivated upper class.

The priests, once chosen by God to be His servants in sanctifying His children, had sunk to buying their positions of service, most notably in the high priest’s office, where God had ordained one high priest to serve the people throughout his life. In Jesus’ day, however, the responsibilities of leading the children of Israel were divvied out, the role often changing hands on one-year terms. Becoming a high priest was a matter of birth. Most high priests came from several large, influential, and wealthy families, as one often had to buy into the opportunity of this office.

It was not only the high priest’s office that was corrupted, but most levels of prominent spiritual leadership were filled by the wealthy elites who had the connections and wealth to be placed into roles of importance amongst the Jews.

This unsavory backdrop gives even more clarity to Jesus’ feelings on the religious leaders of His day. These imposters did not hold their priestly positions to serve His Father, they held them for their own gain, turning the temple into a marketplace and holding the common people hostage through their disputes on the minutiae of the Law.

Unsurprisingly, these leaders looked for a Messiah who would fit their goals, their ideals, and their morals, rather than one that would rebuke and chastise them for their hypocrisy, greed, and selfish ambition. Their view of prophecy had been so twisted and corrupted by their lifestyle that even the miracle of a resurrection could not sway them to view Christ’s power as coming from God. This misconstrued expectation of a conquering commander, riding a horse of war over the political enemies of these elites was pandered to the common Jew as well. Centuries of fighting for just the freedom to worship, as in the case of the Maccabees and the Greeks, had deeply imprinted a sense of nationalism into the collective mind of the Jewish people. The ones who bought into it the most were the ones who received the most from this system of exclusive access to God and His promises. To those who were repressed by the stringent and often man-made laws of Jewish society, a God of peace and love who would draw the needy of the world to Him was more welcome than a Saviour who would simply install another earthly government to rule the poor, oppress the widows, and reward the wicked.

This was not the last time an oppressed people would be deceived, as Roman rule would witness another major misstep in the collective interpretations of God’s people. This time, the teachings of Jesus and the words of His disciples would be misinterpreted to fit the changing political and religious landscape of fourth century Rome. The year was 306, and Diocletian, one of the most brutal persecutors of Christians in the Roman Empire, had abdicated from his position as Caesar. In his wake, he left three contenders for his throne. One of those vying for the seat of power was a young general, experienced in politics, and power hungry. His name was Constantine, son of a prominent Roman officer and a lowly Greek Christian, Helena.

From his youth, Constantine followed in his father’s footsteps, fighting throughout the empire, rising to a rank of general. Now, on campaign in Britain, he turned his eyes to the ultimate prize of a Roman politico, the title of Caesar, and the seat of the emperor.

Constantine’s line to the throne was through his father. Diocletian had, during his rule, appointed additional Caesars to aid in ruling the empire. Constantine’s father was one of these, and despite being simply appointed to the position, it was expected that his status as a Caesar would pass to his son. Matters were not as simple as a mere transfer of titles, however.

Constantine’s rise was bloody, but his grip on power was set, until he remained the sole contender for the throne. The stage was set. He quickly undid the harsh decrees of Diocletian, legalizing Christianity and removing the persecution that had leveled churches, scattered families, and hunted down bishops and other church leadership. Almost overnight, a peace previously unheard of was gifted to these hounded believers.

The changes that Constantine made did not end, however, with merely legalizing Christianity. His sympathies ran deeper, and he made further moves to legitimize it as not only an accepted religion, but as the state religion.

To Christians eager for the return of Christ, this seemed almost unbelievable. In the span of a few short years the government had gone from crucifying, beheading, and torturing them to holding them up as examples to the rest of the empire. The favor seems to have affected the clarity with which they viewed the apparent reconciliation of the world to the church. Not only would they accept a position of power in the empire, but they would also accept Constantine as a benefactor and protector of the church itself. In their minds, the day of the Lord was come, and Constantine was the rod of iron with which God would rule.

And rule he did. The course of the church was soon swayed by this new and outside influence. Constantine sat in on meetings of the bishops, even though at the time he was not baptized nor was he even seeking baptism. The church’s new position as a tool of the state brought schisms, in-fighting, and contention at every turn. There remained a remnant, but most of the church would fall under the sway of a man motivated by a hunger for power, wealth, and influence.

Constantine would be baptized before his death, lending him even further credibility in the eyes of a straying church. Now separated from its original identity as sheep in this world, the coming centuries would see “Christians” become ravening wolves, destroying, killing, and corrupting.

In a matter more recently related to us as Anabaptists, the tale of the infamous Muensterites gives us a further example of the perils of misinterpreting prophecy, especially the prophecy regarding the second coming of Christ.

One of the great disadvantages of a heavily persecuted group is a tendency to lack stability, as evidenced by the varying beliefs developed by Anabaptist groups of the movement's first fifty years. Persecution would deprive a congregation of their leaders, who were often those most targeted by the authorities. A missing elder meant less teaching, which in turn led to more difficulty in guidance, and corrective doctrine. Even the most sincere and interconnected groups could fall into errors developed because of the lack of leadership to bring Biblical clarity and balance the brotherhood.

The situation in the Netherlands was of a rather volatile strain approaching the 1530s. Throughout the country, the Catholic Church remained the predominant religion, clinging to their power through ruthless displays of physical force, most often directed towards the minority Protestant congregations. This focus on quelling the Protestant influence was momentarily successful in this instance, with most of their groups dissolving and reintegrating into the Catholic Church or other groups.

One of the groups that was on the receiving end of this minor diaspora was the fledging Dutch Anabaptist church. For those Protestants who still refused to join the Catholics, the Anabaptists often became their choice of church, rapidly swelling their ranks. This had a profound effect on the local strain of Anabaptism, which without a doubt was fervent, but quite prone to chaos and upheaval.

By 1534 the tensions of this influx of new believers reached a breaking point, and the Anabaptist church of the Netherlands split into two main factions. The first, led by the two Philips brothers, Dirk and Obbe, adhered to the New Testament teachings of separation from church and state, as well as nonresistance. This would be the church of Menno Simmons, and the root of the Mennonite churches of today.

The other faction held to more radical beliefs, led by Jan Matthysz and Jan of Leiden. These two men became increasingly fanatical in their views of Christ’s return, believing that they would be central figures, instrumental in a kingdom that God would set up on Earth.

At the same time, social unrest was brewing, and spilled over in the city of Munster, located in northwest Germany, where the common people rose up, overthrowing their city’s government and expelling their Catholic bishop. The two Jans were quick to act, contacting the new leaders of the city, and eventually winning them over to their views.

The Jans moved to Munser in early 1534, and began sending out prophets and messengers, who called all “Anabaptists” to congregate at this “New Jerusalem”. The unrest of the area made their message all the more appealing, and thousands streamed into the city, intent in being part of this apocalyptic return of Christ.

There was, in fact, an apocalyptic return on the horizon, but not a return of Christ. This one came in the form of the ousted Catholic bishop, who swiftly set siege to the city. His army would stay there for eighteen months.

Inside the city, Jan Matthysz, proclaiming a vision was given to him for a deliverance of the city, left its walls to parade outside, proclaiming a swift delivery of the enemy into his hands. His vision, however, failed him, as he was swiftly delivered into the hands of the enemy, where he was beheaded, and his head set on a pike in front Munster’s gates.

Inside the walls, Jan of Leiden took leadership, ignoring the famine, death, and chaos that now ran rampant within the besieged walls. Instead, he began promoting polygamy, defending it from the Old Testament, killing at least one woman who refused to marry him, and at one point, having sixteen wives.

This abomination soon led to its required end as the city was overcome, with a heavy slaughter being carried out against its inhabitants. The leaders, Jan of Leiden being the most prominent, were captured, tortured, and killed. Their bodies were hung in iron cages on the tower of St. Lamberts Church, the Catholic church in Munster. To this day, the cages still hang, a bleak reminder of the pride and rashness of the two Jans, determined to see their end-time interpretation fulfilled.

In all three of these examples, the prophecy contained in God’s Word was twisted into results that strayed far from the will of God for His children. For the Jews, it caused them to miss the Messiah, failing to recognize the greatest promise God had given them. The fourth century Christians, chafing under the horrific persecution of Diocletian, accepted Constantine as a deliverer, seeing him as a fulfillment of God’s judgement against the kingdoms of this world. Instead of peace, they would sink into a state of ungodliness worse than the pagans around them, with the Catholic Church straying into sin more horrible than even their pagan society. Lastly, the troubled visions and interpretations of the 16th century Munsterites would lead them to an awful fate, sullying the name of the true church.

What have we to learn from these grave errors of those before us? In our time, the end seems imminent, and we are beset with those who would have us believe that we are truly the last of the Christians.

Luke has recorded the instructions of Jesus on this point: …The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them –Luke 17: 22-23. Here are instructions for our conduct in the last days. Let us not be running after the rumors of the end times but let us be obedient to the final admonition of our Lord—that we spread the Word of God and the Gospel of His Son, Jesus throughout the world … and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:14.

Jésus, lors de son ascension vers sa demeure céleste, donna une directive finale à ses disciples, tant à ceux présents physiquement lorsqu’il disparut dans les nuées, qu’à la myriade de croyants qui viendraient à le connaître au fil des âges. L’histoire de sa vie et son évangile devaient être prêchés à tout le monde par ceux qui l’appelaient Seigneur. Cette diffusion mondiale de la Parole, serait, dans la vision postérieure de Jean, proclamée comme l’une des conditions préalables du retour triomphant de Jésus à la fin des temps. Jean lui-même serait vu comme un annonciateur de ces derniers temps, d’après les paroles de Jésus telles qu’enregistrées par Jean … Si je veux qu’il demeure jusqu’à ce que je vienne, qu’y a-t-il pour toi? Toi, suis-moi. Jean 21:22.

Les premiers chrétiens, à juste titre, pensaient que le retour du Christ était imminent, même dès le Ier siècle. L’expansion rapide du christianisme, la dépravation morale complète de la culture romaine et l’intensification des persécutions contre eux semblaient indiquer un retour rapide et triomphant de leur Seigneur.

Or, deux mille ans après que Christ ait fait cette promesse, son retour prochain paraît tout aussi imminent qu’il ne l’était pour les croyants du premier siècle. Les spéculations sur le moment de son retour, sa manière et les facteurs y contribuant sont des sujets toujours actuels et controversés. À la lumière de cette attente fervente et continue de la fin des temps, qu’avons-nous à apprendre de nos interprétations de la prophétie auprès de ceux qui ont tenté de déchiffrer les parties prophétiques des Écritures aux âges antérieurs ?

La première venue de Jésus fut entourée et enveloppée par peut-être la plus reconnaissable des mauvaises interprétations de la prophétie dans la Bible. Environ quatre cents ans de relative silence de la part de Dieu précédèrent son entrée dans le monde en un corps humain et physique. Sa naissance serait inaperçue dans une société qui non seulement avait un besoin désespéré d’un Sauveur, mais qui en attendait aussi l’arrivée. Daniel, écrivant les paroles que Dieu lui avait données, avait annoncé un Messie à venir, et avait même fixé un temps où il apparaîtrait. Maintenant, les Juifs bouillonnaient sous la domination romaine, accrochant leurs espoirs à ce qu’ils croyaient être une extermination soudaine et triomphante des troupes romaines et de leur influence sur leurs terres. Pour nous, il est frappant de constater que leur interprétation de la prophétie n’était pas seulement incorrecte, mais que pour beaucoup elle les égarerait au point qu’ils ne reconnurent même pas ni n’acceptèrent le véritable Rédempteur qui leur avait été envoyé.

Mais qu’est-ce qui causa cette vision erronée ? Pour nous, il semble tout à fait naturel que Jésus se concentre sur les pauvres et les démunis plutôt que d’affronter une armée occupante. Les historiens juifs donnent une réponse intrigante, mais guère surprenante, à l’échec de la majorité de leur peuple à reconnaître le Christ pour ce qu’il était.

L’atmosphère religieuse de l’Israël du premier siècle se caractérisait par la corruption, la concussion, l’appétit du pouvoir et tous les aspects peu reluisants d’une classe supérieure entièrement motivée politiquement.

Les prêtres, autrefois choisis par Dieu pour être ses serviteurs dans la sanctification de ses enfants, s’étaient abaissés à acheter leurs postes de service, notamment celui du grand prêtre, où Dieu avait ordonné qu’un grand prêtre serve le peuple pendant sa vie. Du temps de Jésus, cependant, les responsabilités de conduire les enfants d’Israël étaient partagées, le rôle changeant souvent de mains au terme d’un an. Devenir grand prêtre était une question d’hérédité. La plupart des grands prêtres venaient de quelques grandes familles influentes et riches, car il fallait souvent payer pour accéder à cette fonction.

Ce n’était pas seulement la charge de grand prêtre qui était corrompue; la plupart des niveaux de leadership spirituel éminent étaient occupés par les élites fortunées qui avaient les relations et la richesse pour être placées dans des rôles importants parmi les Juifs.

Cet arrière-plan peu reluisant donne encore plus de clarté aux sentiments de Jésus envers les chefs religieux de son temps. Ces imposteurs ne détenaient pas leurs fonctions sacerdotales pour servir son Père; ils les retenaient pour leur propre gain, transformant le temple en marché et prenant le peuple ordinaire en otage par leurs disputes sur des points de détail de la Loi.

Sans surprise, ces chefs cherchaient un Messie qui s’accordât avec leurs objectifs, leurs idéaux et leur morale, plutôt qu’un Messie qui les réprimandât et les châtiait pour leur hypocrisie, leur avidité et leur ambition égoïste. Leur vision de la prophétie avait été tellement déformée et corrompue par leur mode de vie que même le miracle d’une résurrection ne put les convaincre de voir la puissance du Christ comme venant de Dieu. Cette attente déformée d’un commandant conquérant, chevauchant un cheval de guerre sur les ennemis politiques de ces élites, était également flattée chez le Juif ordinaire. Des siècles de luttes pour la simple liberté de culte, comme dans le cas des Maccabées et des Grecs, avaient profondément imprimé un sentiment de nationalisme dans la conscience collective du peuple juif. Ceux qui y adhéraient le plus étaient ceux qui tiraient le plus de ce système d’accès exclusif à Dieu et à ses promesses. Pour ceux qui étaient réprimés par les lois strictes et souvent fabriquées de la société juive, un Dieu de paix et d’amour qui attirerait les nécessiteux du monde à lui était plus bienvenu qu’un Sauveur qui se contenterait d’instaurer un autre gouvernement terrestre pour gouverner les pauvres, opprimer les veuves et récompenser les méchants.

Ce ne fut pas la dernière fois qu’un peuple opprimé serait trompé, car la domination romaine connaîtrait une autre grave erreur collective dans l’interprétation du peuple de Dieu. Cette fois, les enseignements de Jésus et les paroles de ses disciples furent mal interprétés afin de s’adapter au paysage politique et religieux changeant de la Rome du IVe siècle. L’année était 306, et Dioclétien, l’un des plus brutaux persécuteurs des chrétiens dans l’Empire romain, avait abdiqué de sa position de César. Sur son départ, il laissa trois prétendants à son trône. L’un de ceux qui convoitaient le siège du pouvoir était un jeune général, familier de la politique et avide de pouvoir. Il s’appelait Constantin, fils d’un officier romain éminent et d’une humble chrétienne grecque, Hélène.

Dès sa jeunesse, Constantin suivit les traces de son père, combattant à travers l’empire et gravissant les rangs jusqu’à celui de général. Lors d’une campagne en Bretagne, il posa ses yeux sur le prix ultime d’un politicien romain, le titre de César et le siège de l’empereur.

La voie de Constantin au trône passait par son père. Dioclétien avait, durant son règne, nommé des Césars supplémentaires pour l’aider à gouverner l’empire. Le père de Constantin fut l’un d’eux et, malgré le fait qu’il fût simplement nommé à la fonction, on s’attendait à ce que son statut de César passe à son fils. Les choses n’étaient cependant pas aussi simples qu’un simple transfert de titres.

L’ascension de Constantin fut sanglante, mais son emprise sur le pouvoir se renforça jusqu’à ce qu’il reste le seul prétendant au trône. La scène était prête. Il annula rapidement les décrets sévères de Dioclétien, légalisant le christianisme et mettant fin aux persécutions qui avaient nivelé des églises, dispersé des familles et traqué des évêques et d’autres responsables ecclésiastiques. Presque du jour au lendemain, une paix jusque-là inconnue fut accordée à ces croyants persécutés.

Les changements opérés par Constantin ne se limitèrent cependant pas à la simple légalisation du christianisme. Ses sympathies allaient plus loin, et il fit d’autres actes pour le légitimer non seulement comme une religion acceptée, mais comme la religion d’État.

Pour des chrétiens avides du retour du Christ, cela sembla presque incroyable. En l’espace de quelques années, le gouvernement était passé de la crucifixion, décapitation et torture à les présenter en exemple pour le reste de l’empire. La faveur sembla affecter la clarté avec laquelle ils percevaient la réconciliation apparente du monde avec l’Église. Non seulement ils acceptèrent une position de pouvoir dans l’empire, mais ils acceptèrent aussi Constantin comme bienfaiteur et protecteur de l’Église elle-même. Dans leur esprit, le jour du Seigneur était venu, et Constantin était la verge de fer avec laquelle Dieu gouvernerait.

Et gouverner, il le fit. Le cours de l’Église fut bientôt influencé par cette nouvelle influence extérieure. Constantin assista à des réunions des évêques, bien qu’à l’époque il ne fût pas baptisé et ne cherchât même pas le baptême. La nouvelle position de l’Église comme instrument de l’État entraîna schismes, luttes internes et controverses à chaque tournant. Il resta un reste fidèle, mais la plupart de l’Église tomberait sous l’emprise d’un homme motivé par la faim du pouvoir, de la richesse et de l’influence.

Constantin fut baptisé avant sa mort, ce qui lui donna encore plus de crédibilité aux yeux d’une Église égarée. Désormais séparée de son identité originelle comme brebis dans ce monde, les siècles à venir verraient des “chrétiens” devenir des loups voraces, détruisant, tuant et corrompant.

Dans une histoire plus récemment liée à nous en tant qu’anabaptistes, le récit des infâmes Munsterites nous fournit un exemple supplémentaire des périls d’une mauvaise interprétation de la prophétie, en particulier de la prophétie concernant le second avènement du Christ.

L’un des grands inconvénients d’un groupe fortement persécuté est une tendance au manque de stabilité, comme en témoignent les croyances variables développées par les groupes anabaptistes durant les cinquante premières années du mouvement. La persécution privait une congrégation de ses dirigeants, souvent ceux qui étaient le plus ciblés par les autorités. L’absence d’un ancien signifiait moins d’enseignement, ce qui entraînait à son tour davantage de difficultés pour l’orientation et la doctrine corrective. Même les groupes les plus sincères et interconnectés pouvaient tomber dans des erreurs développées par manque de leadership pour apporter la clarté biblique et équilibrer la fraternité.

La situation aux Pays-Bas était d’une nuance plutôt volatile à l’approche des années 1530. Dans tout le pays, l’Église catholique resta la religion dominante, s’agrippant à son pouvoir par des démonstrations impitoyables de force physique, le plus souvent dirigées contre les congrégations protestantes minoritaires. Cet effort pour réprimer l’influence protestante eut un succès momentané dans ce cas, la plupart de leurs groupes se dissolvant et se réintégrant dans l’Église catholique ou d’autres groupes.

L’un des groupes qui fit les frais de cette diaspora mineure fut l’église anabaptiste néerlandaise naissante. Pour ces protestants qui refusaient encore de se joindre aux catholiques, les anabaptistes devinrent souvent leur choix d’église, augmentant rapidement leurs rangs. Cela eut un effet profond sur la branche locale de l’anabaptisme, qui était sans aucun doute fervente, mais assez sujette au chaos et aux bouleversements.

En 1534, les tensions causées par cet afflux de nouveaux croyants atteignirent un point de rupture, et l’Église anabaptiste des Pays-Bas se scinda en deux factions principales. La première, dirigée par les deux frères Philips, Dirk et Obbe, adhérait aux enseignements du Nouveau Testament sur la séparation de l’Église et de l’État ainsi qu’à la non-résistance. Ce fut l’Église de Menno Simons et la racine des églises mennonites d’aujourd’hui.

L’autre faction soutenait des croyances plus radicales, menée par Jan Matthysz et Jean de Leyde. Ces deux hommes devinrent de plus en plus fanatiques dans leurs vues sur le retour du Christ, croyant qu’ils seraient des figures centrales, instrumentales dans un royaume que Dieu établirait sur la terre.

Au même moment, des troubles sociaux couvaient et éclatèrent dans la ville de Münster, située dans le nord-ouest de l’Allemagne, où le peuple se souleva, renversant le gouvernement de la ville et expulsant leur évêque catholique. Les deux Jans eurent tôt fait d’agir, contactant les nouveaux dirigeants de la cité et finissant par les rallier à leurs vues.

Les Jans se rendirent à Münster au début de 1534 et commencèrent à envoyer des prophètes et des messagers qui appelaient tous les “anabaptistes” à se rassembler dans cette “Nouvelle Jérusalem”. L’agitation de la région rendit leur message d’autant plus attrayant, et des milliers de personnes affluèrent dans la ville, désireuses de faire partie de ce retour apocalyptique du Christ.

Il y eut, en effet, un retour apocalyptique à l’horizon, mais ce ne fut pas le retour du Christ. Celui-ci prit la forme de l’évêque catholique expulsé, qui assiégea rapidement la ville. Son armée y resta pendant dix-huit mois.

À l’intérieur de la cité, Jan Matthysz, proclamant qu’une vision lui avait été donnée pour la délivrance de la ville, quitta ses murs pour parader dehors, proclamant une délivrance rapide de l’ennemi entre ses mains. Sa vision le trahit cependant, car il fut rapidement livré aux mains de l’ennemi, décapité et sa tête placée sur une pique devant les portes de Münster.

À l’intérieur des murailles, Jean de Leyde prit la direction, ignorant la famine, la mort et le chaos qui régnaient désormais dans l’enceinte assiégée. À la place, il commença à promouvoir la polygamie, la justifiant par l’Ancien Testament, tua au moins une femme qui refusa de l’épouser et eut à un moment seize épouses.

Cette abomination conduisit bientôt à sa fin inévitable alors que la ville fut reprise, une lourde tuerie ayant lieu parmi ses habitants. Les dirigeants, Jean de Leyde étant le plus en vue, furent capturés, torturés et mis à mort. Leurs corps furent suspendus dans des cages de fer sur la tour de l’église Saint-Lambert, l’église catholique de Münster. À ce jour, les cages pendent encore, sombre rappel de l’orgueil et de l’imprudence des deux Jans, déterminés à voir leur interprétation des derniers temps s’accomplir.

Dans chacun de ces trois exemples, la prophétie contenue dans la Parole de Dieu fut tordue en des résultats qui s’écartaient largement de la volonté de Dieu pour ses enfants. Pour les Juifs, cela leur fit manquer le Messie, manquant de reconnaître la plus grande promesse que Dieu leur avait faite. Les chrétiens du IVe siècle, oppressés par l’horrible persécution de Dioclétien, acceptèrent Constantin comme un libérateur, le voyant comme l’accomplissement du jugement de Dieu contre les royaumes de ce monde. Au lieu de la paix, ils sombrèrent dans un état d’impiété pire que celui des païens qui les entouraient, l’Église catholique s’égarant dans des péchés plus horribles encore que leur société païenne. Enfin, les visions troublées et les interprétations des Münsterites du XVIe siècle les conduisirent à un destin affreux, ternissant le nom de la véritable Église.

Que devons-nous apprendre de ces graves erreurs de ceux qui nous ont précédés ? En notre temps, la fin semble imminente, et nous sommes assaillis par ceux qui voudraient nous faire croire que nous sommes vraiment les derniers des chrétiens.

Luc a consigné les instructions de Jésus à ce sujet : …Des jours viendront où vous chercherez à voir un des jours du Fils de l’homme, et vous ne le verrez point. Ils vous diront: Voilà ici; voilà là; n’y allez point, et ne les suivez point –Luc 17:22-23. Voici des instructions pour notre conduite dans les derniers jours. Ne courons pas après les rumeurs des derniers temps, mais soyons obéissants à la dernière admonition de notre Seigneur — que nous répandions la Parole de Dieu et l’Évangile de son Fils, Jésus, à travers le monde … et alors viendra la fin –Matthieu 24:14.

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

Зигмунд Фрейд, «отец психологии» и противник христианской веры, много размышлял над «проблемой» преодоления чувства вины, которое, по его мнению, являлось негативным побочным продуктом религиозного учения. Он замечал, что «только через солидарность всех участников (группы) чувство вины может быть ослаблено».

Членство в группе с общим фокусом или целью способно радикально изменить не только мировоззрение и взгляды человека, но и его представления о добре и зле, о правом и неправом и т. п. Это действительно может лишить душу её нормального, Богом данного чувства вины, поскольку стандарты правильного и неправильного модифицируются. Некоторые родители обнаруживали этот факт, когда их молодые люди вступали в молодежную группу. Те, кто раньше уважал авторитет родителей, церкви и Бога, уже не держались тех же убеждений. Если они вошли в группу, чьей целью было развлечение, и при этом полагали, что «утверждённые» правила, факты и истина мешают удовлетворению их плотских желаний, то общество и его правила становились врагом группы. Право и неправо определяются консенсусом группы в соответствии с её целями. Если целью является удовольствие, «недопустимо, чтобы (любой авторитет или правило) вмешивались».

«Ребёнок перенимает характерное поведение той группы, в которой он оказался … он отражает поведенческие модели, установленные … лидером группы» (Курт Левин, в A Sociology of Education).

Хотя это кажется странным, «обычно легче изменить людей, сформированных в группу, чем изменить любого из них поодиночке», по словам Курта Левина. Индивид естественно будет сопротивляться изменению своих личных убеждений. Однако тот, кто уже является членом группы с общей целью (что есть у всех групп), автоматически теряет это сопротивление в отношении взглядов группы. Пример: я часть этой группы, значит взгляд и мнения группы — мои взгляды и мнения. Слишком часто ни один человек в группе не станет тщательно проверять убеждения группы, а принимает их как должное, потому что он принадлежит к этой группе.

«Один из самых занимательных аспектов групповой терапии — в том, что все рождаются заново, рождаются вместе в группе». (Ирвин Д. Ялом). Это легко наблюдается среди людей всех возрастов, объединённых общими интересами.

Адольф Гитлер очень эффективно использовал динамику группы в своих отрядах Гитлерюгенд. Он не только сумел дать им чувство причастности и дело, которое можно поддерживать, но и эффективно изменил моральный компас молодёжи своего времени.

Библия также фиксирует очень действенную групповую динамику и то, как быстро она может влиять на людей без доказательств. В Деяниях 14:1 мы видим, как толпа готова приносить жертвы Павлу как богу, а в следующем стихе они побивают его камнями. В Деяниях 19 группа часами кричит: «Велика Диана эфесская». В стихе 32 говорится, что большинство людей даже не знали, в чём там была суть, но они были готовы убивать ради того, что это было. В этих примерах, возможно, ни один человек всерьёз не задумался о том, что морально правильно или неправильно. Они подхватывали дело группы. Это давало чувство «правильности» и причастности просто потому, что они были участниками дела. Но остановитесь и подумайте — саму причину, действие и последствия следует всегда тщательно взвешивать.

Эти люди не брали на себя индивидуальную ответственность за определение того, что морально правильно и неправильно. Слишком часто люди этого не делают, они функционируют лишь как группа. Но Библия говорит нам, что придёт время, когда мы все будем лично привлечены к ответу за то, что сделали в этой жизни. В тот день то, во что верила или что делала группа, уже не будет иметь значения. Когда мы (каждый из нас) однажды предстанем (в конце времён) пред Божиим судом, нас будут судить по …праведному суду Божьему; Который воздаст каждому по делам его –Римлянам 2:5-6.

Как мы читаем в библейских книгах Царств и Летописей, Израиль как народ действовал согласно сильной групповой динамике. Когда воцарялся хороший царь, народ в целом обращался к Господу. Когда воцарялся злой царь, народ в целом обращался к идолослужению. Были немногие исключения — несколько людей, которые думали самостоятельно — чья верность Богу была сильнее, чем верность царю или нации.

Сама христианская церковь — это группа, влияющая и меняющая взгляды и мораль отдельных людей как в лучшую, так и в худшую сторону. В зависимости от убеждений группы и её лидеров, церковь может быть источником благочестивой нравственности или же может объяснять в сторону библейские понятия о добре и зле.

Между христианской церковью и всеми прочими группами должно существовать существенное различие в том, как действует их групповая динамика. Христианская церковь — это группа с явной целью обратить верность и веру людей к Иисусу Христу, как Он открыт в Своём Слове, а не к самой группе. Церковь, чья цель — привлекать приверженцев к себе, провалилась в своей миссии, описанной в Слове Божьем. Церковь, успешно обращающая людей от всех прочих привязанностей к Иисусу Христу, — успешная церковь. Верность Иисусу включает послушание Его Слову, которое требует повиновения всем властям, включая церковь. Но послушание христианина церкви вторично и является следствием его послушания Иисусу, а не наоборот. Если церковь успешна в том, чтобы направить веру и внимание своих членов к Иисусу, как Он открыт в Своём Слове, то эти члены не позволят церкви принять несвященные современные учения, и церковь останется твердой в …вере, однажды преданной святым –Иуда 1:3.

Пусть каждый из нас, как коллективно, так и индивидуально, направит нашу веру на Иисуса Христа.

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Saluti di amore cristiano a tutti. In questo numero della rivista (estate 2023)… L'articolo di Storia della Chiesa si concentra sulla profezia biblica relativa agli ultimi tempi e su alcuni modi diversi in cui, nel corso degli anni, certi elementi della chiesa si sono allontanati dall'insegnamento biblico per quanto riguardava la loro vita quotidiana. Nel suo articolo, Donny Brechbill, che insieme a sua moglie tiene diversi seminari sul matrimonio ogni anno, si impegna a focalizzarsi su un argomento difficile—alcuni dei problemi di fondo che egli vede nelle donne che stanno lottando nella chiesa. Lee Rufener adotta un approccio senza scuse nel suo sforzo di condividere un insegnamento espositivo su modi pratici per avere una casa santificata. Questa volta abbiamo una nuova autrice per le sorelle che condivide un peso nel suo cuore—instillare la Parola di Dio nei cuori della prossima generazione.

Inoltre, altri argomenti interessanti. Buona lettura.

Se vieni edificato o incoraggiato dal contenuto di uno qualsiasi degli autori, sarebbe una benedizione per noi ricevere una tua risposta per posta o e‑mail. Lo inoltriamo ai nostri scrittori per il loro beneficio.

Di recente riflettevo sul tema del cambiamento. Come ho già scritto, come famiglia abbiamo attraversato un bel po' di cambiamenti. Negli ultimi 1–2 anni ci siamo trasferiti in un altro luogo di residenza, ho acquisito un nuovo lavoro e infine, grazie al Signore, mi sono per lo più ripreso dagli effetti a lungo termine della Covid. Un ringraziamento speciale a ciascuno di voi che ha pregato per la mia salute.

Mentre mi fermavo in un tranquillo rimpianto, sono rimasto sorpreso da tutte le cose che sono cambiate nei più di 40 anni che posso ricordare. (Anche se ho più di 50 anni, in realtà non ricordo molto dei primissimi anni della mia vita.)

Da ragazzo, giravo su veicoli che non avevano cinture di sicurezza e certamente, nessun airbag. Quando entrambi questi dispositivi “salvavita” furono introdotti, ricordo bene le molte discussioni sul fatto che fossero davvero salvavita nel loro effetto o se l'opposto fosse vero. Tutti i veicoli erano di trazione posteriore o a quattro ruote motrici. Quanto sembrava strano quando cominciarono ad apparire le prime auto a trazione anteriore. Ora abbiamo veicoli ibridi con una spinta verso veicoli completamente elettrici.

Più di quaranta anni fa, la maggior parte dei contadini aveva trattori a benzina con carburatore o trattori diesel con pompa iniettore azionata manualmente. Oggi, la maggior parte dei trattori è equipaggiata con un computer e sembrano chilometri di fili e componenti elettronici vari. Allora, la maggior parte degli agricoltori riusciva a mantenere o riparare i propri mezzi; ora c'è bisogno di macchine diagnostiche e strumenti specializzati che costano molto e richiedono molte ore per imparare a usarli. Questo porta la maggior parte degli agricoltori a fare affidamento sull'esperienza di meccanici specializzati che costano anch'essi molto.

Poi c'è stata la Covid. È stato un periodo stressante. Hai notato cosa è cambiato durante, dopo o a causa della Covid? Nel mio interagire con gli altri, di routine qualcuno dirà che questo o quello è diverso dalla Covid. Sono solo io, o da quando è arrivata la Covid il pubblico in generale è meno amichevole e più riservato nelle proprie interazioni? Controlliamo le nostre interazioni per assicurarci che stiamo ancora essendo la “luce” e il “sale” di Dio in questo mondo oscuro, e che non stiamo perdendo la nostra “salinità”. Inoltre, ci sono cartelli ovunque con la scritta «si cerca personale». Perché? Mi sembra che la Covid abbia incoraggiato ciò che rimaneva dell'etica del lavoro nella nostra società a diminuire ancora di più.

Poi c'è la questione dei telefoni cellulari e delle e-bike. Cosa hanno in comune questi due prodotti non collegati? Dal mio punto di osservazione sugli Amish della contea di Holmes, questi due elementi hanno cambiato un popolo e una cultura in modo più significativo di quasi ogni altra cosa negli ultimi tempi.

Dove ci porta tutto questo? L'autore agli Ebrei dice che Perché essendo mutato il sacerdozio, è di necessità mutata anche la legge – Ebrei 7:12. Quindi, vediamo che Dio ha cambiato le cose come ha ritenuto opportuno; dunque, se dobbiamo cambiare per diventare più biblici, allora dovremmo farlo. Ma l'apostolo Paolo dice Che non siamo più fanciulli, smossi qua e là e portati via da ogni vento di dottrina… – Efesini 4:14.

E perché l'iniquità abbonderà, l'amore della maggior parte si raffredderà. Ma chi avrà perseverato fino alla fine, costui sarà salvato – Matteo 24:12-13. Dunque, vigiliamo in questi ultimi tempi mentre il cambiamento accade sempre di più intorno a noi. Possiamo essere tra coloro che persevereranno fino alla fine.

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

Ο Sigmund Freud, ο «πατέρας της ψυχολογίας» και εχθρός της χριστιανικής πίστης, αφιέρωνε πολύ χρόνο στη σκέψη γύρω από το «πρόβλημα» του πώς να ξεπεραστεί το αίσθημα ενοχής, το οποίο πίστευε ότι ήταν το αρνητικό παραπροϊόν της θρησκευτικής διδασκαλίας. Σχολίασε ότι «μόνο μέσω της αλληλεγγύης όλων των συμμετεχόντων (μιας ομάδας) μπορούσε να απαλυνθεί το αίσθημα ενοχής.»

Η συμμετοχή σε μια ομάδα με κοινό προσανατολισμό ή σκοπό έχει την ικανότητα να αλλάξει ριζικά όχι μόνο την οπτική και τις απόψεις του ανθρώπου, αλλά και την αντίληψή του για το σωστό και το λάθος, το καλό και το κακό κ.λπ. Πράγματι μπορεί να απαλλάξει την ψυχή από το φυσιολογικό, δωρεά του Θεού, αίσθημα ενοχής, καθώς τα πρότυπα του σωστού και του λάθους τροποποιούνται. Κάποιοι γονείς ανακάλυψαν αυτό το γεγονός όταν οι νέοι τους εντάχθηκαν σε μια νεανική ομάδα. Άλλοι που προηγουμένως σεβόντουσαν την εξουσία των γονέων τους, της εκκλησίας και του Θεού, δεν διατηρούσαν πλέον τις ίδιες πεποιθήσεις. Εάν εντάχθηκαν σε μια ομάδα που είχε ως στόχο τη διασκέδαση και πίστεψαν ότι οι «εγκατεστημένοι» κανόνες, τα γεγονότα και η αλήθεια στεκόντουσαν εμπόδιο στην εκπλήρωση των σαρκικών τους επιθυμιών, τότε το κατεστημένο και οι κανόνες του έγιναν ο εχθρός της ομάδας. Το σωστό και το λάθος καθορίζονται από την ομοφωνία της ομάδας σε σχέση με τους στόχους της. Αν ο στόχος είναι η απόλαυση, «δεν είναι σωστό (κανένα κύρος ή κανένας κανόνας) να παρεμβαίνει.»

«Το παιδί υιοθετεί τη χαρακτηριστική συμπεριφορά της ομάδας στην οποία τοποθετείται … αντανακλά τα πρότυπα συμπεριφοράς που θέτονται από τον … ηγέτη της ομάδας» (Kurt Lewin, στο A Sociology of Education).

Αν και φαίνεται παράξενο, «συνήθως είναι ευκολότερο να αλλάξεις άτομα σχηματισμένα σε ομάδα παρά να αλλάξεις οποιονδήποτε από αυτά ξεχωριστά», σύμφωνα με τον Kurt Lewin. Ένα άτομο από τη φύση του θα αντισταθεί στην αλλαγή των προσωπικών του πεποιθήσεων. Όμως, κάποιος που ήδη είναι μέλος μιας ομάδας με κοινό στόχο (που έχουν όλες οι ομάδες), θα δει αυτή την αντίσταση να διασπάται αυτόματα, όσον αφορά τις στάσεις της ομάδας. Παράδειγμα: είμαι μέλος αυτής της ομάδας, άρα η οπτική και οι απόψεις της ομάδας είναι η δική μου οπτική και απόψεις. Πολύ συχνά, κανένα άτομο της ομάδας δεν θα εξετάσει διεξοδικά τις πεποιθήσεις της ομάδας, αλλά θα τις θεωρήσει δεδομένες επειδή αποτελεί μέρος της ομάδας στην οποία ανήκει.

«Ένα από τα πιο συναρπαστικά στοιχεία της ομαδικής θεραπείας είναι ότι όλοι γεννιούνται ξανά, γεννιούνται μαζί μέσα στην ομάδα». (Irvin D. Yalom). Αυτό μπορεί εύκολα να παρατηρηθεί σε όλες τις ηλικίες που αποτελούν μέρος μιας ομάδας λόγω κοινών ενδιαφερόντων.

Ο Adolf Hitler έκανε πολύ αποτελεσματική χρήση της δυναμικής των ομάδων με τις ομάδες της Νεολαίας του Χίτλερ. Όχι μόνο μπόρεσε να τους δώσει αίσθημα του ανήκειν και έναν σκοπό να υποστηρίξουν, αλλά μπόρεσε και να αλλάξει αποτελεσματικά την ηθική πυξίδα της νεολαίας της εποχής του.

Η Βίβλος επίσης καταγράφει πολύ αποτελεσματική δυναμική ομάδων και πόσο γρήγορα μπορούν να επηρεάσουν ανθρώπους χωρίς αποδείξεις. Στο Πράξεις 14:1 βλέπουμε την ομάδα έτοιμη να προσφέρει θυσίες στον Παύλο ως θεό, και στον επόμενο στίχο τον λιθοβόλησαν. Η Πράξεις 19 αναφέρει μια ομάδα που φώναζε «Μέγα εστὶ τὴν Διὰνάν τὴν Ἐφέσων» επί ώρες. Ο στίχος 32 λέει ότι οι περισσότεροι από τους ανθρώπους δεν ήξεραν καν για ποιο λόγο η αναστάτωση, αλλά θα είχαν σκοτώσει για οτιδήποτε κι αν ήταν. Σε αυτά τα παραδείγματα, πιθανώς ούτε ένα άτομο δεν σκέφτηκε σοβαρά τι ήταν ηθικά σωστό ή λάθος. Υιοθετούσαν την υπόθεση της ομάδας. Έδινε ένα αίσθημα «ορθότητας» και ανήκειν, απλώς το να είναι κανείς ένας συνεισφέρων υποστηρικτής της υπόθεσης. Αλλά σταματήστε και σκεφτείτε—η υπόθεση, η ενέργεια και οι συνέπειες πρέπει πάντα να εξετάζονται προσεκτικά.

Αυτοί οι άνθρωποι δεν αναλάμβαναν ατομική ευθύνη για να προσδιορίσουν τι είναι ηθικά σωστό και λάθος. Πολύ συχνά οι άνθρωποι δεν το κάνουν, αλλά λειτουργούν μόνο ως ομάδα. Όμως η Βίβλος μας λέει ότι θα έρθει χρόνος όταν όλοι θα κληθούμε να λογοδοτήσουμε προσωπικά για όσα κάναμε σε αυτή τη ζωή. Εκείνη την ημέρα, ό,τι πίστευε ή έκανε η ομάδα δεν θα έχει καμία σημασία. Όταν εμείς (ο καθένας από εμάς) θα σταθούμε μια μέρα (στο τέλος των καιρών) ενώπιον του θρόνου της κρίσεως του Θεού, θα κριθούμε σύμφωνα με …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

Όπως διαβάζουμε στα βιβλία των Βασιλέων και των Χρονικών, το Ισραήλ ως έθνος λειτουργούσε με ισχυρή δυναμική ομάδων. Όταν ανέβαινε στον θρόνο ένας καλός βασιλιάς, το έθνος γενικά στρεφόταν προς τον Κύριο. Όταν ανέβαινε ένας πονηρός βασιλιάς, το έθνος γενικά στρεφόταν στη λατρεία ειδώλων. Υπήρχαν λίγες εξαιρέσεις—λίγα άτομα που σκέφτονταν για τον εαυτό τους—των οποίων η αφοσίωση προς τον Θεό ήταν μεγαλύτερη από την αφοσίωση προς τον βασιλιά ή το έθνος.

Η χριστιανική εκκλησία η ίδια είναι μια ομάδα, που επηρεάζει και αλλάζει τις προοπτικές και την ηθική των ατόμων προς το σωστό ή το λάθος. Ανάλογα με τις πεποιθήσεις της ομάδας και των ηγετών της, η εκκλησία μπορεί να είναι επιρροή θεόπνευστης ηθικής, ή μπορεί να εξηγεί μακριά τις βιβλικές έννοιες του καλού και του κακού.

Πρέπει να υπάρχει μια σημαντική διαφορά μεταξύ της χριστιανικής εκκλησίας και όλων των άλλων ομάδων όσον αφορά τον τρόπο που λειτουργεί η δυναμική τους. Η χριστιανική εκκλησία είναι μια ομάδα με τον ειδικό σκοπό να στρέψει την αφοσίωση και την πίστη των ανθρώπων στον Ιησού Χριστό όπως αποκαλύπτεται στον Λόγο Του, παρά προς την ίδια την ομάδα. Μια εκκλησία που έχει ως στόχο να αποκτήσει οπαδούς για τον εαυτό της έχει αποτύχει στην αποστολή της όπως περιγράφεται στον Λόγο του Θεού. Μια εκκλησία που επιτυγχάνει να στρέψει τους ανθρώπους από κάθε άλλη αφοσίωση προς τον Ιησού Χριστό είναι μια επιτυχημένη εκκλησία. Η αφοσίωση προς τον Ιησού περιλαμβάνει υπακοή στον Λόγο Του που απαιτεί υπακοή σε όλες τις εξουσίες, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της εκκλησίας. Αλλά η υπακοή του χριστιανού στην εκκλησία είναι δευτερεύουσα και αποτέλεσμα της υπακοής του στον Ιησού, όχι το αντίστροφο. Εάν μια εκκλησία έχει επιτυχία στο να στρέψει την πίστη και την προσοχή των μελών της προς τον Ιησού όπως αποκαλύπτεται στον Λόγο Του, τότε αυτά τα μέλη δε θα επιτρέψουν στην εκκλησία να αποδεχθεί ασκηρές σύγχρονες διδασκαλίες, και η εκκλησία θα παραμείνει υγιής στο …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

Είθε ο καθένας από εμάς, συλλογικά και ατομικά, να εστιάσει την πίστη του στον Ιησού Χριστό.
