تبدأ هذه القصة في سويسرا، في القرن السادس عشر. مجموعة من المؤمنين المسيحيين، راغبين في طاعة يسوع والعودة إلى تعاليم الرسل والكنيسة الأولى، انفصلت عن كل من الكنيسة الكاثوليكية والكنائس البروتستانتية التي تديرها الدولة في عدة كانتونات بسويسرا. أُطلق عليهم اسم الإخوة السويسريين واعتُبروا أعداءً للدولة، من قبل الكاثوليك والبروتستانت على حد سواء. أطلق أعداؤهم عليهم اسم «المعادين للتعميد» لأنهم رفضوا تعميد الرضع. كما امتنعوا عن الخدمة العسكرية، مطيعين أوامر المسيح بـ «باركوا لاعنيكم» و«أحبوا أعداءكم». كثيرون تم اعتقالهم وسجنهم وتعذيبهم بلا رحمة، وفي النهاية استشهد العديد منهم لرفضهم التراجع عن إيمانهم. في أوائل القرن السابع عشر، عندما عجزت السلطات عن إيقاف الحركة بهذه الطريقة، بدأت بمصادرة بيوت المؤمنين ومزارعهم وممتلكاتهم، ثم نفّتهم من سويسرا.

كان أوروبا قد مرت لتوها بتخريب حرب الثلاثين عاماً (1618-1648). في بعض المناطق، مثل بالاتينات (Pfaltzland) في ألمانيا، توفي ما يصل إلى 70% من السكان إما بسبب الحرب أو المرض. أُحرقت العديد من الحُصون المنزلية/الحظائر وتركّت الحقول دون حراثة لسنوات. في منتصف القرن السابع عشر، دعا الأمير المحلي، الناخب لودفيج، الإخوة السويسريين المنفيين إلى بالاتينات لمساعدته في إعادة بناء المزارع بسبب سمعتهم كفلاّحيْن ممتازين ومران في تهيئة الأرض.

كانت هناك ثلاث كنائس رسمية معترف بها من قبل الألمان: الكاثوليكية واللوثرية والمصلحة (Reformed). رغم أن الإخوة السويسريين كانوا مرغوبين اقتصادياً وتُسامح عقيدتهم، لم تُعترَف كنائسهم. كانت هناك حدود على عدد الذين يمكن أن يجتمعوا في وقت واحد، وغالباً لم يُسمح لهم بشراء المزارع التي كانوا يحسّنونها لأنهم اعتُبروا أجانب.

فعلاً ازدهرت المزارع التي يديرها السويسريون مع مرور الوقت، جزئياً بسبب استخدامهم لنظام تناوب المحاصيل المتفوّق، الذي ساعدهم على إطعام عدد أكبر من الأبقار الحلوب، ومن ثمّ مكّنهم من إنتاج الحليب خلال فصول الشتاء. ومن التحسينات الكبيرة أيضاً إدخال نبات البقوليات، البرسيم. جاء ذلك من بذور أهدتها لهم المينونيت الهولنديون. بعد نحو خمسين عاماً، كان الفرق الذي أحدثه السويسريون في الزراعة ملحوظاً بما فيه الكفاية لدرجة أن بعض الجيران الألمان المحبطين اتّهموهم بـ «فيرهيكسنغ» (المصطلح البنسلفاني الهولندي يعني السحر) للأرض (وهو بالطبع لم يكن صحيحاً). لذا، لم تكن الحياة في Pfaltzland تتحسّن للإخوة السويسريين.

في سنة 1708، شهدوا شتاءً قاسياً وطويلاً جداً. كان بارداً لدرجة أن بعض محاصيلهم المخزنة من الجذور تجمّدت في الأقبية الباردة. بعد ذلك بفترة، سمع ويليام بن والكوكرز عن محنة هؤلاء المعمدانيين السويسريين. في 1682، مُنح ويليام بن مستعمرة بنسلفانيا وكان يرغب في إجراء ما سماه «التجربة المقدسة». تخيّل أرضاً يمكن لجميع الأعراق والأديان أن تسكن فيها بسلام. كان لديه اهتمام خاص بتلك الجماعات المضطهدة من قبل كنائس الدولة الأوروبية. وبصفتِه كوكري، فقد تعرّض أيضاً للاضطهاد من كنيسة الدولة في إنكلترا. رحّب بالكوكرز من إنكلترا، والهوجونوت من فرنسا، والمينونيت من هولندا، والمعمدانيين الألمان، وشفينكفيلدرز والبياتيست من ألمانيا، وكذلك الإخوة السويسريين واليهود من حيثما كانوا يقيمون أو يعانون.

هذا هو الخلفية لحكايتنا عن هانز غروف (غروف) الذي عاش تقريباً من نحو 1661 إلى 1746. كان هانز قد أسلم لإيمان الإخوة السويسريين، لكن زوجته آنا (باري) غروف بقيت مع كنيسة الدولة البروتستانتية. عندما فُتح الباب للذهاب إلى بنسلفانيا كمهاجرين روّاد، كان هانز مهتماً بالذهاب، لكن آنا لم تكن كذلك. ربما خططا لأن يستقر هو هناك ثم يعود ليأخذها. جاء هانز إلى بنسلفانيا لأول مرة في 1696. لاحقاً، انتهى به الأمر إلى قيادة مجموعة صغيرة من الإخوة السويسريين (هانز وكريستيان هير، مارتن ميلين، جاكوب مولر، مارتن كنديق، مارتن أوبرهولتزر، ويندل باومَن والفانكس على سبيل المثال) إلى جيرمانتاون، على بُعد نحو سبع أميال شمال فيلادلفيا آنذاك، والتي كانت أول مستوطنة دائمة للمعمدانيين في العالم الجديد. العديد من هؤلاء المستوطنين الأوائل كانوا من هولندا والسويد وكانوا جزءاً من كنيسة المينونيت في هولندا. قضى المهاجرون السويسريون شتاء 1709 في جيرمانتاون — النساء يقمن بالغزل للعديد من النسّاجين في جيرمانتاون والرجال يسافرون إلى مستوطنة معمدانية جديدة في سكيباك، حيث كانوا يتعلّمون العديد من المهارات اللازمة للذهاب إلى الحدود البرية. يبدو أنه هنا أصبحت الإخوة السويسرية معروفة لأول مرة باسم المينونيين أو المينونيت.

في 1710، انتقلت المجموعة إلى وادي كونستوغا حيث كان هانز غروف قد حدّد سابقاً بعض الأراضي الغنية والمروّية جيداً، على بُعد 60 ميلاً غرب جيرمانتاون والحضارة. وللوهلة الأولى، كانت الحياة ستصعب فعلاً. الذئاب والدببة والفهود والقطط البرية الجبلية والحيوانات المفترسة الأخرى كانت كثيرة. كما وُجدت الأيائل وثيران الخشب والغزلان البيضاء الوفيرة (التي كانت تسعد بأكل ما يزرعه المستوطنون). أشجار جوز الكرفس والهيكوري والكاستناء والقيقب والصنوبر الأبيض والبلوط، بعضها بقطر نحو ستة أقدام وطول يزيد عن 100 قدم، غطّت الكثير من أراضيهم الجديدة (باستثناء بعض المروج المفتوحة، التي تركها السكان الأصليون والمناطق الرطبة). هذه الأشجار الضخمة كان يجب قطعها يدوياً بالفؤوس ومنشارين لزوجين. أقرب طبيب أو صيدلية أو معدات أو متجر عام كان على بُعد 60 ميلاً. كان عملاً مليئاً بالتحدّي والخطر، لكنهم كانوا أحرار! أحرار في طاعة ضمائرهم. أحرار في ممارسة دينهم. أحرار في امتلاك الأرض في هذه البرية الجميلة. أحرار في محبة وشهادة لجيرانهم — قبيلة الكونستوغا والتجار الفرنسيين. حصلوا على براءة أرض مسجلة لمساحة 10,000 فدان لأسرهم ولآخرين قد يأتون لاحقاً.

جزئياً بسبب الاضطهاد الشديد، في 1710، انتقل مجموعة من الإخوة السويسريين إلى منطقة مانهايم في ألمانيا. بعد سبع سنوات، في 1717، قطعوا المحيط الأطلسي. جاء أكثر من 60 أسرة إلى وادي كونستوغا في خريف تلك السنة، بما في ذلك أسلافي، هانز ومجدالينا هيس وأطفالهما الثلاثة (لمباركة الله لاحقاً بأن أُعطيا في المجموع 11 طفلاً). ويمكن أن يقال إن منذ ذلك الحين، فتحت البركات بواباتها، وهربت جموع المعمدانيين من أوروبا إلى «أرض بن الموعودة». من 1730 فصاعداً، ومع تدجين هذه البرية، جاء أيضاً كثير من اللوثريين والمصلحة والكاثوليك من ألمانيا بحثاً عن فرص مالية أفضل، مما ملأ هذا الجزء من بنسلفانيا بالعديد من الناطقين باللهجة الألمانية.

استمتعت كثيراً بالحديث مع المؤرخ المعمداني البارز في مقاطعة لانكستر، آموس هوفر، أثناء كتابة هذا المقال. قدّم رؤى وتفاصيل عديدة، لكن اتفقنا كلانا أنه من الصعب جمع كل الحقائق والتفاصيل من زمن بعيد كهذا. مستنبطاً من حسابات بعض المؤلفين، تسير القصة تقريباً هكذا:

سوء تفاهم

في وقت ما بعد أن أمضى عدة سنوات في غابات بن، تلقّى هانز غروف نبأً يفيد بأن زوجته، آنا (باري) غروف، في أوروبا، قد توفيت. حزن حزناً شديداً وكَبُر في مِثْلِه لأنه لم يكن يعلم بذلك ولم يكن هناك ليشارك في دفنها. بعد بضع سنوات، تزوّج من سوزانا كنديق. عاشا أولاً في منطقة ستراسبرغ، ثم بنيا مسكناً قوياً في المنطقة التي تُسمَّى الآن غروفديل. أُنعِمت عليهما تسعة أطفال.

بعد سنوات، ظهرت امرأة في المجتمع وقدّمت نفسها كسيدة هانز غروف. كانت قد أسلمت للإيمان المعمداني في أوروبا وقامت بالرحلة الخطيرة عبر المحيط الأطلسي لتلتحق بزوجها. حسب قولها، فإن امرأة تحمل نفس اسمها قد ماتت، والكلمة التي نُقلت إلى هانز بشأن وفاة زوجته الأولى لم تكن صحيحة. شعر هانز بالذعر، رغم أنه كان بريئاً فيما يتعلق بزواجه الثاني. لم يكن لديه رغبة أن يكون متعدداً الزوجات أو أن يرتكب زنى. تشاور قادة كنيسة الحدود ومنحوا توصية — أن الزوجة الشابة الرائدة التي لديها هذا العدد من الأطفال الصغار تحتاج إلى الزوج ليعيلهم. ويقال إن هانز لم يشعر بالوضوح للبقاء مع أيٍّ منهما لكنه أَدَّى واجبه في إعالة كلتا المرأتين وأطفالهما مادياً. كان معروفاً عنه ككثير السفر، يركب إلى فيلادلفيا بالفرو ثم يعود إلى الحدود الشاسعة ببطانيات ومرجل نحاسي وسلع تجارية أخرى للسكان الأصليين. إن كنت قد سمعت أو قرأت هذا السرد بتفاصيل مختلفة، فأنا كذلك. وحدها الأبدية ستكشف كل هذه التفاصيل بدقة.

الطب

اختارت زوجة هانز الأولى أن تعيش كأخت عازبة في جماعة الكنيسة تلك. بدلاً من أن تصبح مريرة من زوجها أو من إيمانها أو من ظروفها، اختارت حياة خدمة لجيرانها. عاشت في بيت صغير، مع حظيرة صغيرة (ربما بناها لها هانز) على قمة تل حاد يطل على فارمرسفيل، يُدعى «تل ظهر القطة». كانت آثار هذا البيت والحظيرة المبكرة من أوائل القرن الثامن عشر واضحة حتى قبل أقل من خمسين عاماً. على ما يبدو كانت قابلة قبل مجيئها إلى هذا البلد واستمرّت في هذا المهنة حينما كانت هنا. كان لديها خبرة كبيرة في زراعة الأعشاب وصنع الأدوية العشبية. ربما كانت الأقرب لأن تكون طبيبة لمسافات شاسعة حولها. مما استطعت أن أبحث عنه، أمضت وقتها في أن تكون بركة للمجتمع المحلي بمعرفتها الطبية وحكمتها وأدويتَها العشبية المصنوعة منزلياً ومهنتها في القبالة. كثير من آباء مقاطعتنا في لانكستر لما كانوا لينجو من حياة الرواد القاسية لو لم تكن هذه الأخت العزيزة بخدمتها ومعرفتها الطبية. ومن الطريف أنه بعد سنوات، سافر أحد أبناء هانز من الزوجة الثانية، ديفيد غروف، لدراسة الطب. وبعد إكمال دراساته، عاد كطبيب وساعد زوجة والده الأولى في خدمة الكثير من المستوطنين في مقاطعة لانكستر المتنامية بسرعة.

تمنحنا هذه القصة لمحة عن بعض التفاصيل المثيرة المحيطة بحياة المعمدانيين المحافظين قبل وأثناء تأسيس أمريكا الاستعمارية. كانت هناك صعوبات متعلقة بحرية الدين والعبادة في أوطانهم في أوروبا، لكن رحلاتهم وإقامتهم اليومية في بلد جديد حرّ واجهت تحديات أيضاً. ومن التشجيعات التي نراها في هذه القصة استعداد هؤلاء الأفراد لأن يسمحوا بمبادئ الله أن تقودهم في كل خطوة من الطريق.

{"language_guidance":"Use standard contemporary Italian.","language_tag":"it","source":{"html":"

Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:4-7.

“Oh God, give us mothers like Eunice and grandmothers like Lois. Give us women who are women of faith. Give us women who know how to stand for truth against the tide of human rationalization that is destroying the lives of so many well-meaning people. Give us women who are unwavering in their loyalty to Jesus Christ, to their husbands, and to their calling to represent the spirit of Jesus in all of life. Amen”.

History has proven that women are as influential as men in forming the fabric of society and of the Christian community. An argument could be made that they exert an even greater influence if you consider the fact that they have a huge role in shaping the values of little children and, whether or not they dress and conduct themselves according to godly modesty, they can influence the morality of the masses of men around them.

Hence the call for women to be women of faith. Not only does a woman’s faith influence those around her, but every woman has her own personal journey. Her journey is a search for identity, security, and purpose for her life.

Today’s women are inundated with voices that claim to offer the fulfillment that their heart desires. As with their mother Eve, many of these voices appeal to her feminine spirit, but as their mother Eve discovered, unless it is the voice of God, it leads to death and destruction.

The Bible abounds with accounts of women who lived by faith. Consider the harlot Rahab. Bible scholars cannot agree that she was worthy of that title, but it has come down to us as such. She heard the stories of the God of Israel. When she encountered the spies and heard their ominous prediction for her city she chose to believe.

She was a native of Jericho. Jericho was her home. Jericho had high stone walls and brave defenders. She would have had many reasons to place her faith in that which was familiar to her, and which had sustained her in the past.

She chose to place her faith in the God of Israel. The men of Israel told her that if she would hang a scarlet thread from her window on the wall, her house and her life would be spared. A scarlet thread. Not much by way of identity or security, but Rahab hung her faith on a scarlet thread. That scarlet thread represented the power of the God of Israel and, as we know today, it is a beautiful type of the blood of Jesus.

The call to be a woman of faith is a call to turn away from the ideology of the world and to embrace what in the eyes of the world is a futile remedy—a scarlet thread. Rahab’s faith was rooted in her knowledge of the God of Israel and His plan to judge her people. The scarlet thread was her hope of deliverance.

I would like for us to consider how faith in God impacts the primary desires of the feminine heart. Every woman longs for identity, security, and purpose. Jesus has come to meet that heart longing.

Identity –“Who am I?”

This is a question that everyone is compelled to ask at some point in their life—often in adolescence. Young men tend to carve out their identity based in whom they admire and their vocational inclinations. Young women, especially in our Anabaptist communities, are largely at the mercy of the prominent men in their lives to define their identity.

This is not purely cultural. When God said to Eve, …thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee –Genesis 3:16, He was declaring that she and her female descendants would look to the man to define an essential part of their nature.

Fathers play a key role in the early development of a little girl’s identity. Abusive fathers, absent fathers, and indifferent fathers leave in their wake little girls who are uncertain of who they are, or of their value as a person. A father who affirms his daughter’s godly femininity gives her a priceless gift. By that, I mean praising her for qualities of feminine virtue, blessing her for efforts to be chaste and modest, and yes, telling her that she is beautiful.

A woman’s heart will ultimately turn toward a husband. God said, “Thy desire shall be to thy husband”, not to thy father. Most women marry thinking that they have at last found their “savior” and rightly so. Did Paul not say in Ephesians chapter five that the husband is “the savior of the body”? Should a wife not expect to receive from her husband love, affirmation, protection, and provision? This is due to her by divine decree. A godly husband will do everything in his power to provide for her in this way.

“Thy desire shall be to thy husband” is given in the context of the fall. It was one of the consequences of the fall. It is a statement without the promise of fulfillment. This leaves us to believe that, although driven by desire, that desire may go unfulfilled.

What is a woman to do if her husband is unwilling or unable to satisfy her heart’s desire? What if a woman does not have a husband? She must become a woman of faith. Until a woman has found her identity in Jesus, no man will be able to satisfy the deepest longings of her heart.

Many marriages suffer because the wife expects her husband to meet the deep longings of her heart that only Jesus can fulfill. Many men are made to feel inadequate and withdraw when they are expected to be, and to do, for their wives what only Jesus can do.

Calling all women to be women of faith

Women of faith are women who know who they are in Christ Jesus. They have found the deepest longings of their feminine heart met in Him. Because their heart longings are satisfied, they have become a well spring of life to their husband, to their children, and to others.

Security –“Who will protect me?”

Being a woman has always been risky. Women are very vulnerable. In addition to the fact that they are physically more delicate, women are more susceptible to emotional vacillations, and I believe that based on what the Bible has to say about Eve’s deception, that women tend to be more vulnerable to spiritual deception (see 1 Timothy 2:14).

This does not make them inferior to men. Their emotional sensitivity makes them more attune to the many realities of relational problems than many men are. In this, their insight can be a positive thing, helping to balance us men in some of our natural weaknesses. Whatever comparisons we choose to make, I think we can all agree that women need the protection that men offer.

What if the man that is supposed to be protecting you is a coward? We have an example of just such a situation in the Bible. The man’s name is Abraham—yes… the father of faith. Even strong men sometimes make cowardly decisions.

Abraham and Sarah were traveling into Egypt. As they neared Egypt, Abraham became afraid for his life. His wife Sarah was a beautiful woman and Abraham was aware that Egypt was a heathen nation with very loose morals. He was afraid that the Egyptians would kill him so they could have his wife. Abraham said to Sarah, Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee –Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was indeed Abraham’s half-sister. They had the same father, but not the same mother. Abraham’s contingency plan leaves Sarah in a very difficult position. We read nothing of Sarah’s reaction to Abraham’s plan. All we know is that …Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:6.

It would appear that Sarah was not afraid. Her faith was not dependent on Abraham’s protection. She was relying on a higher power. Sarah’s faith gave her a place in the hall of faith in Hebrews chapter 11 and made her Peter’s example of how wives are to relate to their husbands.

The substance of this story is in the outcome. Because of Sarah’s faith, she was delivered from the hand of Pharaoh, the most powerful world ruler of the day. It was Sarah’s faith, not Abraham’s, which protected her.

Women look to men for security, and it is right that they should. Men protect their women as best they can. I believe that when men and women are living within their God-given roles, there is a lot of protection and security available; however, we do live in a fallen world. We do not always honorably fulfill our roles and sometimes God allows evil to befall even the most pious.

Calling all women to be women of faith even as Sarah

Do you have faith to believe that God is bigger than your husband or your father? Are you willing to trust God to overrule where your husband may be weak or even rebellious against God or the church?

A woman of faith is a woman who chooses to trust God in the absence of a reasonable path forward. A woman of faith continues to do what is right, even though it may not be a path of guaranteed security because …The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me –Hebrews 13:6.

Purpose – “Why am I here?”

This is a question that everyone asks at some point in life. We want our lives to have meaning and purpose. The futility of a meaningless living drives men and women into depression and despair. Living purposefully blesses us and others and brings honor to our Creator.

When men think of living purposefully, they envision… a battle to fight, a mountain to conquer, a noble goal to strive for. We men tend to be vision-oriented and goal-focused.

What does it mean for a woman to live purposefully?

Luke gives us some insight into this in the account of Jesus’ visit to the home of Mary and Martha. (See Luke 10:38-42) Jesus would frequently stop by this home when He was passing through Bethany. Here He knew He would find great hospitality and engaging conversation. Today was no exception.

As He relaxed in their sitting room, Mary sat at His feet asking questions and listening intently as He revealed to her the purpose of His life and His future destiny. Mary came to understand things about Jesus that even His disciples had failed to grasp.

Matthew records that when Jesus was dining in the house of Simon a woman, thought to be Mary of Bethany, entered, and knelt and anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive ointment. When the disciples complained about “this waste” Jesus said to them: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial –Matthew 26:12.

Where did Mary get this understanding? Was it not when she was “sitting at Jesus feet?”

Martha on the other hand was “cumbered about much serving”. Now Jesus had to eat. Someone needed to prepare food and I am certain that Jesus enjoyed Martha’s delicious provisions. But Jesus chided her with “Martha, Martha”. Notice the familial tone of his voice.

He was not judging her nor condemning her. He was challenging her to take time for the important things in life. He commended Mary for she …hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her –Luke 10:42.

I would like to suggest that most of our anxiety is of our own making. We set goals for our life that Jesus never required. We place expectations upon ourselves that have no eternal merit. Like Martha, we stress over frivolity, and damage relationships over trivial matters. Yes, supper must be served, and Mary should help, but not to neglect the “better part”.

Calling all women to be women of faith as Mary who loved to linger at Jesus feet

Life for a wife and mother is full of pressing demands. Defuse your life of stress and anxiety by spending time listening for the voice of Jesus—that “still small voice” that Elijah finally heard.

Stress and anxiety will melt away in the presence of Jesus. God speaks to us by His Holy Spirit through His Word. If it is a challenge for you to find time to sit down with your Bible, then you can quiet your spirit with your hands in the dishwater, or while folding the laundry, or as you once again prepare a meal for your family. At times like this you can commune with God. You can pray to your Father in heaven. You can say things like “I love you Lord Jesus, speak to me through Your Word, bring peace to my soul; quiet the wrestlings of my mind; help me to enter into Your rest; give me Your peace.” Then you can listen as His Spirit prompts your spirit with nuggets of truth from the Scriptures that are hidden away in your heart.

Summary –Calling all women to be women of faith

For your own personal wellbeing:

Women today are bombarded by self-help resources in the form of books, podcasts, social media, and seminars. Much of it is good and can be helpful, but nothing will replace a personal relationship and a daily walk with Jesus.

For the wellbeing of your children:

Today, more than ever we need mothers to be women of faith who can project onto their children that walking with God is real and satisfying. Young Timothy was influenced by the unfeigned faith of his mother and of his grandmother. Never underestimate the effect of the influence of your life on the lives of those who follow you.

For the strength of your husband:

Men today need the support of faithful women, especially their wife. A man’s daily walk can be fortified or diminished by the woman in his life. It has been said “Behind every successful man is woman”. A man is tremendously influenced for good or ill by the women in his life.

For the good of the Church:

Woman of faith, the church needs you. Women bring a grace to the church that is desperately needed. Your prayers are needed. Your testimony gives encouragement. Your song moves our hearts. Your smile gives hope. Your peaceful, joyful countenance of a soul that’s at rest in Jesus is an influence that is rivaled by little else in this world.

Desiderando grandemente di vederti, ricordando le tue lacrime, per essere pieno di gioia; Quando rievoco la fede non simulata che è in te, la quale prima abitò in tua nonna Loide e in tua madre Eunice; e sono persuaso che anche in te. Perciò ti ricordo che ravvivi il dono di Dio che è in te mediante l’imposizione delle mie mani. Infatti Dio non ci ha dato uno spirito di timidezza, ma di potenza, di amore e di equilibrio –2 Timoteo 1:4-7.

“Oh Dio, dacci madri come Eunice e nonne come Loide. Dacci donne che siano donne di fede. Dacci donne che sappiano difendere la verità contro la marea della razionalizzazione umana che sta distruggendo la vita di tante persone benintenzionate. Dacci donne che siano incrollabili nella loro lealtà a Gesù Cristo, ai loro mariti e alla loro vocazione di rappresentare lo spirito di Gesù in tutta la vita. Amen”.

La storia ha dimostrato che le donne sono tanto influenti quanto gli uomini nel plasmare il tessuto della società e della comunità cristiana. Si potrebbe sostenere che esercitano un’influenza ancora maggiore se si considera che hanno un ruolo enorme nel formare i valori dei bambini piccoli e, che si vestano e si comportino o meno secondo la modestia cristiana, possono influenzare la moralità delle masse di uomini intorno a loro.

Da qui la chiamata affinché le donne siano donne di fede. La fede di una donna non solo influenza chi le sta intorno, ma ogni donna ha il proprio cammino personale. Il suo viaggio è una ricerca di identità, sicurezza e scopo per la sua vita.

Le donne di oggi sono tempestare di voci che dicono di offrire l’appagamento che il loro cuore desidera. Come per la loro madre Eva, molte di queste voci fanno appello al suo spirito femminile, ma come scoprì la madre Eva, a meno che non sia la voce di Dio, conduce a morte e distruzione.

La Bibbia abbonda di racconti di donne che vissero per fede. Considera la prostituta Rahab. Gli studiosi della Bibbia non concordano sul fatto che fosse degna di quel titolo, ma questa è la tradizione che ci è pervenuta. Essa ascoltò le storie del Dio d’Israele. Quando incontrò gli esploratori e udì la loro sinistra previsione per la sua città scelse di credere.

Era originaria di Gerico. Gerico era la sua casa. Gerico aveva alte mura di pietra e valorosi difensori. Avrebbe avuto molte ragioni per riporre la sua fiducia in ciò che le era familiare e che l’aveva sostenuta in passato.

Scelse di porre la sua fiducia nel Dio d’Israele. I messaggeri d’Israele le dissero che se avesse appeso un filo scarlatto alla sua finestra sul muro, la sua casa e la sua vita sarebbero state risparmiate. Un filo scarlatto. Non molto in termini di identità o sicurezza, ma Rahab appese la sua fede a un filo scarlatto. Quel filo rappresentava il potere del Dio d’Israele e, come sappiamo oggi, è un bel tipo del sangue di Gesù.

La chiamata a essere donna di fede è una chiamata a volgere le spalle all’ideologia del mondo e ad abbracciare ciò che agli occhi del mondo appare un rimedio futile—un filo scarlatto. La fede di Rahab era radicata nella sua conoscenza del Dio d’Israele e del Suo piano di giudicare il suo popolo. Il filo scarlatto era la sua speranza di liberazione.

Vorrei che considerassimo come la fede in Dio incide sui desideri primari del cuore femminile. Ogni donna anela a identità, sicurezza e scopo. Gesù è venuto per incontrare quell’anelito del cuore.

Identità –“Chi sono io?”

Questa è una domanda che tutti sono costretti a porsi a un certo punto della loro vita—spesso nell’adolescenza. I giovani tendono a forgiare la loro identità basandosi su chi ammirano e sulle loro inclinazioni professionali. Le giovani donne, specialmente nelle nostre comunità anabattiste, sono in gran parte alla mercé degli uomini prominenti nella loro vita per definire la loro identità.

Questo non è puramente culturale. Quando Dio disse ad Eva, …il tuo desiderio sarà verso tuo marito, ed egli dominerà su di te –Genesi 3:16, stava dichiarando che lei e le sue discendenti femminili avrebbero guardato all’uomo per definire una parte essenziale della loro natura.

I padri svolgono un ruolo chiave nello sviluppo precoce dell’identità di una bambina. Padri abusivi, padri assenti e padri indifferenti lasciano dietro di sé bambine incerte su chi siano o sul loro valore come persone. Un padre che afferma la femminilità timorata di Dio di sua figlia le fa un dono inestimabile. Con ciò intendo lodarla per qualità di virtù femminile, benedirla per gli sforzi di essere casta e modesta e, sì, dirle che è bella.

Il cuore di una donna alla fine si volgerà verso un marito. Dio disse: “Il tuo desiderio sarà verso tuo marito”, non verso tuo padre. Molte donne sposano pensando di aver finalmente trovato il loro “salvatore” e a ragione. Paolo non affermò in Efesini capitolo cinque che il marito è “il salvatore del corpo”? Una moglie non dovrebbe aspettarsi di ricevere dal marito amore, approvazione, protezione e sostentamento? Ciò le è dovuto per decreto divino. Un marito timorato di Dio farà tutto ciò che è in suo potere per provvederle in questo modo.

“Il tuo desiderio sarà verso tuo marito” è dato nel contesto della caduta. Era una delle conseguenze della caduta. È un’affermazione priva della promessa di adempimento. Questo ci porta a credere che, pur essendo guidato dal desiderio, quel desiderio possa restare insoddisfatto.

Cosa deve fare una donna se il marito è restio o incapace di soddisfare il desiderio del suo cuore? E se una donna non ha un marito? Deve diventare una donna di fede. Finché una donna non ha trovato la sua identità in Gesù, nessun uomo sarà in grado di soddisfare i desideri più profondi del suo cuore.

Molti matrimoni soffrono perché la moglie si aspetta che il marito colmi i profondi aneliti del suo cuore che solo Gesù può soddisfare. Molti uomini si sentono inadeguati e si ritirano quando ci si aspetta che essi siano, e facciano, per le loro mogli ciò che solo Gesù può fare.

Chiamata a tutte le donne a essere donne di fede

Le donne di fede sono donne che sanno chi sono in Cristo Gesù. Hanno trovato i desideri più profondi del loro cuore femminile soddisfatti in Lui. Poiché i loro desideri di cuore sono appagati, sono diventate una sorgente di vita per il loro marito, per i loro figli e per gli altri.

Sicurezza –“Chi mi proteggerà?”

Essere donna è sempre stato rischioso. Le donne sono molto vulnerabili. Oltre al fatto che sono fisicamente più delicate, le donne sono più soggette a oscillazioni emotive, e credo che, basandomi su quanto la Bibbia dice dell’inganno di Eva, le donne tendano a essere più vulnerabili all’inganno spirituale (vedi 1 Timoteo 2:14).

Questo non le rende inferiori agli uomini. La loro sensibilità emotiva le rende più sintonizzate sulle molte realtà dei problemi relazionali rispetto a molti uomini. In questo, la loro intuizione può essere una cosa positiva, aiutando a bilanciarci gli uomini in alcune delle nostre debolezze naturali. Qualunque confronto scegliamo di fare, penso che possiamo tutti concordare che le donne hanno bisogno della protezione che gli uomini offrono.

E se l’uomo che dovrebbe proteggerti fosse un codardo? Abbiamo un esempio di una situazione del genere nella Bibbia. L’uomo si chiama Abramo—sì… il padre della fede. Anche gli uomini forti a volte prendono decisioni codarde.

Abramo e Sara stavano viaggiando verso l’Egitto. Avvicinandosi all’Egitto, Abramo ebbe paura per la sua vita. Sua moglie Sara era una donna bella e Abramo era consapevole che l’Egitto era una nazione pagana dai costumi molto disinvolti. Temette che gli Egiziani lo avrebbero ucciso per avere sua moglie. Abramo disse a Sara, Di’ pur che sei mia sorella, perché possa trattarsi bene a causa tua, e io viva per causa tua –Genesi 12:13.

Sara era effettivamente la sorellastra di Abramo. Avevano lo stesso padre, ma non la stessa madre. Il piano di contingenza di Abramo lasciava Sara in una posizione molto difficile. Non leggiamo nulla della reazione di Sara al piano di Abramo. Tutto ciò che sappiamo è che …Sara obbedì ad Abramo, chiamandolo padrone: di cui siete figlie, mentre fate bene, e non vi spaventi alcun timore –1 Pietro 3:6.

Sembrerebbe che Sara non avesse paura. La sua fede non dipendeva dalla protezione di Abramo. Ella confidava in un potere più alto. La fede di Sara le dette un posto nel “registro della fede” in Ebrei capitolo 11 e la rese l’esempio di Pietro di come le mogli devono rapportarsi ai loro mariti.

La sostanza di questa storia sta nell’esito. A causa della fede di Sara, fu liberata dalla mano del Faraone, il più potente sovrano del mondo di allora. Fu la fede di Sara, non quella di Abramo, a proteggerla.

Le donne guardano agli uomini per la sicurezza, ed è giusto che lo facciano. Gli uomini proteggono le loro donne nel miglior modo possibile. Credo che quando uomini e donne vivono nei loro ruoli dati da Dio, ci sia molta protezione e sicurezza disponibili; tuttavia viviamo in un mondo caduto. Non sempre adempiamo i nostri ruoli con onore e a volte Dio permette che il male colpisca anche i più pii.

Chiamata a tutte le donne a essere donne di fede come Sara

Hai fede per credere che Dio è più grande di tuo marito o di tuo padre? Sei disposta a fidarti che Dio sovrintenda dove tuo marito può essere debole o persino ribelle contro Dio o la chiesa?

Una donna di fede è una donna che sceglie di confidare in Dio in assenza di un cammino ragionevole da seguire. Una donna di fede continua a fare ciò che è giusto, anche se non è una strada di sicurezza garantita perché …Il Signore è il mio aiuto, non temerò; che mi può fare un uomo? –Ebrei 13:6.

Scopo – “Perché sono qui?”

Questa è una domanda che tutti si pongono a un certo punto della vita. Vogliamo che le nostre vite abbiano significato e scopo. La futilità di una vita senza senso spinge uomini e donne nella depressione e nella disperazione. Vivere con uno scopo ci benedice e benedice gli altri e rende onore al nostro Creatore.

Quando gli uomini pensano a vivere con uno scopo, immaginano… una battaglia da combattere, una montagna da conquistare, un nobile obiettivo da perseguire. Noi uomini tendiamo a essere orientati alla visione e focalizzati sugli obiettivi.

Cosa significa per una donna vivere con uno scopo?

Luca ci dà qualche intuizione in questo nel racconto della visita di Gesù nella casa di Maria e Marta. (Vedi Luca 10:38-42) Gesù si fermava spesso in quella casa quando passava per Betania. Qui sapeva di poter trovare grande ospitalità e conversazioni stimolanti. Oggi non era un’eccezione.

Mentre si rilassava nella loro sala, Maria si sedette ai suoi piedi ponendo domande e ascoltando intensamente mentre Egli le rivelava lo scopo della Sua vita e il Suo destino futuro. Maria giunse a comprendere cose su Gesù che persino i Suoi discepoli non avevano afferrato.

Matteo riporta che quando Gesù cenava nella casa di Simone una donna, ritenuta Maria di Betania, entrò, si inginocchiò e unse i piedi di Gesù con profumo costoso. Quando i discepoli si lamentarono di “questo spreco” Gesù disse loro: Poiché in quanto ella ha spalmato questo unguento sul mio corpo, lo ha fatto per la mia sepoltura –Matteo 26:12.

Da dove le venne questa comprensione? Non fu quando stava “seduta ai piedi di Gesù”?

Marta invece era “affaccendata con molti servizi”. Ormai Gesù doveva mangiare. Qualcuno doveva preparare il cibo e sono certo che Gesù apprezzasse le delizie preparate da Marta. Ma Gesù la rimproverò dicendo “Marta, Marta”. Nota il tono confidenziale della sua voce.

Non la giudicava né la condannava. La stava sfidando a prendersi del tempo per le cose importanti della vita. Egli lodò Maria perché …ha scelto la parte buona, che non le sarà tolta –Luca 10:42.

Vorrei suggerire che la maggior parte della nostra ansia è frutto delle nostre stesse azioni. Fissiamo obiettivi per la nostra vita che Gesù non richiese mai. Ci carichiamo di aspettative che non hanno alcun merito eterno. Come Marta, ci stressiamo per frivolezze e danneggiamo relazioni per motivi futili. Sì, la cena deve essere servita, e Maria dovrebbe aiutare, ma non trascurando la “parte migliore”.

Chiamata a tutte le donne a essere donne di fede come Maria che amava indugiare ai piedi di Gesù

La vita per una moglie e madre è piena di esigenze pressanti. Dissipa lo stress e l’ansia della tua vita trascorrendo tempo ad ascoltare la voce di Gesù—quella “voce sommessa” che Elia alla fine udì.

Lo stress e l’ansia si scioglieranno in presenza di Gesù. Dio ci parla per mezzo del Suo Santo Spirito attraverso la Sua Parola. Se per te è difficile trovare il tempo per sederti con la Bibbia, puoi placare il tuo spirito con le mani nell’acqua dei piatti, mentre pieghi il bucato o mentre prepari ancora una volta un pasto per la tua famiglia. In momenti come questi puoi comunicare con Dio. Puoi pregare il tuo Padre celeste. Puoi dire cose come “Ti amo, Signore Gesù, parlami attraverso la Tua Parola, porta pace alla mia anima; placa le lotte della mia mente; aiutami ad entrare nel Tuo riposo; darmi la Tua pace.” Poi puoi ascoltare mentre il Suo Spirito ispira il tuo spirito con pepite di verità dalle Scritture che sono custodite nel tuo cuore.

Riepilogo –Chiamata a tutte le donne a essere donne di fede

Per il tuo benessere personale:

Le donne oggi sono bombardate da risorse di auto-aiuto sotto forma di libri, podcast, social media e seminari. Molto di questo è buono e può essere d’aiuto, ma nulla potrà sostituire una relazione personale e una camminata quotidiana con Gesù.

Per il benessere dei tuoi figli:

Oggi, più che mai, abbiamo bisogno che le madri siano donne di fede che possano trasmettere ai loro figli che camminare con Dio è reale e appagante. Il giovane Timoteo fu influenzato dalla fede non simulata di sua madre e di sua nonna. Non sottovalutare mai l’effetto dell’influenza della tua vita sulle vite di coloro che ti seguono.

Per la forza di tuo marito:

Gli uomini di oggi hanno bisogno del sostegno di donne fedeli, specialmente della loro moglie. Il cammino quotidiano di un uomo può essere rafforzato o indebolito dalla donna nella sua vita. Si dice: “Dietro ogni uomo di successo c’è una donna”. Un uomo è enormemente influenzato in bene o in male dalle donne della sua vita.

Per il bene della Chiesa:

Donna di fede, la chiesa ha bisogno di te. Le donne portano una grazia nella chiesa di cui si sente disperato bisogno. Le tue preghiere sono necessarie. La tua testimonianza dà incoraggiamento. Il tuo canto muove i nostri cuori. Il tuo sorriso dà speranza. Il tuo contegno pacifico e gioioso di un’anima che riposa in Gesù è un’influenza che è paragonabile a ben poche cose in questo mondo.

Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:4-7.

“Oh God, give us mothers like Eunice and grandmothers like Lois. Give us women who are women of faith. Give us women who know how to stand for truth against the tide of human rationalization that is destroying the lives of so many well-meaning people. Give us women who are unwavering in their loyalty to Jesus Christ, to their husbands, and to their calling to represent the spirit of Jesus in all of life. Amen”.

History has proven that women are as influential as men in forming the fabric of society and of the Christian community. An argument could be made that they exert an even greater influence if you consider the fact that they have a huge role in shaping the values of little children and, whether or not they dress and conduct themselves according to godly modesty, they can influence the morality of the masses of men around them.

Hence the call for women to be women of faith. Not only does a woman’s faith influence those around her, but every woman has her own personal journey. Her journey is a search for identity, security, and purpose for her life.

Today’s women are inundated with voices that claim to offer the fulfillment that their heart desires. As with their mother Eve, many of these voices appeal to her feminine spirit, but as their mother Eve discovered, unless it is the voice of God, it leads to death and destruction.

The Bible abounds with accounts of women who lived by faith. Consider the harlot Rahab. Bible scholars cannot agree that she was worthy of that title, but it has come down to us as such. She heard the stories of the God of Israel. When she encountered the spies and heard their ominous prediction for her city she chose to believe.

She was a native of Jericho. Jericho was her home. Jericho had high stone walls and brave defenders. She would have had many reasons to place her faith in that which was familiar to her, and which had sustained her in the past.

She chose to place her faith in the God of Israel. The men of Israel told her that if she would hang a scarlet thread from her window on the wall, her house and her life would be spared. A scarlet thread. Not much by way of identity or security, but Rahab hung her faith on a scarlet thread. That scarlet thread represented the power of the God of Israel and, as we know today, it is a beautiful type of the blood of Jesus.

The call to be a woman of faith is a call to turn away from the ideology of the world and to embrace what in the eyes of the world is a futile remedy—a scarlet thread. Rahab’s faith was rooted in her knowledge of the God of Israel and His plan to judge her people. The scarlet thread was her hope of deliverance.

I would like for us to consider how faith in God impacts the primary desires of the feminine heart. Every woman longs for identity, security, and purpose. Jesus has come to meet that heart longing.

Identity –“Who am I?”

This is a question that everyone is compelled to ask at some point in their life—often in adolescence. Young men tend to carve out their identity based in whom they admire and their vocational inclinations. Young women, especially in our Anabaptist communities, are largely at the mercy of the prominent men in their lives to define their identity.

This is not purely cultural. When God said to Eve, …thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee –Genesis 3:16, He was declaring that she and her female descendants would look to the man to define an essential part of their nature.

Fathers play a key role in the early development of a little girl’s identity. Abusive fathers, absent fathers, and indifferent fathers leave in their wake little girls who are uncertain of who they are, or of their value as a person. A father who affirms his daughter’s godly femininity gives her a priceless gift. By that, I mean praising her for qualities of feminine virtue, blessing her for efforts to be chaste and modest, and yes, telling her that she is beautiful.

A woman’s heart will ultimately turn toward a husband. God said, “Thy desire shall be to thy husband”, not to thy father. Most women marry thinking that they have at last found their “savior” and rightly so. Did Paul not say in Ephesians chapter five that the husband is “the savior of the body”? Should a wife not expect to receive from her husband love, affirmation, protection, and provision? This is due to her by divine decree. A godly husband will do everything in his power to provide for her in this way.

“Thy desire shall be to thy husband” is given in the context of the fall. It was one of the consequences of the fall. It is a statement without the promise of fulfillment. This leaves us to believe that, although driven by desire, that desire may go unfulfilled.

What is a woman to do if her husband is unwilling or unable to satisfy her heart’s desire? What if a woman does not have a husband? She must become a woman of faith. Until a woman has found her identity in Jesus, no man will be able to satisfy the deepest longings of her heart.

Many marriages suffer because the wife expects her husband to meet the deep longings of her heart that only Jesus can fulfill. Many men are made to feel inadequate and withdraw when they are expected to be, and to do, for their wives what only Jesus can do.

Calling all women to be women of faith

Women of faith are women who know who they are in Christ Jesus. They have found the deepest longings of their feminine heart met in Him. Because their heart longings are satisfied, they have become a well spring of life to their husband, to their children, and to others.

Security –“Who will protect me?”

Being a woman has always been risky. Women are very vulnerable. In addition to the fact that they are physically more delicate, women are more susceptible to emotional vacillations, and I believe that based on what the Bible has to say about Eve’s deception, that women tend to be more vulnerable to spiritual deception (see 1 Timothy 2:14).

This does not make them inferior to men. Their emotional sensitivity makes them more attune to the many realities of relational problems than many men are. In this, their insight can be a positive thing, helping to balance us men in some of our natural weaknesses. Whatever comparisons we choose to make, I think we can all agree that women need the protection that men offer.

What if the man that is supposed to be protecting you is a coward? We have an example of just such a situation in the Bible. The man’s name is Abraham—yes… the father of faith. Even strong men sometimes make cowardly decisions.

Abraham and Sarah were traveling into Egypt. As they neared Egypt, Abraham became afraid for his life. His wife Sarah was a beautiful woman and Abraham was aware that Egypt was a heathen nation with very loose morals. He was afraid that the Egyptians would kill him so they could have his wife. Abraham said to Sarah, Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee –Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was indeed Abraham’s half-sister. They had the same father, but not the same mother. Abraham’s contingency plan leaves Sarah in a very difficult position. We read nothing of Sarah’s reaction to Abraham’s plan. All we know is that …Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:6.

It would appear that Sarah was not afraid. Her faith was not dependent on Abraham’s protection. She was relying on a higher power. Sarah’s faith gave her a place in the hall of faith in Hebrews chapter 11 and made her Peter’s example of how wives are to relate to their husbands.

The substance of this story is in the outcome. Because of Sarah’s faith, she was delivered from the hand of Pharaoh, the most powerful world ruler of the day. It was Sarah’s faith, not Abraham’s, which protected her.

Women look to men for security, and it is right that they should. Men protect their women as best they can. I believe that when men and women are living within their God-given roles, there is a lot of protection and security available; however, we do live in a fallen world. We do not always honorably fulfill our roles and sometimes God allows evil to befall even the most pious.

Calling all women to be women of faith even as Sarah

Do you have faith to believe that God is bigger than your husband or your father? Are you willing to trust God to overrule where your husband may be weak or even rebellious against God or the church?

A woman of faith is a woman who chooses to trust God in the absence of a reasonable path forward. A woman of faith continues to do what is right, even though it may not be a path of guaranteed security because …The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me –Hebrews 13:6.

Purpose – “Why am I here?”

This is a question that everyone asks at some point in life. We want our lives to have meaning and purpose. The futility of a meaningless living drives men and women into depression and despair. Living purposefully blesses us and others and brings honor to our Creator.

When men think of living purposefully, they envision… a battle to fight, a mountain to conquer, a noble goal to strive for. We men tend to be vision-oriented and goal-focused.

What does it mean for a woman to live purposefully?

Luke gives us some insight into this in the account of Jesus’ visit to the home of Mary and Martha. (See Luke 10:38-42) Jesus would frequently stop by this home when He was passing through Bethany. Here He knew He would find great hospitality and engaging conversation. Today was no exception.

As He relaxed in their sitting room, Mary sat at His feet asking questions and listening intently as He revealed to her the purpose of His life and His future destiny. Mary came to understand things about Jesus that even His disciples had failed to grasp.

Matthew records that when Jesus was dining in the house of Simon a woman, thought to be Mary of Bethany, entered, and knelt and anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive ointment. When the disciples complained about “this waste” Jesus said to them: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial –Matthew 26:12.

Where did Mary get this understanding? Was it not when she was “sitting at Jesus feet?”

Martha on the other hand was “cumbered about much serving”. Now Jesus had to eat. Someone needed to prepare food and I am certain that Jesus enjoyed Martha’s delicious provisions. But Jesus chided her with “Martha, Martha”. Notice the familial tone of his voice.

He was not judging her nor condemning her. He was challenging her to take time for the important things in life. He commended Mary for she …hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her –Luke 10:42.

I would like to suggest that most of our anxiety is of our own making. We set goals for our life that Jesus never required. We place expectations upon ourselves that have no eternal merit. Like Martha, we stress over frivolity, and damage relationships over trivial matters. Yes, supper must be served, and Mary should help, but not to neglect the “better part”.

Calling all women to be women of faith as Mary who loved to linger at Jesus feet

Life for a wife and mother is full of pressing demands. Defuse your life of stress and anxiety by spending time listening for the voice of Jesus—that “still small voice” that Elijah finally heard.

Stress and anxiety will melt away in the presence of Jesus. God speaks to us by His Holy Spirit through His Word. If it is a challenge for you to find time to sit down with your Bible, then you can quiet your spirit with your hands in the dishwater, or while folding the laundry, or as you once again prepare a meal for your family. At times like this you can commune with God. You can pray to your Father in heaven. You can say things like “I love you Lord Jesus, speak to me through Your Word, bring peace to my soul; quiet the wrestlings of my mind; help me to enter into Your rest; give me Your peace.” Then you can listen as His Spirit prompts your spirit with nuggets of truth from the Scriptures that are hidden away in your heart.

Summary –Calling all women to be women of faith

For your own personal wellbeing:

Women today are bombarded by self-help resources in the form of books, podcasts, social media, and seminars. Much of it is good and can be helpful, but nothing will replace a personal relationship and a daily walk with Jesus.

For the wellbeing of your children:

Today, more than ever we need mothers to be women of faith who can project onto their children that walking with God is real and satisfying. Young Timothy was influenced by the unfeigned faith of his mother and of his grandmother. Never underestimate the effect of the influence of your life on the lives of those who follow you.

For the strength of your husband:

Men today need the support of faithful women, especially their wife. A man’s daily walk can be fortified or diminished by the woman in his life. It has been said “Behind every successful man is woman”. A man is tremendously influenced for good or ill by the women in his life.

For the good of the Church:

Woman of faith, the church needs you. Women bring a grace to the church that is desperately needed. Your prayers are needed. Your testimony gives encouragement. Your song moves our hearts. Your smile gives hope. Your peaceful, joyful countenance of a soul that’s at rest in Jesus is an influence that is rivaled by little else in this world.

Groot verlangen u te zien, en mij het gedenken van uw tranen in gedachten hebbende, opdat ik mijn blijdschap vervuld worde; Wanneer ik mij het ongeveinsde geloof herinner dat in u is, dat eerst gewoond heeft in uw grootmoeder Lois en in uw moeder Eunice; en ik ben overtuigd, dat het ook in u is. Daarom herinner ik u erom, dat gij het vuur van Gods gave ontvlammt, dat in u is door het opleggen van mijn handen. Want God heeft ons niet gegeven een geest van vrees, maar van kracht, en van liefde, en van bezonnenheid – 2 Timoteüs 1:4-7.

“O God, geef ons moeders zoals Eunice en grootmoeders zoals Lois. Geef ons vrouwen die vrouwen van geloof zijn. Geef ons vrouwen die weten hoe ze voor de waarheid moeten opkomen tegen de stroom van menselijke rationalisaties die het leven van zoveel welmenende mensen kapotmaakt. Geef ons vrouwen die onverzettelijk zijn in hun trouw aan Jezus Christus, aan hun mannen, en aan hun roeping om de geest van Jezus in heel het leven te vertegenwoordigen. Amen”.

De geschiedenis heeft bewezen dat vrouwen evenveel invloed uitoefenen als mannen bij het vormen van het weefsel van de maatschappij en van de christelijke gemeenschap. Er valt te beargumenteren dat zij zelfs een nog grotere invloed hebben, wanneer men bedenkt dat zij een grote rol spelen in het vormen van de waarden van kleine kinderen en, of zij zich nu kleden en gedragen naar goddelijke kuisheid of niet, zij de moraliteit van de massa mannen om hen heen kunnen beïnvloeden.

Daarom de oproep aan vrouwen om vrouwen van geloof te zijn. Niet alleen beïnvloedt het geloof van een vrouw degenen om haar heen, maar elke vrouw heeft haar eigen persoonlijke reis. Haar reis is een zoeken naar identiteit, zekerheid en doel voor haar leven.

De vrouwen van vandaag worden overspoeld met stemmen die beweren de vervulling te bieden die hun hart verlangt. Zoals bij hun moeder Eva, spreken veel van deze stemmen de vrouwelijke geest aan, maar zoals hun moeder Eva ontdekte, leidt het, tenzij het de stem van God is, tot dood en verderf.

De Bijbel staat vol met verhalen over vrouwen die door geloof leefden. Denk aan de hoer Rachab. Bijbelgeleerden zijn het niet eens over haar waardigheid voor die titel, maar ze is ons zo overgeleverd. Ze hoorde de verhalen over de God van Israël. Toen ze de verkenners ontmoette en hun onheilspellende voorspelling voor haar stad hoorde, koos ze te geloven.

Ze was een inwoonster van Jericho. Jericho was haar thuis. Jericho had hoge stenen muren en dappere verdedigers. Ze zou veel redenen hebben gehad haar geloof te stellen in dat wat haar vertrouwd was en wat haar in het verleden had onderhouden.

Ze koos haar geloof te stellen in de God van Israël. De mannen van Israël zeiden haar dat als ze een karmozijnrode draad uit haar raam aan de muur zou hangen, haar huis en haar leven gespaard zouden worden. Een karmozijnrode draad. Niet veel qua identiteit of zekerheid, maar Rachab hing haar geloof aan een karmozijnrode draad. Die draad vertegenwoordigde de macht van de God van Israël en, zoals wij nu weten, is het een beeld van het bloed van Jezus.

De oproep om een vrouw van geloof te zijn is een oproep om af te keren van de ideologie van de wereld en te omarmen wat in de ogen van de wereld een vergeefse remedie is—een karmozijnrode draad. Rachabs geloof was geworteld in haar kennis van de God van Israël en Zijn plan om haar volk te oordelen. De karmozijnrode draad was haar hoop op bevrijding.

Ik wil dat we overwegen hoe geloof in God de primaire verlangens van het vrouwelijke hart beïnvloedt. Elke vrouw verlangt naar identiteit, zekerheid en doel. Jezus is gekomen om dat hartenverlangen te ontmoeten.

Identiteit – “Wie ben ik?”

Dit is een vraag die iedereen op enig moment in zijn leven gesteld wordt—vaak in de adolescentie. Jongens neigen ertoe hun identiteit te vormen op basis van wie zij bewonderen en hun beroepsneigingen. Jonge vrouwen, vooral in onze anabaptistische gemeenschappen, zijn grotendeels overgeleverd aan de prominente mannen in hun leven om hun identiteit te definiëren.

Dit is niet louter cultureel. Toen God tegen Eva zei, …uw begeerte zal zijn tot uw man, en hij zal over u heersen – Genesis 3:16, verklaarde Hij dat zij en haar vrouwelijke nakomelingen tot de man zouden opkijken om een essentieel deel van hun aard te definiëren.

Vaders spelen een sleutelrol in de vroege ontwikkeling van de identiteit van een klein meisje. Mishandelende vaders, afwezige vaders en onverschillige vaders laten achter hen meisjes die onzeker zijn over wie zij zijn, of over hun waarde als persoon. Een vader die de goddelijke vrouwelijkheid van zijn dochter bevestigt, geeft haar een onschatbaar geschenk. Daarmee bedoel ik het prijzen van haar voor eigenschappen van vrouwelijke deugd, haar zegenen voor pogingen kuis en bescheiden te zijn, en ja, haar vertellen dat ze mooi is.

Het hart van een vrouw zal uiteindelijk zich toe wenden naar een man. God zei: “Uw begeerte zal zijn tot uw man”, niet tot uw vader. De meeste vrouwen trouwen in de overtuiging dat zij eindelijk hun “redder” hebben gevonden en terecht. Zei Paulus niet in Efeziërs hoofdstuk vijf dat de man “de redder van het lichaam” is? Zou een vrouw niet verwachten van haar man liefde, bevestiging, bescherming en voorziening te ontvangen? Dit is haar toekomend bij goddelijk gebod. Een godvrezende man zal alles in zijn vermogen doen om haar op deze wijze te voorzien.

“Uw begeerte zal zijn tot uw man” wordt gegeven in de context van de val. Het was één van de gevolgen van de val. Het is een uitspraak zonder de belofte van vervulling. Dit laat ons geloven dat, hoewel gedreven door begeerte, die begeerte onvervuld kan blijven.

Wat moet een vrouw doen als haar man niet bereid of niet in staat is het verlangen van haar hart te bevredigen? Wat als een vrouw geen man heeft? Zij moet een vrouw van geloof worden. Totdat een vrouw haar identiteit in Jezus heeft gevonden, zal geen man in staat zijn de diepste verlangens van haar hart te vervullen.

Veel huwelijken lijden omdat de vrouw verwacht dat haar man de diepe verlangens van haar hart vervult die alleen Jezus kan vervullen. Veel mannen voelen zich ontoereikend en trekken zich terug wanneer van hen verwacht wordt te zijn, en te doen, voor hun vrouwen wat alleen Jezus kan doen.

Oproep aan alle vrouwen om vrouwen van geloof te zijn

Vrouwen van geloof zijn vrouwen die weten wie ze zijn in Christus Jesus. Zij hebben de diepste verlangens van hun vrouwelijke hart in Hem gevonden. Omdat hun harten verlangens bevredigd zijn, zijn zij een levensbron geworden voor hun man, voor hun kinderen en voor anderen.

Zekerheid – “Wie zal mij beschermen?”

Vrouw zijn is altijd riskant geweest. Vrouwen zijn erg kwetsbaar. Naast het feit dat zij lichamelijk fragieler zijn, zijn vrouwen meer vatbaar voor emotionele schommelingen, en ik geloof dat, op basis van wat de Bijbel zegt over de verleiding van Eva, vrouwen geneigd zijn meer kwetsbaar te zijn voor geestelijke misleiding (zie 1 Timoteüs 2:14).

Dit maakt hen niet inferieur aan mannen. Hun emotionele gevoeligheid maakt hen ontvankelijker voor de vele realiteiten van relationele problemen dan veel mannen zijn. Daarmee kan hun inzicht iets positiefs zijn, ter balans voor ons mannen in enkele van onze natuurlijke zwakheden. Welke vergelijkingen we ook kiezen, ik denk dat we het erover eens kunnen zijn dat vrouwen de bescherming nodig hebben die mannen bieden.

Wat als de man die jou zou moeten beschermen een lafaard is? We hebben een voorbeeld van zo’n situatie in de Bijbel. De man heet Abraham—ja… de vader des geloofs. Zelfs sterke mannen nemen soms lafhartige beslissingen.

Abraham en Sarah reisden naar Egypte. Toen zij Egypte naderden, werd Abraham bevreesd voor zijn leven. Zijn vrouw Sarah was een mooie vrouw en Abraham wist dat Egypte een heidens land was met zeer losse zeden. Hij was bang dat de Egyptianen hem zouden doden om zijn vrouw te hebben. Abraham zei tegen Sarah, Zeg van mij, ik bid u, dat gij mijn zuster zijt: opdat het mij wel moge zijn om uwentwil, en mijn ziel levende zij wegens u – Genesis 12:13.

Sarah was inderdaad Abrahams halfzuster. Zij hadden dezelfde vader, maar niet dezelfde moeder. Abrahams noodmaatregel bracht Sarah in een zeer moeilijke positie. We lezen niets over Sarahs reactie op Abrahams plan. Alles wat we weten is dat …Sara Abraham gehoorzaamde, hem heer noemend: wier dochters gij zijt, tot zolang gij goed doet, en niet vreest voor enigerlei ontsteltenis – 1 Petrus 3:6.

Het lijkt erop dat Sarah niet bang was. Haar geloof was niet afhankelijk van Abrahams bescherming. Zij vertrouwde op een hogere macht. Sarahs geloof gaf haar een plaats in de roemlijst van het geloof in Hebreeën hoofdstuk 11 en maakte haar tot Petrus’ voorbeeld van hoe vrouwen zich tot hun mannen behoren te verhouden.

De kern van dit verhaal ligt in de uitkomst. Door Sarahs geloof werd zij bevrijd uit de hand van Farao, de machtigste wereldheerser van die tijd. Het was Sarahs geloof, niet dat van Abraham, dat haar beschermde.

Vrouwen zoeken bij mannen zekerheid, en het is terecht dat zij dat doen. Mannen beschermen hun vrouwen zo goed zij kunnen. Ik geloof dat wanneer mannen en vrouwen binnen hun door God gegeven rollen leven, er veel bescherming en zekerheid beschikbaar is; echter wij leven in een gevallen wereld. Wij vervullen onze rollen niet altijd eervol en soms laat God het kwade zelfs de vroomsten treffen.

Oproep aan alle vrouwen om vrouwen van geloof te zijn, zoals Sarah

Hebt u het geloof te geloven dat God groter is dan uw man of uw vader? Bent u bereid God te vertrouwen te overrulen waar uw man zwak is of zelfs rebels tegenover God of de kerk?

Een vrouw van geloof is een vrouw die kiest God te vertrouwen bij afwezigheid van een redelijke uitweg. Een vrouw van geloof blijft doen wat juist is, ook al is het geen weg van gegarandeerde zekerheid, omdat …De Heere is mijn helper, ik zal niet vrezen wat de mens mij doen zal – Hebreeën 13:6.

Doel – “Waarom ben ik hier?”

Dit is een vraag die iedereen op enig moment in het leven stelt. Wij willen dat ons leven betekenis en doel heeft. De zinloosheid van een betekenisloos bestaan drijft mannen en vrouwen tot depressie en wanhoop. Doelgericht leven zegenen ons en anderen en brengt eer aan onze Schepper.

Wanneer mannen nadenken over doelgericht leven, beelden zij zich in… een strijd om te voeren, een berg om te overwinnen, een nobel doel om naar te streven. Wij mannen zijn geneigd visionair en doelgericht te zijn.

Wat betekent het voor een vrouw om doelgericht te leven?

Lucas geeft ons enig inzicht hierin in het verslag van Jezus’ bezoek aan het huis van Maria en Martha. (Zie Lucas 10:38-42) Jezus stapte vaak dit huis binnen wanneer Hij langs Betanië kwam. Daar wist Hij grote gastvrijheid en boeiende gesprekken te vinden. Deze dag was geen uitzondering.

Terwijl Hij zich ontspande in hun zitkamer, zat Maria aan Zijn voeten vragen te stellen en aandachtig te luisteren terwijl Hij haar het doel van Zijn leven en Zijn toekomstige bestemming onthulde. Maria begon dingen over Jezus te begrijpen die zelfs Zijn discipelen niet hadden begrepen.

Mattheüs verhaalt dat toen Jezus at in het huis van Simon een vrouw, vermoedelijk Maria van Betanië, binnenkwam, neerknielde en Jezus’ voeten zalfde met kostbare balsem. Toen de discipelen klaagden over “deze verspilling” zei Jezus tegen hen: Want waarin zij deze zalf op mijn lichaam uitgegoten heeft, heeft zij het gedaan tot mijn begraving – Mattheüs 26:12.

Waar kreeg Maria dit inzicht vandaan? Was het niet toen zij “aan Jezus’ voeten zat?”

Martha daarentegen was “bezorgd en bezig met veel dienen”. Nu moest Jezus eten. Iemand moest het eten bereiden en ik ben er zeker van dat Jezus van Marthas heerlijke spijzen genoot. Maar Jezus berispte haar met “Martha, Martha”. Let op de familiaire toon van Zijn stem.

Hij veroordeelde haar niet. Hij daagde haar uit tijd te nemen voor de belangrijke dingen in het leven. Hij prees Maria omdat zij …dat goede deel gekozen heeft, dat niet van haar zal worden weggenomen – Lucas 10:42.

Ik wil suggereren dat het merendeel van onze angst onszelf toedoen is. Wij stellen doelen voor ons leven die Jezus nooit geëist heeft. Wij leggen verwachtingen op onszelf die geen eeuwige waarde hebben. Zoals Martha stressen wij over nietige zaken en beschadigen relaties over triviale aangelegenheden. Ja, het avondeten moet geserveerd worden, en Maria moet helpen, maar niet ten koste van het “betere deel”.

Oproep aan alle vrouwen om vrouwen van geloof te zijn zoals Maria die graag bij Jezus’ voeten bleef

Het leven van een vrouw en moeder is vol dringende eisen. Maak uw leven vrij van stress en angst door tijd te nemen te luisteren naar de stem van Jezus—die “stille, zachte stem” die Elia uiteindelijk hoorde.

Stress en angst zullen wegsmelten in de aanwezigheid van Jezus. God spreekt tot ons door Zijn Heilige Geest via Zijn Woord. Als het voor u een uitdaging is tijd te vinden om met uw Bijbel te zitten, dan kunt u uw geest stilmaken met uw handen in het afwaswater, of terwijl u de was opvouwt, of terwijl u weer een maaltijd voor uw gezin bereidt. In zulke momenten kunt u gemeenschap hebben met God. U kunt bidden tot uw hemelse Vader. U kunt dingen zeggen als “Ik houd van U, Heer Jezus, spreek tot mij door Uw Woord, breng vrede in mijn ziel; stille de worstelingen van mijn geest; help mij in Uw rust te komen; geef mij Uw vrede.” Dan kunt u luisteren terwijl Zijn Geest uw geest prikkelt met waarheden uit de Schrift die in uw hart verborgen liggen.

Samenvatting – Oproep aan alle vrouwen om vrouwen van geloof te zijn

Voor uw eigen persoonlijk welzijn:

Vrouwen van vandaag worden gebombardeerd met zelfhulpbronnen in de vorm van boeken, podcasts, sociale media en seminars. Veel daarvan is goed en kan behulpzaam zijn, maar niets zal een persoonlijke relatie en een dagelijks wandel met Jezus vervangen.

Voor het welzijn van uw kinderen:

Meer dan ooit hebben we vandaag moeders nodig die vrouwen van geloof zijn en die op hun kinderen uitstralen dat wandelen met God echt en bevredigend is. De jonge Timoteüs werd beïnvloed door het ongeveinsde geloof van zijn moeder en van zijn grootmoeder. Onderschat nooit het effect van de invloed van uw leven op het leven van hen die u volgen.

Voor de sterkte van uw man:

Mannen hebben vandaag de steun nodig van trouwe vrouwen, vooral van hun vrouw. De dagelijkse wandel van een man kan versterkt of verzwakt worden door de vrouw in zijn leven. Er wordt gezegd: “Achter elke succesvolle man staat een vrouw”. Een man wordt enorm positief of negatief beïnvloed door de vrouwen in zijn leven.

Voor het welzijn van de Kerk:

Vrouw van geloof, de kerk heeft u nodig. Vrouwen brengen een genade naar de kerk die wanhopig nodig is. Uw gebeden zijn nodig. Uw getuigenis bemoedigt. Uw lied beweegt onze harten. Uw glimlach geeft hoop. Uw vredige, blije gelaat van een ziel die rust in Jezus is een invloed die door weinig anders in deze wereld geëvenaard wordt.
