Jesus, upon His ascension back into His heavenly home, gave a final directive to His disciples, both to those physically present as He disappeared into the clouds, and to the myriad of believers who would come to know Him down through the ages. The story of His life and His gospel were to be preached unto all the world by those who called Him Lord. This global spreading of the Word, would, in the later vision of John, be proclaimed as one of the prerequisites of Jesus’ triumphant return at the end of time. John himself would be seen as a harbinger of these end times, based on Jesus’ words as recorded by John … If I will that he [John] tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. John 21:22.

The early Christians, understandably, felt that the return of Christ was imminent, even within the first century. The rapid expansion of Christianity, the complete moral depravity of the Roman culture, and the increasing intensity of persecution against them seemed to point to a swift and triumphant return of their Lord.

Now, two thousand years since Christ gave that promise, His soon return seems just as imminent as it did to the first century believers. Speculation on the time of His return, the manner of it, and the contributing factors are always current and controversial subjects. In the light of this continued earnest expectation of the end times, what have we to learn about our interpretations of prophecy from those who have attempted to decipher the prophetic portions of Scripture in earlier ages?

Jesus' first coming was surrounded and enveloped by perhaps the most recognizable misinterpretation of prophecy in the Bible. Roughly four hundred years of relative silence from God precluded His entry into the world in a physical, human body. His birth would be unnoticed in a society that was not only in desperate need of, but also expecting, a Savior to arrive. Daniel, writing the words God gave him, had told of a Messiah to come, and had even given a time that He would appear. Now, the Jews seethed under Roman rule, hanging their hopes on what they thought would be a sudden and triumphant extermination of the Roman troops and influence from their lands. To us, it is glaringly obvious that their interpretation of prophecy was not only incorrect, but for many, would lead them astray so that they did not even recognize or acknowledge the true Redeemer that was sent to them.

But what was it that caused this misinterpreted view? To us, it seems completely in order that Jesus would focus on the poor and destitute rather than opposing an occupying army. Jewish historians give an intriguing, but scarcely surprising, answer to the failure of the majority of their people to recognize Christ for who He was.

The religious atmosphere of first century Israel was one defined by corruption, bribery, lust for power, and all the unsavory aspects of a completely politically motivated upper class.

The priests, once chosen by God to be His servants in sanctifying His children, had sunk to buying their positions of service, most notably in the high priest’s office, where God had ordained one high priest to serve the people throughout his life. In Jesus’ day, however, the responsibilities of leading the children of Israel were divvied out, the role often changing hands on one-year terms. Becoming a high priest was a matter of birth. Most high priests came from several large, influential, and wealthy families, as one often had to buy into the opportunity of this office.

It was not only the high priest’s office that was corrupted, but most levels of prominent spiritual leadership were filled by the wealthy elites who had the connections and wealth to be placed into roles of importance amongst the Jews.

This unsavory backdrop gives even more clarity to Jesus’ feelings on the religious leaders of His day. These imposters did not hold their priestly positions to serve His Father, they held them for their own gain, turning the temple into a marketplace and holding the common people hostage through their disputes on the minutiae of the Law.

Unsurprisingly, these leaders looked for a Messiah who would fit their goals, their ideals, and their morals, rather than one that would rebuke and chastise them for their hypocrisy, greed, and selfish ambition. Their view of prophecy had been so twisted and corrupted by their lifestyle that even the miracle of a resurrection could not sway them to view Christ’s power as coming from God. This misconstrued expectation of a conquering commander, riding a horse of war over the political enemies of these elites was pandered to the common Jew as well. Centuries of fighting for just the freedom to worship, as in the case of the Maccabees and the Greeks, had deeply imprinted a sense of nationalism into the collective mind of the Jewish people. The ones who bought into it the most were the ones who received the most from this system of exclusive access to God and His promises. To those who were repressed by the stringent and often man-made laws of Jewish society, a God of peace and love who would draw the needy of the world to Him was more welcome than a Saviour who would simply install another earthly government to rule the poor, oppress the widows, and reward the wicked.

This was not the last time an oppressed people would be deceived, as Roman rule would witness another major misstep in the collective interpretations of God’s people. This time, the teachings of Jesus and the words of His disciples would be misinterpreted to fit the changing political and religious landscape of fourth century Rome. The year was 306, and Diocletian, one of the most brutal persecutors of Christians in the Roman Empire, had abdicated from his position as Caesar. In his wake, he left three contenders for his throne. One of those vying for the seat of power was a young general, experienced in politics, and power hungry. His name was Constantine, son of a prominent Roman officer and a lowly Greek Christian, Helena.

From his youth, Constantine followed in his father’s footsteps, fighting throughout the empire, rising to a rank of general. Now, on campaign in Britain, he turned his eyes to the ultimate prize of a Roman politico, the title of Caesar, and the seat of the emperor.

Constantine’s line to the throne was through his father. Diocletian had, during his rule, appointed additional Caesars to aid in ruling the empire. Constantine’s father was one of these, and despite being simply appointed to the position, it was expected that his status as a Caesar would pass to his son. Matters were not as simple as a mere transfer of titles, however.

Constantine’s rise was bloody, but his grip on power was set, until he remained the sole contender for the throne. The stage was set. He quickly undid the harsh decrees of Diocletian, legalizing Christianity and removing the persecution that had leveled churches, scattered families, and hunted down bishops and other church leadership. Almost overnight, a peace previously unheard of was gifted to these hounded believers.

The changes that Constantine made did not end, however, with merely legalizing Christianity. His sympathies ran deeper, and he made further moves to legitimize it as not only an accepted religion, but as the state religion.

To Christians eager for the return of Christ, this seemed almost unbelievable. In the span of a few short years the government had gone from crucifying, beheading, and torturing them to holding them up as examples to the rest of the empire. The favor seems to have affected the clarity with which they viewed the apparent reconciliation of the world to the church. Not only would they accept a position of power in the empire, but they would also accept Constantine as a benefactor and protector of the church itself. In their minds, the day of the Lord was come, and Constantine was the rod of iron with which God would rule.

And rule he did. The course of the church was soon swayed by this new and outside influence. Constantine sat in on meetings of the bishops, even though at the time he was not baptized nor was he even seeking baptism. The church’s new position as a tool of the state brought schisms, in-fighting, and contention at every turn. There remained a remnant, but most of the church would fall under the sway of a man motivated by a hunger for power, wealth, and influence.

Constantine would be baptized before his death, lending him even further credibility in the eyes of a straying church. Now separated from its original identity as sheep in this world, the coming centuries would see “Christians” become ravening wolves, destroying, killing, and corrupting.

In a matter more recently related to us as Anabaptists, the tale of the infamous Muensterites gives us a further example of the perils of misinterpreting prophecy, especially the prophecy regarding the second coming of Christ.

One of the great disadvantages of a heavily persecuted group is a tendency to lack stability, as evidenced by the varying beliefs developed by Anabaptist groups of the movement's first fifty years. Persecution would deprive a congregation of their leaders, who were often those most targeted by the authorities. A missing elder meant less teaching, which in turn led to more difficulty in guidance, and corrective doctrine. Even the most sincere and interconnected groups could fall into errors developed because of the lack of leadership to bring Biblical clarity and balance the brotherhood.

The situation in the Netherlands was of a rather volatile strain approaching the 1530s. Throughout the country, the Catholic Church remained the predominant religion, clinging to their power through ruthless displays of physical force, most often directed towards the minority Protestant congregations. This focus on quelling the Protestant influence was momentarily successful in this instance, with most of their groups dissolving and reintegrating into the Catholic Church or other groups.

One of the groups that was on the receiving end of this minor diaspora was the fledging Dutch Anabaptist church. For those Protestants who still refused to join the Catholics, the Anabaptists often became their choice of church, rapidly swelling their ranks. This had a profound effect on the local strain of Anabaptism, which without a doubt was fervent, but quite prone to chaos and upheaval.

By 1534 the tensions of this influx of new believers reached a breaking point, and the Anabaptist church of the Netherlands split into two main factions. The first, led by the two Philips brothers, Dirk and Obbe, adhered to the New Testament teachings of separation from church and state, as well as nonresistance. This would be the church of Menno Simmons, and the root of the Mennonite churches of today.

The other faction held to more radical beliefs, led by Jan Matthysz and Jan of Leiden. These two men became increasingly fanatical in their views of Christ’s return, believing that they would be central figures, instrumental in a kingdom that God would set up on Earth.

At the same time, social unrest was brewing, and spilled over in the city of Munster, located in northwest Germany, where the common people rose up, overthrowing their city’s government and expelling their Catholic bishop. The two Jans were quick to act, contacting the new leaders of the city, and eventually winning them over to their views.

The Jans moved to Munser in early 1534, and began sending out prophets and messengers, who called all “Anabaptists” to congregate at this “New Jerusalem”. The unrest of the area made their message all the more appealing, and thousands streamed into the city, intent in being part of this apocalyptic return of Christ.

There was, in fact, an apocalyptic return on the horizon, but not a return of Christ. This one came in the form of the ousted Catholic bishop, who swiftly set siege to the city. His army would stay there for eighteen months.

Inside the city, Jan Matthysz, proclaiming a vision was given to him for a deliverance of the city, left its walls to parade outside, proclaiming a swift delivery of the enemy into his hands. His vision, however, failed him, as he was swiftly delivered into the hands of the enemy, where he was beheaded, and his head set on a pike in front Munster’s gates.

Inside the walls, Jan of Leiden took leadership, ignoring the famine, death, and chaos that now ran rampant within the besieged walls. Instead, he began promoting polygamy, defending it from the Old Testament, killing at least one woman who refused to marry him, and at one point, having sixteen wives.

This abomination soon led to its required end as the city was overcome, with a heavy slaughter being carried out against its inhabitants. The leaders, Jan of Leiden being the most prominent, were captured, tortured, and killed. Their bodies were hung in iron cages on the tower of St. Lamberts Church, the Catholic church in Munster. To this day, the cages still hang, a bleak reminder of the pride and rashness of the two Jans, determined to see their end-time interpretation fulfilled.

In all three of these examples, the prophecy contained in God’s Word was twisted into results that strayed far from the will of God for His children. For the Jews, it caused them to miss the Messiah, failing to recognize the greatest promise God had given them. The fourth century Christians, chafing under the horrific persecution of Diocletian, accepted Constantine as a deliverer, seeing him as a fulfillment of God’s judgement against the kingdoms of this world. Instead of peace, they would sink into a state of ungodliness worse than the pagans around them, with the Catholic Church straying into sin more horrible than even their pagan society. Lastly, the troubled visions and interpretations of the 16th century Munsterites would lead them to an awful fate, sullying the name of the true church.

What have we to learn from these grave errors of those before us? In our time, the end seems imminent, and we are beset with those who would have us believe that we are truly the last of the Christians.

Luke has recorded the instructions of Jesus on this point: …The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them –Luke 17: 22-23. Here are instructions for our conduct in the last days. Let us not be running after the rumors of the end times but let us be obedient to the final admonition of our Lord—that we spread the Word of God and the Gospel of His Son, Jesus throughout the world … and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:14.

यीशु ने, स्वर्गीय घर की ओर अपनी आरोहण के समय, अपने शिष्यों को अंतिम निर्देश दिया—उन सभी को जो उस समय भौतिक रूप से मौजूद थे जब वह बादलों में विलीन हुए, और उन अनगिनत विश्वासियों को जो आने वाली सदियों में उन्हें जानेंगे। उनके जीवन और उनके सुसमाचार की कहानी उन लोगों द्वारा पूरी दुनिया में प्रचारित की जानी थी जो उन्हें प्रभु पुकारते थे। इस वचन का यह वैश्विक प्रसार, यूहन्ना के बाद की दृष्टि में, समय के अंत में यीशु की विजयोगानिक वापसी की एक आवश्यक शर्त के रूप में उद्घोषित किया जाएगा। यूहन्ना स्वयं को इन अंतिम दिनों का अग्रदूत माना जाएगा, यीशु के उन शब्दों के आधार पर जिन्हें यूहन्ना ने अंकित किया … यदि मैं चाहूँ कि वह [यूहन्ना] रहकर तब तक रहे जब मैं आऊँ, तेरा मुझसे क्या काम? तू मेरे पीछे आ; यूहन्ना 21:22।

प्रारंभिक ईसाइयों को, स्वाभाविक रूप से, ऐसा लगा कि मसीह की वापसी निकट है, यहां तक कि पहले शताब्दी के भीतर भी। ईसाइयत का तीव्र विस्तार, रोमन संस्कृति की पूर्ण नैतिक गिरावट, और उन पर बढ़ती प्रताड़ना की तीव्रता ऐसा प्रतीत होती थी कि उनके प्रभु की शीघ्र और विजयशाली वापसी निकट है।

अब, उन दो हजार वर्षों के बाद जब मसीह ने वह वादा दिया था, उनकी जल्द वापसी उतनी ही निकट प्रतीत होती है जितनी पहले शताब्दी के विश्वासियों को दिखी। उनकी वापसी के समय, उसके ढंग, और सहायक कारणों पर अटकलबाज़ियाँ हमेशा चलती रहती हैं और विवादास्पद विषय हैं। इस निरंतर गंभीर अपेक्षा के प्रकाश में कि अंत के दिन होंगे, हमने उनसे जो भविष्यद्वाणी की व्याख्या करने का प्रयास किया है—पूर्वकाल के लोगों से हम अपनी भविष्यद्वाणियों की व्याख्याओं के बारे में क्या सीखते हैं?

यीशु का पहला आगमन शायद बाइबिल में भविष्यद्वाणी की सबसे पहचानने योग्य गलत व्याख्या से घिरा और आच्छादित था। परमेश्वर की ओर से लगभग चार सौ वर्षों की अपेक्षाकृत मौनता ने उसे एक भौतिक, मानवीय देह में दुनिया में प्रवेश करने से पहले रोका। उसका जन्म उस समाज में अनदेखा रह जाता, जो न केवल क्रोध और विषम परिस्थितियों में था, बल्कि एक उद्धारकर्ता के आगमन की आशा भी रखता था। दानिय्येल ने परमेश्वर द्वारा दिए गए शब्द लिखे थे और आने वाले मसीह का वर्णन किया था, यहां तक कि उसने ऐसा समय भी दिया था जब वह प्रकट होगा। अब, यहूदी रोमन शासन के तहत उबल रहे थे और वे अपने भूभागों से रोमन सैन्य और प्रभाव के त्वरित और विजयकारी विनाश की आशा पर लट्टू थे। हमें स्पष्टतः दिखता है कि उनकी भविष्यद्वाणी की व्याख्या न केवल गलत थी, बल्कि कई लोगों के लिए वह मार्गभ्रष्ट करने वाली सिद्ध हुई, जिससे वे सच्चे उद्धारकर्ता को पहचानने या स्वीकार करने में भी असमर्थ रहे।

परन्तु उस गलत व्याख्या का कारण क्या था? हमें तो यह बिल्कुल स्वाभाविक लगता है कि यीशु दमनकारी सेना के विरुद्ध लड़ने के बजाय गरीबों और दरिद्रों पर ध्यान दें। यहूदियों के इतिहासकार एक रोचक, परन्तु कम से कम आश्चर्यजनक उत्तर देते हैं—उनके लोगों के बहुलांश के मसीह को न पहचान पाने के कारण का।

पहली शताब्दी इस्राएल का धार्मिक माहौल भ्रष्टाचार, घूसखोरी, सत्ता की लालसा और बिल्कुल राजनीतिक प्रेरित उच्च वर्ग के सभी कुपरिणामों से परिभाषित था।

यहोवा द्वारा एक समय चुने गए पुजारी, जो उसके लोगों को पवित्र करने के लिए सेवा करते थे, अपनी सेवाओं के पद खरीदने तक नीच हो गए थे, विशेषकर महाप्रहर्य का पद, जिसे परमेश्वर ने एक महाप्रहर्य को उसके जीवनकाल में लोगों की सेवा के लिए नियुक्त किया था। परन्तु यीशु के समय में इस्राएल के बच्चों का नेतृत्व करने की जिम्मेदारियाँ बांटी जाती थीं, और यह भूमिका अक्सर एक-वर्षीय कार्यकाल पर बदल जाती थी। महाप्रहर्य बनना जन्म का मामला बन चुका था। अधिकांश महाप्रहर्य कुछ बड़े, प्रभावशाली और धनाढ्य परिवारों से आते थे, क्योंकि इस पद में आने का अवसर अक्सर खरीदना पड़ता था।

सिर्फ महाप्रहर्य का पद ही भ्रष्ट नहीं था, बल्कि प्रमुख आध्यात्मिक नेतृत्व के अधिकांश स्तर उन धनवान अभिजात वर्गों से भरे हुए थे जिनके पास यह पद पाने के लिए संबंध और संपत्ति थी।

यह काइली परिदृश्य यीशु की अपने दिनों के धार्मिक नेताओं के प्रति भावनाओं को और भी स्पष्ट कर देता है। ये धोखेबाज अपने धार्मिक पदों को अपने पिता की सेवा के लिए नहीं रखते थे; वे उन्हें अपने स्वार्थ के लिए रखते थे, मंदिर को एक बाज़ार में बदल देते थे और क़ानून के छोटे-छोटे प्रश्नों पर विवादों के माध्यम से आम लोगों को बंधक बनाकर रखते थे।

अचरज की बात नहीं, ये नेता ऐसे मसीह की खोज में थे जो उनके लक्ष्य, आदर्श और नैतिकताओं के अनुकूल हो, न कि ऐसा जो उन्हें उनके पाखंड, लोभ और स्वार्थी महत्वाकांक्षा के लिए डांटे और फटकारते। उनके जीवनशैली से भविष्यद्वाणी की व्याख्या इतनी मुड़ी और भ्रष्ट हो चुकी थी कि पुनरुत्थान के चमत्कार ने भी उन्हें मसीह की शक्ति को परमेश्वर से आता हुआ स्वीकार करने के लिए मोड़ा नहीं। विजयी सेनानायक की इस गलत अपेक्षा को, जो युद्ध के घोड़े पर सवार होकर इन अभिजात वर्गों के राजनीतिक शत्रुओं पर क़ब्ज़ा कर देगा, आम यहूदी को भी लुभाया गया। मकाबियों और यूनानियों के मामलों की तरह सैकड़ों वर्षों तक पूजा की आज़ादी के लिए लड़ने ने यहूदी जनता के सामूहिक मन पर राष्ट्रवाद की एक गहरी छाप छोड़ी थी। जो लोग सबसे अधिक इस प्रणाली में निवेश कर चुके थे वे वही थे जिन्हें इस विशिष्ट परमेश्वर और उसके वायदों तक विशेष पहुँच से सबसे अधिक लाभ मिलता था। जिन लोगों को यहूदी समाज के कठोर और अक्सर मानवनिर्मित कानूनों ने दमन किया था, उनके लिए शांति और प्रेम के एक ऐसे परमेश्वर का स्वागत अधिक था जो संसार के जरूरतमंदों को अपनी ओर आकर्षित करे, बनिस्बत ऐसे उद्धारकर्ता के जो सिर्फ एक और सांसारिक सरकार स्थापित करे जो गरीबों को राज करे, विधवाओं को दमन करे और दुष्टों को पुरस्कृत करे।

यह आख़िर नहीं था जब दमनित लोग धोखा खाए गए; रोमन शासन ने अपने लोगों की साझा व्याख्याओं में एक और बड़ी चूक देखी। इस बार, यीशु की शिक्षाओं और उनके शिष्यों के शब्दों को चौथी शताब्दी के रोम के बदलते राजनीतिक और धार्मिक परिदृश्य के अनुरूप गलत समझा गया। वर्ष 306 था, और डियोक्लेशियन—जिसने रोमन साम्राज्य में ईसाइयों पर सबसे भयंकर प्रलाप किए थे—ने सीज़र के पद से त्याग दिया था। उनके पीछे तीन सम्राटों के प्रत्याशी बच गए। उन प्रत्याशियों में से एक युवा सेना-नायक था, राजनीति में निपुण और सत्ता के प्रति लालायित। उसका नाम कॉन्स्टेंटाइन था, एक प्रमुख रोमन अधिकारी के पुत्र और एक नीची ग्रीक ईसाई, हेलेना की संतान।

काँन्स्टेन्टाइन ने अपने युवावस्था से ही अपने पिता के पदचिन्हों पर चला, पूरे साम्राज्य में लड़ता रहा और जनरल के रैंक तक पहुंचा। अब, ब्रिटेन में अभियान के बीच उसने रोमन राजनीतिज्ञ का परम लक्ष्य—सीज़र का पद और सम्राट की सिंहासन—की ओर अपना ध्यान लगाया।

काँन्स्टेन्टाइन का सिंहासन तक पहुँच का रास्ता उसके पिता के माध्यम से था। डियोक्लेशियन ने अपने शासनकाल के दौरान सम्राज्य के शासन में सहायता के लिए अतिरिक्त सीज़रों की नियुक्ति की थी। कॉन्स्टेंटाइन के पिता इन में से एक थे, और भले ही उन्हें केवल नियुक्त किया गया था, यह अनुमान था कि सीज़र का उनका दर्जा उनके पुत्र को पारित होगा। परन्तु बातें केवल शीर्षक के स्थानांतरण जितनी सरल नहीं थीं।

काँन्स्टेन्टाइन का उदय रक्तरंजित था, पर उसकी सत्ता पकड़ सेट हो गई, जब तक कि वह सिंहासन के अकेले प्रतिद्वंद्वी न रह गया। मंच तैयार हो गया। उसने शीघ्रता से डियोक्लेशियन के कठोर आदेशों को उलट दिया, ईसाइयत को वैध कर दिया और उस प्रताड़ना को हटा दिया जिसने गिरजाघरों को ध्वस्त किया, परिवारों को बिखेर दिया और बिशपों और अन्य गिरजा नेतृत्व का शिकार किया था। लगभग रातोंरात, इन सताए हुए विश्वासियों को एक ऐसी शांति का उपहार दिया गया जो पहले अनसुनी थी।

काँन्स्टेन्टाइन के किए केवल ईसाइयत को वैध करने तक सीमित नहीं रहे। उसकी सहानुभूतियाँ गहरी थीं, और उसने इसे न केवल स्वीकार्य धर्म बनाकर बल्कि राज्य धर्म के रूप में वैधता प्रदान करने के और कदम उठाए।

प्रभु की वापसी के उत्सुक ईसाइयों के लिए यह लगभग अविश्वसनीय लगा। कुछ ही वर्षों में सरकार ने उन्हें सूली पर चढ़ाने, सिर काटने और यातना देने से उन पर इतना अनुग्रह दिखाया कि उन्होंने उन्हें साम्राज्य के बाकी हिस्सों के लिए आदर्श बना दिया। इस कृपा ने उस स्पष्टता को प्रभावित किया जिससे वे संसार के गिरजे से मेल-मिलाप को देखते थे। वे न केवल साम्राज्य में सत्ता की स्थिति स्वीकार करेंगे, बल्कि काँन्स्टेन्टाइन को गिरजे का रक्षक और समर्थक भी मान लेंगे। उनके विचार में प्रभु का दिन आ गया था, और काँन्स्टेन्टाइन वही लोहे की छड़ी था जिससे परमेश्वर शासन करेगा।

और उसने शासन किया भी। गिरजे का पाठ शीघ्र ही इस नए और बाहरी प्रभाव से प्रभावित हुआ। काँन्स्टेन्टाइन बिशपों की बैठकों में बैठता था, हालांकि उस समय वह बपतिस्मा नहीं लिया था और न ही वह बपतिस्मा मांग रहा था। गिरजे की नई स्थिति, राज्य के एक उपकरण के रूप में, हर मोड़ पर फूट, अंदरूनी लड़ाई और कलह लेकर आई। एक अवशेष बचा रहा, पर गिरजा के अधिकांश लोग ऐसे व्यक्ति के प्रभाव में आ गए जो सत्ता, धन और प्रभाव के भूखे थे।

काँन्स्टेन्टाइन अपनी मृत्यु से पहले बपतिस्मा लेगा, जिससे उसे भटका हुआ गिरजे की आँखों में और भी अधिक विश्वसनीयता मिल गई। अब अपनी असली पहचान से पृथक होकर, आने वाली सदियाँ यह देखने वाली थीं कि “ईसाई” भक्षक भेड़ों में बदल जाएंगे, विनाश, हत्या और भ्रष्टाचार में लिप्त होंगे।

एक अधिक हालिया और अनाबप्तिस्टों से जुड़ी घटना में, कुख्यात मुन्स्टरवादियों की कथा हमें भविष्यद्वाणी की, विशेषकर मसीह की दूसरी आगमन संबंधी भविष्यद्वाणी की, गलत व्याख्या के खतरों का एक और उदाहरण देती है।

एक लंबे समय तक अत्याचार झेलने वाले समूह की एक बड़ी हानि यह होती है कि उनकी स्थिरता की कमी रहती है, जैसा कि आंदोलन के पहले पचास वर्षों में अनाबप्तिस्ट समूहों द्वारा विकसित विविध विश्वासों से स्पष्ट है। उत्पीड़न एक सभासद को उनके नेताओं से वंचित कर देता, जो अक्सर अधिकारियों के लक्षित होने वाले सबसे अधिक उद्देश्य होते थे। एक लापता बड़ों का अर्थ कम शिक्षा था, जो बदले में मार्गदर्शन और सुधारात्मक शिक्षाशास्त्र में कठिनाई लाया। यहां तक कि सबसे ईमानदार और आपस में जुड़े हुए समूह भी ऐसी त्रुटियों में पड़ सकते थे जो बाइबिलीय स्पष्टता लाने और भाईचारे में संतुलन बनाए रखने के लिए नेतृत्व की कमी के कारण विकसित हुईं।

1530 के दशक के निकट होने पर नीदरलैंड में स्थिति काफी अस्थिर थी। पूरे देश में कैथोलिक गिरजा प्रमुख धर्म बना रहा, जो अक्सर अल्पसंख्यक प्रोटेस्टेंट सभाओं के खिलाफ निर्दयता से शारीरिक शक्ति दिखा कर अपनी शक्ति पकड़े रहा। प्रोटेस्टेंट प्रभाव को दबाने पर यह ध्यान कुछ समय के लिए सफल रहा, और उनके अधिकांश समूह विलीन होकर कैथोलिक गिरजे या अन्य समूहों में वापस समा गए।

उन समूहों में से एक जो इस छोटे विस्थापन का शिकार हुआ, वह था प्रारम्भिक डच अनाबप्तिस्ट गिरजा। जो प्रोटेस्टेंट अभी भी कैथोलिकों में शामिल होने से इनकार करते थे, उनके लिए अनाबप्तिस्ट अक्सर उनकी गिरजा का विकल्प बन गए, और उनके रैंकों में तीव्रता से वृद्धि हुई। इसका स्थानीय अनाबप्तिज़्म पर गहरा प्रभाव पड़ा, जो निस्संदेह उत्साही था पर बहुत अराजकता और उथल-पुथल के प्रति प्रवण भी था।

1534 तक नए विश्वासियों के इस प्रवाह से तनाव इतना बढ़ गया कि नीदरलैंड की अनाबप्तिस्ट गिरजा दो मुख्य धाराओं में विभाजित हो गई। पहली, फिलिप्स भाइयों—डिर्क और ओबे—के नेतृत्व में थी और उस पर नए नियम की शिक्षाओं के अनुरूप गिरजा और राज्य से पृथक्करण तथा अहिंसा की पालना थी। यह मेन्नो सिमंस की गिरजा और आज की मेनोनाइट गिरजाओं की जड़ बनी।

दूसरी शाखा अधिक कट्टर विश्वासों पर टिके थी, जिसका नेतृत्व जान माथिस्ज़ और लेइडेन के जान कर रहे थे। इन दोनों पुरुषों का मसीह की वापसी के संबंध में दृष्टिकोण दिन प्रतिदिन अधिक उग्र होता गया, और वे मानने लगे कि वे इस पृथ्वी पर परमेश्वर द्वारा स्थापित किए जाने वाले राज्य में केंद्रीय हस्तियाँ होंगे।

उसी समय सामाजिक अशांति उफन रही थी और यह उत्तरी-पश्चिम जर्मनी के मुन्स्टर शहर में फूट पड़ी, जहां आम जनता ने विद्रोह कर अपने शहर की सरकार को उखाड़ फेंका और अपने कैथोलिक बिशप को निकाल दिया। दोनों जान जल्दी से सक्रिय हुए, शहर के नए नेताओं से संपर्क किया और अंततः उन्हें अपनी दृष् eटियों के अनुकूल कर लिया।

जाने मुन्स्टर में 1534 की शुरुआत में आए और संदेशवाहकों और भविष्यद्वक्ताओं को भेजना शुरू किया, जो सभी “अनाबप्तिस्टों” को इस “नई यरूशलेम” में एकत्र होने की बुलाहट दे रहे थे। क्षेत्र की अशांति ने उनके संदेश को और अधिक आकर्षक बना दिया, और हजारों लोग शहर की ओर उमड़ पड़े, ताकि इस प्रलयंकारी मसीह की वापसी का हिस्सा बन सकें।

वास्तव में, क्षितिज पर एक प्रलयंकारी वापसी थी, परन्तु वह मसीह की वापसी नहीं थी। यह एक निकाले गए कैथोलिक बिशप के रूप में आया, जिसने शीघ्रता से शहर पर घेराबंदी कर दी। उसकी सेना वहाँ अठारह महीनों तक रही।

शहर के भीतर, जान माथिस्ज़ ने घोषणा करते हुए कि उसे शहर की मुक्ति के लिए एक दर्शन दिया गया है, दीवारों से बाहर परेड करने के लिए निकला और शत्रु के शीघ्र नाश की घोषणा की। परन्तु उसका दर्शन उसे धोखा दे गया—वह शीघ्रता से शत्रु के हाथों पकड़ लिया गया, उसे सिर काट दिया गया और उसका सिर मुन्स्टर के द्वार पर एक कांटे पर लटका दिया गया।

दीवारों के भीतर, लेइडेन के जान ने नेतृत्व ग्रहण किया, और वह घेराबंदी की भीषण अकाल, मृत्यु और उथल-पुथल को नजरअंदाज करके बहुविवाह का प्रचार करने लगा, उसे पुराने नियम से बचाने की बहस करता रहा, कम से कम एक महिला को मार डाला जिसने उससे विवाह करने से इनकार किया, और एक बिंदु पर उसके सोलह पत्नियाँ थीं।

यह घृणित कृत्य शीघ्र ही अपने आवश्यक अंत की ओर ले गया जब शहर पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया गया और वहाँ के निवासियों के विरुद्ध भारी नरसंहार किया गया। नेताओं को, जिनमें लेइडेन के जान सबसे प्रमुख थे, पकड़कर यातनाएँ दी गईं और मार डाला गया। उनके शव सेंट लैम्बर्ट्स चर्च की मीनार पर लोहे के पिंजड़ों में लटका दिए गए—मुन्स्टर का कैथोलिक गिरजा। आज भी वे पिंजरे लटके हुए हैं, उन दो जानों के गर्व और जल्दबाज़ी की निराशाजनक याद के रूप में, जिन्होंने अपनी अंतिम-कालीन व्याख्या के पूरा होने के लिए दृढ़ संकल्प दिखाया।

इन तीनों उदाहरणों में, परमेश्वर के वचन में निहित भविष्यद्वाणी ऐसे परिणामों में मोड़ी गई जो उसके बच्चों के लिए परमेश्वर की इच्छाओं से बहुत भटक गए। यहूदियों के लिए, इसने उन्हें मसीह से चूक करवा दिया, उन्हें परमेश्वर द्वारा दिया गया सर्वश्रेष्ठ वादा पहचानने में विफल किया। चौथी शताब्दी के ईसाइयों ने डियोक्लेशियन की भयानक प्रताड़ना के तहत काँन्स्टेन्टाइन को उद्धारक मान लिया, उसे इस संसार की राजधानियों के विरुद्ध परमेश्वर के न्याय के पूरा होने के रूप में देखा। शांति के स्थान पर वे उन धर्मनिरपेक्षों से भी बदतर धर्महीनता में डूब गए, उनके कैथोलिक गिरजे ने पाप में ऐसी गहराई धारण की जो यहाँ तक कि उनके परिवेश के मूर्तिपूजक समाज से भी भयानक थी। अंत में, 16वीं सदी के मुन्स्टरियों के परेशान दर्शन और व्याख्याओं ने उन्हें एक भयानक भाग्य की ओर भेज दिया, जिसने सच्चे गिरजे के नाम को कलंकित कर दिया।

हमें उन लोगों की इन गंभीर गलतियों से क्या सीखनी चाहिए जो हमारे पहले आए? हमारे समय में, अंत निकट प्रतीत होता है, और हम उन लोगों से घिरे हुए हैं जो हमें विश्वास दिलाना चाहते हैं कि हम वास्तव में ईसाइयों के अंतिम वंश हैं।

लूका ने इस बिंदु पर यीशु के निर्देश दर्ज किए हैं: …दिन आएँगे जब तुम मनुष्य-पुत्र के दिनों में से एक को देखने की लालसा करोगे, और तुम उसे न देख पाओगे। और वे तुमसे कहेंगे, ‘यहाँ देखो’; या, ‘वहाँ देखो’; मत जाओ उनके पीछे, और उन्हें मत मानो—लूका 17:22-23। ये अंतिम दिनों में हमारे आचरण के लिए निर्देश हैं। आइए हम अंत के समय के अफवाहों के पीछे न दौड़ें, बल्कि अपने प्रभु की अंतिम उपदेश का पालन करें—कि हम परमेश्वर के वचन और उसके पुत्र यीशु के सुसमाचार को सारी दुनिया में फैलाएँ … और तब अंत आएगा—मत्ती 24:14।

Jesus, upon His ascension back into His heavenly home, gave a final directive to His disciples, both to those physically present as He disappeared into the clouds, and to the myriad of believers who would come to know Him down through the ages. The story of His life and His gospel were to be preached unto all the world by those who called Him Lord. This global spreading of the Word, would, in the later vision of John, be proclaimed as one of the prerequisites of Jesus’ triumphant return at the end of time. John himself would be seen as a harbinger of these end times, based on Jesus’ words as recorded by John … If I will that he [John] tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. John 21:22.

The early Christians, understandably, felt that the return of Christ was imminent, even within the first century. The rapid expansion of Christianity, the complete moral depravity of the Roman culture, and the increasing intensity of persecution against them seemed to point to a swift and triumphant return of their Lord.

Now, two thousand years since Christ gave that promise, His soon return seems just as imminent as it did to the first century believers. Speculation on the time of His return, the manner of it, and the contributing factors are always current and controversial subjects. In the light of this continued earnest expectation of the end times, what have we to learn about our interpretations of prophecy from those who have attempted to decipher the prophetic portions of Scripture in earlier ages?

Jesus' first coming was surrounded and enveloped by perhaps the most recognizable misinterpretation of prophecy in the Bible. Roughly four hundred years of relative silence from God precluded His entry into the world in a physical, human body. His birth would be unnoticed in a society that was not only in desperate need of, but also expecting, a Savior to arrive. Daniel, writing the words God gave him, had told of a Messiah to come, and had even given a time that He would appear. Now, the Jews seethed under Roman rule, hanging their hopes on what they thought would be a sudden and triumphant extermination of the Roman troops and influence from their lands. To us, it is glaringly obvious that their interpretation of prophecy was not only incorrect, but for many, would lead them astray so that they did not even recognize or acknowledge the true Redeemer that was sent to them.

But what was it that caused this misinterpreted view? To us, it seems completely in order that Jesus would focus on the poor and destitute rather than opposing an occupying army. Jewish historians give an intriguing, but scarcely surprising, answer to the failure of the majority of their people to recognize Christ for who He was.

The religious atmosphere of first century Israel was one defined by corruption, bribery, lust for power, and all the unsavory aspects of a completely politically motivated upper class.

The priests, once chosen by God to be His servants in sanctifying His children, had sunk to buying their positions of service, most notably in the high priest’s office, where God had ordained one high priest to serve the people throughout his life. In Jesus’ day, however, the responsibilities of leading the children of Israel were divvied out, the role often changing hands on one-year terms. Becoming a high priest was a matter of birth. Most high priests came from several large, influential, and wealthy families, as one often had to buy into the opportunity of this office.

It was not only the high priest’s office that was corrupted, but most levels of prominent spiritual leadership were filled by the wealthy elites who had the connections and wealth to be placed into roles of importance amongst the Jews.

This unsavory backdrop gives even more clarity to Jesus’ feelings on the religious leaders of His day. These imposters did not hold their priestly positions to serve His Father, they held them for their own gain, turning the temple into a marketplace and holding the common people hostage through their disputes on the minutiae of the Law.

Unsurprisingly, these leaders looked for a Messiah who would fit their goals, their ideals, and their morals, rather than one that would rebuke and chastise them for their hypocrisy, greed, and selfish ambition. Their view of prophecy had been so twisted and corrupted by their lifestyle that even the miracle of a resurrection could not sway them to view Christ’s power as coming from God. This misconstrued expectation of a conquering commander, riding a horse of war over the political enemies of these elites was pandered to the common Jew as well. Centuries of fighting for just the freedom to worship, as in the case of the Maccabees and the Greeks, had deeply imprinted a sense of nationalism into the collective mind of the Jewish people. The ones who bought into it the most were the ones who received the most from this system of exclusive access to God and His promises. To those who were repressed by the stringent and often man-made laws of Jewish society, a God of peace and love who would draw the needy of the world to Him was more welcome than a Saviour who would simply install another earthly government to rule the poor, oppress the widows, and reward the wicked.

This was not the last time an oppressed people would be deceived, as Roman rule would witness another major misstep in the collective interpretations of God’s people. This time, the teachings of Jesus and the words of His disciples would be misinterpreted to fit the changing political and religious landscape of fourth century Rome. The year was 306, and Diocletian, one of the most brutal persecutors of Christians in the Roman Empire, had abdicated from his position as Caesar. In his wake, he left three contenders for his throne. One of those vying for the seat of power was a young general, experienced in politics, and power hungry. His name was Constantine, son of a prominent Roman officer and a lowly Greek Christian, Helena.

From his youth, Constantine followed in his father’s footsteps, fighting throughout the empire, rising to a rank of general. Now, on campaign in Britain, he turned his eyes to the ultimate prize of a Roman politico, the title of Caesar, and the seat of the emperor.

Constantine’s line to the throne was through his father. Diocletian had, during his rule, appointed additional Caesars to aid in ruling the empire. Constantine’s father was one of these, and despite being simply appointed to the position, it was expected that his status as a Caesar would pass to his son. Matters were not as simple as a mere transfer of titles, however.

Constantine’s rise was bloody, but his grip on power was set, until he remained the sole contender for the throne. The stage was set. He quickly undid the harsh decrees of Diocletian, legalizing Christianity and removing the persecution that had leveled churches, scattered families, and hunted down bishops and other church leadership. Almost overnight, a peace previously unheard of was gifted to these hounded believers.

The changes that Constantine made did not end, however, with merely legalizing Christianity. His sympathies ran deeper, and he made further moves to legitimize it as not only an accepted religion, but as the state religion.

To Christians eager for the return of Christ, this seemed almost unbelievable. In the span of a few short years the government had gone from crucifying, beheading, and torturing them to holding them up as examples to the rest of the empire. The favor seems to have affected the clarity with which they viewed the apparent reconciliation of the world to the church. Not only would they accept a position of power in the empire, but they would also accept Constantine as a benefactor and protector of the church itself. In their minds, the day of the Lord was come, and Constantine was the rod of iron with which God would rule.

And rule he did. The course of the church was soon swayed by this new and outside influence. Constantine sat in on meetings of the bishops, even though at the time he was not baptized nor was he even seeking baptism. The church’s new position as a tool of the state brought schisms, in-fighting, and contention at every turn. There remained a remnant, but most of the church would fall under the sway of a man motivated by a hunger for power, wealth, and influence.

Constantine would be baptized before his death, lending him even further credibility in the eyes of a straying church. Now separated from its original identity as sheep in this world, the coming centuries would see “Christians” become ravening wolves, destroying, killing, and corrupting.

In a matter more recently related to us as Anabaptists, the tale of the infamous Muensterites gives us a further example of the perils of misinterpreting prophecy, especially the prophecy regarding the second coming of Christ.

One of the great disadvantages of a heavily persecuted group is a tendency to lack stability, as evidenced by the varying beliefs developed by Anabaptist groups of the movement's first fifty years. Persecution would deprive a congregation of their leaders, who were often those most targeted by the authorities. A missing elder meant less teaching, which in turn led to more difficulty in guidance, and corrective doctrine. Even the most sincere and interconnected groups could fall into errors developed because of the lack of leadership to bring Biblical clarity and balance the brotherhood.

The situation in the Netherlands was of a rather volatile strain approaching the 1530s. Throughout the country, the Catholic Church remained the predominant religion, clinging to their power through ruthless displays of physical force, most often directed towards the minority Protestant congregations. This focus on quelling the Protestant influence was momentarily successful in this instance, with most of their groups dissolving and reintegrating into the Catholic Church or other groups.

One of the groups that was on the receiving end of this minor diaspora was the fledging Dutch Anabaptist church. For those Protestants who still refused to join the Catholics, the Anabaptists often became their choice of church, rapidly swelling their ranks. This had a profound effect on the local strain of Anabaptism, which without a doubt was fervent, but quite prone to chaos and upheaval.

By 1534 the tensions of this influx of new believers reached a breaking point, and the Anabaptist church of the Netherlands split into two main factions. The first, led by the two Philips brothers, Dirk and Obbe, adhered to the New Testament teachings of separation from church and state, as well as nonresistance. This would be the church of Menno Simmons, and the root of the Mennonite churches of today.

The other faction held to more radical beliefs, led by Jan Matthysz and Jan of Leiden. These two men became increasingly fanatical in their views of Christ’s return, believing that they would be central figures, instrumental in a kingdom that God would set up on Earth.

At the same time, social unrest was brewing, and spilled over in the city of Munster, located in northwest Germany, where the common people rose up, overthrowing their city’s government and expelling their Catholic bishop. The two Jans were quick to act, contacting the new leaders of the city, and eventually winning them over to their views.

The Jans moved to Munser in early 1534, and began sending out prophets and messengers, who called all “Anabaptists” to congregate at this “New Jerusalem”. The unrest of the area made their message all the more appealing, and thousands streamed into the city, intent in being part of this apocalyptic return of Christ.

There was, in fact, an apocalyptic return on the horizon, but not a return of Christ. This one came in the form of the ousted Catholic bishop, who swiftly set siege to the city. His army would stay there for eighteen months.

Inside the city, Jan Matthysz, proclaiming a vision was given to him for a deliverance of the city, left its walls to parade outside, proclaiming a swift delivery of the enemy into his hands. His vision, however, failed him, as he was swiftly delivered into the hands of the enemy, where he was beheaded, and his head set on a pike in front Munster’s gates.

Inside the walls, Jan of Leiden took leadership, ignoring the famine, death, and chaos that now ran rampant within the besieged walls. Instead, he began promoting polygamy, defending it from the Old Testament, killing at least one woman who refused to marry him, and at one point, having sixteen wives.

This abomination soon led to its required end as the city was overcome, with a heavy slaughter being carried out against its inhabitants. The leaders, Jan of Leiden being the most prominent, were captured, tortured, and killed. Their bodies were hung in iron cages on the tower of St. Lamberts Church, the Catholic church in Munster. To this day, the cages still hang, a bleak reminder of the pride and rashness of the two Jans, determined to see their end-time interpretation fulfilled.

In all three of these examples, the prophecy contained in God’s Word was twisted into results that strayed far from the will of God for His children. For the Jews, it caused them to miss the Messiah, failing to recognize the greatest promise God had given them. The fourth century Christians, chafing under the horrific persecution of Diocletian, accepted Constantine as a deliverer, seeing him as a fulfillment of God’s judgement against the kingdoms of this world. Instead of peace, they would sink into a state of ungodliness worse than the pagans around them, with the Catholic Church straying into sin more horrible than even their pagan society. Lastly, the troubled visions and interpretations of the 16th century Munsterites would lead them to an awful fate, sullying the name of the true church.

What have we to learn from these grave errors of those before us? In our time, the end seems imminent, and we are beset with those who would have us believe that we are truly the last of the Christians.

Luke has recorded the instructions of Jesus on this point: …The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them –Luke 17: 22-23. Here are instructions for our conduct in the last days. Let us not be running after the rumors of the end times but let us be obedient to the final admonition of our Lord—that we spread the Word of God and the Gospel of His Son, Jesus throughout the world … and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:14.

عند صعوده عائداً إلى موطنه السماوي، منح يسوع توجيهاً نهائياً لتلاميذه، سواء لأولئك الحاضرين جسدياً حين اختفى في السحب، وللجمع الغفير من المؤمنين الذين سيعرفونه عبر العصور. كان يُؤمر أن يُبشَّر بقصة حياته وإنجيله في جميع أنحاء العالم على يد الذين يدعونَهُ ربّاً. هذا الانتشار العالمي للكلمة، كما سيُعلَن في رؤية يوحنا اللاحقة، كان أحد الشروط المسبقة لعودة يسوع المنتصرة في نهاية الزمن. وسيُنظر إلى يوحنا نفسه كنبَذَةٍ لتلك الأيام الأخيرة، استناداً إلى كلمات يسوع المسجلة على لسان يوحنا … فَإِنْ شِئْتُ أَنَّهُ يَبْقَى إِلَى مَجِيئِي، فَمَا لَكَ؟ اتَّبِعْ أَنَا. يوحنا 21:22.

شعر المسيحيون الأوائل، ومن البديهي، أن عودة المسيح وشيكة، حتى في القرن الأول. بدا أن الانتشار السريع للمسيحية، والانحلال الأخلاقي التام في الثقافة الرومانية، وتصاعد الاضطهاد ضدهم كلها تشير إلى عودة سريعة ومنتصرة لربهم.

الآن، بعد ألفي عام منذ أن أعطى المسيح ذلك الوعد، تبدو عودته القريبة بنفس الوضوح الذي كان لدى المؤمنين في القرن الأول. التكهن بزمان عودته، وطريقة حدوثها، والعوامل المساهمة فيها كلها مواضيع دائمة الجدل والحالية. في ضوء هذا التوقع الجاد المستمر لأيام النهاية، ماذا نتعلم عن تفسيراتنا للنبوءة من الذين حاولوا فك شيفرات الأجزاء النبوية من الكتاب المقدس في العصور السابقة؟

جاء مجيء يسوع الأول محاطاً وربما مغلفاً بأكثر سوء تفسير للنبوءة شهرة في الكتاب المقدس. حُجبت نحو أربعمائة سنة من الصمت النسبي من الله قبل دخوله إلى العالم في جسد بشري. ولِمولده لم يكن لفتٌ للانتباه في مجتمع كان بأمس الحاجة إلى مخلص، وكان يتوقع أيضاً قدوم مخلص. لقد أخبر دانيال، كاتب الكلمات التي أعطاها الله له، عن مسيح قادم، وحتى أعطى وقتاً يظهر فيه. الآن، كان اليهود يغلي تحت الحكم الروماني، معلقين آمالهم على ما ظنوا أنه إبادة مفاجئة ومنتصرة لقوات الرومان ونفوذهم من أرضهم. بالنسبة لنا، من الواضح جلياً أن تفسيرهم للنبوءة لم يكن خاطئاً فحسب، بل سيقود كثيرين منهم إلى الضلال بحيث لم يعترفوا حتى بالمخلص الحقيقي الذي أُرسل إليهم.

لكن ما الذي تسبب في هذا الفهم الخاطئ؟ يبدو لنا من الطبيعي أن يركّز يسوع على الفقراء والمحتاجين بدل مواجهة جيش محتّل. يقدم المؤرخون اليهود إجابة مثيرة للاهتمام، وإن لم تكن مفاجئة إلى حد كبير، لفشل غالبية شعبهم في التعرف على المسيح على حقيقته.

كان الجو الديني في إسرائيل القرن الأول مُعرَّفاً بالفساد والرِشوة والشهوة للسلطة، وكل الجوانب الكريهة لطبقة عليا محركها سياسي بحت.

لقد نزل الكهنة، الذين اختارهم الله ذات يوم ليكونوا خدامه في تقديس شعبه، إلى درجة شراء مناصب خدمتهم، لا سيما في منصب الكاهن الأعظم، حيث كان الله قد أمر بكاهن أعظم واحد ليخدم الشعب طوال حياته. في أيام يسوع، ومع ذلك، كانت مسؤوليات قيادة أبناء إسرائيل تُقسَّم، وغالباً ما تتغير الوظيفة بسنةٍ تلو الأخرى. أصبح أن تكون كاهناً أعظم مسألة ولادة. جاء معظم الكهنة العظماء من عدة عائلات كبيرة و ذات نفوذ وثروة، إذ كان على المرء غالباً أن يشتري فرصة هذا المنصب.

لم يقتصر الفساد على مكتب الكاهن الأعظم فحسب، بل امتلأت معظم مستويات القيادة الروحية البارزة بالنخب الثرية التي كانت تملك الاتصالات والثروة لتُعين في أدوارٍ ذات أهمية بين اليهود.

تمنح هذه الخلفية البشعة مزيداً من الوضوح لمشاعر يسوع تجاه قادة دينه في زمنه. هؤلاء المحتالون لم يحملوا مناصبهم الكهنوتية لخدمة أبيه، بل احتفظوا بها لمصلحة أنفسهم، محولين الهيكل إلى سوق وممسكين بالشعب العادي رهينة عبر نزاعاتهم حول تفاصيل دقيقة من الناموس.

ليس من المستغرب أن هؤلاء القادة كانوا يتطلعون إلى مسيح يتناسب مع أهدافهم ومثلهم وأخلاقهم، بدلاً من واحد يوبّخهم ويعاقبهم على نفاقهم وطمعهم وطموحهم الأناني. لقد شُوّهت نظرتهم للنبوءة وأُفسدت بأسلوب حياتهم لدرجة أن حتى معجزة قيامة لم تَقُدهم إلى رؤية قوة المسيح كمصدرها الله. كان هذا التوقع المغلوط لقائد منتصر، يركب فرس حرب يحمل على الأعداء السياسيين لهؤلاء النخب، مُرضياً أيضاً بالنسبة لليهود العاديين. فقد ختمت قرون النضال من أجل مجرد حرية العبادة، كما في حالة المكابيين واليونانيين، إحساساً قوياً بالوطنية في العقل الجمعي للشعب اليهودي. أولئك الذين تمسّكوا بهذا الاعتقاد أكثر هم أنفسهم الذين استفادوا أكثر من نظام الوصول الحصري إلى الله ووعوده. بالنسبة للمقهورين من قوانين المجتمع اليهودي الصارمة وغالباً المصنوعة بيد البشر، كان إله سلام ومحبة يجذب إليه المحتاجين في العالم مفضلين عن مخلص يركّب ببساطة حكومة أرضية أخرى تحكم الفقراء، وتظلم الأرامل، وتكافئ الأشرار.

لم تكن هذه آخر مرة خُدع فيها شعب مضطهد، كما شهد الحكم الروماني بعد ذلك زلة كبيرة أخرى في تفسيرات شعب الله. في هذه المرة، سُوِّغت تعاليم يسوع وكلمات تلاميذه لتتلاءم مع المشهد السياسي والديني المتغيّر في روما القرن الرابع. كان العام 306، وقد تتخلّى دقلديانوس، أحد أقسى مضطهدي المسيحيين في الإمبراطورية الرومانية، عن منصبه كقيصر. في أعقابه، ترك ثلاثة متنافسين على عرشه. أحد هؤلاء الطامعين في المقعد كان جنرالاً شابًا، ذو خبرة في السياسة وجائعًا للسلطة. كان اسمه قسطنطين، ابن ضابط روماني بارز وامرأة يونانية مسيحية بسيطة، هيلانة.

منذ شبابه سار قسطنطين على خطى والده، يقاتل في أنحاء الإمبراطورية، ويرتقي إلى رتبة جنرال. والآن، وهو في حملة في بريطانيا، وجه نظره إلى الجائزة القصوى للسياسي الروماني، لقب قيصر، ومقعد الإمبراطور.

كان طريق قسطنطين إلى العرش عبر والده. فقد عيّن دقلديانوس خلال حكمه قيصرات إضافيين لمساعدة في حكم الإمبراطورية. كان والد قسطنطين أحد هؤلاء، وعلى الرغم من كونه معيناً فقط في المنصب، كان متوقعاً أن تنتقل مرتبته كقيصر إلى ابنه. لم تكن الأمور بسيطة كما لو كانت مجرد نقل ألقاب، مع ذلك.

كانت صعود قسطنطين دموية، لكن قبضته على السلطة رسخت، حتى لم يبقَ منافس على العرش. تهيأت الساحة. سرعان ما ألغى الأوامر القاسية لدقلديانوس، مرخّصاً بالمسيحية وغانياً الاضطهاد الذي دمَّر الكنائس، وشَّت العوائل، وطارد الأساقفة وغيرهم من قيادات الكنيسة. كأنما بين عشية وضحاها أُعطي هؤلاء المؤمنين المطاردين سلام لم يعهدوه من قبل.

لم تتوقف التغييرات التي أجراها قسطنطين عند مجرد تقنين المسيحية. فقد كانت تعاطفه أعمق، فقام بمزيد من الخطوات لإضفاء الشرعية عليها ليس فقط كدين مقبول، بل كدين الدولة.

بالنسبة للمسيحيين المتلهفين لعودة المسيح، بدا هذا الأمر شبه لا يُصدَّق. ففي غضون سنوات قليلة تحول وضع الحكومة من صلب وقطع رؤوس وتعذيب لهم إلى أن تُعرض عليهم أمثلة يحتذى بها في سائر الإمبراطورية. بدا أن النعمة قد أثرت في وضوح رؤيتهم لمظاهر مصالح العالم مع الكنيسة. لم يكتفوا بقبول موضع قوة في الإمبراطورية، بل قبلوا أيضاً قسطنطين كمانح للنعمة وحام للكنيسة نفسها. في أذهانهم، قد حل يوم الرب، وكان قسطنطين عود الحديد التي سيحكم بها الله.

وحكَم بالفعل. سرعان ما تأثر مسار الكنيسة بهذا التأثير الجديد والخارجي. جلس قسطنطين في اجتماعات الأساقفة، رغم أنه في ذلك الوقت لم يكن قد اعتمد ولا كان يسعى للمعمودية. جلب موقع الكنيسة الجديد كأداة للدولة انقسامات وصراعات ونزاعات في كل منعطف. بقي بقايا، لكن معظم الكنيسة سيخضع لتأثير رجل دافعته شهية للسلطة والثروة والنفوذ.

سيعتمد قسطنطين قبل موته، مما منحه مزيداً من المصداقية في أعين كنيسة تَحَيَّرَت. الآن، منفصلة عن هويتها الأصلية كخراف في هذا العالم، ستشهد القرون اللاحقة تحول "المسيحيين" إلى ذئاب منكوبة، مدمرة، قاتلة، وفاسدة.

في شأن ذي صلة أحدث ترويه لنا كأنابابتستيين، تعطينا حكاية المنستريين الشهيرة مثالاً آخر على مخاطر تفسير النبوءة خطأ، خاصة نبوءة عودة المسيح الثانية.

أحد الأعطاب الكبيرة لجماعة مُضطهدة بشدة هو الميل إلى افتقار الاستقرار، كما يتضح من المعتقدات المتباينة التي طورتها مجموعات الأنابابتست خلال الخمسين سنة الأولى للحركة. كان الاضطهاد يحرم الجماعة من قادتها، الذين غالباً ما كانوا أكثر المستهدفين من السلطات. غياب شيخ يعني نقص التعليم، مما يؤدي بدوره إلى صعوبات أكبر في التوجيه والعقيدة التصحيحية. حتى الجماعات الأكثر إخلاصاً وترابطاً قد تسقط في أخطاء تطورت بسبب غياب القيادة التي تجلب الوضوح الكتابي وتوازن الأخوة.

كان الوضع في هولندا متقلباً إلى حد كبير مع اقتراب الثلاثينيات من القرن السادس عشر. في أنحاء البلاد بقيت الكنيسة الكاثوليكية الدين السائد، متشبثة بسلطتها عبر عروض قمعية وحشية غالباً ما كانت موجهة ضد جماعات البروتستانت الأقلية. كان هذا التركيز على قمع التأثير البروتستانتي ناجحاً مؤقتاً في هذه الحال، مع ذوبان معظم مجموعاتهم وإعادة دمجهم في الكنيسة الكاثوليكية أو مجموعات أخرى.

إحدى المجموعات التي كانت على طرف هذا التشرد الصغير كانت كنيسة الأنابابتست الهولندية الناشئة. بالنسبة لأولئك البروتستانت الذين رفضوا الانضمام إلى الكاثوليك، غالباً ما أصبحت الأنابابتست خيارهم الكنسي، ما ولَّد تضخماً سريعاً في صفوفهم. كان لهذا تأثير عميق على التيار المحلي للأنابابتست، الذي بلا شك كان حارًّا، لكنه عرضة للفوضى والانقلابات.

بحلول عام 1534 بلغ التوتر نتيجة هذا التدفق من المؤمنين الجدد نقطة الانهيار، فانقسمت الكنيسة الأنابابتستية في هولندا إلى فصيلين رئيسيين. الأول، بقيادة الأخوين فيليبس، ديرك وأوبي، تمسّك بتعاليم العهد الجديد عن الانفصال بين الكنيسة والدولة، وعن عدم المقاومة. كانت هذه كنيسة مينو سيمونز وجذر الكنائس المينونية اليوم.

الفصيل الآخر تشبث بمعتقدات أكثر تطرفاً، بقيادة يان ماثيز ويان ليدن. أصبح هذان الرجلان متعصبين بشكل متزايد في آرائهما حول عودة المسيح، معتقدين أنهما سيكونان شخصيتين محوريّتين، ومؤثرين في مملكة سيقيمها الله على الأرض.

في الوقت نفسه كان التوتر الاجتماعي يتصاعد، وانفجر في مدينة مونستر الواقعة في شمال غربي ألمانيا، حيث ثار الشعب العادي، وأطاح بحكومة مدينتهم وطرد أسقفهم الكاثوليكي. تحرك الاثنان يان بسرعة، فاتصلا بقادة المدينة الجدد، وفازا بهم في نهاية المطاف على آرائهما.

انتقل الاثنان يان إلى مونستر في أوائل عام 1534، وبدآ بإرسال أنبياء ورسُل، دعوا فيها جميع "الأنابابتست" للتجمّع في هذه "أورشليم الجديدة". زاد اضطراب المنطقة من جاذبية رسالتهما، وتدفّق الآلاف إلى المدينة، عازمين على أن يكونوا جزءاً من هذا الارتداد الأبوكاليپي لعودة المسيح.

في الواقع كان هناك عودة نهايةٍ وشيكة، لكنها لم تكن لعودة المسيح. جاءت هذه العودة على شكل الأسقف الكاثوليكي المطرود، الذي نَصَبَ الحصار على المدينة بسرعة. بقي جيشه هناك ثمانية عشر شهراً.

داخل المدينة أعلن يان ماثيز عن رؤية أُعطيت له لمُنجاة المدينة، وخرج من أسوارها ليتجول خارجها معلناً الانتصار السريع للعدو بين يديه. ومع ذلك خانته رؤياه، إذ سُلم إلى أيدي العدو بسرعة، حيث ذُبِح وقطعت رأسه، ووُضِعت رأسه على رمح أمام بوابات مونستر.

داخل الأسوار تزعّم يان ليدن القيادة، متجاهلاً المجاعة والموت والفوضى التي اجتاحت الآن داخل الجدران المحاصرة. بل بدأ يروّج للتعدد الزوجي، مدافعاً عنه بالنظر إلى العهد القديم، وقتل على الأقل امرأة رفضت الزواج به، وفي مرحلة كان له ست عشرة زوجة.

قاد هذا التجديف سريعاً إلى نهايته الحتمية حين غُلِبَت المدينة، ونُفِّذَت مذبحة هائلة ضد سكانها. اُعتُقِل القادة، وكان يان ليدن الأبرز بينهم، وعُذِّبوا وقُتلوا. عُلِّقت جثثهم في أقفاص حديدية على برج كنيسة سانت لامبرت، الكنيسة الكاثوليكية في مونستر. ولا تزال تلك الأقفاص معلقة حتى اليوم، تذكاراً قاتماً لغطرسة وتهور الاثنين يان، المصممين على تحقيق تفسيرهما لأيام النهاية.

في كلٍ من هذه الأمثلة الثلاثة، حُوِّلت النبوءة الواردة في كلمة الله إلى نتائج تباعدت كثيراً عن مشيئة الله لأبناءه. بالنسبة لليهود، سبّب ذلك أن يفقدوا المسيح، عجزوا عن التعرف على أعظم وعد أعطاه الله لهم. المسيحيون في القرن الرابع، المتأوّهون تحت وطأة اضطهاد دقلديانوس الرهيب، قبلوا قسطنطين كمُخلِّص، ورأوه تحقيقاً لحكم الله على ممالك هذا العالم. وبدلاً من السلام، غرِقوا في حالة من فساد أعظم من الوثنيين من حولهم، مع انحراف الكنيسة الكاثوليكية إلى خطايا أشد فظاعة حتى من مجتمعهم الوثني. أخيراً، أدت الرؤى المضطربة وتفسيرات منستريين في القرن السادس عشر إلى نهايات مروعة، لَطَّخت اسم الكنيسة الحقيقية.

ماذا نتعلّم من هذه الأخطاء الجسيمة لمن سبقونا؟ في زماننا يبدو الأمر وشيكاً، ونُحاط بمن يدعون أننا حقاً آخر المسيحيين.

سجّل لوقا تعليمات يسوع في هذا الشأن: …تَاْتِي أَيَّامٌ تَتَمَنُّونَ أَنْ تَرَوْا فِيهَا يَوْماً مِنْ أَيَّامِ ابْنِ الإِنْسَانِ، وَلَكِنَّكُمْ لاَ تَرَوْنَهُ. وَيَقُولُونَ لَكُمْ: اُنْظُرُوا ههُنَا، أَوْ اُنْظُرُوا هُنَاكَ. لاَ تَتَّبِعُوهُمْ وَلاَ تَجْرُوا وَرَاءَهُمْ. – لوقا 17:22-23. ها هي تعليمات لسلوكنا في الأيام الأخيرة. فلنَكُنْ لا نركض وراء إشاعات نهاية الأزمنة بل لنكن مطيعين للتوبيخ النهائي لربنا—أن ننشر كلمة الله وإنجيل ابنه يسوع في جميع أنحاء العالم … ثُمَّ يَأْتِي النِّهَايةُ. – متى 24:14.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

Porque el marido incrédulo es santificado por la mujer, y la mujer incrédula es santificada por el marido: de otra manera vuestros hijos serían inmundos; pero ahora son santos … Porque, ¿qué sabes tú, oh mujer, si salvarás a tu marido? ¿o cómo sabes tú, oh hombre, si salvarás a tu mujer? –1 Corintios 7:14-16.

Al contemplar el conjunto de hogares que nos rodean, nos entristecemos al ver una tragedia cristiana tras otra. Casi todo cristiano tiene algún pariente cercano que ha pasado por un divorcio, un hijo rebelde o relaciones matrimoniales tensas. Quizá clamamos a Dios preguntándonos por qué es así, pues ciertamente no es Su plan. Aquí vemos al apóstol Pablo exponiendo un principio asombroso que se entiende poco y se aplica menos: un hogar santificado. Es lo que todo creyente sincero desea y busca, pero pocos comprenden. El cristianismo no es un sello automático que clona a la prole en el mismo molde. Aun así la Escritura debe ser verdad y debe haber, en efecto, un efecto santificador que un verdadero creyente aporta al hogar. Esto no garantiza que el cónyuge incrédulo o los hijos de la unión sean salvos, pero cuando un marido o una mujer creyente actúa de acuerdo con la Escritura y el Espíritu de Dios, el efecto que tienen en el hogar permitirá que el poder de Dios sea evidente y se derrame una vía de gracia en el camino de todos los que habitan en él.

Nuestra impotencia no se debe a la falta del poder de Dios, sino a que nuestra entendimiento tenue está infestado e infiltrado por las influencias de este mundo presente. La fe en Dios solamente es inevitablemente una fuerza poderosa, mientras que la fe inyectada por razonamientos humanos e impaciencia difícilmente resultará más efectiva que los intentos de Abraham y Agar por producir un hijo santo y santificado.

¿Qué, pues, santifica el hogar? La observación casual notará que simplemente ser creyente no es suficiente para lograrlo. Santificar es hacer puro y santo. Es un proceso de filtrado y una separación de aquello que es impuro para traer mayor pureza al objeto santificado. Los fariseos comprendían bien el principio. Pasaban muchas horas rigurosas atendiendo a incontables detalles minúsculos para hacer santos sus vasos. Aun así, fracasaron de manera crítica.

¡Ay de vosotros, escribas y fariseos, hipócritas! porque limpiáis lo de fuera de la copa y del plato, mas por dentro estáis llenos de rapacidad y de desenfreno. ¡Fariseo ciego! limpia primero lo de dentro de la copa y del plato, para que también lo de fuera sea limpio –Mateo 23:25-26.

Lo interior santificado por la fe y la oración

Qué necio sería que un hombre lavase solo el exterior de una copa, que es lo que se mira, y dejase su interior sucio, que es lo que se usa. Y, sin embargo, hay quienes evitan únicamente los pecados escandalosos —aquellos que arruinarían su reputación ante los hombres— pero se permiten orgullo y decadencia moral en el corazón. Esto los hace aborrecibles para el Dios puro y santo. Así sucede cuando un hombre o una mujer busca purificar su hogar mediante limpiezas superficiales. Los intentos farisaicos de arrancar y eliminar los detalles superficiales e incoherencias de la vida de su cónyuge y de sus hijos, con el fin de santificarlos, suelen ser infructuosos.

Por agudeza que tengan en otras cosas, Cristo los llama ciegos. A la estimación de Cristo, los que no conocen la maldad de sus propios corazones —los que no ven, ni aborrecen, el pecado secreto que está alojado dentro— son extraños a la santificación. La ignorancia de uno mismo es la ignorancia más vergonzosa y dañina. La regla es: “Limpia primero lo que está dentro, para ser limpiado de la inmundicia del espíritu.” Los afecciones e inclinaciones corruptas, las lujurias secretas que acechan en el alma, no vistas ni observadas, deben ser primero reconocidas, mortificadas y sujetadas. Si se cuida debidamente eso, lo externo, por extensión, también quedará limpio. Motivos e incentivos externos pueden mantener lo de fuera limpio mientras lo de dentro permanece sucio; pero si la gracia santificadora renovada limpia lo interior, eso tendrá una influencia duradera y profunda sobre lo exterior, porque el principio dominante está dentro. Si el corazón está bien guardado, todo está bien, …porque de él brotan los manantiales de la vida –Proverbios 4:23.

Asimismo vosotras, mujeres, estad sujetas a vuestros maridos; para que, los que no creen a la palabra, sean ganados sin palabra por la conducta de las mujeres; considerando vuestra conducta casta juntamente con temor. Porque el adorno de vosotras no sea el externo de peinarse, y de adornos de oro, ni de vestidos lujosos; sino el hombre interno del corazón, en lo incorruptible, el de un espíritu afable y apacible, que es de grande estima delante de Dios. Porque así se adornaban también en otro tiempo las santas mujeres que esperaban en Dios, estando sujetas a sus maridos: como Sara obedecía a Abraham, llamándole señor; de la cual vosotras sois hijas, si hacéis bien y no teméis ninguna amenaza. Vosotros, maridos, igualmente, vivid con ellas sabiamente, dando honor a la mujer como a vaso más frágil, y como coherederas de la gracia de la vida; para que vuestras oraciones no sean estorbadas –1 Pedro 3:1-7.

Aquí Pedro habla de una esposa que gana a su marido con la benevolencia debida mencionada en Corintios. Aunque ella no tiene garantía incondicional de santificar a su marido, ciertamente tendrá escaso éxito sin ello. Eunice era una judía que, al abrazar la fe en Cristo, se encontró en un yugo desigual con un griego. Leemos que la fe sincera fue primeramente obrada en su madre Loida, y eso afectó a Eunice. Esto, a su vez, tuvo un efecto santificador sobre el joven Timoteo, quien fue entonces preparado para la obra del Señor. No tenemos registro de que su padre se agregase a la fe, pero puede imaginarse la lucha inicial en el pecho de esta joven judía mientras honraba reverentemente a su cabeza y no circuncidaba a su hijo sino que más bien lo encomendó a la oración. Aquí nos lleva a la otra dimensión vital de la santificación del hogar. Aunque ella no se atrevió a enseñar a su marido, aparentemente había ganado su respeto lo suficiente como para poder instruir a su hijo en el hogar. Esto lo hizo diligentemente… Porque es santificado por la palabra de Dios y por la oración –1 Timoteo 4:5.

Y que desde la niñez has sabido las Sagradas Escrituras, que te pueden hacer sabio para la salvación por la fe que es en Cristo Jesús. Toda la Escritura es inspirada por Dios, y útil para enseñar, para redargüir, para corregir, para instruir en justicia –2 Timoteo 3:15-16.

Lo exterior santificado por la Palabra

Cuando primero se trata el corazón del creyente, las dimensiones visibles del hogar encajan en su debido orden. Las influencias mundanas tienen poco atractivo para el niño de Dios en ciernes. La Palabra de Dios debe ocupar su pleno lugar siendo administrada a los hijos así como a los adultos, pues es útil para la santificación. Un marido debe lavar a su mujer y a sus hijos (así como a sí mismo) administrando la Palabra de Dios para que pueda santificar y limpiar su hogar.

Maridos, amad a vuestras mujeres, así como Cristo amó a la iglesia, y se entregó a sí mismo por ella; para santificarla y limpiarla en el lavamiento del agua por la palabra; para presentársela a sí mismo una iglesia gloriosa, que no tuviera mancha ni arruga ni cosa semejante; sino que fuera santa y sin mancha –Efesios 5:25-27.

Cuando la Palabra de Dios recibe plena autoridad en el hogar, se convierte en el principio rector alrededor del cual opera la casa. Debe permitirse que filtre los medios de las masas y las influencias de todas las comunicaciones perniciosas, que corromperán las buenas costumbres.

Bienaventurado el varón que no anda en consejo de malos, ni está en camino de pecadores, ni se sienta en silla de escarnecedores –Salmo 1:1.

Los individuos dentro del hogar pueden no siempre apreciar la dirección recibida de ella, pero deben someterse a ella, y por lo general lo hacen de buen grado. La mayoría de nosotros hemos recibido direcciones de nuestros padres que no apreciamos en su momento, pero años más tarde hemos llegado a comprender la bienaventuranza de su liderazgo. Un liderazgo que no conduce, no está expresando amor, y dejará el hogar no santificado y a sus miembros desconectados. Aunque es incómodo e inconveniente pedir a los niños que prescindan de lo que otros disfrutan, no se santifican al seguir a sus compañeros, sino por la verdad. Para nosotros, como padres, no hay mayor gozo que saber que nuestros hijos caminan en la verdad. Igualmente, no hay mayor gozo para ellos que caminar en ella. Las devociones familiares diarias son una fuerza cohesionadora dentro del hogar que es central e integral para la santificación del hogar. No debemos disculparnos por la autoridad que damos a la Palabra, ni flojear en su uso. Es un evangelio erróneo creer que las almas son sofocadas cuando se las sujeta a los mandatos contenidos en ella.

Aquí está el resumen de Cristo sobre Su hogar.

He manifestado tu nombre a los hombres que me diste del mundo: tuyos eran, y me los diste; y han guardado tu palabra. Ahora han conocido que todas las cosas que me diste son de ti. Porque las palabras que me diste, yo se las di; y han recibido ellas, y han conocido con certeza que yo salí de ti, y han creído que tú me enviaste. Yo ruego por ellos; no ruego por el mundo, sino por los que me diste; porque tuyos son. Y todas mis cosas son tuyas, y tuyas son mías; y yo he sido glorificado en ellos. Y ahora ya no estoy en el mundo, pero estos están en el mundo, y yo voy a ti. Padre santo, guarda en tu nombre a los que me diste, para que sean uno, así como nosotros. Mientras estuve con ellos en el mundo, los guardé en tu nombre; a los que me diste, yo los guardé, y ninguno de ellos se perdió, sino el hijo de perdición, para que se cumpliese la Escritura. Y ahora voy a ti; y estas cosas hablo en el mundo, para que tengan mi gozo cumplido en sí mismos. Yo les he dado tu palabra; y el mundo los aborreció, porque no son del mundo, como tampoco yo soy del mundo. No ruego que los quites del mundo, sino que los guardes del mal. No son del mundo, como tampoco yo soy del mundo. Santifícalos en tu verdad: tu palabra es verdad –Juan 17:6-17.

Cristo, como cabeza de Su hogar, no empleó medios complicados para la santificación de Sus hijos. Su vida manifestó una constante preservación en el amor de Dios mediante la fe y la oración, y la administración de la Palabra de Dios a los que estaban alrededor de Él. A veces tropezaban con ella, luchaban interiormente y lo malentendían, pero la fuerza que los guardaba no descansaba en laureles de palabras convincentes, fuerza adamantina, actividades divertidas ni razonamientos prudentes.

Si bien un hogar debe emplear estos recursos de vez en cuando, por sí mismos no poseen el poder santificador. Porque es santificado por la palabra de Dios y por la oración –1 Timoteo 4:5.
