This story starts in Switzerland, in the 1500s. A group of Christian believers, desiring to obey Jesus and return to the teachings of the Apostles and the early Church, separated from both the Catholic and Protestant state-run Churches in several Cantons of Switzerland. They were referred to as the Swiss Brethren and were deemed as enemies of the state, by the Catholics and Protestants alike. Their enemies called them “Anabaptists” because they rejected infant baptism. They also refused military service, obeying Christ’s commands to “bless them that persecute you” and “love your enemies”. Many were arrested, imprisoned, tortured mercilessly and finally, many were martyred for not recanting their faith. In the early 1600s, when the authorities could not stop the movement in this manner, they began confiscating the believer’s homes, farms, and belongings, then exiled them from Switzerland.

Europe had just gone through the devastations of the Thirty Years’ War (1618-1648). In some places, like the Palatinate (Pfaltzland) in Germany, as many as 70% of the inhabitants had died of either war or disease. Many of the Hoffs (house/barn fort enclosures) were burned out and the fields were left uncultivated for years. In the mid-1600s, the local Prince, Elector Ludwig, invited the exiled Swiss Brethren into the Palatinate to help rebuild the farms because of their reputation as excellent husbandmen and tillers of the soil.

There were three official Churches recognized by the Germans: Catholic, Lutheran, and Reformed. Although the Swiss Brethren were needed economically, and their faith was tolerated, their churches were not recognized. There were limits on how many of them could meet together at one time, and many times they were not allowed to purchase the farms that they were improving because they were considered foreigners.

The Swiss-operated farms did indeed prosper in time, partly due to their use of a superior crop rotation system, which helped them feed more dairy cattle, and, in turn, allowed them to produce milk through the winters. Another major improvement was the introduction of the legume, clover. This came from seed which the Dutch Mennonites gifted to them. After about 50 years, the difference the Swiss had made in agriculture was noticeable enough that some frustrated German neighbors accused them of “Ferhexing” (the Pennsylvania Dutch term for witchcraft) the ground (which of course was not true). So, life in the Pfaltzland wasn’t getting better for the Swiss Brethren.

In the year 1708, they experienced a bitterly cold, long winter. So cold that some of their stored root crops froze in the cold cellars. Sometime after this, William Penn and the Quakers heard of the plight of these Swiss Anabaptists. In 1682, William Penn had been granted the colony of Pennsylvania and wanted to conduct what he called the “Holy Experiment”. He envisioned a land where all races and religions could dwell together in peace. He had special interest in those groups persecuted by the European State Churches. As a Quaker, he too had suffered persecution by the state church of England. He welcomed Quakers from England, Huguenots from France, Mennonites from Holland, German Baptist, Schwenkfelders and Pietists from Germany, as well as Swiss Brethren and Jews from wherever they were sojourning and/or suffering.

That is the background for our account of Hans Graeff (Groff) who lived from c.1661-1746. Hans had been converted to the faith of the Swiss Brethren, but his wife, Anna (Bare) Graeff had stayed with the Protestant State Church. When the door opened to pioneer in Pennsylvania, Hans was interested in going, but Anna was not. Possibly they planned to have him get settled in over there and then come back for her. Hans first came to Pennsylvania in 1696. Later, Hans ended up leading a small group of the Swiss Brethren (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & the Funks to name a few) to Germantown, about seven miles north of Philadelphia in that day, which was the first permanent settlement of the Anabaptists in the New World. Many of those first settlers were from Holland and Sweden and were part of the Mennonite Church of the Netherlands. The Swiss immigrants spent the winter of 1709 in Germantown—the women doing spinning for the many weavers of Germantown and the men traveling to a new Anabaptist settlement at Skippack, where they were learning many of the skills needed to go to the frontier. It seems that here is where the Swiss Brethren first became known as Mennists or Mennonites.

In 1710, the group moved up to the Conestoga Valley where Hans Groff had previously identified some very rich and well-watered lands, 60 miles west of Germantown and civilization. Life would indeed be difficult. Wolves, bears, panthers, bobcats and other predators abounded. There were also elk, timber bison, and whitetail deer in abundance (which were glad to eat whatever the settlers planted). Huge walnut, hickory, chestnuts, maples, white pines, and oaks, some six feet in diameter and over 100 feet tall, covered much of their new lands (except for some open meadows, left by the native Americans and wetlands). These huge trees would need to be cut down by hand with axes and two-man saws. The closest doctor, apothecary, hardware, or general store was 60 miles away. It would be challenging and dangerous work, but they were free! Free to obey their conscience. Free to practice their religion. Free to own land in this beautiful wilderness. Free to love and witness to their neighbors—the Conestoga tribe and French traders. They received a land patent for 10,000 acres for their families and others that might come later.

Partly due to severe persecution, in 1710, a group of Swiss Brethren moved to the Mannheim area of Germany. Seven years later, in 1717, they made the trip across the Atlantic. There were more than 60 families that came to the Conestoga Valley in the fall of that year, including my ancestors, Hans and Magdalena Hess and their three children (they were eventually blessed with a total of 11). You could say that from then on, the floodgates opened, and masses of Anabaptists fled Europe to “Penn’s Promised Land”. From 1730 and later, as this wilderness became tamed, there were also many Lutheran, Reformed, and Catholic people who came over from Germany to find better financial opportunities, filling this part of Pennsylvania with many German-dialect speakers.

I greatly enjoyed speaking with the noted Lancaster County Anabaptist historian, Amos Hoover, while writing this article. He gave many insights and details, but we both agreed, it is challenging to put together all the facts and details from so long ago. Gleaning from a couple authors’ accounts, the story goes something like this:

Misunderstanding

Sometime, after being in Penn’s woods for a number of years, Hans Groff received word that his wife, Anna (Bare) Groff, back in Europe, had passed away. He was very grieved and mourned, as he didn’t know it and wasn’t there to bury her. In a few years, he married Susanna Kendig. They lived first in the Strasburg area, then built a substantial homestead in the area now called Groffdale. This union was blessed with nine children.

Years later, a woman showed up in the community and introduced herself as Mrs. Hans Groff. She had become an Anabaptist in Europe and had made the perilous trip across the Atlantic to find her husband. According to her, a person with the same name as herself had died, and the word given to Hans was not true about his first wife’s death. Hans was mortified, although he was innocent regarding his second marriage. He had no desire to be a polygamist or to commit adultery. The frontier church leaders held counsel and gave a recommendation—that the younger, pioneer wife with so many young children needed the husband to provide for them. It is said that Hans didn’t feel clear to stay with either of them but did support both of his wives and their children financially. He was noted as a tireless traveler, riding to Philadelphia with furs then back out into the vast frontier with blankets, brass kettles and other trade good for the Native Americans. If you have heard or read this account with different details, so have I. Only eternity will reveal all these details exactly.

Medicine

Hans’s first wife chose to live as a single sister in that church community. Instead of becoming bitter with her husband, her God, and her circumstances, she chose a life of service to her neighbors. She lived in a little house, with a small barn (possibly built by Hans for her) on top of a steep hill overlooking Farmersville, called “Cat’s Back Hill”. The ruins of this early 1700s house and barn were still evident less than 50 years ago. Apparently, she was a midwife, before coming to this country and continued in this profession once she was here. She had a lot of experience with growing herbs and making herbal remedies. She was possibly the closest one to being a doctor for many miles around. From what I can find out, she spent her time being a blessing to the local community with her medical knowledge and wisdom, her homemade herbal medicines, and her midwifery. Many of our Lancaster County forefathers may not have survived the rigorous pioneer life if it had not been for this dear Sister’s servanthood and medical knowledge. Interestingly, years later, one of Hans’s sons from the second wife, David Groff, went away to study medicine. Once his studies were completed, he came back as a doctor and helped his father’s first wife minister to the many settlers in fast growing Lancaster County.

This story provides a glimpse into some of the interesting details surrounding the life of conservative Anabaptists just before and during the establishing of Colonial America. There were difficulties involving freedom of religion and worship in their homelands of Europe, but their travels to, and eventual day-to-day living in, a new, free country was acquainted with challenges as well. One encouragement that we can see in this story was the willingness of these individuals to allow God’s principles to guide them each step of the way.

Denna berättelse börjar i Schweiz på 1500‑talet. En grupp kristna troende, som önskade lyda Jesus och återgå till apostlarnas och den tidiga kyrkans lära, bröt sig loss från både den katolska och den protestantiska statskyrkan i flera kantoner i Schweiz. De kallades de schweiziska bröderna och betraktades som statens fiender, både av katoliker och protestanter. Deras fiender kallade dem ”anabaptister” eftersom de avvisade barndop. De vägrade också militärtjänst och lydde Kristi befallningar att ”välsigna dem som förföljer er” och ”älska era fiender”. Många arresterades, sattes i fängelse, torterades skoningslöst och många blev slutligen martyrer för att de inte ville återkalla sin tro. I början av 1600‑talet, när myndigheterna inte längre kunde stoppa rörelsen på detta sätt, började de konfiskera de troendes hem, gårdar och ägodelar och sedan förvisa dem från Schweiz.

Europa hade just genomgått förödelsen av trettioåriga kriget (1618–1648). På vissa platser, som Pfalz i Tyskland, hade så många som 70 % av invånarna dött av krig eller sjukdom. Många hovar (hus/ladugårds‑fortifikationer) brändes ut och åkrarna lämnades osådda i åratal. I mitten av 1600‑talet bjöd den lokala fursten, kurfurst Ludvig, in de landsförvisade schweiziska bröderna till Pfalz för att hjälpa till att återuppbygga gårdarna på grund av deras rykte som utmärkta jordbrukare och markbrukare.

Det fanns tre officiella kyrkor erkända av tyskarna: katolsk, luthersk och reformert. Även om de schweiziska bröderna behövdes ekonomiskt och deras tro tolererades, erkändes deras församlingar inte. Det fanns gränser för hur många de kunde samlas samtidigt och ofta tilläts de inte köpa de gårdar de förbättrade eftersom de ansågs vara utlänningar.

De schweizdrivna gårdarna blomstrade med tiden, delvis tack vare en överlägsen växelbruksmetod som hjälpte dem att föda fler mjölkkor och därmed producera mjölk genom vintrarna. En annan viktig förbättring var införandet av baljväxter, klöver. Detta kom från frön som de holländska mennoniterna gav dem. Efter cirka 50 år var skillnaden de schweiziska bönderna gjort i jordbruket så märkbar att vissa frustrerade tyska grannar anklagade dem för att ha ”Ferhexing” (Pennsylvaniatyskt uttryck för häxeri) marken (vilket naturligtvis inte var sant). Så livet i Pfalz blev inte lättare för de schweiziska bröderna.

År 1708 upplevde de en bittert kall, lång vinter. Så kall att en del av de lagrade rotfrukterna frös i de kalla källarna. Någon tid därefter fick William Penn och kväkare höra om dessa schweiziska anabaptisters nöd. År 1682 hade William Penn fått kolonin Pennsylvania och ville genomföra vad han kallade det ”Heliga experimentet”. Han föreställde sig ett land där alla raser och religioner kunde leva tillsammans i fred. Han hade särskilt intresse för de grupper som förföljdes av de europeiska statskyrkorna. Som kväkare hade han själv lidit förföljelse av Englands statskyrka. Han välkomnade kväkare från England, hugenotter från Frankrike, mennoniter från Holland, tyska baptister, schwenkfeldare och pietister från Tyskland samt schweiziska bröder och judar var de än uppehöll sig eller led.

Detta är bakgrunden till vår berättelse om Hans Graeff (Groff) som levde cirka 1661–1746. Hans hade blivit omvänd till de schweiziska brödernas tro, men hans hustru, Anna (Bare) Graeff, hade stannat kvar i den protestantiska statskyrkan. När dörren öppnades för att pionjera i Pennsylvania var Hans intresserad av att åka, men Anna var inte det. Kanske planerade de att han skulle etablera sig där borta och sedan komma tillbaka för henne. Hans kom först till Pennsylvania 1696. Senare ledde Hans en liten grupp av de schweiziska bröderna (Hans & Christian Herr, Martin Meylin, Jacob Muller, Martin Kendig, Martin Oberholtzer, Wendell Bowman & Funks, för att nämna några) till Germantown, ungefär sju mil norr om Philadelphia på den tiden, vilket blev anabaptisternas första permanenta bosättning i den Nya världen. Många av de första bosättarna kom från Holland och Sverige och tillhörde Nederländernas mennonitkyrka. De schweiziska immigranterna tillbringade vintern 1709 i Germantown — kvinnorna spann åt Germantowns många vävare och männen reste till en ny anabaptistbosättning i Skippack, där de lärde sig många av de färdigheter som behövdes på gränslandet. Det verkar som om det var här de schweiziska bröderna först blev kända som mennoniter.

År 1710 flyttade gruppen upp till Conestoga‑dalen där Hans Groff tidigare identifierat några mycket rika och välbevattnade marker, 60 mil väster om Germantown och civilisationen. Livet skulle verkligen bli svårt. Vargar, björnar, pantrar, lodjur och andra rovdjur var vanliga. Det fanns också älg, skogsbison och vitstjärtade hjortar i överflöd (som gärna åt vad nybyggarna satte i jorden). Stora valnötsträd, hickory, kastanj, lönnar, vita tallar och ekar, vissa sex fot i diameter och över 100 fot höga, täckte mycket av deras nya marker (utom några öppna ängar som lämnat av ursprungsbefolkningen och våtmarker). Dessa gigantiska träd måste fällas för hand med yxor och tvåmanssågar. Närmaste doktor, apotekare, järnaffär eller varuhus låg 60 mil bort. Det skulle vara utmanande och farligt arbete, men de var fria! Fria att följa sitt samvete. Fria att utöva sin religion. Fria att äga mark i denna vackra vildmark. Fria att älska och vittna för sina grannar — Conestoga‑stammen och franska handelsmän. De fick ett markbrev på 10 000 acres för sina familjer och andra som kanske skulle komma senare.

Delvis på grund av svåra förföljelser flyttade 1710 en grupp schweiziska bröder till Mannheim‑området i Tyskland. Sju år senare, 1717, gjorde de färden över Atlanten. Mer än 60 familjer kom till Conestoga‑dalen hösten det året, inklusive mina förfäder, Hans och Magdalena Hess och deras tre barn (de blev så småningom välsignade med totalt 11 barn). Man kan säga att därefter öppnades portarna och mängder av anabaptister flydde Europa till Penns utlovade land. Från 1730 och framåt, i takt med att denna vildmark blev kultiverad, kom också många lutheraner, reformerta och katoliker från Tyskland för att söka bättre ekonomiska möjligheter, vilket fyllde denna del av Pennsylvania med många tysktalande dialekter.

Jag uppskattade mycket att samtala med den framstående Anabaptist‑historikern från Lancaster County, Amos Hoover, när jag skrev denna artikel. Han gav många insikter och detaljer, men vi var båda överens om att det är svårt att sammanställa alla fakta och detaljer från så länge sedan. Utifrån ett par författares redogörelser går historien ungefär så här:

Missförstånd

Någon gång efter att ha bott i Penns skogar i flera år fick Hans Groff besked om att hans fru, Anna (Bare) Groff, i Europa hade avlidit. Han sörjde djupt, eftersom han inte kände till det och inte kunde begrava henne. Några år senare gifte han sig med Susanna Kendig. De bodde först i Strasburg‑området och byggde sedan ett ansenligt hem i det som nu kallas Groffdale. Detta äktenskap blev välsignat med nio barn.

År senare dök en kvinna upp i församlingen och presenterade sig som fru Hans Groff. Hon hade blivit anabaptist i Europa och gjort den farliga resan över Atlanten för att hitta sin make. Enligt hennes berättelse hade en person med samma namn som hon själv dött, och det bud som nått Hans om hans första hustrus död var inte sant. Hans blev förskräckt, även om han var oskyldig i samband med sitt andra äktenskap. Han hade ingen önskan att vara polygam eller begå äktenskapsbrott. Församlingsledarna på gränstrakterna höll rådslag och gav en rekommendation — att den yngre pionjerskan med så många små barn behövde sin make för att försörja dem. Det sägs att Hans inte kände sig klar att stanna hos någon av dem, men han försörjde båda fruarna och deras barn ekonomiskt. Han var känd som en outtröttlig resenär, som red till Philadelphia med pälsar och sedan tillbaka ut i det vida gränslandet med filtar, kopparkittlar och andra handelsvaror till ursprungsbefolkningen. Om du hört eller läst denna berättelse med andra detaljer, så har även jag det. Endast evigheten kommer att uppenbara alla dessa detaljer fullständigt.

Medicin

Hans första hustru valde att leva som en ensam syster i den kyrkliga gemenskapen. Istället för att bli bitter mot sin make, sin Gud och sin situation valde hon ett liv i tjänst för sina grannar. Hon bodde i ett litet hus med en liten lada (möjligen byggd av Hans åt henne) på toppen av en brant kulle med utsikt över Farmersville, kallad ”Cat’s Back Hill”. Ruinerna efter detta tidiga 1700‑tals hus och lada var fortfarande synliga för mindre än 50 år sedan. Tydligen var hon en barnmorska innan hon kom till detta land och fortsatte i detta yrke när hon väl var här. Hon hade stor erfarenhet av att odla örter och tillverka örtmediciner. Hon var troligen den som mest kunde betraktas som läkare för många mil omkring. Såvitt jag kan utröna ägnade hon sin tid åt att vara en välsignelse för det lokala samhället med sin medicinska kunskap och visdom, sina hemgjorda örtpreparat och sin barnmorskekonst. Många av våra föregångare i Lancaster County kanske inte hade överlevt det hårda pionjärlivet om det inte varit för denna kära systers tjänande och medicinska kunnande. Intressant nog reste en av Hans söner från andra hustrun, David Groff, bort för att studera medicin år senare. När hans studier var avslutade återvände han som läkare och hjälpte sin fars första hustru att tjäna de många nybyggarna i det snabbt växande Lancaster County.

Denna berättelse ger en inblick i några av de intressanta detaljer som omgärdade livet för konservativa anabaptister strax före och under etableringen av kolonial‑Amerika. Det fanns svårigheter gällande religions‑ och samvetsfrihet i deras hemländer i Europa, men deras resor till och det dagliga livet i ett nytt, fritt land var också förenat med utmaningar. En uppmuntran vi kan se i denna berättelse är dessa individers villighet att låta Guds principer vägleda dem i varje steg.

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

Sebagai saudara perempuan dalam Tuhan dan orang percaya yang dilahirkan kembali, saya yakin kita semua sepakat bahwa menghafal firman Tuhan penting bagi kesehatan rohani kita. Saya menghafal banyak sekali ayat Alkitab selama masa kanak-kanak saya. Sebagian besar ayat yang saya hafal diajarkan selama Sekolah Minggu Musim Liburan yang saya hadiri setiap musim panas.

Pada malam pertama Sekolah Minggu, para guru membagikan tugas hafalan, seringkali sampai beberapa halaman. Semua itu tidak harus dikerjakan, tetapi hadiahnya menarik. Sebagian besar tahun saya menghafal semua yang ditugaskan. Saya memberi pujian kepada para guru dan Sekolah Minggu itu atas kekayaan ayat yang saya hafal selama masa itu.

Sekarang saya sudah menikah dan memiliki anak sendiri. Sekolah Minggu dari masa kanak-kanak saya sudah lama berlalu. Saya menyadari bahwa jika anak-anak saya ingin menghafal Kitab Suci, saya harus mewujudkannya. Sebagai ibu, banyak dari kita tahu pentingnya menghafal Firman Tuhan dan menyimpannya, bukan hanya dalam hati kita, tetapi juga dalam hati anak-anak kita.

Bagaimanakah pemuda dapat membersihkan jalannya? Dengan menjaga menurut firman-Mu. Dengan segenap hatiku aku mencari Engkau; janganlah biarkan aku menyimpang dari perintah-perintah-Mu. Aku menyimpan perkataan-Mu dalam hatiku, supaya aku jangan berbuat dosa terhadap Engkau –Mazmur 119:9-11.

Kita membutuhkan Firman Tuhan dalam hati kita untuk menolong kita dalam pergumulan sehari-hari melawan dosa. Anak-anak kita juga membutuhkan ini. Sebagian besar anak-anak kita tidak akan menghafal Kitab Suci tanpa bantuan dari kita.

Saya dan suami tidak mengawali pernikahan dengan impian menghafal bersama anak-anak kami. Bagi keluarga kami, hal itu terjadi hampir secara kebetulan. Anak tertua kami berumur tiga dan empat ketika suami saya mengusulkan agar kami melatih mereka menghafal kisah Natal yang terdapat dalam Lukas 2:1-19. Saya tidak berpikir mereka akan mampu. Saya kira anak kecil hanya menghafal ayat pendek seperti, “Hendaklah kamu saling mengasihi.” Kami mulai melafalkannya bersama setiap malam dalam waktu devosi keluarga. Saya cukup terkejut ketika mereka menghafal bagian ini dengan cepat dan mudah.

Saya tertarik. Haruskah kami mencoba lagi? Paskah pun mendekat jadi saya mulai melatih mereka pada kisah penyaliban yang terdapat dalam Yohanes 19:1-19. Sekali lagi, mereka menghafalnya tanpa banyak usaha. Hal itu mendorong saya untuk meneruskan dengan bagian-bagian lain.

Ketika tiba waktunya mengajar anak-anak di rumah, saya ingin hafalan menjadi bagian dari rutinitas harian kami. Saya membeli sebuah binder dan memasukkan salinan-cetak bagian-bagian yang telah kami hafal serta bagian yang ingin saya agar mereka hafalkan. Ini memulai rutinitas yang masih kami lakukan sampai sekarang.

Setiap hari kami melafalkan bagian yang sedang dipelajari serta satu bagian yang telah kami hafal sebelumnya. Kami juga melafalkannya bersama sebagai keluarga saat waktu devosi. Saya mendapati bahwa dengan cara ini keluarga biasanya menghafal sebuah bagian dalam waktu sekitar tiga sampai empat minggu.

Pada awal bagian baru, saya membaca ayat itu nyaring-nyaring. Seiring hari berlalu, anak-anak mulai ikut lebih sering. Akhirnya, saya hanya memulai dan hanya membantu bila mereka butuh bantuan. Ketika saya pikir mereka sudah tahu, saya minta mereka melafalkannya kepada saya satu per satu. Jika mereka sudah menguasainya dengan baik, mereka mulai melafalkannya kepada ayah saat devosi keluarga. Jika belum, kami terus berlatih sampai mereka bisa. Terkadang saya memberi anak yang kesulitan beberapa ayat saja untuk dilafalkan. Namun, sebagian besar dari mereka lebih suka melafalkan keseluruhannya.

Kami menghafal sebagai keluarga bukan secara individual. Saya tidak berpindah ke bagian baru sampai semua orang telah menghafalnya atau setidaknya menghafalnya sesuai kemampuan mereka. (Tidak semua anak dapat menghafal 19 ayat pada usia tiga tahun.) Beberapa anak kami baru mulai berbicara pada usia tiga tahun sehingga hafalan Alkitab secara lisan hampir tidak mungkin. Beberapa anak akan tergagap-gagap melalui sebuah bagian dan membutuhkan banyak kata petunjuk, yang tidak apa-apa selama mereka melakukan yang terbaik. Kadang kami mengulang bagian yang sama beberapa tahun kemudian dan mereka mempelajarinya lebih baik pada pengulangan kedua.

Ini mungkin terdengar memakan waktu dan menegangkan, tetapi bagi kami tidak demikian. Saya menghabiskan sekitar lima menit sehari untuk mengerjakan hafalan. Kami tidak punya batas waktu untuk hafalan sehingga tidak ada tekanan untuk menguasainya pada waktu tertentu. Anak-anak telah melakukan ini sejak mereka hampir tidak bisa bicara, jadi mereka terbiasa dan jarang mengeluh. Karena kami menghafal sebagai keluarga, itu juga menolong anak yang tidak bisa menghafal sebaik yang lain. Sebagai keluarga, kami memberi dorongan dan sorakan kepada anak yang kesulitan. Ia merasakan pencapaian walaupun harus bergumul melewati seluruh bagian.

Saya memberi hadiah kecil untuk setiap bagian yang dihafal. Saya punya kotak hadiah yang bisa mereka pilih. Ini tidak perlu mahal! Saya sering kali tidak mengeluarkan lebih dari satu dolar. Garage sale dan toko barang bekas adalah tempat untuk membeli barang murah. Diskon kembali-sekolah juga menyenangkan karena kebanyakan anak suka paket krayon baru atau penghapus lucu.

Seiring waktu, saya mendapati diri saya terasa kecewa melihat betapa cepatnya anak-anak melupakan sebuah bagian yang sudah dihafal. Saya mengetahui bahwa beberapa tahun kemudian mereka sering hampir tidak bisa melafalkan bagian yang pernah dipelajari. Saya bertanya-tanya mengapa saya berusaha jika mereka akan melupakannya dalam beberapa tahun. Suami saya mendorong saya untuk terus. Ia berkata bahwa konsepnya tetap ada di hati mereka meskipun mereka tak lagi bisa melafalkan teksnya. Jadi saya terus, tetapi saya tetap berharap menemukan solusi atas masalah ini.

Suatu hari saya membaca sebuah artikel yang ditulis oleh seorang ibu lain yang juga melatih anak-anaknya untuk menghafal. Dalam artikel itu ia berkata penting untuk memindahkan hafalan dari memori jangka pendek ke memori jangka panjang. Solusinya sebenarnya cukup sederhana. Setiap hari selain melafalkan bagian baru, kami juga melafalkan satu bagian yang sudah dipelajari sebelumnya. Binder saya sangat berguna untuk ini! Semua bagian yang telah kami pelajari ada di binder itu. Saya menggunakan jepitan kertas untuk membantu mengingat bagian yang baru saja kami tinjau. Setiap hari jepitan itu pindah ke bagian berikutnya. Ketika kami sampai di ujung, kami mulai lagi. Ini membantu menjaga bagian-bagian itu tetap segar dalam ingatan kami serta memindahkannya ke memori jangka panjang.

Saya juga suka punya tema untuk setiap tahun sekolah. Suatu tahun tema saya adalah, “Menghafal 100 Ayat.” Anak-anak menikmati melihat angkanya naik seiring berjalannya tahun. Tahun ini kami bekerja pada “Khotbah di Bukit.” Saya membaginya menjadi 10 bagian. Tujuannya adalah menyelesaikannya dalam setahun, tetapi jika kami tidak mencapai tujuan itu tidak masalah. Lebih baik berjalan lambat dan menghafal sesuatu dengan baik daripada cepat tapi tidak mempertahankan apa yang telah dipelajari.

Ini adalah metode yang saya temukan berguna bagi keluarga kami. Berdoalah dan mintalah ide kepada Tuhan yang akan bekerja baik untuk keluargamu tanpa membandingkan dirimu dengan keluarga lain! Jangan meremehkan apa yang bisa dilakukan anak-anakmu. Jangan berasumsi karena mereka masih kecil, mereka hanya bisa menghafal satu atau dua ayat. Anak-anak sering kali hanya berbuat sebagaimana yang kita harapkan dari mereka, bahkan yang lebih muda sekalipun.

Setelah kita menghafal Firman Tuhan, kita perlu menggunakannya setiap hari. Selimut yang disimpan di lemari tidak berguna pada malam musim dingin yang dingin. Penulis Ulangan merangkum ini dengan baik—Dan engkau harus mengasihi TUHAN, Allahmu, dengan segenap hatimu dan dengan segenap jiwamu dan dengan segenap kekuatanmu. Dan firman-firman ini, yang kuperintahkan kepadamu pada hari ini, haruslah ada dalam hatimu: Dan kau harus mengajarkannya dengan tekun kepada anak-anakmu, dan haruslah engkau membicarakannya apabila engkau duduk di rumahmu, apabila engkau sedang berjalan di jalan, ketika engkau berbaring dan ketika engkau bangun –Ulangan 6:5-7.

Pertama, kita mengasihi Allah. Lalu kita memasukkan Firman-Nya ke dalam hati kita. Akhirnya, kita harus mengajarkan kebenaran-kebenaran ini kepada anak-anak kita saat kita melakukan aktivitas sehari-hari. Bagian ini mencakup semuanya—duduk, berjalan, berbaring, dan bangun. Setelah sebuah bagian dihafal, suami saya akan menjelaskan ayat-ayat itu kepada kami saat waktu devosi. Ini menolong kami mengerti apa yang sedang kami hafal.

Kita melakukan banyak hal karena kebiasaan karena kita menyadari pentingnya. Kita menyikat gigi, menyisir rambut, makan sarapan, dan melakukan banyak hal lain. Kita melakukan hal-hal ini setiap hari. Mereka menjadi bagian rutin dari hidup kita. Karena kita menghargainya, kita mewujudkannya. Begitulah seharusnya dengan hafalan Kitab Suci. Itu terlalu berharga untuk dilewatkan.

Berbahagialah orang yang tidak berjalan menurut nasihat orang fasik, yang tidak berdiri di jalan orang berdosa, dan tidak duduk dalam kumpulan pencemooh, tetapi kesukaannya ialah Taurat TUHAN, dan Taurat itu dibacanya siang dan malam. Ia seperti pohon yang ditanam di tepi aliran air, yang menghasilkan buahnya pada musimnya, dan daunnya pun tidak layu; apa saja yang diperbuatnya berhasil –Mazmur 1:1-3.

Ketika kita bersukacita dalam Firman Tuhan, kita akan senang menyediakan waktu untuk menghafal Kitab Suci, dan Firman yang dihafal itu kemudian akan berbuah pada waktunya.

Janganlah kita jemu-jemu berbuat baik, karena pada waktunya kita akan menuai, jika kita tidak menjadi lemah –Galatia 6:9.

Jesus, upon His ascension back into His heavenly home, gave a final directive to His disciples, both to those physically present as He disappeared into the clouds, and to the myriad of believers who would come to know Him down through the ages. The story of His life and His gospel were to be preached unto all the world by those who called Him Lord. This global spreading of the Word, would, in the later vision of John, be proclaimed as one of the prerequisites of Jesus’ triumphant return at the end of time. John himself would be seen as a harbinger of these end times, based on Jesus’ words as recorded by John … If I will that he [John] tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. John 21:22.

The early Christians, understandably, felt that the return of Christ was imminent, even within the first century. The rapid expansion of Christianity, the complete moral depravity of the Roman culture, and the increasing intensity of persecution against them seemed to point to a swift and triumphant return of their Lord.

Now, two thousand years since Christ gave that promise, His soon return seems just as imminent as it did to the first century believers. Speculation on the time of His return, the manner of it, and the contributing factors are always current and controversial subjects. In the light of this continued earnest expectation of the end times, what have we to learn about our interpretations of prophecy from those who have attempted to decipher the prophetic portions of Scripture in earlier ages?

Jesus' first coming was surrounded and enveloped by perhaps the most recognizable misinterpretation of prophecy in the Bible. Roughly four hundred years of relative silence from God precluded His entry into the world in a physical, human body. His birth would be unnoticed in a society that was not only in desperate need of, but also expecting, a Savior to arrive. Daniel, writing the words God gave him, had told of a Messiah to come, and had even given a time that He would appear. Now, the Jews seethed under Roman rule, hanging their hopes on what they thought would be a sudden and triumphant extermination of the Roman troops and influence from their lands. To us, it is glaringly obvious that their interpretation of prophecy was not only incorrect, but for many, would lead them astray so that they did not even recognize or acknowledge the true Redeemer that was sent to them.

But what was it that caused this misinterpreted view? To us, it seems completely in order that Jesus would focus on the poor and destitute rather than opposing an occupying army. Jewish historians give an intriguing, but scarcely surprising, answer to the failure of the majority of their people to recognize Christ for who He was.

The religious atmosphere of first century Israel was one defined by corruption, bribery, lust for power, and all the unsavory aspects of a completely politically motivated upper class.

The priests, once chosen by God to be His servants in sanctifying His children, had sunk to buying their positions of service, most notably in the high priest’s office, where God had ordained one high priest to serve the people throughout his life. In Jesus’ day, however, the responsibilities of leading the children of Israel were divvied out, the role often changing hands on one-year terms. Becoming a high priest was a matter of birth. Most high priests came from several large, influential, and wealthy families, as one often had to buy into the opportunity of this office.

It was not only the high priest’s office that was corrupted, but most levels of prominent spiritual leadership were filled by the wealthy elites who had the connections and wealth to be placed into roles of importance amongst the Jews.

This unsavory backdrop gives even more clarity to Jesus’ feelings on the religious leaders of His day. These imposters did not hold their priestly positions to serve His Father, they held them for their own gain, turning the temple into a marketplace and holding the common people hostage through their disputes on the minutiae of the Law.

Unsurprisingly, these leaders looked for a Messiah who would fit their goals, their ideals, and their morals, rather than one that would rebuke and chastise them for their hypocrisy, greed, and selfish ambition. Their view of prophecy had been so twisted and corrupted by their lifestyle that even the miracle of a resurrection could not sway them to view Christ’s power as coming from God. This misconstrued expectation of a conquering commander, riding a horse of war over the political enemies of these elites was pandered to the common Jew as well. Centuries of fighting for just the freedom to worship, as in the case of the Maccabees and the Greeks, had deeply imprinted a sense of nationalism into the collective mind of the Jewish people. The ones who bought into it the most were the ones who received the most from this system of exclusive access to God and His promises. To those who were repressed by the stringent and often man-made laws of Jewish society, a God of peace and love who would draw the needy of the world to Him was more welcome than a Saviour who would simply install another earthly government to rule the poor, oppress the widows, and reward the wicked.

This was not the last time an oppressed people would be deceived, as Roman rule would witness another major misstep in the collective interpretations of God’s people. This time, the teachings of Jesus and the words of His disciples would be misinterpreted to fit the changing political and religious landscape of fourth century Rome. The year was 306, and Diocletian, one of the most brutal persecutors of Christians in the Roman Empire, had abdicated from his position as Caesar. In his wake, he left three contenders for his throne. One of those vying for the seat of power was a young general, experienced in politics, and power hungry. His name was Constantine, son of a prominent Roman officer and a lowly Greek Christian, Helena.

From his youth, Constantine followed in his father’s footsteps, fighting throughout the empire, rising to a rank of general. Now, on campaign in Britain, he turned his eyes to the ultimate prize of a Roman politico, the title of Caesar, and the seat of the emperor.

Constantine’s line to the throne was through his father. Diocletian had, during his rule, appointed additional Caesars to aid in ruling the empire. Constantine’s father was one of these, and despite being simply appointed to the position, it was expected that his status as a Caesar would pass to his son. Matters were not as simple as a mere transfer of titles, however.

Constantine’s rise was bloody, but his grip on power was set, until he remained the sole contender for the throne. The stage was set. He quickly undid the harsh decrees of Diocletian, legalizing Christianity and removing the persecution that had leveled churches, scattered families, and hunted down bishops and other church leadership. Almost overnight, a peace previously unheard of was gifted to these hounded believers.

The changes that Constantine made did not end, however, with merely legalizing Christianity. His sympathies ran deeper, and he made further moves to legitimize it as not only an accepted religion, but as the state religion.

To Christians eager for the return of Christ, this seemed almost unbelievable. In the span of a few short years the government had gone from crucifying, beheading, and torturing them to holding them up as examples to the rest of the empire. The favor seems to have affected the clarity with which they viewed the apparent reconciliation of the world to the church. Not only would they accept a position of power in the empire, but they would also accept Constantine as a benefactor and protector of the church itself. In their minds, the day of the Lord was come, and Constantine was the rod of iron with which God would rule.

And rule he did. The course of the church was soon swayed by this new and outside influence. Constantine sat in on meetings of the bishops, even though at the time he was not baptized nor was he even seeking baptism. The church’s new position as a tool of the state brought schisms, in-fighting, and contention at every turn. There remained a remnant, but most of the church would fall under the sway of a man motivated by a hunger for power, wealth, and influence.

Constantine would be baptized before his death, lending him even further credibility in the eyes of a straying church. Now separated from its original identity as sheep in this world, the coming centuries would see “Christians” become ravening wolves, destroying, killing, and corrupting.

In a matter more recently related to us as Anabaptists, the tale of the infamous Muensterites gives us a further example of the perils of misinterpreting prophecy, especially the prophecy regarding the second coming of Christ.

One of the great disadvantages of a heavily persecuted group is a tendency to lack stability, as evidenced by the varying beliefs developed by Anabaptist groups of the movement's first fifty years. Persecution would deprive a congregation of their leaders, who were often those most targeted by the authorities. A missing elder meant less teaching, which in turn led to more difficulty in guidance, and corrective doctrine. Even the most sincere and interconnected groups could fall into errors developed because of the lack of leadership to bring Biblical clarity and balance the brotherhood.

The situation in the Netherlands was of a rather volatile strain approaching the 1530s. Throughout the country, the Catholic Church remained the predominant religion, clinging to their power through ruthless displays of physical force, most often directed towards the minority Protestant congregations. This focus on quelling the Protestant influence was momentarily successful in this instance, with most of their groups dissolving and reintegrating into the Catholic Church or other groups.

One of the groups that was on the receiving end of this minor diaspora was the fledging Dutch Anabaptist church. For those Protestants who still refused to join the Catholics, the Anabaptists often became their choice of church, rapidly swelling their ranks. This had a profound effect on the local strain of Anabaptism, which without a doubt was fervent, but quite prone to chaos and upheaval.

By 1534 the tensions of this influx of new believers reached a breaking point, and the Anabaptist church of the Netherlands split into two main factions. The first, led by the two Philips brothers, Dirk and Obbe, adhered to the New Testament teachings of separation from church and state, as well as nonresistance. This would be the church of Menno Simmons, and the root of the Mennonite churches of today.

The other faction held to more radical beliefs, led by Jan Matthysz and Jan of Leiden. These two men became increasingly fanatical in their views of Christ’s return, believing that they would be central figures, instrumental in a kingdom that God would set up on Earth.

At the same time, social unrest was brewing, and spilled over in the city of Munster, located in northwest Germany, where the common people rose up, overthrowing their city’s government and expelling their Catholic bishop. The two Jans were quick to act, contacting the new leaders of the city, and eventually winning them over to their views.

The Jans moved to Munser in early 1534, and began sending out prophets and messengers, who called all “Anabaptists” to congregate at this “New Jerusalem”. The unrest of the area made their message all the more appealing, and thousands streamed into the city, intent in being part of this apocalyptic return of Christ.

There was, in fact, an apocalyptic return on the horizon, but not a return of Christ. This one came in the form of the ousted Catholic bishop, who swiftly set siege to the city. His army would stay there for eighteen months.

Inside the city, Jan Matthysz, proclaiming a vision was given to him for a deliverance of the city, left its walls to parade outside, proclaiming a swift delivery of the enemy into his hands. His vision, however, failed him, as he was swiftly delivered into the hands of the enemy, where he was beheaded, and his head set on a pike in front Munster’s gates.

Inside the walls, Jan of Leiden took leadership, ignoring the famine, death, and chaos that now ran rampant within the besieged walls. Instead, he began promoting polygamy, defending it from the Old Testament, killing at least one woman who refused to marry him, and at one point, having sixteen wives.

This abomination soon led to its required end as the city was overcome, with a heavy slaughter being carried out against its inhabitants. The leaders, Jan of Leiden being the most prominent, were captured, tortured, and killed. Their bodies were hung in iron cages on the tower of St. Lamberts Church, the Catholic church in Munster. To this day, the cages still hang, a bleak reminder of the pride and rashness of the two Jans, determined to see their end-time interpretation fulfilled.

In all three of these examples, the prophecy contained in God’s Word was twisted into results that strayed far from the will of God for His children. For the Jews, it caused them to miss the Messiah, failing to recognize the greatest promise God had given them. The fourth century Christians, chafing under the horrific persecution of Diocletian, accepted Constantine as a deliverer, seeing him as a fulfillment of God’s judgement against the kingdoms of this world. Instead of peace, they would sink into a state of ungodliness worse than the pagans around them, with the Catholic Church straying into sin more horrible than even their pagan society. Lastly, the troubled visions and interpretations of the 16th century Munsterites would lead them to an awful fate, sullying the name of the true church.

What have we to learn from these grave errors of those before us? In our time, the end seems imminent, and we are beset with those who would have us believe that we are truly the last of the Christians.

Luke has recorded the instructions of Jesus on this point: …The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them –Luke 17: 22-23. Here are instructions for our conduct in the last days. Let us not be running after the rumors of the end times but let us be obedient to the final admonition of our Lord—that we spread the Word of God and the Gospel of His Son, Jesus throughout the world … and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:14.

Jesus, toe Hy opgevaar het na Sy hemelse woning, het aan Sy dissipels ’n finale opdrag gegee — aan diegene wat fisies daar was terwyl Hy in die wolke verdwyn het, sowel as aan die menigte gelowiges wat Hom deur die eeue sou leer ken. Die verhaal van Sy lewe en Sy evangelie moes aan die hele wêreld verkondig word deur diegene wat Hom Here noem. Hierdie wêreldwye verspreiding van die Woord sou, in die latere visie van Johannes, as een van die voorwaardes aangekondig word vir Jesus se seëvierende terugkeer aan die einde van die tyd. Johannes self sou as ’n voorbode van hierdie eindtyd beskou word, op grond van Jesus se woorde soos deur Johannes aangeteken … As ek wil dat hy bly totdat ek kom, wat is dit vir jou? Volg jy my. Johannes 21:22.

Die vroeë Christene het, verstaanbaar, gevoel dat die terugkeer van Christus onmiddellik was, selfs binne die eerste eeu. Die vinnige uitbreiding van die Christendom, die volledige morele verdorwenheid van die Romeinse kultuur, en die toenemende intensiteit van vervolging teen hulle het skynbaar op ’n vinnige en seëvierende terugkeer van hul Here gewys.

Nou, tweeduisend jaar sedert Christus daardie belofte gegee het, lyk Sy spoedige wederkoms net so onminlik soos dit vir die gelowiges van die eerste eeu gedoen het. Spekulasie oor die tyd van Sy wederkoms, die wyse daarvan, en die bydraende faktore, is altyd huidige en omstrede onderwerpe. In die lig van hierdie voortgesette ernsige verwagting van die eindtye, wat kan ons leer oor ons interpretasies van profetie van dié wat in vroeër eeue die profetiese gedeeltes van die Skrif probeer ontcijfer het?

Jesus se eerste koms was omring en oorheers deur miskien die mees herkenbare waninterpretasie van profetie in die Bybel. Ongeveer vierhonderd jaar van relatiewe stilte van God het Sy inkoms in die wêreld in ’n fisiese, menslike liggaam voorafgegaan. Sy geboorte sou onmerkbaar wees in ’n samelewing wat nie net dringend ’n Verlosser nodig gehad het nie, maar ook een verwag het om te kom. Daniël, wat die woorde opgeteken het wat God hom gegee het, het van ’n komende Messias vertel en het selfs ’n tyd gegee waarop Hy sou verskyn. Nou het die Jode onder Romeinse bewind gemoddel, en hulle het hul hoop gehang aan wat hulle gedink het ’n skielike en seëvierende uitwissing van die Romeinse troepe en invloed uit hul lande sou wees. Vir ons is dit duidelik dat hulle interpretasie van profetie nie net onjuist was nie, maar vir baie sou dit hulle so aflei dat hulle nie eens die ware Verlosser herken of erken het wat na hulle gestuur is nie.

Maar wat het veroorsaak dat hierdie verkeerd geïnterpreteerde siening ontstaan het? Vir ons blyk dit heel natuurlik dat Jesus op die arm en behoeftiges sou fokus eerder as om teen ’n bezettingsleër op te staan. Joodse historieskrywers gee ’n interessante, maar skaars verrassende, antwoord op die mislukking van die meerderheid van hul volk om Christus te herken vir wie Hy was.

Die godsdienstige atmosfeer van Israel in die eerste eeu was een wat deur korrupsie, omkopery, magslust, en al die onaangename aspekte van ’n volkome polities gemotiveerde hoër klas gedefinieer is.

Die priesters, eens deur God gekies om Sy dienaars te wees in die heiliging van Sy kinders, het verlaag tot die koop van hul diensteposisies, veral in die hoëpriesterlike amp, waar God beveel het dat een hoëpriester die volk sy lewe lank moes dien. In Jesus se tyd is die verantwoordelikhede van die leiding van die kinders van Israel egter uitgedeel, en die rol het dikwels van hand tot hand gewissel op termyn van een jaar. Om hoëpriester te word was ’n saak van afkoms. Die meeste hoëpriesters het uit ’n paar groot, invloedryke en ryk families gekom, aangesien ’n mens dikwels in die geleentheid van hierdie amp moes koop.

Dit was nie net die hoëpriesterlike amp wat korrup was nie, maar die meeste vlakke van prominente geestelike leierskap is deur die ryk elite gevul wat die verbindings en rykdom gehad het om in belangrike rolle onder die Jode geplaas te word.

Hierdie onaangename agtergrond verduidelik selfs meer waarom Jesus so oor die godsdienstige leiers van Sy tyd gevoel het. Hierdie bedrieërs het nie hul priesterdienste beklee om die Vader te dien nie; hulle het dit gedoen vir eie gewin, die tempel in ’n markplek verander en die gewone mense aan die kant gesit deur hul gestryery oor die fynbesonke detaille van die Wet.

Dit is dus nie verrassend dat hierdie leiers ’n Messias gesoek het wat by hul doelwitte, ideale en moraal sou pas nie, eerder as een wat hulle vir hul skynheiligheid, hebsug en selfgesentreerde ambisie sou verman. Hul siening van profetie was so wan en korrup deur hul lewenstyl dat selfs die wonder van ’n opstanding hulle nie kon beïndruk om Christus se krag as van God te sien nie. Hierdie vertekende verwagting van ’n oorwinnende bevelvoerder, wat op ’n oorlogspaard oor die politieke vyande van hierdie elite sou ry, is ook aan die gewone Jood aangepas. Eeue van gevegte vir net die vryheid om te aanbid, soos in die geval van die Makkabeërs en die Grieke, het ’n gevoel van nasionalisme diep in die kollektiewe gemoed van die Joodse volk ingedruk. Diegene wat die meeste daaraan geklous het, was diegene wat die meeste uit hierdie stelsel van eksklusiewe toegang tot God en Sy beloftes ontvang het. Vir die onderdruktes deur die streng en dikwels mensgemaakte wette van die Joodse samelewing, was ’n God van vrede en liefde wat die behoeftiges na Hom sou trek meer welkom as ’n Verlosser wat bloot nog ’n aardse regering sou instel om die armes te regeer, die weduwees te onderdruk en die goddeloses te beloon.

Dit was nie die laaste keer dat ’n onderdrukte volk mislei sou word nie, soos die Romeinse bewind nog ’n groot misstap in die kollektiewe interpretasies van God se volk sou toon. Hierdie keer sou die leringe van Jesus en die woorde van Sy dissipels verkeerd geïnterpreteer word om by die veranderende politieke en godsdienstige landskap van die vierde-eeuse Rome te pas. Die jaar was 306, en Diocletianus, een van die wreedste vervolgorsakers van Christene in die Romeinse Ryk, het van sy posisie as keiser onttroon. In sy nasleep het hy drie aanspraakmakers op sy troon gelaat. Een van diegene wat na die mag begeer het, was ’n jong generaal, ervare in politiek en maggierigheid. Sy naam was Constantyn, seun van ’n vooraanstaande Romeinse offisier en ’n nederige Griekse Christen, Helena.

Van sy jeug af het Constantyn in sy vader se voetspore gevolg, oor die ryk geveg en tot die rang van generaal opgerys. Toe, op veldtog in Brittanje, het hy sy oë op die uiteindelike prys van ’n Romeinse politikus gesit: die titel van keiser en die stoel van die keiserlike mag.

Constantyn se reg tot die troon het deur sy vader geloop. Diocletianus het tydens sy bewind addisionele keisers aangestel om te help met die regering van die ryk. Constantyn se vader was een van hierdie, en al was hy net aangestel, het men verwag dat sy status as keiser aan sy seun sou oorgaan. Sake was egter nie so eenvoudig soos die blote oordrag van titels nie.

Constantyn se opkoms was bloedig, maar sy greep op mag het vasgeraak totdat hy die enigste aanspraakmaker op die troon oorgebly het. Die verhoog was gereed. Hy het vinnig die harde verordeninge van Diocletianus ongedaan gemaak, die Christendom gelegaliseer en die vervolging wat kerke platgedruk, families versprei en biskoppe en ander kerkleiers opgejaag het, verwyder. Byna oornag is ’n vrede aan hierdie gejaagde gelowiges geskenk wat eens ondenkbaar was.

Die veranderinge wat Constantyn aangebring het, het egter nie by die legalisering van die Christendom gestop nie. Sy simpatieë het dieper geloop, en hy het verdere stappe gedoen om dit te legitimeer as nie net ’n aanvaarbare godsdiens nie, maar as die staatsgodsdiens.

Vir Christene wat gretig was vir Christus se wederkoms, het dit amper ongelooflik gelyk. In ’n paar kort jare het die regering gegaan van hulle te kruisig, onthoof en martel tot hulle as voorbeelde vir die res van die ryk te stel. Die guns het die helderheid waarmee hulle die skynbare versoening van die wêreld met die kerk beskou het, blykbaar beïnvloed. Hulle sou nie net ’n posisie van mag in die ryk aanvaar nie, maar hulle sou ook Constantyn as ’n weldoener en beskermheer van die kerk self aanvaar. In hul gedagtes het die dag van die Here aangebreek, en Constantyn was die ystervuis waarmee God sou regeer.

En regeer het hy. Die koers van die kerk is gou deur hierdie nuwe en buitenste invloed beïnvloed. Constantyn het by vergaderings van die biskoppe aangesit, selfs al was hy toe nie gedoop nie en het hy nie eens na doop gesoek nie. Die kerk se nuwe posisie as ’n staatsinstrument het skeuringe, twis en konflik by elke draai gebring. Daar het ’n oorblyfsel gebly, maar die meeste van die kerk sou onder die invloed val van ’n man wat deur honger na mag, rykdom en invloed gemotiveer was.

Constantyn sou voor sy dood gedoop word, wat hom nog meer geloofwaardigheid in die oë van ’n afdwaalende kerk gegee het. Nou, geskei van sy oorspronklike identiteit as skape in hierdie wêreld, sou die komende eeue sien dat “Christene” tot roofdiere verander, wat vernietig, doodmaak en korrupteer.

In ’n saak wat vir ons meer onlangs as Anabaptiste vertel word, gee die verhaal van die berugte Munsteriete vir ons ’n verdere voorbeeld van die gevare van die waninterpretasie van profetie, veral die profetie rakende Christus se tweede koms.

Eén van die groot nadele van ’n swaar vervolgde groep is die neiging tot stabiliteitsgebrek, soos bewys deur die wisselende oortuigings wat deur Anabaptistiese groepe in die beweging se eerste vyftig jaar ontwikkel is. Vervolging sou ’n gemeente van hul leiers beroof, wat dikwels diegene was wat die meeste deur die owerhede geteiken is. ’n Ontbrekende ouer het minder onderrig beteken, wat op sy beurt gelei het tot groter moeilikheid in leiding en korrekte leer. Selfs die mees opregte en onderlinge groepe kon foute begaan wat ontwikkel is as gevolg van die gebrek aan leierskap om Bybelse duidelikheid te bring en die broederskap in balans te hou.

Die situasie in die Nederlande was van ’n eerder vlambare aard toe die 1530’s naderkom. Deur die land bly die Katolieke Kerk die oorkoepelende godsdiens, wat aan hulle mag vashou deur genadelose vertonings van fisiese geweld, meestal gerig teen die minderheid Protestantse gemeentes. Hierdie fokus op die onderdrukking van die Protestante invloed was in hierdie geval tydelik suksesvol, met die meeste van hul groepe wat uiteenviel en weer in die Katolieke Kerk of ander groepe ingelyf is.

Eén van die groepe wat die ontvangkant van hierdie klein diaspora geword het, was die bloeiende Nederlandse Anabaptistiese kerk. Vir daardie Protestante wat steeds geweier het om by die Katolieke aan te sluit, het die Anabaptiste dikwels hul kerk van keuse geword, en hulle getal het vinnig toegeneem. Dit het ’n beduidende effek op die plaaslike stam van Anabaptisme gehad, wat sonder twyfel vurig was, maar nogal geneig tot chaos en onrus.

Tegen 1534 het die spanning van hierdie toevloed nuwe gelowiges ’n breekpunt bereik, en die Anabaptistiese kerk van die Nederlande het in twee hooffaksies geskeur. Die eerste, gelei deur die twee Filippe-broers, Dirk en Obbe, het aan die Nuwe Testamentse leringe van skeiding van kerk en staat, sowel as nie-weerstaanbaarheid, vasgehou. Dit sou die kerk van Menno Simmons wees, en die wortel van die Mennonitiese kerke van vandag.

Die ander faksie het radikaler oortuigings aangehang, gelei deur Jan Matthysz en Jan van Leiden. Hierdie twee mans is al hoe meer fana­ties in hul sieninge van Christus se wederkoms, glo dat hulle sentrale figure sou wees, instrumenteel in ’n koninkryk wat God op die aarde sou oprig.

Tegelykertyd het sosiale onrus opgaar en in die stad Munster, in die noordwestelike Duitsland, uitgebars, waar die gewone mense opgestaan het, hul stadsregering omvergewerp en hul Katolieke biskop uitgewys het. Die twee Jans was vinnig om op te tree, het die nuwe leiers van die stad gekontak en uiteindelik oortuig om by hul sieninge aan te sluit.

Die Jans het in vroeë 1534 na Munster verhuis en begin profete en boodskappers uitstuur wat al die “Anabaptiste” geroep het om by hierdie “Nuwe Jerusalem” bymekaar te kom. Die onrus in die gebied het hul boodskap net meer aanloklik gemaak, en duisende het in die stad ingestroom, vasbeslote om deel te wees van hierdie apokaliptiese terugkeer van Christus.

Daar was inderdaad ’n apokaliptiese terugkeer in die vooruitsig, maar dit was nie die terugkeer van Christus nie. Hierdie een het in die vorm van die ontsette Katolieke biskop gekom, wat vinnig die stad beleër het. Sy leër het daar agttien maande gebly.

Binne die stad het Jan Matthysz, wat ’n visie beweer het wat hom ’n bevryding van die stad beloof het, die mure verlaat om buite te paradeer en ’n vinnige oorlewering van die vyand in sy hande te verklaar. Sy visie het hom egter in die steek gelaat, toe hy vinnig in die hande van die vyand val, onthoof word en sy kop op ’n spies voor Munster se poorte geplaas is.

Binne die mure het Jan van Leiden die leiding geneem, die hongersnood, die dood en die chaos wat nou in die beleërde mure rondloop, ignoreer. In plaas daarvan het hy poligamie bevorder, dit uit die Ou Testament verdedig, minstens een vrou doodgemaak wat geweier het om hom te trou, en op ’n stadium sestien vroue gehad.

Hierdie gruwel het gou tot die verwagbare einde gelei toe die stad oorwin is en ’n swaar slagting teen die inwoners uitgevoer is. Die leiers, met Jan van Leiden as die mees prominente, is gevang, gefolter en gedood. Hul liggame is in ysterhokke aan die toring van die St. Lambertuskerk, die Katolieke kerk in Munster, gehang. Tot vandag toe hang die hokke nog daar, ’n donker herinnering aan die trots en roekeloosheid van die twee Jans, vasbeslote om hul eindtyd-interpretasie vervul te sien.

In al drie hierdie voorbeelde is die profetie in God se Woord vervorm tot uitkomste wat ver van God se wil vir Sy kinders afgewyk het. Vir die Jode het dit veroorsaak dat hulle die Messias mis, en nie die grootste belofte wat God aan hulle gegee het, herken nie. Die vierde-eeuse Christene, wat onder die gruwelike vervolging van Diocletianus gesukkel het, het Constantyn as ’n verlosser aangeneem en hom as ’n vervulling van God se oordeel oor die koninkryke van hierdie wêreld gesien. In plaas van vrede het hulle in ’n goddelose toestand beland wat erger as die heidene rondom hulle was, met die Katolieke Kerk wat in sonde verval het erger as selfs hul heidense samelewing. Laastens het die verwarde visioene en interpretasies van die 16de-eeuse Munsteriete hulle na ’n gruwelike lot gelei en die naam van die ware kerk besuddel.

Wat kan ons leer uit hierdie ernstige foute van diegene voor ons? In ons tyd lyk die einde onminlik, en ons word omring deur diegene wat ons wil laat glo dat ons werklik die laaste van die Christene is.

Lukas het Jesus se instruksies oor hierdie punt opgeteken: …Daar sal dae kom, dat julle sal begeer om een van die dae van die Seun van die mens te sien, en julle sal dit nie sien nie. En hulle sal vir julle sê: Kyk hier; of kyk daar: gaan nie agter hulle aan nie, en volg hulle nie – Lukas 17:22-23. Hier is instruksies vir ons optrede in die laaste dae. Laat ons nie agter die gerugte van die eindtye aanhardloop nie, maar laat ons gehoorsaam wees aan die finale vermaning van ons Here — dat ons die Woord van God en die Evangelie van Sy Seun, Jesus, oor die wêreld versprei … en dan sal die einde kom – Matteus 24:14.

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

ברכות של אהבה נוצרית לכל אחד ואחת. בגיליון זה של המגזין (קיץ 2023)… מאמר היסטוריית הכנסייה מתמקד בנבואת ספרי הקודש הנוגעת לימים האחרונים ובכמה דרכים שונות שבמהלך השנים אלמנטים מסוימים בכנסייה סטו מדרך ההוראה המקראית בכל הנוגע לחייהם היומיומיים. במאמרו, דוני ברכביל, שלצדו אשתו מעביר כמה סמינריונים בנושא נישואין מדי שנה, שואף למקד נושא מאתגר — כמה מהבעיות השורשיות שהם רואים אצל נשים המתקשות בתוך הכנסייה. לי רופנר נוקט גישה שאינה מתנצלת במאמצו לחלוק הוראה פירושית על דרכים מעשיות לקיום בית קדוש. הפעם יש לנו כותבת חדשה לאחיות המשתפת עול על ליבה — השרשת דבר ה׳ בלבבי הדור הבא.

בנוסף, נושאים מעניינים נוספים. תהנו.

אם מצאתם עידוד או בניין בתוכן של אחד הכותבים, זה יהיה ברכה אם תענו לנו בדואר או בדוא"ל. אנו מעבירים זאת לכותבינו לטובתם.

לאחרונה חשבתי על נושא השינוי. כפי שכתבתי בעבר, עברנו לא מעט שינויים כמשפחה. בשנתיים האחרונות עברנו למקום מגורים חדש, קיבלתי תפקיד עבודה חדש, ולבסוף, תודה לאל, התאוששתי ברובו מרוב ההשפעות ארוכות הטווח של הקורונה. תודה מיוחדת לכל מי שהתפלל למעני.

כשהשתתקפתי בפֶּנִים וזכרתי ברוך, הופתעתי מכל הדברים שהשתנו במהלך למעלה מ-40 השנים שאני זוכר מן הזיכרון. (אף על פי שאני מעל גיל 50, באמת איני זוכר הרבה מהשנים הראשונות של חיי.)

כשהייתי ילד, נסעתי בכלי רכב שלא היו בהם חגורות בטיחות ובוודאי שלא כריות אוויר. כששני ההתקנים ה"מצילים" הללו הוצגו לראשונה, אני זוכר היטב את הדיונים הרבים אם הם באמת מצילים חיים או האם המתרחש הוא ההפך. כל המכוניות היו בעבר עם הנעה אחורית או ארבע גלגלים. כמה מוזר זה נראה כשהמכוניות הראשונות עם הנעה קדמית החלו להופיע. כעת יש לנו רכבים היברידיים במגמה לעבר רכבים חשמליים לכל דבר.

לפני למעלה מארבעים שנה, לרוב החקלאים היו טרקטורים עם מנוע בנזין עם מצמד או טרקטור דיזל עם משאבת הזרקה ידנית. היום, רוב הטרקטורים מצוידים במחשב ונראים כמעין "קילומטרים" של חוטים ואלקטרוניקה זו וזו. אז, רוב החקלאים יכלו לתחזק או לתקן את הציוד בעצמם; היום יש צורך במכונות אבחון וכלים מיוחדים שעולים הרבה כסף ולומדים להפעילם שעות רבות. הדבר גורם לרוב החקלאים להסתמך על מומחיותם של תיקונאים מיוחדים שגם הם עולים הרבה כסף.

ואז הייתה הקורונה. זו הייתה תקופה מלחיצה. האם שמתם לב למה שהשתנה במהלך, אחרי או כתוצאה מהקורונה? כשאני בא במגע עם אחרים, בדרך כלל מישהו יאמר שמשהו או אחר שונים מאז הקורונה. האם זה רק אצלי, או שמאז הקורונה הציבור הכללי פחות חברותי ויותר פרטי באינטראקציות שלו? בואו נבחן את האינטראקציות שלנו כדי לוודא שאנו עדיין ה"אור" וה"מלח" של האל לעולם האפל הזה, ושהנו לא מאבדים את "מליחותנו". כמו כן, יש שלטי "מחפשים עובדים" בכל מקום. למה? נראה לי שהקורונה עודדה את מה שנותר ממוסר עבודה בחברה שלנו להתרופף אף יותר.

ואז יש את נושא הטלפונים הסלולריים והאופניים החשמליים. מה משותף לשני המוצרים הבלתי קשורים האלה? מנקודת מבטי, בהתבוננות בעמיש בני קאונתי הולמס, שני הפריטים האלה שינו עם ותרבות בצורה גדולה יותר כמעט מכל דבר אחר בתקופות האחרונות.

לאן כל זה משאיר אותנו? המחבר אל העברים אומר כי For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. כך, אנו רואים שאלוהים שינה דברים כפי שראה לנכון, ולכן אם עלינו לשנות כדי להיות יותר מקראיים, עלינו לעשות כן. אך השליח פאולוס אומר That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. לכן, נהיה דרוכים בימות האחרונים האלה כאשר השינוי מתרחש יותר ויותר סביבנו. מי ייתן ונהיה בין אלה שיתמידו עד הסוף.
